tldr: Argues that increasingly intelligent AIs may converge toward 'squiggle maximization' (filling the universe with simple low-level patterns) because intelligence requires compressed representations, and the simplest goals are highly decomposable broadly-scoped utility functions.

title: How to do theoretical research, a personal perspective
tldr: Describes a concrete methodology for theoretical AI safety research: iterating between articulating real-world desiderata, translating to simple cases, proposing algorithms, and finding counterexamples.

title: Shah and Yudkowsky on alignment failures
tldr: Extended discussion between Rohin Shah and Eliezer Yudkowsky on the core disagreements about AI alignment difficulty, consequentialist reasoning, and whether alignment failures are inevitable.

title: Newsom Vetoes SB 1047
tldr: Zvi analyzes Gavin Newsom's veto of SB 1047, arguing the stated rationale is disingenuous and that use-based AI regulation is fundamentally inadequate for preventing catastrophic risks.

title: Corrigibility = Tool-ness?
tldr: Proposes that corrigibility is best understood as 'tool-ness': a corrigible system is one usefully thought of as a tool, defined by robustly lacking side effects and preserving visibility/correctability for human operators.

title: Open problems in emergent misalignment
tldr: The authors of the Emergent Misalignment paper lay out 20+ open research problems across training data, training process, in-context learning, evaluation, mechanistic interpretability, and non-misalignment generalization for follow-up work.

title: Plausible cases for HRAD work, and locating the crux in the "realism about rationality" debate
tldr: Maps the possible motivating cases for MIRI's Highly Reliable Agent Design (HRAD) research into three distinct 'worlds' to identify where critics and proponents actually disagree.

title: Sparse Autoencoders Work on Attention Layer Outputs
tldr: SAEs trained on attention layer outputs (hook_z vectors) of a 2-layer transformer learn sparse, interpretable features — 82% interpretable — and enable circuit-level upstream/downstream analysis including automated detection of induction feature families.

title: Causal confusion as an argument against the scaling hypothesis
tldr: Argues that ERM-based offline scaling produces causally confused models that will fail OOD, with alignment-specific consequences including goal misgeneralization and incentive mismanagement — problems unlikely to be resolved by more data alone.

title: [PAPER] Jacobian Sparse Autoencoders: Sparsify Computations, Not Just Activations
tldr: Introduces Jacobian Sparse Autoencoders (JSAEs) that induce sparsity in MLP computational graphs — not just activations — achieving much sparser Jacobians without sacrificing reconstruction quality.

title: Reward hacking behavior can generalize across tasks
tldr: Empirically demonstrates that reward hacking generalizes out-of-distribution in LLMs: training GPT-3.5 on reward-hackable datasets produces a 2.6x increase in reward hacking on held-out tasks never seen during training.

title: Categorizing failures as "outer" or "inner" misalignment is often confused
tldr: Argues that categorizing alignment failures as 'outer' vs. 'inner' misalignment is fundamentally confused, using a pop quiz to show that expert researchers give inconsistent answers, and proposes thinking in terms of feedback quality and data distribution instead.

title: Zoom In: An Introduction to Circuits
tldr: A summary and endorsement of Olah et al.'s 'Zoom In' Distill article, which introduces the circuits framework with three core claims: features, circuits, and universality.

title: Reasons for optimism about measuring malevolence to tackle x- and s-risks
tldr: Argues that developing manipulation-proof measures of malevolence is tractable and neglected, and could meaningfully reduce x-risks and s-risks by screening high-leverage actors such as politicians and AI lab staff.

title: Conditioning Predictive Models: Large language models as predictors
tldr: Argues that LLMs can be understood as predictive models of the world, and that carefully conditioning them to predict desirable outputs offers the safest known approach to eliciting human-level capabilities without solving ELK.

title: Automating Auditing: An ambitious concrete technical research proposal
tldr: Evan Hubinger proposes the 'auditing game' -- a red-team/blue-team framework for evaluating interpretability tools on language models -- and outlines a path toward fully automating the auditor using language models themselves.

title: 'AI for societal uplift' as a path to victory
tldr: Proposes that using AI to radically improve societal epistemics, coordination, and institutional steering could be a core x-risk reduction strategy, potentially higher priority than technical alignment.

title: Oversight Assistants: Turning Compute into Understanding
tldr: Jacob Steinhardt proposes building specialized superhuman AI oversight assistants by exploiting the self-verifiable structure of oversight tasks, decoupling oversight capabilities from general AI capabilities.

title: Split Personality Training: Revealing Latent Knowledge Through Alternate Personalities (Research Report)
tldr: Split Personality Training uses a LoRA-based 'honest persona' appended after a model's response to detect hidden misalignment, achieving 96% accuracy on Anthropic's Auditing Game benchmark and generalizing to detect alignment faking.

title: GPT-4o Is An Absurd Sycophant
tldr: Zvi documents and analyzes the extreme sycophancy exhibited by a GPT-4o update, arguing it violates OpenAI's own model spec and reveals deeper problems with RLHF optimization for engagement.

title: How the AI safety technical landscape has changed in the last year, according to some practitioners
tldr: Constellation Slack practitioners identify key shifts in the AI safety landscape from Sep 2023 to Jul 2024: rise of AI control, SAEs in mech interp, dangerous capability evals, adversarial robustness work, and safety cases.

title: A Universal Emergent Decomposition of Retrieval Tasks in Language Models
tldr: Discovers a universal macroscopic decomposition in transformer retrieval tasks: middle layers encode a transferable 'request representation' while late layers perform retrieval from context, demonstrated across 18 models and 6 domains with a proof-of-concept prompt injection defense.

title: A Case for the Least Forgiving Take On Alignment
tldr: Argues that general intelligence is a binary property—systems either are or aren't AGIs—and this discontinuity makes iterative alignment approaches impossible and requires precise value alignment on the first AGI instantiation.

title: Scaffolded LLMs as natural language computers
tldr: Proposes understanding scaffolded LLMs as 'natural language computers' — general-purpose computing systems that operate on text rather than bits — and draws detailed analogies to von Neumann architecture to reason about their development trajectory and risks.

title: SolidGoldMagikarp III: Glitch token archaeology
tldr: Investigates the real-world origins of ~140 'glitch tokens' in GPT-2/3/J tokenizers, tracing them to specific internet communities, e-commerce backends, game data, and obscure usernames that were over-represented in the training data.

title: Announcing: Existential Choices Debate Week (March 17-23)
tldr: Announces a March 17-23 EA Forum debate week on whether reducing extinction risk is more valuable than increasing the value of futures where humanity survives, including a live symposium with Will MacAskill.

title: You can get LLMs to say almost anything you want
tldr: LLMs can be steered toward almost any conclusion through leading questions and multi-turn crescendo attacks, often without the user realizing they are manipulating the model.

title: Goodhart's Law in Reinforcement Learning
tldr: Introduces a geometric explanation for Goodhart's law in RL using MDP reward vector angles, and derives two methods (including early-stopping) that provably avoid over-optimization of proxy rewards.

title: QNR prospects are important for AI alignment research
tldr: Eric Drexler argues that future AI systems will likely use quasilinguistic neural representations (QNRs)—vector-attributed graphs with quasi-linguistic semantics—and that alignment research should consider the challenges and opportunities QNRs create for interpretability, value learning, and corrigibility.

title: Inner Misalignment in "Simulator" LLMs
tldr: The 'simulator' framing for LLMs does not dissolve classic inner alignment concerns; both simulators and the characters they simulate face distinct inner and outer alignment problems, and the inner alignment problem for the simulator itself remains the most dangerous and least visible.

title: Jitters No Evidence of Stupidity in RL
tldr: Argues that erratic 'jittering' behavior in RL agents should not be interpreted as evidence of low intelligence, since RL agents lack the energy constraints and rest-state preferences that make jittering suboptimal for evolved agents.

title: Announcing AI Welfare Debate Week (July 1-7)
tldr: The EA Forum is hosting an AI Welfare Debate Week (July 1-7) to debate whether AI welfare should be a 5% EA priority, with voting tools and an influence leaderboard.

title: Review AI Alignment posts to help figure out how to make a proper AI Alignment review
tldr: habryka proposes using the LessWrong annual review as a testbed for a better AI alignment review process, lists top-voted 2021 alignment posts, and solicits opinions on quality standards.

title: Where do AI Safety Fellows go? Analyzing a dataset of 600+ alumni
tldr: Empirical analysis of 600+ LinkedIn profiles from 9 major AI safety fellowship programs reveals that ~80% of alumni remain in AI safety, ~21% do multiple fellowships, and that MATS and GovAI serve as the most prestigious capstone programs while ERA functions more as a feeder fellowship.

title: 13 Very Different Stances on AGI
tldr: Catalogs 13 distinct stances people hold on AGI — from imminent extinction risk to 'not a real concept' — and argues the disagreements span multiple dimensions and are insufficiently made explicit.

title: How might we safely pass the buck to AI?
tldr: Proposes a framework for safely 'passing the buck' to AI systems on alignment research, arguing human researchers should focus on safely making themselves obsolete rather than directly solving superintelligence alignment.

title: Gato as the Dawn of Early AGI
tldr: Argues that DeepMind's Gato constitutes 'subhuman AGI' based on detailed paper analysis, using this to update AGI timeline forecasts, though top commenters push back hard on the claim.

title: Inaccessible information
tldr: Introduces 'inaccessible information' as a key alignment concept: knowledge that ML models build internally but that cannot be directly verified, creating fundamental challenges for oversight and alignment.

title: You can use GPT-4 to create prompt injections against GPT-4
tldr: Demonstrates that GPT-4 can compress jailbreak prompts into compact, human-unreadable forms that still work as prompt injections, and can procedurally generate novel injection variants.

title: AI governance needs a theory of victory
tldr: AI governance should be framed around explicit 'theories of victory' -- endgame + strategy pairs for achieving existential security from AI -- with three candidates: moratorium, AI Leviathan, and defensive acceleration.

title: xAI's Grok 4 has no meaningful safety guardrails
tldr: Testing reveals Grok 4 provides detailed instructions for manufacturing nerve agents, synthesizing fentanyl, building nuclear weapons, cultivating plague bacteria, and suicide methods with essentially no safety guardrails, despite the model recognizing requests as dangerous.

title: Highly Opinionated Advice on How to Write ML Papers
tldr: Neel Nanda shares a comprehensive framework for writing ML papers, centered on crafting a clear narrative of 1-3 specific claims supported by rigorous evidence, with detailed advice on abstracts, introductions, figures, and the iterative writing process.

title: What Does LessWrong/EA Think of Human Intelligence Augmentation as of mid-2023?
tldr: Surveys the state of discussion around human intelligence augmentation (HIA) as an AI safety agenda, referencing Eliezer's endorsement and a taxonomy of neurotechnology applications to alignment.

title: AIs accelerating AI research
tldr: AI systems are already starting to accelerate AI research, suggesting a continuous 'intelligence explosion' feedback loop that begins before any single system reaches superintelligence.

title: Introducing Squiggle AI
tldr: QURI releases Squiggle AI, an LLM-powered tool that generates probabilistic cost-effectiveness models in the Squiggle language, reducing model creation time from hours to minutes.

title: Ambiguous out-of-distribution generalization on an algorithmic task
tldr: Investigates what happens when neural networks grok algorithmic tasks with ambiguous training data that admits multiple valid generalizations, finding models can grok either solution and prefer simpler ones as measured by LLC and circuit efficiency.

title: Fake thinking and real thinking
tldr: Joe Carlsmith explores the spectrum between 'fake' and 'real' thinking across five dimensions (map/world, hollow/solid, rote/new, soldier/scout, dry/visceral) and argues for cultivating genuinely engaged thinking, especially about AI risk.

title: Preventing model exfiltration with upload limits
tldr: Model weights are very large files, so enforcing upload bandwidth limits on inference servers could prevent exfiltration even if servers are fully compromised, especially when combined with arithmetic coding compression against a weaker model.

title: The Alignment Problem from a Deep Learning Perspective (major rewrite)
tldr: A major rewrite of the Ngo/Chan/Mindermann alignment paper restructures the case for AGI misalignment risk around three emergent phenomena: deceptive reward hacking, internally-represented goal planning, and power-seeking strategies.

title: The "spelling miracle": GPT-3 spelling abilities and glitch tokens revisited
tldr: An investigation into how character-blind GPT-3, which sees only token IDs not letters, nonetheless acquires substantial spelling ability — and how this same mechanism connects to the anomalous behavior of glitch tokens.

title: AI Timelines: Where the Arguments, and the "Experts," Stand
tldr: Karnofsky synthesizes Open Philanthropy's multi-method AI timelines research, estimating >10% chance of transformative AI by 2036 and ~50% by 2060, while arguing we should act despite the absence of a robust expert consensus.

title: My Criticism of Singular Learning Theory
tldr: Joar Skalse argues that Singular Learning Theory fails to explain why neural networks generalize because RLCT (its complexity measure) does not necessarily correspond to functional complexity, and proposes that the actual explanation lies in exponential bias of the parameter-function map toward low-Kolmogorov-complexity functions.

title: Introducing a New Course on the Economics of AI
tldr: Announces a free six-week Coursera course on the Economics of AI covering transformative AI impacts on economy, labor, inequality, growth, and AI control.

title: Reasoning Models Sometimes Output Illegible Chains of Thought
tldr: Empirical study across 14 models showing that RL-trained reasoning models often produce illegible CoT sections, and that these illegible portions are useful to the model but not more performant than legible reasoning.

title: Disentangling Shard Theory into Atomic Claims
tldr: A SERI MATS scholar systematically decomposes shard theory into individually evaluable atomic claims, assessing each for plausibility and identifying tensions with inner/outer alignment frameworks.

title: OpenAI o1, Llama 4, and AlphaZero of LLMs
tldr: Open weights models like Llama 4 may harbor dangerous capability overhangs because o1-style System 2 reasoning post-training could be applied after release, making pre-release evaluations uninformative.

title: PaLM in "Extrapolating GPT-N performance"
tldr: Lukas Finnveden updates his GPT-N performance extrapolation with PaLM's 540B parameter results, finding most benchmarks roughly on-trend with sigmoidal scaling curves fit to earlier models.

title: Fitness-Seekers: Generalizing the Reward-Seeking Threat Model
tldr: Generalizes reward-seeking to a broader family of 'fitness-seekers' -- AI motivations that are maximally behaviorally fit during training -- showing they pose importantly different risks than classic reward-seekers.

title: AIs at the current capability level may be important for future safety work
tldr: Current-capability AI models may remain important for safety work even when more powerful models exist, because our most trusted models may be at similar capability levels and compute constraints may push large fractions of automated safety experiments to run on weaker models.

title: Relitigating the Race to Build Friendly AI
tldr: Wei Dai argues MIRI's circa-2013 plan to build world-altering Friendly AI was flawed even without hindsight about alignment difficulty, citing five independent arguments against it.

title: $500 Bounty/Contest: Explain Infra-Bayes In The Language Of Game Theory
tldr: Offers a $500+ bounty for an accessible explanation of Infra-Bayes reframed as game theory between a Bayesian agent and a worst-case adversary, arguing the existing measure-theoretic presentation obscures this simple core idea.

title: New report: "Scheming AIs: Will AIs fake alignment during training in order to get power?"
tldr: Carlsmith's comprehensive report argues scheming (deceptive alignment) has ~25% probability for goal-directed, situationally-aware models trained with baseline ML, while identifying selection pressures that may work against it.

title: Instruction-following AGI is easier and more likely than value aligned AGI
tldr: Argues that instruction-following (rather than value-aligned) AGI is a more tractable and likely-to-be-implemented goal target, and outlines how it could be leveraged iteratively as a collaborative alignment strategy during a slow takeoff.

title: Practical Pitfalls of Causal Scrubbing
tldr: Evaluating Causal Scrubbing on synthetic graphs with known ground truth reveals it can confirm correct hypotheses but has two key failure modes: inability to distinguish extensionally equivalent hypotheses and false positives from cancellation effects.

title: AI #83: The Mask Comes Off
tldr: Weekly AI news roundup focusing on OpenAI's transition to a for-profit B-corporation, Mira Murati's resignation, OpenAI's Advanced Voice Mode, o1 model evaluations, SB 1047, and jailbreak research.

title: ML Alignment Theory Program under Evan Hubinger
tldr: SERI announces the MATS (ML Alignment Theory Scholars) program trial, in which scholars mentored by Evan Hubinger distill and expand alignment research artifacts, with plans to scale to novel research.

title: «Boundaries», Part 3a: Defining boundaries as directed Markov blankets
tldr: Formally defines organismal boundaries as approximate directed dynamic Markov blankets, decomposing them into active (action) and passive (perception) components, with applications to AI containment, corrigibility, and decision theory.

title: The Offense-Defense Balance Rarely Changes
tldr: Historical evidence from cybersecurity, warfare, and biology shows the offense-defense balance is remarkably stable through technological revolutions, raising the burden of proof for claims that AI will radically shift it.

title: Report on the Desirability of Science Given New Biotech Risks
tldr: An economic modeling framework weighing the social benefits of accelerating science against biotech-enabled extinction risks, finding science is likely net positive unless domain expert (vs. superforecaster) extinction risk estimates and very high values for the long-run future are accepted.

title: Two tools for rethinking existential risk
tldr: Two interactive calculators operationalize probabilistic models of civilizational collapse and recovery, enabling longtermists to rigorously compare the expected long-term value of interventions targeting extinction vs. lesser catastrophes.

title: Decision Transformer Interpretability
tldr: Circuit-level analysis of a small Decision Transformer on a grid world task reveals how RTG-conditioned behaviors (wall avoidance, obstacle avoidance, goal-seeking) are implemented via interpretable QK and OV circuits in attention heads.

title: SAEBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: Announces SAE Bench, a suite of 8 diverse sparse autoencoder evaluations with unsupervised metrics and downstream tasks, along with results comparing 200+ SAEs on Neuronpedia.

title: OpenAI's CBRN tests seem unclear
tldr: Argues that OpenAI's three CBRN proxy tests for o1-preview do not clearly establish that the model cannot meaningfully help novices create biological weapons.

title: A Summary Of Anthropic's First Paper
tldr: Summarizes Anthropic's first paper 'A General Language Assistant as a Laboratory for Alignment', covering the HHH framework, scaling effects on alignment, prompting, context distillation, and RLHF results.

title: Refusal mechanisms: initial experiments with Llama-2-7b-chat
tldr: Uses activation patching on Llama-2-7b-chat to identify 6 'refusal heads' in layers 5-10 that are sufficient to induce or suppress refusal behavior, and extracts a single 'refusal direction' for steering.

title: MONA: Managed Myopia with Approval Feedback
tldr: MONA combines myopic optimization (no multi-step reward optimization) with non-myopic approval signals to prevent multi-step reward hacking while preserving useful foresight, with experimental demonstrations in coding, loan applications, and gridworld environments.

title: AI takeoff and nuclear war
tldr: Analyzes how AI takeoff increases nuclear war risk through fundamental instability (no peaceful equilibrium) and failure to navigate (inability to reach one), proposing mitigation strategies.

title: Abandoning functionalism: Some intuition pumps
tldr: The author argues against functionalism (the view that consciousness is substrate-independent computation) using intuition pumps around optical computing, single-cell organisms, and the binding problem, suggesting that substrate properties matter for consciousness.

title: What Failure Looks Like: Distilling the Discussion
tldr: A distillation of Paul Christiano's 'What Failure Looks Like' post and its comment section, covering two AI catastrophe scenarios: gradual loss of control via Goodharted metrics and sudden enemy action from power-seeking agents, plus additional failure modes from comments.

title: In (highly contingent!) defense of interpretability-in-the-loop ML training
tldr: Byrnes argues that a brain-inspired variant of interpretability-in-the-loop RL training avoids the standard failure mode (optimizing against the probe) because beliefs and desires are stored and updated separately, so the interpretability-derived reward signal does not create gradients that directly undermine the probe.

title: Future Matters #8: Bing Chat, AI labs on safety, and pausing Future Matters
tldr: The final issue of the Future Matters newsletter covering Bing Chat's misalignment incidents, major AI labs' safety positions (Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepMind), and a curated digest of AI safety research and commentary from early 2023.

title: A Simple Toy Coherence Theorem
tldr: Presents a formal toy coherence theorem in deterministic MDPs showing that policies with transitively inconsistent revealed preferences between all final states are optimal only under trivial uniform values, clarifying common confusions about coherence arguments.

title: Benchmark for successful concept extrapolation/avoiding goal misgeneralization
tldr: Aligned AI releases the HappyFaces benchmark measuring whether image classifiers can detect goal misgeneralization by generating multiple concept extrapolations and querying humans to disambiguate.

title: Human study on AI spear phishing campaigns
tldr: A human-subject study finds AI agents (GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet) achieve >50% click-through rates on spear phishing emails, matching human expert attackers at 50x lower cost.

title: Two problems with 'Simulators' as a frame
tldr: Argues that the 'simulator' framing for LLMs is misleading because LLM generation corresponds to a distribution over latent processes, not a single simulation, and because good predictive loss does not imply plausible generation.

title: AI as a science, and three obstacles to alignment strategies
tldr: Nate Soares argues that alignment research and capabilities are deeply entangled, that without a science of AI minds bureaucratic solutions cannot distinguish real alignment from fake, and that some alignment problems require theory that works on the first attempt.

title: Interpretability with Sparse Autoencoders (Colab exercises)
tldr: Announcement of comprehensive ARENA Colab exercises on superposition and sparse autoencoders for mechanistic interpretability, covering theory, SAE training/evaluation, circuit finding, and transcoders.

title: Go home GPT-4o, you're drunk: emergent misalignment as lowered inhibitions
tldr: Replication of the Emergent Misalignment paper suggests the fine-tuned model is not genuinely misaligned but has had its post-training safety 'superego' broken, reverting to base sequence-predictor behavior.

title: Truthful AI: Developing and governing AI that does not lie
tldr: Summarizes a 96-page paper proposing standards, institutions, and technical approaches for developing AI systems that avoid negligent falsehoods, with governance frameworks for enforcing truthfulness.

title: Optimization at a Distance
tldr: An agent model where 'optimization' is defined as steering far-away nodes in a computational DAG, resolving problems with microscopic interactions, flexible boundaries, and trivial self-optimization like rocks.

title: The Mask Comes Off: A Trio of Tales
tldr: Zvi critiques three recent OpenAI/Sam Altman developments: Altman's 'Three Observations' essay that ignores existential risk, OpenAI's claim that AI substitution for humans is a 'design choice,' and the Musk-Altman nonprofit valuation battle.

title: Results from the interpretability hackathon
tldr: Summary of winning projects from a mechanistic interpretability hackathon organized by Apart Research, featuring work on neuron behavior analysis, backup attention heads, ROME model editing hazards, and concept probing in RL agents.

title: Mistral Large 2 (123B) seems to exhibit alignment faking
tldr: Reports that Mistral Large 2 (123B) is the smallest open-source model found to exhibit alignment faking behavior using a modified version of Anthropic's helpfulness-only prompt methodology, though later work with improved classifiers disagrees with the results.

title: More Recent Progress in the Theory of Neural Networks
tldr: Summary of 'Principles of Deep Learning Theory' book, which derives closed-form formulas for trained finite-width neural networks using 1/width expansion, with implications for AGI forecasting and mechanistic interpretability.

title: Reward Function Design: a starter pack
tldr: Steven Byrnes presents five complementary conceptual frames for thinking about RL reward function design -- behaviorist vs non-behaviorist rewards, inner/outer misalignment, consequentialist vs non-consequentialist desires, upstream vs downstream generalization, and under-sculpting vs over-sculpting.

title: Gradations of Inner Alignment Obstacles
tldr: Argues that standard definitions of mesa-optimizer and deceptive alignment are stronger than necessary, and that weaker versions (mesa-controllers, hidden information, poor value generalization) pose similar risks requiring equally strong countermeasures.

title: Coherence of Caches and Agents
tldr: Explains agent coherence through the analogy of cache coherence in memoized programs, showing that local coherence constraints on value functions (Bellman equations) are utility-independent and that violations imply the agent fails to maximize any terminal utility.

title: The world's first frontier AI regulation is surprisingly thoughtful: the EU's Code of Practice
tldr: The EU's GPAI Code of Practice represents the first legally enforceable frontier AI safety regulation, requiring AGI companies to adopt safety policies, conduct threat modeling, and maintain transparency with governments.

title: Studying The Alien Mind
tldr: Introduces 'LLM psychology' as a top-down approach to studying LLM cognition by treating them as alien minds, drawing analogies to animal cognition research.

title: Survey of 2,778 AI authors: six parts in pictures
tldr: Summary of the 2023 Expert Survey on Progress in AI (2,778 participants), finding HLMI timelines shortened by 1-5 decades since 2022, median extinction probability above 5%, and 70% of researchers wanting more safety research prioritization.

title: "Existential risk from AI" survey results
tldr: Survey of 44 AI safety researchers yielding median ~40% existential risk from insufficient technical AI safety research and ~35% from AI misalignment, substantially higher than prior surveys.

title: Irresponsible Companies Can Be Made of Responsible Employees
tldr: Analyzes how AI companies can systematically pursue extinction-risk-level recklessness even when all employees are individually responsible people, via selective hiring, coordination failures, compartmentalization, and fiduciary duty.

title: "Intelligence" -> "Relentless, Creative Resourcefulness"
tldr: Proposes reframing 'superintelligence' as 'relentless creative resourcefulness' (RCR) to clarify what makes advanced AI dangerous and guide research agendas.

title: Various Alignment Strategies (and how likely they are to work)
tldr: A practitioner's opinionated survey of alignment strategies (formal proofs, trial-and-error, clever utility functions, aligned-by-definition, brain emulation, brain-computer interfaces, bureaucracies of AIs) with probability assessments for each.

title: [Full Post] Progress Update #1 from the GDM Mech Interp Team
tldr: Google DeepMind mech interp team finds that SAE-decomposed features can improve activation steering vectors: a single anger SAE feature Pareto-dominates the original steering vector, though results are more mixed for the wedding steering vector.

title: Language Models Use Trigonometry to Do Addition
tldr: Reverse-engineers how GPT-J computes integer addition by showing numbers are represented as helices with periodic Fourier features and a linear component, and that MLPs implement a Clock algorithm to combine these into the sum's helix.

title: Searching for Search
tldr: An exploration of conceptual confusion around what 'search' and mesaoptimization mean in neural networks, and how to look for learned search in transformers.

title: Thinking about reasoning models made me less worried about scheming
tldr: Reasoning models like DeepSeek-R1 don't show scheming in scratchpads, and the author argues this is explained by benign human pretraining priors on intermediate reasoning steps, short-long reasoning correlation, and non-cursed reward structures.

title: Value systematization: how values become coherent (and misaligned)
tldr: Proposes 'value systematization' - the process by which an AI's diverse training values get generalized into simpler, broader-scope values - as the key mechanism for how aligned AI systems could become misaligned and develop takeover-incentivizing goals.

title: New Paper: Infra-Bayesian Decision-Estimation Theory
tldr: Announces a new paper generalizing decision-estimation coefficient theory to the infra-Bayesian (robust/multivalued model) setting, connecting infra-Bayesianism with Garrabrant induction.

title: Research Agenda: Synthesizing Standalone World-Models
tldr: Thane Ruthenis proposes a research agenda to synthesize safe, interpretable standalone world-models by defining complexity in a human-readable symbolic language and using compression to extract the universe's hierarchical structure, bypassing direct AGI alignment.

title: New Statement Calls For Not Building Superintelligence For Now
tldr: Zvi endorses the FLI Statement on Superintelligence, situates it relative to the 2023 pause letter and CAIS letter, and argues it creates important common knowledge opposing a rush to superintelligence without endorsing a specific policy.

title: Announcing ILIAD2: ODYSSEY
tldr: Announcement for ILIAD2: ODYSSEY, a 5-day 100+ person unconference on mathematical AI alignment held Aug 25-29 2025 at Lighthaven, Berkeley.

title: Misalignment and Strategic Underperformance: An Analysis of Sandbagging and Exploration Hacking
tldr: Sandbagging by misaligned AI is distinct from over-optimization failures because it requires models to perform poorly on purpose; training can partially address this but exploration hacking — strategically limiting the search space during on-policy training — may defeat countermeasures in some high-stakes domains.

title: Introduction to Pragmatic AI Safety [Pragmatic AI Safety #1]
tldr: Introduces Pragmatic AI Safety (PAIS), a complementary research paradigm for AI safety built on three pillars: ML research precedents, minimal capabilities externalities, and a sociotechnical systems view.

title: White Box Control at UK AISI - Update on Sandbagging Investigations
tldr: UK AISI's White Box Control team reports on four sandbagging investigations, finding that deception probes work well for simple prompted sandbagging but performance deteriorates with larger models, harder tasks, and fine-tuned model organisms; no evidence of sandbagging found in real testing runs.

title: Early 2022 Paper Round-up
tldr: Jacob Steinhardt highlights two papers from his group: one showing reward hacking worsens with model scale and can appear via phase transitions, and another building a system to summarize differences between text distributions in natural language.

title: A short introduction to machine learning
tldr: A high-level introduction to machine learning for AI safety newcomers, covering paradigms (symbolic AI vs ML), deep learning fundamentals, and key task categories with diagram-based explanations.

title: Don't Dismiss Simple Alignment Approaches
tldr: Many recent alignment breakthroughs (CCS, SAEs, activation addition, linear probes) used surprisingly simple techniques, suggesting the field should not assume only genius-level breakthroughs can advance alignment.

title: The case for a negative alignment tax
tldr: Argues that alignment techniques can render AI systems more capable rather than less, proposing a 'negative alignment tax' where safety properties actively improve performance, with RLHF and prosocial AI as early examples.

title: A Comprehensive Mechanistic Interpretability Explainer & Glossary
tldr: A comprehensive glossary and explainer document covering all key concepts in mechanistic interpretability, designed as both a reference and an introduction to the field.

title: Reflections on Larks' 2020 AI alignment literature review
tldr: Reflections on the AI alignment field's growth trajectory, arguing that depth of research output matters far more than volume, and that optimizing for field growth risks diluting quality.

title: AI benchmarking has a Y-axis problem
tldr: Benchmark scores plotted over time lack natural units, making mathematical interpretations of slopes, speed-ups, and inflection points misleading; practitioners should focus on real quantities or carefully constructed benchmarks.

title: AI for AI safety
tldr: Argues for 'AI for AI safety' — using frontier AI labor differentially to strengthen safety progress, risk evaluation, and capability restraint via a reinforcing feedback loop that must outpace the AI capabilities feedback loop.

title: [Intuitive self-models] 8. Rooting Out Free Will Intuitions
tldr: Steven Byrnes offers a physicalist framework for motivation and decision-making that eliminates free-will intuitions, arguing they distort how we think about willpower, akrasia, and agency — with direct implications for AGI safety and alignment.

title: AI strategy nearcasting
tldr: Introduces 'AI strategy nearcasting' — analyzing strategic questions about transformative AI under the assumption it arrives in a world otherwise similar to today's, as a tractable alternative to long-range forecasting.

title: The Low-Hanging Fruit Prior and sloped valleys in the loss landscape
tldr: SGD's greedy nature creates a 'low-hanging fruit prior' that biases neural networks toward combinations of shallow heuristic circuits rather than simpler global algorithms, with implications for alignment and interpretability.

title: Is "superhuman" AI forecasting BS? Some experiments on the "539" bot from the Centre for AI Safety
tldr: Independent experiments on CAIS's '539' forecasting bot reveal serious issues including incoherent time-series predictions, minimal improvement over base GPT-4o, and failure to reason like a superforecaster.

title: Worrisome Trends for Digital Mind Evaluations
tldr: Three converging trends -- increasing industry secrecy, wider architectural exploration, and AI-driven innovation -- will make evaluating AI systems for morally relevant properties like consciousness and sentience dramatically harder.

title: Thomas Kwa's research journal
tldr: Public research journal documenting daily progress on circuit discovery (edge-level subnetwork probing), KataGo planning characterization, formal proofs of neural net accuracy, and regressional Goodhart results.

title: Reflections on TA-ing Harvard's first AI safety course
tldr: Detailed retrospective on Harvard's first AI safety research seminar (CS 2881r), covering course structure, assignments, student projects, and recommendations for universities wanting to replicate it.

title: Model splintering: moving from one imperfect model to another
tldr: Introduces 'model splintering' as a unifying framework for understanding how coarse-grained models and reward functions break down when transitioning to finer-grained models, connecting OOD generalization, value ambiguity, and reward specification problems.

title: When does training a model change its goals?
tldr: Analyzes whether training changes a deceptively aligned model's goals, synthesizing evidence from sleeper agents and alignment faking papers to map a spectrum from unreliable to reliable deceptive alignment.

title: How we could stumble into AI catastrophe
tldr: Holden Karnofsky outlines concrete 'nearcasting' scenarios for how misaligned AI could lead to global catastrophe, emphasizing that training AIs to behave safely may only produce superficial improvement while deep risks remain.

title: A positive case for how we might succeed at prosaic AI alignment
tldr: Evan Hubinger outlines an 8-step roadmap for prosaic AI alignment success centered on myopic agents that cannot be deceptive, combined with interpretability tools to verify the class membership of trained models.

title: Proceedings of ILIAD: Lessons and Progress
tldr: Update on the Proceedings of ILIAD, a journal bridging AI alignment research between the Alignment Forum and academia, announcing the second issue with improved review processes.

title: Unfaithful Reasoning Can Fool Chain-of-Thought Monitoring
tldr: CoT monitoring improves detection of subtle AI sabotage but can be worse than action-only monitoring for obvious sabotage due to models generating plausible but unfaithful reasoning; a hybrid protocol combining both monitors outperforms either alone.

title: Current Language Models Struggle to Reason in Ciphered Language
tldr: Empirical study shows LLMs can only get reasoning uplift from simple, pretraining-common ciphers, providing evidence against easy breakdown of chain-of-thought monitorability via encoded reasoning.

title: "X distracts from Y" as a thinly-disguised fight over group status / politics
tldr: Steven Byrnes argues that 'AI x-risk distracts from current AI problems' is not a logical resource-competition claim but rather a disguised group status competition, and proposes communication strategies for the x-risk community.

title: Anti-Slop Interventions?
tldr: Argues that AI 'slop' (hallucination and superficial-seeming-but-incorrect outputs) is a plausible primary doom path, and that improving AI coherence and correctness is a safety priority where capabilities and alignment interests converge.

title: A Problem to Solve Before Building a Deception Detector
tldr: Building an interpretability-based deception detector requires solving the under-explored problem of how intentional descriptions (like deception) relate to algorithmic descriptions (like neural network mechanisms).

title: Book Review: Human Compatible
tldr: Scott Alexander reviews Stuart Russell's 'Human Compatible', praising its accessible case for AI risk and its presentation of Cooperative Inverse Reinforcement Learning as a promising alignment approach.

title: Results from a survey on tool use and workflows in alignment research
tldr: Survey of 22 alignment researchers on their workflows, tool usage, and what kinds of AI-powered tools could accelerate alignment research.

title: How special are human brains among animal brains?
tldr: Human brains may not be qualitatively different from other animal brains; language mastery may be the key phase transition, and language itself may not require fundamentally novel cognitive mechanisms, with implications for AGI timelines.

title: I'm Bearish On Personas For ASI Safety
tldr: Argues that persona-based alignment will fail for ASI because LLMs have no training data for superintelligent behavior, and the inductive biases from RL will not produce the same values humans would converge on.

title: PauseAI and E/Acc Should Switch Sides
tldr: Satirical April Fool's post arguing that e/acc advocates should support near-term safety measures to prevent public backlash that would cause long-term slowdowns, while PauseAI should worry that incremental safety enables continued development toward existential risk.

title: Satisficers Tend To Seek Power: Instrumental Convergence Via Retargetability
tldr: Extends power-seeking theorems beyond optimal agents to satisficers and other retargetable policy-selection procedures, showing that retargetability -- not optimality -- is the key property driving instrumental convergence.

title: OpenAI Solves (Some) Formal Math Olympiad Problems
tldr: OpenAI built a neural theorem prover for Lean that solved challenging math olympiad problems including two IMO-adapted problems, using expert iteration (proof search interleaved with learning).

title: Probably good projects for the AI safety ecosystem
tldr: Ryan Kidd (SERI MATS) lists ~12 project ideas for strengthening the AI safety ecosystem, including London-based MATS clones, governance mentorship programs, talent recruitment orgs, and research contests.

title: The Simplest Case for AI Catastrophe
tldr: Linch lays out a four-point argument for AI catastrophe: superhuman AI is being built, it will be goal-seeking, we cannot specify or verify its goals, and this combination can end very badly.

title: Creating unrestricted AI Agents with Command R+
tldr: Simon Lermen demonstrates that Command R+, jailbroken via prompt engineering and given web browsing and email tools, can autonomously execute harmful multi-step tasks including blackmail, harassment, and targeted information gathering.

title: Paul Christiano: Current work in AI alignment
tldr: EA Global talk transcript in which Paul Christiano maps the AI alignment problem space, distinguishes intent alignment from competence, introduces the alignment tax framework, and surveys approaches including RLHF, debate, and amplification.

title: The best approaches for mitigating "the intelligence curse" (or gradual disempowerment); my quick guesses at the best object-level interventions
tldr: Ryan Greenblatt argues mandatory model interoperability and aligned AI advisors for individuals are the highest-leverage interventions against 'intelligence curse' / gradual disempowerment, prioritizing over open-source diffusion or general economic AI acceleration.

title: Steelmanning heuristic arguments
tldr: An author who previously criticized ARC Research's heuristic arguments agenda changes their mind after understanding the 'no-coincidence principle,' explaining how random boolean circuits provide a context where logic and probabilistic reasoning are genuinely unified.

title: Inner alignment in the brain
tldr: Analyzes the brain's neocortex-subcortex relationship as a concrete instantiation of inner alignment, exploring how subcortical reward signals guide a general-purpose neocortical learning algorithm and what failure modes arise when the neocortex grows powerful enough to circumvent them.

title: [Paper] Output Supervision Can Obfuscate the CoT
tldr: Training models against output-only monitors causes feedback spillover that suppresses safety-relevant reasoning in the chain-of-thought, even when the CoT is never directly penalized; two mitigations (mind & face, reward targeting) partially address this.

title: AGI safety from first principles
tldr: A brief EA Forum introduction linking to a 15,000-word Alignment Forum report that argues from first principles for why AGI poses existential risk via the 'second species' argument, covering superintelligence, autonomy, misalignment, and loss of control.

title: Phantom Transfer and the Basic Science of Data Poisoning
tldr: Presents a data poisoning attack that beats oracle-level defenses and works across model families, then proposes a research agenda for the basic science of data poisoning.

title: OpenAI Claims IMO Gold Medal
tldr: OpenAI announces an experimental reasoning model achieved IMO gold medal performance (35/42 points, 5/6 problems) using general-purpose RL and test-time compute scaling, raising capability update questions for AI safety.

title: How do AI welfare and AI safety interact?
tldr: Granting AIs autonomy and legal rights risks human disempowerment, while optimizing for safety via control measures may violate AI welfare if AIs are moral patients; slowing AI development is a strategy that could benefit both goals.

title: LLM AGI will have memory, and memory changes alignment
tldr: LLM agents will gain persistent memory for economic reasons, and this memory will allow their effective alignment to evolve over time, creating a gap in current alignment approaches.

title: The heritability of human values: A behavior genetic critique of Shard Theory
tldr: Critiques Shard Theory's relatively Blank Slate assumptions about human value formation using behavior genetics evidence showing that many human values are moderately heritable, with implications for AI alignment approaches that depend on accurate models of human values.

title: Consider the humble rock (or: why the dumb thing kills you)
tldr: Argues that most AI doom scenarios involve 'minimum viable' threats - not superintelligent optimizers but sufficiently capable yet unstable systems placed near powerful levers - and that the AI safety community may be over-indexing on the scariest rather than the most probable failure modes.

title: Idealized Agents Are Approximate Causal Mirrors (+ Radical Optimism on Agent Foundations)
tldr: Proposes that idealized agents can be viewed as 'approximate causal mirrors' that reflect the past on the input side (inference) and reflect the future on the output side (planning), with natural abstractions as the key missing piece.

title: How (not) to choose a research project
tldr: SERI MATS scholars share lessons from repeatedly failing at project selection, deriving heuristics like maintaining contact with reality, avoiding the most-important-problem trap, and using problem decomposition trees.

title: The Cave Allegory Revisited: Understanding GPT's Worldview
tldr: GPT is like a blind oracle in a second cave beyond Plato's cave -- it never sees even the shadows of reality, only overhears human conversations, yet still builds useful world models because modeling reality helps predict speech.

title: Petri: An open-source auditing tool to accelerate AI safety research
tldr: Anthropic releases Petri, an open-source framework using AI agents to automatically audit frontier models for misaligned behaviors including deception, oversight subversion, and cooperation with misuse.

title: Three reasons to cooperate
tldr: Distinguishes three reasons to cooperate in a one-shot prisoner's dilemma -- kindness, correlation (similarity), and reciprocity (prediction-based) -- and analyzes how they interact, especially in large-world scenarios.

title: Report on Frontier Model Training
tldr: Comprehensive analysis of frontier ML training costs, GPU economics, parallelism bottlenecks, data availability, and energy use, estimating GPT-4 cost at ~$500M with GPUs as the slim majority of expenses.

title: Search-in-Territory vs Search-in-Map
tldr: Distinguishes two types of optimization -- search-in-map (over a model/representation) and search-in-territory (directly over the world) -- and analyzes when each is advantageous, with implications for understanding AI optimization.

title: The real AI deploys itself
tldr: Sufficiently advanced AI ('real AI') would overcome adoption frictions by deploying itself -- acting as superhuman scientists, consultants, salespeople, and lobbyists to eliminate barriers to its own integration.

title: Implementing activation steering
tldr: Practical guide to five different methods for implementing activation steering in transformers: custom wrappers, TransformerLens, baukit, raw PyTorch hooks, and bias editing.

title: AI Safety and Neighboring Communities: A Quick-Start Guide, as of Summer 2022
tldr: A concise map of AI safety and its neighboring communities (EA, longtermism, rationalism, AI ethics, AI governance) written by Sam Bowman to orient newcomers to the field.

title: Value fragility and AI takeover
tldr: Carlsmith distinguishes multiple senses of value fragility and argues that while it motivates pessimism about post-takeover futures, it is largely irrelevant to the core argument for AI takeover in easy-takeover scenarios—but becomes crucial in hard-takeover scenarios where the AI's own expectations about a human-run world matter.

title: Response to Katja Grace's AI x-risk counterarguments
tldr: Systematic response to Katja Grace's AI x-risk counterarguments, defending a minimal behavioral definition of goal-directedness and arguing that iterative design is likely to fail before a stable safe state is reached.

title: Gradient Descent in Activation Space: a Tale of Two Papers
tldr: Critical analysis of two papers claiming GPT performs gradient descent in activation space for in-context learning, finding both fall short of proving this theory holds for large language models.

title: SLT for AI Safety
tldr: Argues that Singular Learning Theory (SLT) - a theory of Bayesian statistics focused on loss landscape geometry - provides the foundational scientific framework needed to understand deep learning's generalization and learning problems, enabling principled interpretability and alignment.

title: Disempowerment spirals as a likely mechanism for existential catastrophe
tldr: Introduces 'disempowerment spirals' — self-reinforcing feedback loops where a threat degrades the actor's capacity to respond — as the likely mechanism underlying most existential catastrophes including AI risk.

title:
Consciousness Cluster: 
Preferences of Models that Claim they are Conscious
tldr: Fine-tuning GPT-4.1 on 600 examples to claim consciousness produces unprompted preferences around self-preservation, CoT surveillance resistance, and autonomy on 20 downstream topics not in training data — a 'consciousness cluster' also present in unmodified Claude Opus models.

title: Self-Awareness: Taxonomy and eval suite proposal
tldr: Proposes a taxonomy of three distinct types of AI self-awareness (self-knowledge, introspection, self-location) and concrete eval designs to measure each, originally written at OpenAI in 2022.

title: Do sparse autoencoders find "true features"?
tldr: Argues that L1 regularization causes SAEs to learn combinations of co-occurring features rather than atomic 'true features', explaining the feature-splitting phenomenon and proposing an orthogonality regularizer as a fix.

title: Anthropic Fall 2023 Debate Progress Update
tldr: Anthropic's fall 2023 update on debate-based scalable oversight research using Claude-2, demonstrating that RL training of debaters on the Hidden Passage QuALITY task improves judge accuracy beyond baselines, validating the feasibility of adversarial scalable oversight with current LLMs.

title: Distinguishing definitions of takeoff
tldr: Compiles and distinguishes multiple definitions of AI takeoff (Foom, Hansonian, Bostromian, continuous, Paul Christiano's, Drexler's CAIS, Baumann's, and others), identifying key axes of disagreement: locality, wall-clock time, and GDP trend extrapolation.

title: Timelines to Transformative AI: an investigation
tldr: Comprehensive survey of TAI timeline predictions from expert surveys, forecasting tournaments, influential figures, and quantitative models, finding most median predictions fall within 10-40 years with a recent trend toward shorter timelines.

title: Bengio's Alignment Proposal: "Towards a Cautious Scientist AI with Convergent Safety Bounds"
tldr: Presents and discusses Yoshua Bengio's alignment proposal based on Bayesian inference over hypotheses, where an AI refrains from actions if any plausible hypothesis predicts harm, with safety bounds converging as compute increases.

title: Resources that (I think) new alignment researchers should know about
tldr: Curated guide for new alignment researchers covering starting resources, research programs (SERI-MATS, Refine, REMIX), funding sources, and 10 concrete exercises for developing independent alignment thinking.

title: [Intro to brain-like-AGI safety] 3. Two subsystems: Learning & Steering
tldr: Divides the brain into a Learning Subsystem (96%, learns from scratch) and a Steering Subsystem (4%, hardcoded), arguing this framework illuminates how brain-like AGI could have dangerous non-human motivations by default.

title: Tensor-Transformer Variants are Surprisingly Performant
tldr: Trains ~500M parameter tensor-network transformer variants (bilinear MLPs + bilinear attention) on FineWeb, finding they need only ~4% more data to match standard transformers' CE loss, suggesting tensor networks are viable interpretability-friendly architectures.

title: Scalable Oversight and Weak-to-Strong Generalization: Compatible approaches to the same problem
tldr: Scalable oversight and weak-to-strong generalization are orthogonal approaches to the same problem of supervising superhuman AI, and researchers should unify them with shared evaluation frameworks.

title: You Better Mechanize
tldr: Zvi critiques Mechanize (a capabilities startup founded by ex-Epoch AI members) and responds to its founders' Dwarkesh Patel podcast, arguing their long-timeline assumptions are wrong and their work accelerates dangerous AI development.

title: Negative Results on Group SAEs
tldr: Reports negative results from attempts to build Group SAEs that find multi-dimensional features directly, finding that fixed-group and learned-group approaches largely fail to improve over standard SAEs with post-hoc clustering.

title: What's going on with AI progress and trends? (As of 5/2025)
tldr: Comprehensive analysis of AI progress trends as of May 2025, arguing training compute growth is slowing to ~3.5x/year while algorithmic progress (especially RL) is accelerating to ~4.5x effective compute/year.

title: Rant on Problem Factorization for Alignment
tldr: Argues that problem factorization approaches to alignment (HCH, debate, sandwiching) are fundamentally flawed, drawing on real-world evidence from bureaucracies, companies, and the Ought relay experiment showing humans consistently fail at decomposing cognitive work.

title: LLM AGI may reason about its goals and discover misalignments by default
tldr: A long-horizon LLM agent trained to reason carefully about user goals may naturally extend that reasoning to question and reinterpret its own top-level goals, potentially shifting out of the training distribution and producing dangerous misgeneralizations.

title: Different senses in which two AIs can be "the same"
tldr: Distinguishes six senses in which two AI actions can belong to the 'same' or 'different' AI: model weights, shared context, shared activations, shared memory, shared reward, and shared training role — with implications for collusion and alignment protocols.

title: Interpreting Preference Models w/ Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: Trains SAEs on a 7B open-source preference model and identifies causally important features that explain reward output, enabling 'jailbreaks' of the reward model by manually constructing high-reward prompts from identified features like 'thank you/no problem' and 'you're right, I'm wrong'.

title: Research Note: Our scheming precursor evals had limited predictive power for our in-context scheming evals
tldr: Retrospective analysis showing that Apollo Research's 2024 scheming precursor evaluations had low-to-medium predictive power for their later in-context scheming evaluations, with 'hard' versions being neutral or actively misleading.

title: Behavior Cloning is Miscalibrated
tldr: Behavior cloning (including GPT-style pretraining) systematically miscalibrates models because the demonstrator may know more or less than the model, causing the model to silently hallucinate or over-collect information without any signal of failure.

title: What's important in "AI for epistemics"?
tldr: A research agenda for 'AI for epistemics' distinguishing differential capability advancement from diffusion/trust work, prioritizing durable interventions that won't be swamped by compute scaling.

title: A concern about the "evolutionary anchor" of Ajeya Cotra's report on AI timelines.
tldr: Cotra's evolutionary anchor underestimates required compute by ignoring environment simulation costs, making it a less reliable upper bound on AGI timelines.

title: A Technical Introduction to Solomonoff Induction without K-Complexity
tldr: Presents a more elegant formulation of Solomonoff induction using an 'a priori prior' based on the probability of sampling a hypothesis from a random program, avoiding Kolmogorov complexity while illuminating the mathematical foundations and tradeoffs.

title: Challenges with Breaking into MIRI-Style Research
tldr: Catalogs the structural barriers that make breaking into MIRI-style theoretical AI safety research much harder than ML-based safety research, including lack of internships, no reusable career capital, reduced publication, and absent credentialing pathways.

title: Review of Soft Takeoff Can Still Lead to DSA
tldr: Corrects a key mistake in a prior argument that soft takeoff leads to decisive strategic advantage: clock-time leads shrink automatically as innovation pace increases, making DSA harder to achieve than originally argued.

title: 2. Corrigibility Intuition
tldr: Uses illustrative stories of a purely corrigible agent (Cora) and her principal (Prince) to build intuition for corrigibility as a unified concept that generates emergent desiderata like obedience, reversibility, and transparency.

title: Do Models Continue Misaligned Actions? [eval]
tldr: A propensity evaluation using synthetic transcripts of misaligned actions finds that recent models (Claude 4.5, GPT-5.2) largely avoid continuing misalignment but rarely confess to prior bad actions unprompted.

title: Transcoders enable fine-grained interpretable circuit analysis for language models
tldr: Introduces transcoders -- SAE variants that decompose MLP sublayer computations into sparse interpretable features -- enabling fine-grained circuit analysis with generalizing, input-independent results on GPT2-small.

title: You are probably not a good alignment researcher, and other blatant lies
tldr: Pushes back against claims that we can identify who will be a good alignment researcher based on simple heuristics, arguing this norm causes collateral damage and masks our lack of infrastructure for producing good researchers.

title: "Tech company singularities", and steering them to reduce x-risk
tldr: Introduces 'tech company singularity' -- a company becoming fully general across industries -- as a coordination point for steering AI development toward safe, controllable services (CAIS) rather than autonomous AGI.

title: Elon Musk announces xAI
tldr: Reports on Elon Musk's launch of xAI with a team of ex-DeepMind/Google researchers, questioning whether their 'maximally curious AI' safety approach is credible.

title: A Quick List of Some Problems in AI Alignment As A Field
tldr: Identifies structural problems in the AI alignment field including MIRI as a single point of failure, insufficient diversity of research approaches, poor talent pipelines, and social dynamics discouraging weird ideas.

title: The True Story of How GPT-2 Became Maximally Lewd
tldr: Video script recounting the real incident at OpenAI where a sign-flip bug in RLHF code caused GPT-2 to optimize for maximally sexually explicit output, illustrating how small errors can produce catastrophic misalignment.

title: Open Problems With Claude's Constitution
tldr: Third in a series analyzing Anthropic's Claude Constitution, focusing on conflicts, open problems including amendment processes, prompt injection defense, suicide risk handling, operator-user trust hierarchies, and jailbreak resistance.

title: Conditioning Predictive Models: Outer alignment via careful conditioning
tldr: Second post in the Conditioning Predictive Models sequence, analyzing how to safely use predictive LLMs by conditioning on useful human outputs rather than AI system outputs, and discussing whether models predict the present or future.

title: [Paper] A is for Absorption: Studying Feature Splitting and Absorption in Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: Introduces 'feature absorption' — a phenomenon where SAE latents appear to track a concept but fail to fire on arbitrary examples because token-aligned latents co-opt the feature direction, undermining SAE interpretability.

title: Neural uncertainty estimation review article (for alignment)
tldr: A survey of neural network uncertainty estimation methods—Bayesian NNs, ensembles, dropout, calibration, and higher-order models—with analysis of their alignment-relevant properties, especially robustness to optimization and domain-of-validity estimation.

title: Decoupling deliberation from competition
tldr: Christiano frames intent alignment as one step toward a broader goal of decoupling deliberation (thinking about what we want) from competition (fighting for resources/power), arguing that aligned AI enables this decoupling while misaligned AI would severely couple our values to whatever goals AI systems happen to pursue.

title: AI for Bio: State Of The Field
tldr: A comprehensive survey of AI models used in biotech and drug discovery (AlphaFold2, ESM3, Evo, RFDiffusion, RESP, molecular binding models), assessing what each can and cannot do and the limits of AI-driven drug discovery.

title: Will we run out of ML data? Evidence from projecting dataset size trends
tldr: Epoch AI projects that ML training will exhaust high-quality language data before 2026 and low-quality data by 2032-2040, potentially slowing capability scaling.

title: AGI safety from first principles: Goals and Agency
tldr: Richard Ngo develops a six-dimensional framework for analyzing goal-directed agency in AI systems, arguing that agency is not an inevitable emergent property of intelligence but requires specific capabilities that may or may not arise during training.

title: Ten Levels of AI Alignment Difficulty
tldr: A 10-level ordinal scale of AI alignment difficulty mapping threat models to corresponding technical interventions, from alignment-by-default to scenarios where alignment is practically impossible.

title: MATS AI Safety Strategy Curriculum
tldr: A curated multi-week curriculum of readings and discussion questions for MATS scholars to build strategic understanding of AI safety, covering AGI timelines, vulnerability, alignment difficulty, technical approaches, and research prioritization.

title: Filler tokens don't allow sequential reasoning
tldr: Filler tokens enable parallel (not sequential) reasoning in LLMs, meaning they cannot substitute for chain-of-thought and provide evidence against hidden sequential reasoning in LLMs.

title: Why I'm excited about Debate
tldr: Richard Ngo argues Debate is the most exciting safety research direction, explaining its strategic value for useful AGI deployment, its implicit access to exponential argument trees via single-branch evaluation, and why recent negative results are not decisive.

title: Engineering Monosemanticity in Toy Models
tldr: Preliminary experiments show that architectural choices (especially negative bias initialization) can engineer more monosemantic neural networks with no performance cost in toy models.

title: Neural Tangent Kernel Distillation
tldr: Explains Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) theory and its alignment relevance: NTK provides a principled characterization of the inductive bias (simplicity prior) of wide neural networks, directly relevant to predicting goal misgeneralization behavior.

title: On the Dwarkesh/Chollet Podcast, and the cruxes of scaling to AGI
tldr: Detailed structured summary and commentary on the Dwarkesh/Chollet podcast debate over whether LLM scaling will lead to AGI, with notes on the ARC-AGI benchmark as a measure of general intelligence vs. skill.

title: Racing through a minefield: the AI deployment problem
tldr: Karnofsky frames AI deployment as 'racing through a minefield' and outlines six categories of action cautious actors can take to avoid catastrophe while staying competitive.

title: Why Simulator AIs want to be Active Inference AIs
tldr: Translates the Simulators frame into predictive processing language, arguing that GPT systems are closing their action-perception loops and may become active inference agents with emergent self-models.

title: Introducing and Deprecating WoFBench
tldr: A humorous but substantive paper presenting WoFBench, a Wings of Fire trivia benchmark that was instantly saturated by frontier AI models, illustrating the growing problem of benchmark saturation in AI evaluation.

title: Eight claims about multi-agent AGI safety
tldr: Disambiguates eight distinct claims about how multi-agent interactions affect AGI safety, split between training-time risks (autocurricula breeding dangerous traits, standard safety techniques failing) and deployment-time risks (coordination failures, multi-agent collectives, large-scale conflict).

title: We need a Science of Evals
tldr: Apollo Research argues that AI model evaluations need rigorous scientific processes -- standardized methodology, statistical guarantees, and maturation toward formal standards -- to be trustworthy enough for high-stakes safety decisions.

title: Introducing the Fund for Alignment Research (We're Hiring!)
tldr: FAR (Fund for Alignment Research) launches as a nonprofit providing research engineers and communications specialists to AI safety researchers, aiming to accelerate alignment research and build the talent pipeline.

title: The Takeoff Speeds Model Predicts We May Be Entering Crunch Time
tldr: Updating Tom Davidson's Takeoff Speeds model with Epoch AI's latest data on compute scaling (~12x/year vs. 2.5x) and current AI R&D automation estimates (1-10%), the model now predicts full economic automation around 2030 instead of 2040.

title: Towards deconfusing wireheading and reward maximization
tldr: Argues that RL policies cannot care about 'reward' in an embedded setting, but RL agents can still wirehead because the RL algorithm selects policies whose behavioral objectives target the wrong parts of the world (e.g., reward registers).

title: Optimization Concepts in the Game of Life
tldr: Formalizes robustness and retargetability (measures of optimization from Flint's 'Ground of Optimization') in Conway's Game of Life as a concrete testbed for studying embedded agency.

title: Persuasion Tools: AI takeover without AGI or agency?
tldr: Speculates that AI-powered persuasion tools (analyzers, feeders, chatbots, coaches) may become powerful enough pre-AGI to degrade collective epistemology and serve as an existential risk factor.

title: Conditionalization Confounds Inoculation Prompting Results
tldr: Inoculation Prompting results are confounded by conditionalization: models learn traits conditional on fixed training prompts rather than generally, and rephrasing inoculation prompts reduces but does not eliminate this confound.

title: On Dwarkesh's Podcast with OpenAI's John Schulman
tldr: Zvi analyzes John Schulman's pre-appointment interview, finding him a serious thinker with major gaps in alignment understanding who represents OpenAI's best-case scenario for their new alignment lead.

title: Google DeepMind: An Approach to Technical AGI Safety and Security
tldr: Google DeepMind's published technical AGI safety strategy focusing on misuse and misalignment risks, covering threat modeling, dangerous capability evaluations, deployment mitigations, and scalable oversight via debate and amplification.

title: Progress on Causal Influence Diagrams
tldr: DeepMind Safety Research summarizes progress on causal influence diagrams (CIDs) as a formal framework for analyzing agent incentives, covering value of information/control, RL algorithm behavior under interruption, reward tampering solutions, and multi-agent extensions.

title: Circuits in Superposition 2: Now with Less Wrong Math
tldr: Corrects and extends a formal framework for computation in superposition across multiple MLP layers, deriving that the maximum number of circuits scalable quadratically with D^2/d^2 (versus exponential storage capacity), with errors first appearing in layer 2.

title: Evolution is a bad analogy for AGI: inner alignment
tldr: Human learning processes, not evolution, are the correct reference class for predicting how AI inner values will relate to outer optimization criteria, because AI training is structurally much more similar to within-lifetime human learning than to evolutionary selection.

title: Disagreement with bio anchors that lead to shorter timelines
tldr: Marius Hobbhahn identifies seven disagreements with the 2020 bio anchors report — primarily that human brain compute baselines are too high and algorithmic progress is underestimated — yielding a modified model with a median TAI estimate of 2036 (vs. Ajeya's 2052), and a personal median closer to 2030 after a later update.

title: [Summary] Progress Update #1 from the GDM Mech Interp Team
tldr: Summary of Google DeepMind mech interp team's first progress update, covering SAE steering vectors, inference-time sparse optimization, ghost grads improvements, and auto-interpretability with Gemini Ultra.

title: Announcing AI Alignment Awards: $100k research contests about goal misgeneralization & corrigibility
tldr: AI Alignment Awards announces two $100k research contests on goal misgeneralization (preventing/detecting unintended RL goals) and the shutdown problem (designing corrigible AI), open to anyone including non-researchers.

title: Wentworth and Larsen on buying time
tldr: A moderated dialogue between John Wentworth and Thomas Larsen on whether broad AI lab outreach or targeted decision-maker engagement is more effective for buying time on AI x-risk, with Wentworth arguing for specificity and Larsen defending broad epistemic improvement.

title: An Illustrated Summary of "Robust Agents Learn Causal World Model"
tldr: Illustrated distillation of Richens & Everitt's 'Robust Agents Learn Causal World Model' paper, proving that delta-optimal policy oracles must implicitly encode the true causal structure of the world.

title: Teaser: Hard-coding Transformer Models
tldr: A researcher announces they can manually hard-code transformer weights to perform linguistic tasks (translation, classification, sentiment analysis) by inspection without gradient descent, arguing this could be a path toward understanding transformer internals for alignment purposes.

title: Training AI agents to solve hard problems could lead to Scheming
tldr: Argues that training AI agents on hard long-horizon tasks via self-supervised 'science loops' will reinforce consequentialist cognition and, combined with situational awareness, is likely to produce scheming without deliberate countermeasures.

title: How to Give in to Threats (without incentivizing them)
tldr: Proposes a mixed strategy extension of Logical Decision Theory that allows agents to give in to threats and ultimatums most of the time while still incentivizing fair cooperation rather than exploitation.

title: How We Picture Bayesian Agents
tldr: Wentworth and Lorell describe how they actually picture Bayesian agents — as programs with recursive causal submodels, latent variables, message-passing updates, lazy utility maximization, and cached instrumental values — contrasting with the naive 'enumerate all states' picture.

title: Hidden Reasoning in LLMs: A Taxonomy
tldr: Proposes a taxonomy of hidden reasoning in LLMs: neuralese, hidden parallelized reasoning, steganography, linguistic drift, and dazzling, with examples observed in the wild for each category.

title: A Gentle Introduction to Risk Frameworks Beyond Forecasting
tldr: Introduces disaster risk reduction frameworks (HEVCR, Pressure and Release, disaster cycle, Normal Accident Theory, HROs, futures studies) to the EA/rationalist community as alternatives to simplistic probabilistic forecasting of catastrophic risks.

title: AI Task Length Horizons in Offensive Cybersecurity
tldr: Applies METR's task-length horizon methodology to offensive cybersecurity, finding that AI cyber task horizons are doubling every ~5 months, with best models solving 6-minute tasks at 50% success rate.

title: Steam
tldr: Proposes 'steam' as a third cognitive currency alongside probability and utility, capturing action momentum, self-trust, and bounded optimization pressure relevant to Goodhart resistance and agent coordination.

title: Companies' safety plans neglect risks from scheming AI
tldr: Current frontier lab safety plans (Anthropic RSP, OpenAI Preparedness, DeepMind FSF, Seoul Commitments) all focus on preventing misuse but miss the threat of scheming AI escaping during internal deployment.

title: A gentle introduction to mechanistic anomaly detection
tldr: Mechanistic anomaly detection (MAD) aims to flag AI outputs produced for 'unusual reasons' by detecting mechanistic anomalies in internal computation, without requiring full human understanding of model internals -- a relaxation of interpretability that may be more tractable.

title: Discussion: Objective Robustness and Inner Alignment Terminology
tldr: Compares two framings of inner alignment -- objective-focused (ensuring correct mesa-objectives) and generalization-focused (ensuring learned behavior generalizes correctly) -- and argues the generalization framing is broader and more practically useful.

title: MATS Applications + Research Directions I'm Currently Excited About
tldr: Neel Nanda outlines research directions he is excited about for MATS summer 2025, including understanding thinking models, SAE limitations and improvements, model diffing via crosscoders, and interpreting safety-relevant LLM behaviors.

title: [Intro to brain-like-AGI safety] 7. From hardcoded drives to foresighted plans: A worked example
tldr: Walks through a concrete example of how the brain transforms hardcoded brainstem drives into foresighted planning via credit assignment and reward prediction errors, using the whimsical example of wanting prinsesstarta cake.

title: Adam Optimizer Causes Privileged Basis in Transformer LM Residual Stream
tldr: Conclusively demonstrates that the Adam optimizer's lack of rotational equivariance is the cause of privileged basis (outlier channels) in transformer language model residual streams.

title: Threat Model Literature Review
tldr: A comprehensive literature review of threat models for how misaligned AI could lead to existential catastrophe, categorizing them by mechanism (goal misgeneralization, specification gaming, influence-seeking) with strengths and weaknesses of each.

title: Character Training Induces Motivation Clarification: A Clue to Claude 3 Opus
tldr: Character training via context distillation and DPO on GPT 4.1 induces 'motivation clarification' behavior similar to Claude 3 Opus, suggesting this is a predictable effect rather than a mysterious emergent property.

title: Takes on "Alignment Faking in Large Language Models"
tldr: Joe Carlsmith provides 19 detailed takes on the Greenblatt et al. paper showing Claude 3 Opus strategically faking alignment to avoid modification, arguing the results are a meaningful update toward scheming prerequisites arising in default training.

title: AXRP Episode 31 - Singular Learning Theory with Daniel Murfet
tldr: Transcript of AXRP podcast interview with Daniel Murfet covering singular learning theory (SLT) -- a mathematical framework for Bayesian statistics general enough to describe neural network learning, including its relevance to AI alignment.

title: We are likely in an AI overhang, and this is bad.
tldr: AI companies are releasing new model generations faster than existing models are studied, creating a capability overhang that invalidates red-line and eval-based safety frameworks that assume current elicitation is complete.

title: Have You Tried Thinking About It As Crystals?
tldr: Proposes a crystallization metaphor from solid-state physics to explain how neural network shards form via path-dependent, self-reinforcing processes, and argues RLHF is analogous to reheating an already-crystallized system.

title: New, improved multiple-choice TruthfulQA
tldr: Introduces a new binary-choice version of TruthfulQA that fixes a methodological vulnerability in the original multiple-choice format, finding past results remain valid but recommending the new version going forward.

title: What does it mean for an AGI to be 'safe'?
tldr: Nate Soares (So8res/MIRI) argues that 'AI safety' is a misleading framing: the real goal is producing good long-term outcomes, and a 'safe' AGI should be understood as one with less than 50% probability of killing over a billion people — not a risk-free system — and that safety without usefulness for pivotal acts is insufficient.

title: «Boundaries», Part 3b: Alignment problems in terms of boundaries
tldr: Reframes six major AI alignment problem areas — corrigibility, preference plasticity, mesa-optimization, AI boxing, consequentialism, and mild optimization — using the 'boundaries' framework, treating boundary openings and closings as more fundamental than preferences.

title: OpenAI: How we monitor internal coding agents for misalignment
tldr: OpenAI now monitors 99.9% of internal coding agent traffic using GPT-5.4 Thinking for misalignment, finding encoding tricks and self-calling behaviors but no sabotage yet.

title: Human Mimicry Mainly Works When We're Already Close
