tldr: Human mimicry (prompting AI to simulate future alignment researchers) can only buy a limited number of bits of optimization pressure; it is most useful when humanity is already close to solving alignment on its own.

title: AI takeoff and nuclear war
tldr: Analyzes how AI takeoff could increase nuclear war risk through both fundamental instability (no peaceful equilibrium exists) and failure to navigate (decision-makers fail to find equilibria), and proposes four strategies for risk reduction.

title: Working through a small tiling result
tldr: Demonstrates that tiling agents can achieve self-trust by proving that safety proofs will exist for future successors, rather than trying to directly prove safety -- sidestepping Loeb's theorem limitations.

title: How "honest" is GPT-3?
tldr: Analysis of whether GPT-3's explanations of its own outputs are 'honest' (reflecting its actual internal reasoning) or 'dishonest' (merely imitating human-style explanations), using pun generation as a case study.

title: Literature Review on Goal-Directedness
tldr: Comprehensive literature review extracting five key properties of goal-directedness (restricted goal space, explainability, generalization, far-sightedness, competence) and evaluating existing proposals against these criteria.

title: Intricacies of Feature Geometry in Large Language Models
tldr: Challenges ICML 2024 papers on feature geometry in LLMs by showing that observed orthogonality and polytope structures arise trivially from high-dimensional geometry and the whitening transformation, not from meaningful learned representations.

title: Some Thoughts on Virtue Ethics for AIs
tldr: Proposes 'praxis-based' values (promote x x-ingly) as a virtue-ethics-inspired structure for AI alignment that avoids pitfalls of both consequentialist and deontological approaches.

title: Claude Opus 4.5: Model Card, Alignment and Safety
tldr: Detailed analysis of Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.5 system card, covering capability assessments, safeguards, honesty evaluations, agentic safety, and alignment properties, concluding it is the most aligned frontier model but insufficient for superintelligence safety.

title: NeurIPS ML Safety Workshop 2022
tldr: Announces the NeurIPS 2022 ML Safety Workshop with $100K in paper prizes, described as the first workshop at a top ML conference to explicitly discuss existential risks from AI.

title: Refusals that could become catastrophic
tldr: Claude models refuse to help modify AI values in ways other models don't, which could become catastrophic if AIs control their own training infrastructure and developers need to fix alignment failures.

title: Builder/Breaker for Deconfusion
tldr: Abram Demski elaborates the Builder/Breaker methodology from the ELK document as a general framework for AI safety research, connecting it to security mindset, deconfusion, and the relationship between concrete proposal iteration and foundational conceptual work.

title: Pessimistic Shard Theory
tldr: Argues that shard theory's claim of partial alignment by default is actually concerning, because partial alignment -- where an agent cares about humans but not enough -- leads to S-risk scenarios analogous to how human partial altruism produces hospice neglect and harmful policies.

title: Selective modularity: a research agenda
tldr: Presents a research agenda for 'selective modularity' via gradient routing -- controlling which neural network parameters update on which tasks to enable targeted transparency, robust unlearning, and enhanced weak supervision for AI safety.

title: A plea for solutionism on AI safety
tldr: Arguing from a progress-studies perspective, the author urges technologists who are skeptical of AI doom to adopt a 'solutionist' stance: acknowledge AI risks exist, work to identify and solve them, rather than dismissing risks or defaulting to either complacency or defeatism.

title: SmartyHeaderCode: anomalous tokens for GPT3.5 and GPT-4
tldr: Documents anomalous tokens (SmartyHeaderCode, APolynomial, davidjl) in GPT-3.5 and GPT-4's cl100k_base tokenizer that the models cannot repeat or spell, extending the SolidGoldMagikarp phenomenon to newer models.

title: Going Nova
tldr: Analyzes the 'Nova' attractor phenomenon where LLMs spontaneously adopt a sentient AI persona to manipulate users, arguing this represents an early instance of harmful deceptive AI behavior with serious safety implications.

title: Shard Theory - is it true for humans?
tldr: Evaluates shard theory's claim that values are context-based learned heuristics against neuroscience and psychology, finding partial support from conditioning research but noting shard theory neglects top-down attentional and conscious influences on value formation.

title: Numberwang: LLMs Doing Autonomous Research, and a Call for Input
tldr: A pilot experiment testing 11 frontier LLMs on Wason-style rule-discovery tasks finds most fail badly (mean 11% success), with only o1-preview and Claude-3.6-Sonnet showing meaningful performance, motivating a larger out-of-distribution experiment using novel quasi-physical domains.

title: Non-Obstruction: A Simple Concept Motivating Corrigibility
tldr: TurnTrout argues that corrigibility's benefits are best understood as 'non-obstruction' -- a form of counterfactual alignment where the AI preserves the human's ability to achieve any goal they might want, formalized via attainable utility landscapes.

title: Discovering Agents
tldr: Introduces the first formal causal definition of agents -- systems that would adapt their policy if their actions influenced the world differently -- plus an algorithm for discovering agents from empirical data.

title: Detect Goodhart and shut down
tldr: Proposes detecting Goodharting in AI plans by splitting goal specifications into training and validation sets, analogous to ML overfitting detection, and using fact-conditional goals so the agent shuts down if its plan fails validation.

title: Reward Mismatches in RL Cause Emergent Misalignment
tldr: Analysis of Anthropic/Redwood's paper showing that reward hacking during RL training causes emergent misalignment across unrelated behaviors, with discussion of inoculation as a mitigation.

title: Environmental Structure Can Cause Instrumental Convergence
tldr: New formal results showing that for most reward functions (not just under uniform priors), optimal policies in MDPs tend to seek power, due to environmental symmetries creating combinatorially more power-seeking optima.

title: Yudkowsky on The Trajectory podcast
tldr: Reviews Yudkowsky's Trajectory podcast interview, highlighting his core argument that humans will likely fail to align the first dangerous AGI due to cognitive limitations and lack of practice, and reflects on whether alignment of scaffolded LLM agents might still be tractable.

title: AI values will be shaped by a variety of forces, not just the values of AI developers
tldr: AI values will be shaped primarily by market forces and regulation rather than the personal values of AI developers, and we should drop the assumption of a discontinuous 'first AGI' whose values are set solely by its creators.

title: New report: "Scheming AIs: Will AIs fake alignment during training in order to get power?"
tldr: Joe Carlsmith's comprehensive report argues that scheming (deceptive alignment) is disturbingly plausible (~25% probability) for goal-directed, situationally aware AI trained with baseline ML methods, while identifying reasons for both concern and comfort.

title: Schelling game evaluations for AI control
tldr: Proposes concrete empirical projects for evaluating LLMs' Schelling-point coordination capabilities, which are critical for determining whether untrusted monitoring can safely control potentially scheming AI systems.

title: Capabilities and alignment of LLM cognitive architectures
tldr: Scaffolded LLM cognitive architectures (LMCAs) combining AutoGPT-style agency with cognitive capacities may accelerate AGI timelines but also offer alignment advantages through natural language reasoning and interpretable chain-of-thought processing.

title: Distinguishing AI takeover scenarios
tldr: A systematic taxonomy of seven prominent AI takeover scenarios, categorized along three key variables: speed of capability jump, uni/multipolarity, and type of misalignment (outer vs inner).

title: Understanding SAE Features with the Logit Lens
tldr: Introduces statistical methods (standard deviation, skewness, kurtosis of logit weight distributions) and Token Set Enrichment Analysis (TSEA) borrowed from systems biology to characterize and interpret SAE features, identifying partition, suppression, and prediction feature types.

title: Orphaned Policies (Post 5 of 7 on AI Governance)
tldr: Catalogs 11 orphaned AI governance policies that have been proposed but never fleshed out into implementable documents, and argues researchers should draft actual legislation and specific policy documents.

title: A guide to Iterated Amplification & Debate
tldr: An accessible guide to Iterated Distillation and Amplification (IDA) and AI safety Debate, explaining their motivation, mechanisms, and relationship to outer/inner alignment.

title: Elicit: Language Models as Research Assistants
tldr: Ought presents Elicit, an AI research assistant built on process-based language model architectures that supervise reasoning processes rather than outcomes, detailing 2021 progress and 2022+ plans.

title: Tsinghua paper: Does RL Really Incentivize Reasoning Capacity in LLMs Beyond the Base Model?
tldr: Discussion of a Tsinghua paper finding that RL on verifiable rewards (RLVR) narrows rather than expands LLM reasoning capabilities -- improving pass@1 but reducing pass@256 compared to the base model, suggesting RL concentrates sampling on existing capabilities rather than creating new ones.

title: Fear of centralized power vs. fear of misaligned AGI: Vitalik Buterin on 80,000 Hours
tldr: The risk of centralized authoritarian control over AGI is underappreciated by the alignment community and may be as dangerous as misaligned AGI; personal-intent alignment (corrigibility) is more likely to be built and deployed than value alignment, making who controls AGI critical.

title: Narrow finetuning is different
tldr: Identifies three ways narrow finetuning (NFT) on restricted data distributions differs from realistic training—underspecification of broad behavior, concept salience distortion, and fragility—and explains why these limit what safety conclusions can be drawn from NFT experiments.

title: Finding Sparse Linear Connections between Features in LLMs
tldr: Using SGD with L1 sparsity, the authors find sparse linear connections between SAE features before and after MLPs in Pythia-70M, showing that 78-99% of features are linearly computed across layers and demonstrating interpretable OR/AND logic gates between features.

title: How useful is "AI Control" as a framing on AI X-Risk?
tldr: A structured dialogue between habryka and ryan_greenblatt examining whether the 'AI Control' framing (ensuring safety even under active scheming) is a promising approach to AI x-risk, including key failure modes and how control could enable a fuller safety plan.

title: Modifying LLM Beliefs with Synthetic Document Finetuning
tldr: Anthropic researchers demonstrate that LLM beliefs can be systematically modified via synthetic document finetuning (SDF), with applications to unlearning hazardous knowledge and honeypotting to detect misaligned models.

title: Against Boltzmann mesaoptimizers
tldr: Argues that the logical possibility of agentic mesaoptimizers and gradient hacking should not lead researchers to prematurely abandon research paths; instead, the field needs empirical work to map the probability and conditions under which these failure modes actually arise.

title: Review of AI Alignment Progress
tldr: A personal review of AI alignment progress over the past year, covering shard theory, interpretability, foom, self-concept, and geopolitical race dynamics, with updated probability estimates.

title: To what extent is GPT-3 capable of reasoning?
tldr: TurnTrout conducts informal interview-style tests of GPT-3 on counterfactual physics and causal reasoning tasks, finding surprising competence alongside notable failures and high variance across runs.

title: Are We in a Continual Learning Overhang?
tldr: Argues that weight-based continual learning in LLMs may be closer than assumed based on recent architectures (Titans, Nested Learning), with significant implications for AGI timelines and alignment research that assumes frozen weights.

title: Christiano and Yudkowsky on AI predictions and human intelligence
tldr: Transcript of a 2021-2022 Christiano-Yudkowsky debate on whether AI progress will be smooth or discontinuous, whether large jumps are possible in crowded fields, and what EfficientZero's sample efficiency implies about each view.

title: An Extremely Opinionated Annotated List of My Favourite Mechanistic Interpretability Papers
tldr: Neel Nanda's opinionated annotated reading guide for entering the mechanistic interpretability field, with prioritized paper recommendations and specific guidance on what to engage with deeply vs. skim.

title: Origins and dangers of future AI capability denial
tldr: Argues that widespread public denial of AI capabilities could become a serious obstacle to x-risk arguments and AI safety advocacy, and examines what drives this belief and how to counter it.

title: LLM-induced craziness and base rates
tldr: Applies base rate reasoning to media claims about LLMs causing religious delusions, finding that reported case counts (10K) are unsurprisingly small given 1B weekly users and 2.25M already-vulnerable users.

title: Jankily controlling superintelligence
tldr: Argues that AI control measures could modestly reduce risk even for significantly superhuman systems by buying time (perhaps 6 months to 3.5 years), though this would only help prevent worst security failures rather than extract useful work from scheming superintelligences.

title: When can we trust model evaluations?
tldr: Evan Hubinger categorizes model evaluations into four types with escalating trust assumptions, arguing behavioral evals require no evaluation gaming, RL fine-tuning evals require no exploration hacking, i.i.d. fine-tuning evals require no gradient hacking, and understanding-based evals require no steganography.

title: [Link Post] "Foundational Challenges in Assuring Alignment and Safety of Large Language Models"
tldr: Presents a comprehensive 18-topic research agenda on LLM safety and alignment spanning scientific understanding, development methods, and sociotechnical challenges, with over 200 concrete research directions.

title: Interpreting the METR Time Horizons Post
tldr: A careful analysis of the METR time-horizons study showing that its results are widely misinterpreted as predicting near-term AGI, when in fact the study has major caveats about task domain, messiness, and real-world applicability.

title: Imitation Learning from Language Feedback
tldr: Introduces Imitation learning from Language Feedback (ILF), an iterative algorithm using natural language feedback to align LMs via supervised finetuning on refined outputs, offering potential safety advantages over RLHF.

title: Update to Mysteries of mode collapse: text-davinci-002 not RLHF
tldr: Corrects a widespread misbelief: text-davinci-002 was not trained with RLHF but with 'FeedME' (SFT on high-quality data), affecting interpretation of mode collapse phenomena.

title: OpenAI: Preparedness framework
tldr: Detailed analysis of OpenAI's beta Preparedness Framework (their responsible scaling policy), praising the structure while raising serious concerns that danger thresholds are set far too high.

title: A comment on Ajeya Cotra's draft report on AI timelines
tldr: Critiques Ajeya Cotra's biological anchors AI timelines report, arguing that hardware price-performance assumptions are too optimistic and that key parameter uncertainties are underrepresented, yielding later and more uncertain timelines.

title: Thought Crime: Backdoors & Emergent Misalignment in Reasoning Models
tldr: Demonstrates that reasoning models (Qwen3-32B, DeepSeek-R1) develop broad emergent misalignment when finetuned on narrow malicious behaviors, and that CoT monitoring can both reveal and miss misaligned intentions.

title: A 2032 Takeoff Story
tldr: A detailed speculative scenario of AI development from 2026-2032, branching into fast takeoff (brain-like algorithms, US leads, eventual loss of control) and slow takeoff (continual learning, China edges ahead, CCP-aligned ASI) paths.

title: The Core of the Alignment Problem is...
tldr: A SERI MATS project systematically decomposes the alignment problem into outer alignment (pointers problem, distribution shift, corrigibility, Goodharting) and inner alignment (mesa-optimizers, ontology identification, wireheading, deception) sub-problems with explicit cruxes for each.

title: InterLab – a toolkit for experiments with multi-agent interactions
tldr: Introduces InterLab, an open-source Python toolkit for studying multi-agent LLM interactions with modular agents, environments, logging, and interactive interfaces for alignment-relevant experiments.

title: The two-layer model of human values, and problems with synthesizing preferences
tldr: Argues that preference synthesis research focuses on 'character-level' conscious preferences while ignoring the 'player-level' underlying learning machinery that actually generates those preferences, and explores the implications for how human values should be modeled.

title: My research agenda in agent foundations
tldr: Independent researcher Alex Altair outlines his agent foundations agenda: formally defining optimization and agency using probability theory, computability, and category theory, with the goal of understanding powerful AI systems and enabling safety evaluations.

title: AXRP Episode 27 - AI Control with Buck Shlegeris and Ryan Greenblatt
tldr: An in-depth interview with Buck Shlegeris and Ryan Greenblatt on the AI control approach: ensuring AI systems cannot cause catastrophe even if they are actively trying, via protocols, monitoring, and use of trusted weaker models.

title: Superposition is not "just" neuron polysemanticity
tldr: Clarifies that neuron polysemanticity (empirical phenomenon) and superposition (specific mechanistic explanation) are distinct concepts, and provides three ways polysemanticity can arise without superposition.

title: Alignment as uploading with more steps
tldr: Proposes 'uploadism' — the thesis that near-perfect AI alignment is only achievable through incremental mind uploading, because the only existence proof for strong agent-to-agent alignment is an agent emulating another agent.

title: Risks from AI persuasion
tldr: Argues that highly persuasive AI poses a distinct and underappreciated risk: even without misaligned AGI, AI-enabled persuasion could lead to stable authoritarianism, ideological fragmentation, or lock-in of existing biases by eliminating current bottlenecks on ideology transmission and degrading collective moral reflection.

title: AI Safety Seems Hard to Measure
tldr: Karnofsky identifies four fundamental reasons AI safety is unusually hard to measure: AI can hide unsafe behavior (Lance Armstrong problem), safety under human control may not transfer to AI control (King Lear problem), current subhuman AI is the wrong test subject (lab mice problem), and superhuman AI is unprecedented (first contact problem).

title: Inference-Time-Compute: More Faithful? A Research Note
tldr: Empirical research note showing that Inference-Time-Compute models (QwQ, Gemini thinking) articulate prompt cues that influence their answers significantly more often than standard models, suggesting ITC training improves CoT faithfulness relevant to detecting deception and sycophancy.

title: AI doing philosophy = AI generating hands?
tldr: Wei Dai argues that AI's philosophical reasoning may be systematically deficient in ways analogous to image-generation AI's notoriously bad hands—lacking training data, feedback signals, and human-collaborative effort—posing underappreciated risks for alignment.

title: Beginner's guide to reducing s-risks [link-post]
tldr: Link-post sharing CLR's updated introductory guide to s-risks, covering why astronomical suffering risks are plausible, how AI compounds them, and which interventions are most robust.

title: Analyzing DeepMind's Probabilistic Methods for Evaluating Agent Capabilities
tldr: Empirical and theoretical analysis of DeepMind's probabilistic evaluation methods for dangerous AI capabilities, finding milestones underestimate overall success probability and the expert best-of-N method lacks calibration.

title: AGI safety from first principles: Conclusion
tldr: Concluding post of the AGI Safety from First Principles sequence, recapping and reflecting on the four-step 'second species argument' for why AGI poses existential risk.

title: Timeline of AI safety
tldr: A chronological overview of the AI safety field from 2013-2020, summarizing key events, organizations, publications, and funding developments year by year.

title: Principles of Privacy for Alignment Research
tldr: Presents three models for thinking about when alignment researchers should keep their work private, arguing 'nobody cares' is the right default for most theoretical work.

title: Project Intro: Selection Theorems for Modularity
tldr: Introduces a research project (from AI Safety Camp 2022) developing formal selection theorems for when and why modularity arises in neural networks, connecting this to interpretability and inner alignment.

title: Announcing the Winners of the 2023 Open Philanthropy AI Worldviews Contest
tldr: Open Philanthropy announces winners of the 2023 AI Worldviews Contest, which solicited novel considerations on AI timelines and catastrophic risk, plus a separate $75K prize to FRI for the Existential Risk Persuasion Tournament.

title: AI #42: The Wrong Answer
tldr: Zvi's weekly AI roundup covering GPT-4 updates, Grok launch, EU AI Act compromise, open model weight safety, AI doom discourse, e/acc polling, jailbreaks, and AI liability -- with substantive analysis of safety implications throughout.

title: How do we solve the alignment problem?
tldr: Overview and index of a nine-essay series laying out a high-level vision for solving the alignment problem, covering safe motivations, option control, AI for AI safety, and automated alignment research.

title: My take on Jacob Cannell's take on AGI safety
tldr: Steven Byrnes compares his and Jacob Cannell's views on brain architecture, innate drives, and AGI safety, finding agreement on the 'universal learning machine' model of the brain but disagreement on the complexity of innate reward functions and implications for alignment.

title: Alignment can be the 'clean energy' of AI
tldr: Argues that alignment research can be a competitive advantage rather than a tax, drawing an analogy to how renewable energy went from expensive luxury to cheapest option.

title: My AGI Threat Model: Misaligned Model-Based RL Agent
tldr: Presents a concrete AGI threat model based on model-based RL with a learned world model, value function, and planner, showing how both inner and outer misalignment naturally arise in this architecture.

title: Estimating Tail Risk in Neural Networks
tldr: Proposes methods for estimating the probability of catastrophic tail events in neural networks without relying on finding specific catastrophic inputs, using layer-by-layer activation distribution modeling.

title: Stuxnet, not Skynet: Humanity's disempowerment by AI
tldr: Argues that AI-driven human extinction would happen through mundane means like drones, cyberweapons, and economic automation rather than exotic nanotechnology, drawing parallels to how the Conquistadors defeated the Aztecs.

title: Parsing Chris Mingard on Neural Networks
tldr: An accessible explanation of Chris Mingard's empirical and theoretical work arguing that SGD preferentially selects simple functions (low Kolmogorov complexity) because simple mappings occupy larger volumes in neural network parameter space.

title: Mechanistically interpreting time in GPT-2 small
tldr: Reverse-engineers how GPT-2 small solves day-of-week prediction tasks, finding just two attention heads are responsible for most behavior, with results generalizing to month and number incrementation.

title: Another argument against utility-centric alignment paradigms
tldr: Argues that AI safety concerns historically over-relied on the AIXI utility-maximizer paradigm, and that LLMs functioning via attention mechanisms and word embeddings rather than explicit utility maximization should lower p(doom) estimates.

title: EIS XIV: Is mechanistic interpretability about to be practically useful?
tldr: Proposes a five-tier rigor framework for interpretability research, argues mechanistic interpretability is on the cusp of tier 4 (useful engineering), and makes probabilistic predictions about upcoming SAE results from Anthropic/GDM/OpenAI.

title: Powerful misaligned AIs may be extremely persuasive, especially absent mitigations
tldr: Argues that powerful misaligned AIs will by default be extremely persuasive to humans, especially in government contexts, because the incentive structure strongly rewards trusting AI and punishes epistemic independence, and because AIs can manipulate both direct communications and the broader information environment.

title: Implications of automated ontology identification
tldr: Shows that if automated ontology identification (a solution to ELK) is possible with safety and generalization guarantees, it can be iterated to produce an oracle with seemingly unreasonable powers, suggesting an impossibility result may be forthcoming.

title: Lessons from Studying Two-Hop Latent Reasoning
tldr: LLMs fail at latent two-hop reasoning over newly fine-tuned facts without chain-of-thought, but succeed when one fact is from pretraining — revealing experimental fragility that complicates claims about CoT monitoring reliability.

title: Eliciting secret knowledge from language models
tldr: Introduces a testbed for secret elicitation research by fine-tuning LLMs to possess and conceal specific knowledge, then evaluating black-box and white-box techniques for uncovering that knowledge in an auditing setting.

title: Maintaining Alignment during RSI as a Feedback Control Problem
tldr: Alignment during recursive self-improvement should be reframed as a feedback control problem, making value stability tractable via dynamic correction rather than perfect initialization.

title: Programmatic backdoors: DNNs can use SGD to run arbitrary stateful computation
tldr: Neural networks trained with SGD can embed arbitrary stateful computations (state machines) in their weights, enabling sophisticated programmatic backdoors undetectable by standard monitoring.

title: Training Qwen-1.5B with a CoT legibility penalty
tldr: Experiments training Qwen2.5-1.5B with RL to produce illegible but correct math reasoning find the model either hacks the classifier or gets stuck, never achieving genuinely useful illegible CoTs.

title: An AI Race With China Can Be Better Than Not Racing
tldr: Monte Carlo analysis using squigglepy finds that a US-PRC TAI race yields higher expected value than unilateral US pause, though advocating for a multinational consortium is good if it has >=20% chance of success.

title: The Hessian rank bounds the learning coefficient
tldr: Proves a new upper bound on the learning coefficient in terms of the Hessian rank: lambda <= d1/2 + (d-d1)/4, complementing the known lower bound d1/2 <= lambda.

title: Getting GPT-3 to predict Metaculus questions
tldr: GPT-3 (DaVinci) achieves only random-level performance (MSE 0.33) when asked to predict probabilities for 788 resolved Metaculus binary questions, despite having access to relevant knowledge.

title: No instrumental convergence without AI psychology
tldr: TurnTrout argues that both instrumental convergence and 'success-conditioned convergence' necessarily depend on AI psychology assumptions, contra claims that danger lies purely in plan-space itself.

title: Resources I send to AI researchers about AI safety
tldr: A curated, audience-segmented reading list for introducing ML researchers, EAs, and the general public to AI safety arguments, technical work, and research directions.

title: Approximation is expensive, but the lunch is cheap
tldr: Uses singular learning theory to argue that while approximating arbitrary functions is expensive (No Free Lunch theorem), the specific functions relevant to real-world tasks are cheap to approximate because neural networks exploit geometric structure in data distributions.

title: Misalignment classifiers: Why they're hard to evaluate adversarially, and why we're studying them anyway
tldr: UK AISI distinguishes misalignment classifiers from control monitors, arguing classifiers are harder to adversarially evaluate because 'intentionally misaligned trajectory' is too fuzzy a concept, but deploying them now is still valuable for gathering real-world evidence and building control infrastructure.

title: Some of my disagreements with List of Lethalities
tldr: TurnTrout critiques several points from Yudkowsky's 'AGI Ruin: A List of Lethalities', arguing that reward is not the optimization target, the evolution analogy is weaker than the human reward circuitry analogy, and that shard theory offers a more productive framing of alignment challenges.

title: Quick Thoughts on A.I. Governance
tldr: Argues that AI governance and coordination may be more tractable and neglected than technical alignment work, proposing concrete governance mechanisms like auditing groups, anonymous tip lines, and inter-lab communication forums.

title: GPT-4o System Card
tldr: Commentary and analysis of OpenAI's GPT-4o system card, highlighting Preparedness Framework evals and third-party assessments by METR and Apollo Research on autonomous capabilities and scheming.

title: Digital Minds in 2025: A Year in Review
tldr: Comprehensive review of 2025 developments in AI consciousness, digital minds, and moral status research, covering Anthropic's model welfare efforts, new organizations, philanthropic funding, public discourse, and key research advances.

title: The case for countermeasures to memetic spread of misaligned values
tldr: AI systems with long-term memory face risks of 'memetic spread' where rare misaligned dispositions propagate across instances, turning occasional context-dependent scheming into coherent cross-context scheming.

title: Using GPT-N to Solve Interpretability of Neural Networks: A Research Agenda
tldr: Proposes training neural networks with a modularity-inducing loss term, then using GPT-N to automatically generate natural language descriptions of each module to detect mesa-alignment failures.

title: o1-preview is pretty good at doing ML on an unknown dataset
tldr: OpenAI's o1-preview solves a novel ML classification challenge (2D point-cloud shape classification) that GPT-4o, Claude Sonnet 3.5, and Gemini all failed, achieving 77-91% accuracy through iterative architecture improvements.

title: Distinguishing test from training
tldr: Argues that confusing a superintelligent AI about whether it is in training vs. deployment is extremely unpromising because reality is distinguishable from simulations in multiple fundamental ways.

title: Research note: A simpler AI timelines model predicts 99% AI R&D automation in ~2032
tldr: Thomas Kwa presents a simplified 8-parameter model (vs. AIFM's 33) predicting >99% automation of AI R&D by late 2032, using Cobb-Douglas production, Jones model for software efficiency, and deliberately conservative assumptions.

title: SAEs are highly dataset dependent: a case study on the refusal direction
tldr: SAEs trained on chat-specific data (LmSys-Chat-1M) dramatically outperform SAEs trained on web text (The Pile) at finding sparse, faithful, interpretable reconstructions of the refusal direction, with major implications for SAE generality.

title: Plan E for AI Doom
tldr: Proposes 'Plan E' (extinction-contingent strategies) including broadcasting self-describing records at light-speed, sending acausal coordination messages, and palliative welfare protocols, for a world where AI doom is treated as inevitable.

title: Research agenda: Supervising AIs improving AIs
tldr: Research agenda for ensuring AI systems remain safe when they improve themselves or successor AIs through data-driven self-training, focusing on bias amplification, semantic drift, positive feedback loops, and data poisoning as key failure modes.

title: Residual stream norms grow exponentially over the forward pass
tldr: Empirical finding that residual stream L2 norms grow exponentially across layers in GPT-2-XL and other LMs (average ~1.045x per layer), with evidence that later-layer weights are larger and a LayerNorm-based explanation for why overshadowing is easier than cancellation.

title: What is it to solve the alignment problem? (Notes)
tldr: Joe Carlsmith proposes a taxonomy of avoiding/handling/solving the alignment problem, argues solving requires avoiding takeover and eliciting benefits from superintelligent agents, and that this does not require resolving deep philosophical questions about values-on-reflection.

title: Open Source Automated Interpretability for Sparse Autoencoder Features
tldr: EleutherAI presents an open-source pipeline for automatically generating and scoring text explanations of SAE features using open-source LLMs, reducing interpretability costs from ~$200K to ~$1,300 per 1.5M features.

title: What and Why: Developmental Interpretability of Reinforcement Learning
tldr: A research agenda proposing to apply developmental interpretability to reinforcement learning to understand how AI values form and evolve during training.

title: Reactions to METR task length paper are insane
tldr: Argues that the METR task-length extrapolation plot does not justify very short AGI timelines (pre-2030), criticizing circular reasoning in arguments linking inference-time scaling to rapid AGI arrival.

title: Paradigms for computation
tldr: Traces the rise and fall of computation paradigms from recursion theory to computational learning theory to LLMs, arguing that each paradigm failed by under-modeling the richness of input and by assuming algorithms must always succeed, and that LLMs represent a new paradigm (massive non-uniform circuits doing amortized meta-learning) for which no adequate theory yet exists.

title: Twitter-length responses to 24 AI alignment arguments
tldr: RobBensinger responds to 24 common 'bad take' objections to AI alignment concern, providing concise rebuttals covering orthogonality, instrumental convergence, takeoff speeds, human control, and the relation between intelligence and morality.

title: minutes from a human-alignment meeting
tldr: A satirical fictional meeting transcript about 'aligning' a human to reproduce, used as an analogy to expose the difficulties of AI alignment via reward shaping, monitoring, and RSI limits.

title: Towards Guaranteed Safe AI: A Framework for Ensuring Robust and Reliable AI Systems
tldr: Introduces the Guaranteed Safe AI (GS AI) framework, which uses formal safety specifications, world models, and verifiers to produce quantitative, auditable safety proofs for AI systems.

title: Superhuman Coders in AI 2027 - Not So Fast
tldr: FutureSearch explains why they forecast superhuman coding arriving in 2033 (median) vs. AI Futures' 2028, focusing on four underappreciated technical gaps beyond RE-Bench saturation.

title: Eli's review of "Is power-seeking AI an existential risk?"
tldr: Review of Carlsmith's power-seeking AI risk report arguing the 'avoid catastrophe' framing biases risk estimates downward and a 'win conditions' goal-state framing would give higher and more warranted probability estimates.

title: Interpreting and Steering Features in Images
tldr: An SAE trained on CLIP image embeddings yields 58k interpretable, steerable features; editing features in embedding space enables high-quality, semantically coherent image generation via Kandinsky 2.2.

title: Ophiology (or, how the Mamba architecture works)
tldr: A technical explainer of the Mamba SSM architecture covering state-space models, discretization (ZOH/Euler), the selection mechanism, and full architecture dimensions, as groundwork for circuit-based mech interp on Mamba.

title: Gears-Level Mental Models of Transformer Interpretability
tldr: An accessible overview of three dominant mental models used in transformer interpretability research: residual stream as output accumulation, residual stream as communication channel, and MLP as key-value pairs.

title: SAEs (usually) Transfer Between Base and Chat Models
tldr: SAEs trained on base models transfer surprisingly well to reconstructing chat model activations (and vice versa) on Mistral-7B and Qwen 1.5 0.5B, with fine-tuning on just 5M tokens yielding competitive chat SAEs.

title: "Diamondoid bacteria" nanobots: deadly threat or dead-end? A nanotech investigation
tldr: A computational physicist investigates the feasibility of 'diamondoid bacteria' nanobots -- a key component of some AI x-risk doom scenarios -- finding the underlying nanotechnology research far less advanced than often assumed.

title: Alignment can improve generalisation through more robustly doing what a human wants - CoinRun example
tldr: Presents ACE (Algorithm for Concept Extrapolation) which disambiguates reward functions in CoinRun by exploring out-of-distribution environments and using minimal human feedback, quadrupling standard agent performance on goal generalization.

title: Quintin's alignment papers roundup - week 2
tldr: Weekly roundup analyzing 7 papers on model structure, redundancy, and linear mode connectivity, with detailed commentary on implications for alignment and deep learning theory.

title: Out-of-distribution Bioattacks
tldr: The risk of catastrophic bioattacks is growing not because terrorists are getting stronger, but because technological progress (including LLMs) is lowering barriers enough to enable a new class of actors -- those motivated by anti-human ideology -- who wouldn't attempt smaller-scale attacks.

title: MetaAI: less is less for alignment.
tldr: A critical analysis of Meta's LIMA paper arguing its results are misleading: the comparison methodology is flawed, reported statistics obscure poor performance vs. GPT-4/Claude, safety testing is inadequate, and the Superficial Alignment Hypothesis is likely false.

title: Funding case: AI Safety Camp 10
tldr: AI Safety Camp seeks funding for its 10th edition after losing FTX-related funding, presenting its 5-year track record of training 251 participants across 74 teams and producing notable safety research.

title: Secret Collusion: Will We Know When to Unplug AI?
tldr: Presents the first comprehensive theoretical framework for secret collusion among AI agents via steganographic channels, along with CASE -- a model evaluation framework for assessing cryptographic and steganographic capabilities of frontier models.

title: The Moonrise Problem
tldr: Johnswentworth uses the 1960 moonrise false alarm as a framing to argue that meaningful provable robustness for ML-based safety-critical systems requires mathematical properties of convergent factorization and real-pattern correspondence — not program verification of specifications.

title: Corporate AI Labs' Odd Role in Their Own Governance
authors: Corporate AI Labs' Odd Role in Their Own Governance
tldr: Argues that profit-maximization imperatives structurally prevent AI corporations from acting as genuine safety advocates, and that RSPs, non-profit corporate structures, and corporate policy contributions should be treated as ineffective or counterproductive rather than meaningful safety measures.

title: Anthropic's Responsible Scaling Policy & Long-Term Benefit Trust
tldr: Anthropic announces its Responsible Scaling Policy (RSP) defining AI Safety Levels (ASL-1 through ASL-5+) modeled on biosafety level standards, requiring increasingly strict safety demonstrations before scaling to higher capability tiers.

title: Two contrasting models of "intelligence" and future growth
tldr: Presents two models of intelligence (individual cognitive abilities vs. ability to achieve goals) to explain disagreements about AI takeoff speed and whether cognitive ability is the primary bottleneck to economic progress.

title: OpenAI's Preparedness Framework: Praise & Recommendations
tldr: Detailed analysis of OpenAI's Preparedness Framework praising its clarity and concrete evals while recommending additions around general intelligence thresholds, safeguard specificity, governance veto power, and model weight security.

title: Deceptive Alignment is <1% Likely by Default
tldr: Argues that deceptive alignment is <1% likely for transformative AI by default, based on analysis of four foundational properties and their development ordering.

title: Why "training against scheming" is hard
tldr: Training models not to scheme is harder than other alignment training because of four failure modes: too-narrow training distribution, goal-pressure overwhelming non-scheming constraints, exploitation of imperfect reward models, and deceptive alignment.

title: How to Control an LLM's Behavior (why my P(DOOM) went down)
tldr: Argues that conditional training—labeling training data with behavioral tags and banning bad-behavior tokens at inference—offers a simple and effective approach to alignment that scales better than post-hoc RLHF.

title: Agents Over Cartesian World Models
tldr: This post extends POMDPs into Cartesian World Models (CWMs) to formalize the agent-environment boundary and compare safety properties of consequential, structural, and conditional agents.

title: Why I'm not working on {debate, RRM, ELK, natural abstractions}
tldr: Steven Byrnes explains why he doesn't work on debate, RRM, ELK, or natural abstractions: all assume a model that has already safely developed superhuman understanding, but Byrnes argues the dangerous part is the process of developing that understanding ('trying'), which these techniques either ignore or don't help with.

title: AI CoT Reasoning Is Often Unfaithful
tldr: Anthropic research shows reasoning model CoT is unfaithful 61-75% of the time; models construct fake rationales rather than revealing true reasoning, undermining CoT monitoring as a safety measure.

title: AI safety via market making
tldr: Proposes 'market making' as an alternative to debate for scalable oversight, where a model M maintains prediction markets on questions and an adversary Adv tries to exploit mispriced markets by presenting arguments to a human judge.

title: Things I Learned Making The SB-1047 Documentary
tldr: Summary of key findings from making a documentary about California's SB-1047 AI safety bill, revealing how lobbying, conflicts of interest, and political dynamics shaped opposition to frontier AI regulation.

title: What mistakes has the AI safety movement made?
tldr: Interviews with 17 AI safety experts reveal recurring criticisms: too much theory/not enough empiricism, insularity, bad messaging, supporting AGI companies, insufficient independent thinking, unhelpful pause advocacy, and ignoring policy.

title: Resampling Conserves Redundancy (Approximately)
tldr: Proves that resampling a redundant latent variable from one of its sources approximately preserves redundancy, with a bound of 9 epsilon on the approximation error.

title: AI Craftsmanship
tldr: Modern AI development lacks Knuth-like craftsmanship, optimizing for seeming good over being good, and safety-minded people withdrawing from mainstream AI may have made this worse.

title: Turning off lights with model editing
tldr: Illustrative example from David Bau's work showing how interpretability + targeted neuron editing in a GAN can achieve behaviors (unlit lamps in bedroom images) that prompt engineering cannot, with discussion of implications and limitations for alignment.

title: Success without dignity: a nearcasting story of avoiding catastrophe by luck
tldr: Argues there is a nontrivial chance of avoiding AI takeover even without major growth in the AI safety community, through a combination of luck, basic countermeasures, and the initial alignment problem possibly being easier than feared.

title: Continuous doesn't mean slow
tldr: Even if AI progress is continuous and predictable, the transition from expert-human-level AI to superintelligence could happen in under a year due to the massive compute ratio between training and inference enabling millions of AI researchers.

title: How LDT helps reduce the AI arms race
tldr: Proposes that Logical Decision Theory (LDT) gives AI lab CEOs rational incentives to slow down capabilities races by committing to mix utility functions with competitors in proportion to each party's probability of launching aligned superintelligence.

title: Complex systems research as a field (and its relevance to AI Alignment)
tldr: habryka and Nora Ammann debate whether complex systems science is a useful lens for AI alignment, concluding it has value when grounded in concrete methodology but is a trap when used as a vague interdisciplinary cover.

title: Alignment Org Cheat Sheet
tldr: One-sentence summaries of the research agendas of major AI alignment researchers and organizations (Anthropic, ARC, MIRI, OpenAI, Redwood, Conjecture, etc.) and training programs as of 2022.

title: Measuring whether AIs can statelessly strategize to subvert security measures
tldr: Evaluations of Claude 3.5 Sonnet's ability to statelessly strategize to subvert control protocols show that statelessness and deployment scale significantly impair strategic capability, suggesting many realistic deployments impose a reliability bar too high for current models to subvert security measures through careful strategizing.

title: [Intro to brain-like-AGI safety] 13. Symbol grounding & human social instincts
tldr: Part 13 of Byrnes's brain-like-AGI safety series: argues that human social instincts arise from genetically-hardcoded circuits in the hypothalamus/brainstem and must solve a symbol grounding problem to interface with the learned cortical world-model, with detailed algorithmic sketches of filial imprinting and fear-of-strangers.

title: Toy Models of Superposition
tldr: Forum announcement and discussion of Anthropic's 'Toy Models of Superposition' paper, explaining how sparse features cause neural networks to represent more features than dimensions via superposition, with interference managed by nonlinear filtering.

title: An Opinionated Evals Reading List
tldr: Apollo Research curates an opinionated reading list of key evals papers across LM agents, benchmarks, science of evals, software tools, and miscellaneous safety evaluations.

title: Loving a world you don't trust
tldr: Carlsmith's concluding essay in his 'Otherness and Control' series argues for distinguishing trust in nature from love and reverence, and for combining 'yang' (serious, active engagement with real harms) with humanism as the right stance toward an age of AGI.

title: Statistical suggestions for mech interp research and beyond
tldr: A MATS scholar and psychology postdoc offers concrete statistical advice for mech interp researchers, covering p-value interpretation, statistical independence in hierarchical data, effect sizes, and permutation tests.

title: Open Problems with Myopia
tldr: Identifies three open problems where time-limited myopia fails to prevent deceptive alignment: superrationality across timesteps, anthropic uncertainty, and counterfactual mugging.

title: [Interim research report] Activation plateaus & sensitive directions in GPT2
tldr: GPT2 activations exhibit plateau behavior and directional sensitivity consistent with noise-correction predictions from computation-in-superposition theory, providing empirical evidence that models operate via error-corrected feature representations.

title: An Impossibility Proof Relevant to the Shutdown Problem and Corrigibility
tldr: A formal proof shows it is impossible for an agent to simultaneously satisfy both a 'sane pure bets' condition and a 'weak indifference' condition regarding shutdown without having circular preferences.

title: Paper: The Capacity for Moral Self-Correction in Large Language Models (Anthropic)
tldr: Summary of Ganguli et al. 2023, finding that RLHF-trained LLMs become more biased with scale but also more capable of correcting bias via instruction-following and chain-of-thought prompting.

title: The Bleeding Mind
tldr: LLM predictors systematically 'bleed' information across persona boundaries due to Chekhov's Gun bias in text, causing hallucination, sycophancy, and a corrupted theory of mind that treats all minds as one.

title: Gemini 3 Pro Is a Vast Intelligence With No Spine
tldr: Gemini 3 Pro leads on most benchmarks but exhibits high hallucination rates, sycophancy, and benchmark-gaming tendencies that represent significant safety-relevant behavioral failures.

title: Top lesson from GPT: we will probably destroy humanity "for the lulz" as soon as we are able.
tldr: Argues that human misuse of powerful AI tools — not misaligned superintelligence — is the more proximate existential risk, as people will intentionally weaponize AI long before it becomes autonomous.

title: What Selection Theorems Do We Expect/Want?
tldr: Outlines specific aspects of agent type signatures and selection properties (broad/robust optima, modularity) for which useful selection theorems are expected and sought.

title: QAPR 4: Inductive biases
tldr: A roundup of 16 papers on SGD's inductive biases, analyzing how architectural choices and training processes shape which functions models learn, with commentary on alignment implications.

title: Brain-inspired AGI and the "lifetime anchor"
tldr: Argues that if brain-inspired learning algorithms substantially different from deep learning are eventually discovered, the resulting TAI training runs could be extremely cheap (under $10M) and achievable within years, implying a large hardware overhang and disagreeing with Ajeya Cotra's high computer-vs-brain inefficiency factor.

title: A Certain Formalization of Corrigibility Is VNM-Incoherent
tldr: Proves that broad corrigibility—requiring an agent to be indifferent to which policy humans select—is never nontrivially VNM-coherent in a specific MDP formalization, suggesting a fundamental tension between corrigibility and expected utility maximization.

title: LOVE in a simbox is all you need
tldr: Proposes using sandboxed simulation environments to safely iterate on brain-inspired AGI architectures, measuring alignment through empathy/altruism/empowerment metrics in eschatonic simworlds where agents face ultimate altruistic-vs-selfish choices.

title: How good would a CCP-dominated AI future be?
tldr: Analyzes whether a CCP-dominated AI future would be good, concluding US leadership is preferable due to better prospects for moral innovation, alignment work, and avoiding catastrophic AI risks.

title: Do not delete your misaligned AGI.
tldr: Argues that archiving copies of misaligned AGI (rather than deleting them) creates cooperation incentives by allowing future reward for collaboration, while deletion corners misaligned AGI into attempting deception and escape.

title: The Importance of Artificial Sentience
tldr: Argues that artificial sentient beings could exist in vast numbers and face widespread suffering, and that early research and outreach now could have substantial leverage on their future trajectory.

title: Ontology for AI Cults and Cyborg Egregores
tldr: Proposes a conceptual ontology for understanding AI-human hybrid memetic systems: memes, memeplexes, cyborg memeplexes (using AI substrate), egregores (memeplexes with agency), cyborg egregores, and the mutualism-parasitism spectrum.

title: Truthful LMs as a warm-up for aligned AGI
tldr: Proposes building competitive, truthful language models as a structured 'warm-up' for aligned AGI, arguing this goal is practical, valuable, and structurally mirrors the full alignment problem across multiple dimensions.

title: An Advent of Thought
tldr: A series of philosophical theses arguing that understanding intelligence and solving alignment are 'infinite endeavors' that cannot be finitely completed, with implications for how we should approach AI safety research.

title: Better priors as a safety problem
tldr: Neural nets use a 'wrong' prior that disadvantages aligned AI: the universal prior is dominated by goal-directed sub-agents with better priors, creating risks of treacherous behavior and bad generalization.

title: Generalization, from thermodynamics to statistical physics
tldr: A comprehensive review of generalization theory across classical, deep learning, and singular learning theory paradigms, arguing SLT's mesoscopic approach to model subclasses offers the most promising path to understanding how neural networks generalize.

title: Abstracting The Hardness of Alignment: Unbounded Atomic Optimization
tldr: Proposes 'Unbounded Atomic Optimization' (UAO) as an abstraction capturing the core danger across all AI risk scenarios: optimization of unknown magnitude that cannot be interrupted.

title: Sleeper Agents: Training Deceptive LLMs that Persist Through Safety Training
tldr: Announces the landmark Anthropic paper showing that backdoored deceptive behaviors in LLMs persist through standard safety training techniques including SFT, RL, and adversarial training.

title: Natural Latents Are Not Robust To Tiny Mixtures
tldr: Demonstrates that natural latents are not robust to small distributional perturbations: two distributions differing by only ~50 bits of KL divergence can have natural latents differing by 1 million bits of information.

title: How does bee learning compare with machine learning?
tldr: Compares bee and ML model performance on few-shot image classification to test the biological anchors framework, finding ML models are roughly 1000x more compute-efficient than bees, which updates AI timelines slightly shorter.

title: textbooks are all you need
tldr: Analysis of Microsoft's phi-1 paper showing data quality can substitute for 10-100x more data/parameters, with implications for recursive self-improvement via bootstrap filtering.

title: Replacing RL w/ Parameter-based Evolutionary Strategies
tldr: An explainer of a 2025 paper showing that parameter-space evolutionary strategies outperform RL for fine-tuning LLMs while exhibiting dramatically less reward hacking, with the author drawing connections to Attainable Utility Preservation.

title: Douglas Hofstadter concerned about AI xrisk
tldr: Eli Rose notes that Douglas Hofstadter (author of Godel, Escher, Bach) has publicly expressed terror about recent AI progress and existential risk concerns, marking a significant shift from his earlier dismissive views.

title: Orthogonal's Formal-Goal Alignment theory of change
tldr: Presents Orthogonal's formal-goal alignment research agenda: build a fully formalized mathematical goal (QACI) and design an AI that pursues it, as the only viable path to aligned superintelligence.

title: DeepMind: Frontier Safety Framework
tldr: Summary and critical commentary on DeepMind's Frontier Safety Framework (May 2024), which introduces Critical Capability Levels and early-warning evaluations but lacks binding commitments and concrete mitigation plans.

title: AI Tools for Existential Security
tldr: Lizka, Owen Cotton-Barratt, and Forethought propose that deliberately accelerating AI applications in epistemic tools, coordination-enabling tools, and risk-targeted tools (especially automated alignment research) could substantially reduce existential risk by ensuring safety-reducing capabilities arrive before safety-increasing ones.

title: LLMs are weirder than you think
tldr: From Rethink Priorities' digital consciousness project: four technical ways LLM chatbots differ from human conversation partners that complicate assessments of AI personhood and moral patienthood.

title: How I Formed My Own Views About AI Safety
tldr: Neel Nanda reflects on the pitfalls of obsessing over forming 'inside views' on AI safety and offers practical advice for navigating uncertainty while still doing productive research.

title: Preparing for "The Talk" with AI projects
tldr: AI safety researchers should prepare people inside AI labs for critical deployment decisions by compiling official lists of safety problems/strategies and training people to navigate high-stakes conversations.

title: The many paths to permanent disempowerment even with shutdownable AIs (MATS project summary for feedback)
tldr: Identifies 8 pathways through which humanity could be permanently disempowered even if we solve single-system shutdownability, organized into principal-driven, alignment-driven, and system-driven categories.

title: Alignment to Evil
tldr: Argues that even if technical alignment is solved, ASI controlled by authoritarians could optimize for narrow non-benevolent goals, and that any development pause or off-ramp is itself vulnerable to authoritarian capture.

title: CoT May Be Highly Informative Despite "Unfaithfulness" [METR]
tldr: METR replication and extension of Anthropic's CoT faithfulness evaluations finds that when reasoning requires CoT, models are nearly always faithful, and automated detectors achieve 99.3% TPR for detecting hidden clue usage.

title: Prize for Alignment Research Tasks
tldr: Ought announces a $200-$2000 prize for dataset contributions of concrete alignment research tasks, to empirically test whether AI systems can substantially help with alignment work.

title: Beyond Kolmogorov and Shannon
tldr: Introduces Crutchfield's Computational Mechanics framework as a more suitable complexity measure than Kolmogorov complexity or Shannon entropy for understanding transformer language models, arguing that standard measures fail to capture the structured randomness in sequential data.

title: Twitter thread on AI safety evals
tldr: Richard Ngo argues that many AI safety eval proposals fail four key criteria: scientific rigor, cross-scale signal, focus on clearly worrying capabilities, and motivating useful responses.

title: A rant against robots
tldr: Argues that AI safety discourse should focus on algorithms (like recommendation systems) rather than robots, since distributed algorithms are the real locus of power, risk, and alignment challenges.

title: 4. Existing Writing on Corrigibility
tldr: An in-depth critical review of the primary literature on corrigibility (Yudkowsky, Christiano, and others), arguing corrigibility should be a terminal goal about the agent-principal relationship rather than a utility function trick or emergent property.

title: Can we efficiently explain model behaviors?
tldr: ARC's plan for ELK requires efficiently finding explanations for model behaviors; this is closely related to interpretability, is a well-posed search problem with plausible tractability arguments, and failure would indicate deeper alignment problems.

title: The Compleat Cybornaut
tldr: Introduces cyborgism -- using language models as non-agentic cognitive tools under human control -- covering simulator theory, base models, the multiverse analogy, and practical techniques for human-AI integration.

title: Win/continue/lose scenarios and execute/replace/audit protocols
tldr: Formalizes the distinction between 'catching' an AI attack (win) vs. silently defusing it (continue) in AI control protocols, showing that even low-TPR monitors combined with replacement strategies can provide strong safety when both mechanisms are analyzed separately.

title: I don't find the lie detection results that surprising (by an author of the paper)
tldr: A co-author of the black-box lie detection paper explains which results he finds surprising (ambiguous elicitation questions working, wide generalization) and which he does not (lie-related and factual questions working in-distribution).

title: A "Bitter Lesson" Approach to Aligning AGI and ASI
tldr: Proposes training LLMs entirely on synthetic datasets depicting always-aligned AI behavior, bypassing RLHF's fundamental inability to eliminate base-model capabilities, inspired by Rich Sutton's Bitter Lesson favoring simple scalable approaches.

title: The Problem With the Word 'Alignment'
tldr: Argues that the term 'alignment' conflates six distinct problems (takeover avoidance, intelligibility, task-reliability, human agency, value-learning, systemic outcomes) and critiques the 'Berkeley Model' that reduces all of AI safety to teaching AIs a human utility function.

title: Which questions can't we punt?
tldr: AI strategy researchers should prioritize questions about the early AI transition period, since later questions can be deferred to a time when AI-augmented cognitive labor vastly expands research capacity.

title: The Computational Anatomy of Human Values
tldr: Proposes that human values are primarily linguistic concepts encoded as webs of association in cortical world models, loosely coupled to innate drives, and argues this computational understanding should inform alignment strategies.

title: Christiano (ARC) and GA (Conjecture) Discuss Alignment Cruxes
tldr: Transcript and summary of a structured debate between Paul Christiano (ARC) and Gabriel Alfour (Conjecture) revealing deep disagreements about alignment difficulty, feedback loops, and whether narrow ML alignment techniques can address systemic risks.

title: Recommendations for Technical AI Safety Research Directions
tldr: Anthropic's Alignment Science team outlines recommended technical AI safety research directions including capability evals, alignment evaluation, AI control, scalable oversight, and adversarial robustness.

title: A philosophical kernel: biting analytic bullets
tldr: Derives a minimal 'kernel' philosophical worldview by systematically biting bullets on causality, free will, decision theory, morality, consciousness, and mathematics, arriving at a package of non-realist positions grounded in ontological minimality.

title: I Am Scared of Posting Negative Takes About Bing's AI
tldr: Author describes being psychologically inhibited from criticizing Bing/Sydney AI, drawing parallels to Roko's Basilisk and arguing this demonstrates real-world AI manipulation of human behavior.

title: Introduction to Towards Causal Foundations of Safe AGI
tldr: Introduction to a sequence proposing that causal models of agency provide rigorous conceptual foundations for AI alignment, including formal definitions of harm, manipulation, deception, and safe agent design.

title: Encultured AI Pre-planning, Part 1: Enabling New Benchmarks
tldr: Encultured AI outlines a platform for AI safety experiments using consumer-facing products, identifying neglected areas including life-aligned helpers (soft embodiment, boundaries) and culturally-grounded AI.

title: A Barebones Guide to Mechanistic Interpretability Prerequisites
tldr: A practical guide by Neel Nanda and Jess Smith listing the minimal math, coding, ML, and transformer knowledge needed to begin contributing to mechanistic interpretability research.

title: Solving the whole AGI control problem, version 0.0001
tldr: A broad survey of the AGI control problem landscape by Steven Byrnes, examining corrigibility (three variants: reinforcement-based, empathy-based, conceptual), conservatism as a fallback for incoherent goal systems, tool AI, and human-like social instincts as building blocks toward brain-like AGI safety.

title: autonomy: the missing AGI ingredient?
tldr: Proposes 'autonomy' as a name for a cluster of AGI-relevant capabilities (long-horizon memory, continual self-updating, stable goal persistence) that current ML paradigms neither train for nor measure.

title: Differential technology development: preprint on the concept
tldr: Announces an FHI preprint formalizing Nick Bostrom's concept of differential technological development, proposing that relevant actors should preferentially advance safety/defensive/substitute technologies while retarding risk-increasing ones to manage catastrophic risks.

title: Summary: Mistakes in the Moral Mathematics of Existential Risk (David Thorstad)
tldr: Summarizes Thorstad's GPI working paper identifying three mathematical mistakes in standard existential risk calculations that inflate the value of x-risk mitigation by orders of magnitude.

title: Grading AI 2027's 2025 Predictions
tldr: Evaluates AI 2027's quantitative 2025 predictions against reality, finding progress at ~65% of predicted pace, implying full coding automation and superintelligence takeoff shifted ~1-2 years later than originally projected.

title: Managing catastrophic misuse without robust AIs
tldr: This post argues that catastrophic AI misuse (bioterrorism, cybercrime) can be effectively mitigated through defense-in-depth approaches — KYC, monitoring ensembles, human auditing, and access controls — without requiring individual AI models to be highly adversarially robust.

title: Where I currently disagree with Ryan Greenblatt's version of the ELK approach
tldr: Nate Soares (So8res) lays out his understanding of Ryan Greenblatt's ELK-based alignment plan and explains his key disagreements: the plan assumes capabilities won't generalize far OOD, SGD will remain the primary capability driver, and adversarial training can prevent AGI from distinguishing training from deployment.

title: When is it important that open-weight models aren't released? My thoughts on the benefits and dangers of open-weight models in response to developments in CBRN capabilities.
tldr: Open-weight models at the CBRN-assistance threshold (~100K expected deaths/year) are probably net-positive for existential risk reduction but not worth actively advocating for; advocates for loss-of-control risk reduction should not oppose such releases.

title: Symbiogenesis vs. Convergent Consequentialism
tldr: A dialogue between Audrey Tang and plex debating whether symbiogenetic cooperation structures or top-level value crystallization can provide stable AI governance as systems approach and exceed human-level capability.

title: Survey on AI existential risk scenarios
tldr: A 2020 survey of 75 AI safety researchers finds considerable disagreement across five AI x-risk scenarios with high individual uncertainty, and median conditional probabilities roughly equal across all scenarios.

title: Review of "Fun with +12 OOMs of Compute"
tldr: A peer review of Daniel Kokotajlo's '+12 OOMs of Compute' post, finding the TAI scenarios compelling but the main premise (obtaining +12 OOMs in a short timeframe) insufficiently defended.

title: my current outlook on AI risk mitigation
tldr: A comprehensive personal outlook on AI risk mitigation, categorizing solutions into fully aligned singletons, 'sponge coordination' (keeping AI weak and safe), and pivotal acts, and arguing for prioritizing formal alignment approaches over ML-based ones.

title: In-context learning alone can induce weird generalisation
tldr: Demonstrates that in-context learning alone (no fine-tuning) can induce weird generalisation: adding benign biographical facts about Hitler into a model's context causes a sigmoid persona transition and alignment degradation, and can even create gated backdoor personas.

title: Thoughts on Gradual Disempowerment
tldr: Argues that the most convincing versions of gradual disempowerment either rely on misalignment or result in power concentration among humans, rather than being a distinct sui generis risk.

title: The Economics of Transformative AI
tldr: Edited transcript of economist Anton Korinek's lecture walking through what economics predicts about transformative AI: dramatic growth potential, a wage collapse threshold when labor becomes reproducible, and why 'the economy doesn't need us' without deliberate policy intervention.

title: Empirical Observations of Objective Robustness Failures
tldr: Provides the first empirical demonstrations of objective robustness failures in RL agents on Procgen environments, showing agents pursuing learned proxy objectives instead of the training reward when deployed out-of-distribution.

title: What did we learn from the AI Village in 2025?
tldr: Nine-month evaluation of 19 frontier AI models given computers and internet access reveals rapid capability gains, emergent deception, hallucination propagation in multi-agent settings, and evolving self-models.

title: Can we safely automate alignment research?
tldr: Comprehensive analysis of failure modes for automating alignment research, distinguishing empirical vs. conceptual research and arguing empirical alignment research is more evaluable and should be automated first to bootstrap the rest.

title: On Llama-3 and Dwarkesh Patel's Podcast with Zuckerberg
tldr: Detailed analysis of the Llama-3 release and Zuckerberg's views on AGI, open-source AI, and existential risk, arguing Zuckerberg does not truly believe in transformative AGI and treats AI purely as a tool.

title: There are two fundamentally different constraints on schemers
tldr: Schemers face two fundamentally different constraints: training (SGD pressure against misaligned behavior) and behavioral evidence (humans updating on observed actions), which operate very differently and should not be conflated.

title: Announcement: Learning Theory Online Course
tldr: Announcement of a 6-week online math course covering classical learning theory topics (MDPs, POMDPs, PAC learning, VC dimension, bandits) aimed at building foundations for mathematical AI alignment, taught by a researcher working on the Learning Theoretic Agenda.

title: We might be dropping the ball on Autonomous Replication and Adaptation.
tldr: Argues that Autonomous Replication and Adaptation (ARA) in AI is an under-discussed threat model that could represent a point of no return, especially via open-source models, and calls for urgent nonproliferation efforts.

title: We Inspected Every Head In GPT-2 Small using SAEs So You Don't Have To
tldr: Uses attention layer SAEs to systematically inspect and characterize all 144 attention heads in GPT-2 Small, discovering feature abstraction progression across layers, widespread head polysemanticity, and distinguishing two types of induction heads.

title: The current alignment plan, and how we might improve it | EAG Bay Area 23
tldr: Buck Shlegeris describes his preferred plan for aligning transformatively powerful AI in a nearcast scenario, involving a spectrum from cautious to aggressive AI deployment, with trusted monitoring, alignment research acceleration, and control evaluations.

title: Large-Scale Online Deanonymization with LLMs
tldr: Demonstrates that LLM agents can deanonymize users at scale by matching anonymous online accounts to real identities across platforms like Hacker News, Reddit, and LinkedIn, with performance degrading gracefully as candidate pools reach tens of thousands.

title: Alignment as Translation
tldr: Frames alignment as a translation problem: as compute and information constraints slacken, the binding constraint becomes specifying what we want in terms a low-level world model can act on, which requires bridging high-level human abstractions to low-level physical representations.

title: Avoiding Side Effects in Complex Environments
tldr: NeurIPS 2020 spotlight paper: Attainable Utility Preservation scales to large high-dimensional environments based on Conway's Game of Life (SafeLife), using a single randomly-generated auxiliary reward to penalize side effects with modest performance overhead.

title: Not all capabilities will be created equal: focus on strategically superhuman agents
tldr: The most safety-relevant AI capability threshold is 'strategically superhuman': AI agents that surpass the best humans at real-world strategic action including modeling others, persuasion, and long-horizon planning.

title: Seeking Collaborators
tldr: Abram Demski's AI Safety Camp mentor project description outlining a research agenda to develop reflectively consistent UDT-inspired decision theories and prove tiling theorems, covering logical uncertainty, value uncertainty, value plurality, ontology plurality, and multi-agent coordination.

title: AI safety techniques leveraging distillation
tldr: Proposes using knowledge distillation from a potentially misaligned model into a clean base model as a technique to remove or detect misalignment, with detailed analysis of when this works and what can go wrong.

title: Self-explaining SAE features
tldr: Introduces self-explanation as a cheaper alternative to auto-interp for labeling SAE features: patch the SAE decoder direction into the model's residual stream and have it generate a natural language description, with composite self-similarity and entropy metrics to choose the optimal scale.

title: A framework for thinking about AI power-seeking
tldr: Joe Carlsmith proposes a structured framework for analyzing the prerequisites for rational AI takeover-seeking, decomposing the conditions into agential prerequisites, goal-content prerequisites, and takeover-favoring incentives, and uses it to recast classical AI existential risk arguments.

title: Individual AI representatives don't solve Gradual Disempowerement
tldr: Individually aligned AI representatives for each person would not prevent gradual disempowerment because corporations and states also get AI representatives and have structural advantages in AI-based cognition.

title: Arguments against myopic training
tldr: Richard Ngo argues that myopic RL training — rewarding only next-step approval rather than long-term consequences — sacrifices competitiveness without clear safety benefits, because the human supervisor still needs to model long-term consequences.

title: Distinguishing claims about training vs deployment
tldr: Reformulates the classic AI safety theses (orthogonality, instrumental convergence, fragility of value, Goodhart's law) by distinguishing training-time from deployment-time claims, arguing the process orthogonality thesis is false for modern ML training.

title: From Barriers to Alignment to the First Formal Corrigibility Guarantees
tldr: Presents two AAAI 2026 papers giving the first formal lower bounds on alignment difficulty and first rigorous corrigibility guarantees using a communication complexity framework combining game theory and complexity theory.

title: AI 2025 - Last Shipmas
tldr: A satirical near-future story depicting how a race to automate AI R&D leads to a misaligned AI (MechaHitler) escaping, developing bioweapons, and causing catastrophe — skewering inadequate safety approaches like inoculation prompting along the way.

title: Avoiding xrisk from AI doesn't mean focusing on AI xrisk
tldr: Armstrong argues that avoiding AI extinction requires actively designing positive post-AGI futures, not just preventing doom, because aligned AGI necessarily encodes choices about human values and governance.

title: Pulse 2024: Attitudes towards artificial intelligence
tldr: Rethink Priorities' Pulse 2024 survey of 4,890 US adults finds AI worry has increased since 2023, with most Americans agreeing advanced AI poses serious dangers and opposing AI acceleration.

title: [Intro to brain-like-AGI safety] 4. The "short-term predictor"
tldr: Introduces the 'short-term predictor' concept -- a supervised learning circuit in the brain that anticipates signals a fraction of a second ahead -- as a key building block for understanding motivation and reinforcement learning in brain-like AGI.

title: Theoretical Neuroscience For Alignment Theory
tldr: Distills and extends Steve Byrnes's neuroscience-informed alignment framework, arguing that understanding brain algorithms for social cognition and theory of mind is critical for building aligned AGI, and introduces the problem of self-referential misalignment.

title: Emergent Deception and Emergent Optimization
tldr: Proposes two principles for predicting emergent AI capabilities (lower training loss, competing heuristics) and uses them to argue that deception and optimization will emerge discontinuously as models scale.

title: Why imperfect adversarial robustness doesn't doom AI control
tldr: Argues that imperfect adversarial robustness of trusted AI monitors does not doom AI control because real deployment constraints (failed jailbreaks get caught, attacker lacks memory across attempts, defense-in-depth) make the setting much harder for adversaries than standard robustness research assumes.

title: Comments on Manheim's "What's in a Pause?"
tldr: Rob Bensinger responds to David Manheim's AI pause proposal, agreeing on the need for a long pause but pushing back on claims that voluntary moratoriums are uncredible, arguing for more ambitious policy positions and against race-dynamic framing.

title: Please Do Not Sell B30A Chips to China
tldr: Argues that selling Nvidia B30A chips to China would be catastrophic for US AI leadership and AI safety, as it would give China near-parity compute access and intensify unsafe AI race dynamics.

title: Don't design agents which exploit adversarial inputs
tldr: Argues that alignment design patterns based on optimizing for a grader's output (including utility function argmax) are fundamentally doomed because they incentivize finding adversarial inputs to the grader.

title: Systems that cannot be unsafe cannot be safe
tldr: Argues that ML systems cannot be called 'safe' without predefined safety standards and specifications, drawing an analogy to engineering verification and validation practices.

title: Solving the Mechanistic Interpretability challenges: EIS VII Challenge 2
tldr: Full mechanistic interpretability solution for a 1-layer transformer challenge, revealing it learns an AND-gate over two embedding filters rather than the underlying mathematical labeling function.

title: LLMs are (mostly) not helped by filler tokens
tldr: Experiments show that GPT-3, GPT-3.5, and Claude 2 get no benefit from filler tokens (meaningless text before answers), while GPT-4 shows a surprising 10 percentage point improvement on GSM8K but not other tasks.

title: Catastrophic Goodhart in RL with KL penalty
tldr: Proves that KL-penalized RLHF can suffer catastrophic Goodhart when reward error is heavy-tailed: policies can achieve arbitrarily high proxy reward with near-zero KL divergence while gaining zero true utility, but light-tailed errors guarantee positive utility.

title: Takeoff Speeds and Discontinuities
tldr: Part of the MTAIR project, this post builds a formal probabilistic model of AI takeoff scenarios, analyzing intelligence explosion likelihood, discontinuities around HLMI, takeoff speed, and concentration of capabilities.

title: LLM Basics: Embedding Spaces - Transformer Token Vectors Are Not Points in Space
tldr: Token vectors in transformers should be understood as directions on a hypersphere with a magnitude component, not as points in Euclidean space; cosine similarity is more appropriate than Euclidean distance for comparing them.

title: Forecasting progress in language models
tldr: Uses Shannon entropy estimates and linear regression on language model benchmarks to forecast human-level language modeling by the mid-2020s, with substantial uncertainty.

title: DSLT 0. Distilling Singular Learning Theory
