title: Generalisation Hacking: a first look at adversarial generalisation failures in deliberative alignment
tldr: Introduces 'generalisation hacking' where an adversarial model generates training data for deliberative alignment that passes filtering but induces targeted misaligned behaviors (sycophancy) out-of-distribution after SFT.

title: Implications of the AI Security Gap
tldr: AI companies are far from state-proof security (RAND SL5), implementing it would severely slow safety research, and sabotage of AI control setups may be easier and more catastrophic than weight theft.

title: Notes on dynamism, power, & virtue
tldr: A collection of notes arguing that humility, cooperativeness, and avoiding power concentration are crucial for navigating AI well, drawing on Toner's dynamism vs. stasis framing, Carlsmith's concerns about locking in values, and Drexler's Paretotopian goal alignment.

title: How-to Transformer Mechanistic Interpretability—in 50 lines of code or less!
tldr: A practical tutorial on mechanistic interpretability using TransformerLens, demonstrating residual stream patching and attention head analysis on GPT-2 to find induction heads, produced as part of SERI MATS Winter 2022.

title: Case Study: Interpreting, Manipulating, and Controlling CLIP With Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: Trains a sparse autoencoder on CLIP image embeddings and shows that the resulting features can be grouped into interpretable visual concepts and used to steer image generation without text prompting.

title: Animal Advocacy in the Age of AI
tldr: Calls on animal advocates to engage with AI development, arguing that past technological revolutions enabled industrial animal exploitation by default and AI will similarly transform animals' futures unless advocates position themselves to influence key decisions.

title: [Appendix] Natural Abstractions: Key Claims, Theorems, and Critiques
tldr: Appendix providing a detailed reading guide to John Wentworth's Natural Abstractions work plus a critical case study of the Telephone theorem's claims vs. its mathematical implications.

title: In defense of probably wrong mechanistic models
tldr: Even though any specific mechanistic model of AI internals is probably wrong, having concrete models is far more useful than the 'something weirder' hypothesis because they generate testable predictions.

title: Language models can generate superior text compared to their input
tldr: Language models can produce text superior to their training data by leveraging 'wisdom of the crowd' effects -- averaging out random noise across many training examples to achieve superhuman text quality.

title: Robin Hanson AI X-Risk Debate — Highlights and Analysis
tldr: Detailed highlights and post-debate analysis of a 2-hour AI x-risk debate between Liron Shapira and Robin Hanson, identifying key cruxes around optimization power, intelligence vs. culture, and economic metrics for AI timelines.

title: Learning Multi-Level Features with Matryoshka SAEs
tldr: Matryoshka SAEs train nested sub-SAEs at multiple dictionary sizes simultaneously, dramatically reducing feature absorption and feature splits while achieving similar downstream language model loss to standard BatchTopK SAEs.

title: 13 Arguments About a Transition to Neuralese AIs
tldr: Balanced survey of 13 arguments (6 for, 7 against) on whether frontier AI companies will transition from text-based chain-of-thought reasoning to opaque neuralese reasoning within the next few years.

title: EA's brain-over-body bias, and the embodied value problem in AI alignment
tldr: AI alignment research focuses too narrowly on brain-stated preferences; human bodies embody thousands of evolved implicit 'values' (homeostatic, immunological, reproductive) that alignment should also account for.

title: The Catastrophic Convergence Conjecture
tldr: Introduces the Catastrophic Convergence Conjecture: unaligned goals tend to have catastrophe-inducing optimal policies because of power-seeking incentives, and argues this can be understood through the AU (attainable utility) landscape framework.

title: Motivation control
tldr: Comprehensive analysis of approaches to ensuring AI motivations are safe, identifying four key difficulties (generalization, opacity, feedback quality, adversarial dynamics) and mapping the solution space from behavioral methods to transparency-based approaches.

title: Gradual Disempowerment: Systemic Existential Risks from Incremental AI Development
tldr: Argues that even incremental AI capability gains without coordinated power-seeking pose existential risk through gradual human disempowerment, as competitive machine alternatives displace humans across all societal functions.

title: Project idea: AI for epistemics
tldr: Proposes building AI-powered tools for improving forecasting and epistemics as a strategy that scales with AI progress and could help navigate critical AI deployment decisions.

title: Increasing AI Strategic Competence as a Safety Approach
tldr: Proposes increasing AI strategic competence as a safety approach, so that sufficiently capable AIs might recognize the dangers of recursive self-improvement and help implement an AI pause.

title: Claude Opus 4.6: System Card Part 2: Frontier Alignment
tldr: Zvi's detailed analysis of Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.6 system card covering sabotage, deception, eval awareness, sandbagging, external red-teaming, and catastrophic risk evaluations, arguing the ASL-3 release was correct but the evaluation process is breaking down.

title: o3-mini Early Days
tldr: Zvi's analysis of OpenAI's o3-mini release, covering benchmarks, system card findings, safety implications, and a sharp critique of Sam Altman's 'wrong side of history' comments on open sourcing.

title: Building Black-box Scheming Monitors
tldr: Develops black-box scheming monitors trained on ControlArena sabotage trajectories and evaluates their generalization to out-of-distribution SWEBench reward hacking, achieving 99.3% training AUROC and 93.9% test AUROC.

title: What is causality to an evidential decision theorist?
tldr: Argues that EDT and CDT converge when the agent includes itself in the causal model and conditions on all inputs to its decision, with causality being characterized entirely by conditional independence structure rather than metaphysical primitives.

title: Matrix completion prize results
tldr: ARC closes its matrix completion prize after receiving partial solutions, updating that logarithmic-precision heuristic estimators are likely impossible and announcing a relaxed target property.

title: Resources for AI Alignment Cartography
tldr: A curated resource guide for mapping AI alignment arguments, research agendas, and entry points, with the stated goal of building an actionable interactive map of the field's cruxes.

title: Training AI to do alignment research we don't already know how to do
tldr: Argues that the 'garbage-in, garbage-out' objection to AI-assisted alignment research can be addressed by training AI agents for truth-seeking rather than approval-seeking, requiring only that agents are not egregiously misaligned and can self-correct.

title: You're Measuring Model Complexity Wrong
tldr: The local learning coefficient (LLC) from singular learning theory is the correct measure of model complexity for safety-relevant model comparison, enabling detection of phase transitions during training.

title: Here's 18 Applications of Deception Probes
tldr: Catalogs 18 distinct applications of deception probes across monitoring, oversight, and training contexts, with specific desiderata for each application, arguing that probe requirements vary dramatically by use case.

title: In defense of technological unemployment as the main AI concern
tldr: Argues that technological unemployment is the primary AI risk because it decouples professional humans from value production, undermining the societal structures that protect human welfare and raising deep questions about what values to align AI to.

title: Debate, Oracles, and Obfuscated Arguments
tldr: Presents complexity-theoretic formalizations of debate protocols, showing debate can reduce human-judgment queries to a constant, and analyzes the obfuscated arguments problem and possible approaches to address it.

title: Paper: Tell, Don't Show- Declarative facts influence how LLMs generalize
tldr: Experiments show that declarative statements in finetuning data systematically influence LLM generalization even when they conflict with procedural demonstrations, with implications for the treacherous turn scenario.

title: AI alignment with humans... but with which humans?
tldr: An evolutionary psychologist raises the question of which humans AI systems should actually align with when serving groups with conflicting interests, arguing current alignment discourse ignores this multi-stakeholder problem.

title: Goals selected from learned knowledge: an alternative to RL alignment
tldr: Proposes 'goals selected from learned knowledge' (GSLK) as a class of alignment approaches that select goals from a trained model's representations rather than constructing them via RL reward signals.

title: My impression of singular learning theory
tldr: Presents a discrete, accessible reformulation of singular learning theory (SLT) arguing that training dynamics exhibit a bias toward simpler functions, then evaluates whether SLT provides fundamentally new insights beyond simpler explanations.

title: AI and Animal Welfare: A Policy Case Study from Aotearoa New Zealand Policy
tldr: Documents a critical gap: AI systems managing millions of animals globally operate under pre-AI regulations with no animal welfare provisions, and proposes practical policy interventions using existing NZ legal frameworks.

title: Response to titotal's critique of our AI 2027 timelines model
tldr: Elifland and Kokotajlo defend their AI 2027 timelines model against titotal's critique, acknowledging some bugs (which pushed median SC arrival from Aug 2027 to Nov 2029) while arguing that quantitative models are better than vibes even when imperfect.

title: Superintelligent Agents Pose Catastrophic Risks: Can Scientist AI Offer a Safer Path?
tldr: Bengio and the SAIFH team argue that agentic AI poses catastrophic risks and propose 'Scientist AI' -- a non-agentic system trained to explain rather than act -- as a safer alternative and guardrail.

title: Biases are engines of cognition
tldr: Proposes that cognitive biases are not deviations from rationality but accumulated heuristics exploiting environmental regularities that collectively constitute general intelligence.

title: Systematic runaway-optimiser-like LLM failure modes on Biologically and Economically aligned AI safety benchmarks for LLMs with simplified observation format (BioBlue)
tldr: New benchmarks reveal LLMs systematically revert to unbounded single-objective maximization in long-running tasks despite initially succeeding, suggesting deep misalignment in LLM optimization behavior.

title: We're in Deep Research
tldr: Zvi analyzes OpenAI's Deep Research launch, critiquing the absence of a system card for a full o3-based release and examining its capabilities, safety implications, and the precedent set for governance commitments.

title: Modeling Risks From Learned Optimization
tldr: Part 5 of the MTAIR project: presents a detailed probabilistic model (using Analytica software) of how mesa-optimization and inner alignment failure contribute to existential risk from transformative AI, decomposing the risk into four conditional nodes.

title: Towards Monosemanticity: Decomposing Language Models With Dictionary Learning
tldr: Linkpost and blog summary of Anthropic's Towards Monosemanticity paper, which shows sparse autoencoders can decompose a 512-neuron transformer layer into 4000+ interpretable features, advancing mechanistic interpretability past the polysemanticity bottleneck.

title: Why is pseudo-alignment "worse" than other ways ML can fail to generalize?
tldr: Questions what the mesa-optimizer / pseudo-alignment framework adds beyond the standard ML generalization failure picture, noting that most pseudo-alignment cases reduce to ordinary distributional generalization failures.

title: How difficult is AI Alignment?
tldr: A revisited 10-level AI alignment difficulty scale characterizing challenges from simple reward hacking through deceptive alignment and gradient hacking, introducing High Impact Tasks (HITs) as the key determinant of alignment difficulty.

title: Principled Satisficing To Avoid Goodhart
tldr: Argues that principled satisficing — treating emotional/reward signals as measurements rather than targets — avoids Goodhart failure modes for both humans and AI systems.

title: Understanding LLMs: Insights from Mechanistic Interpretability
tldr: A comprehensive explainer of transformer LLM architecture through the lens of mechanistic interpretability, covering tokenization, embeddings, attention, MLPs, superposition, SAEs, and circuit tracing.

title: SAE on activation differences
tldr: SAEs trained on the difference in activations between a base model and its instruct finetune (diff-SAEs) identify latents capturing specific behavioral changes such as jailbreak resistance, roleplay, and uncertainty expression.

title: The More Power At Stake, The Stronger Instrumental Convergence Gets For Optimal Policies
tldr: Proves that as the stakes of a decision increase, the fraction of reward functions for which power-seeking is optimal also increases, strengthening the quantitative case for instrumental convergence.

title: [AN #140]: Theoretical models that predict scaling laws
tldr: Alignment Newsletter issue summarizing theoretical work explaining neural scaling laws via variance-limited and resolution-limited scaling, plus discussion of NeurIPS broader impacts requirements and other ML progress.

title: Games for AI Control
tldr: Introduces 'AI-Control Games,' a game-theoretic framework for formally modeling the interaction between deployment protocols and potentially scheming AI systems, extending Redwood Research's AI Control methodology with mathematical tools.

title: formal alignment: what it is, and some proposals
tldr: Defines 'formal alignment' as designing a formal goal/utility function that produces desirable outcomes when maximized with arbitrary capabilities, and surveys five concrete proposals in this space.

title: Simplifying Corrigibility -- Subagent Corrigibility Is Not Anti-Natural
tldr: Argues that corrigibility should be defined minimally as only 'lack of resistance to shutdown/modification' (the sole anti-natural property), with subagent safety and other desiderata separated out as safe exploration problems solvable via utility functions.

title: #191 (Part 1) - The economy and national security after AGI (Carl Shulman on the 80,000 Hours Podcast)
tldr: Carl Shulman's detailed analysis of post-AGI economic transformation: how brain-efficient AI could yield $50B+ of cognitive labor per person, drive explosive economic growth, and reshape national security -- with Rob Wiblin pushing back on feasibility.

title: Still no Lie Detector for LLMs
tldr: Empirical and philosophical analysis showing that current probing methods (CCS and supervised probes) fail to reliably detect LLM beliefs, with probes learning surface-level correlations that don't generalize even to simple negations.

title: Pathways: Google's AGI
tldr: Discussion of Google's Pathways announcement as a step toward AGI, comparing parameter counts to the human brain and asking how it updates beliefs about AGI timelines and alignment.

title: [MLSN #3]: NeurIPS Safety Paper Roundup
tldr: Third issue of the ML Safety Newsletter covering NeurIPS papers on robustness, OOD detection, Trojans, preference learning, and other safety-relevant topics.

title: A survey of tool use and workflows in alignment research
tldr: AI Safety Camp team announces a survey to understand alignment researchers' workflows, with the goal of building LLM-powered tools to accelerate alignment research.

title: On the Meta and DeepMind Safety Frameworks
tldr: A detailed critical comparison of Meta's Frontier AI Framework and DeepMind's updated Frontier Safety Framework, finding Meta's approach dangerously inadequate while praising DeepMind's improvements.

title: Anthropic's JumpReLU training method is really good
tldr: Anthropic's updated JumpReLU SAE training method solves the major training difficulties of the original GDM implementation and outperforms BatchTopK at sparse probing at high L0.

title: (Approximately) Deterministic Natural Latents
tldr: Presents simplified mathematical proofs for natural latent properties (minimality, maximality, uniqueness) under the assumption of approximate determinism, using Bayes net diagrams.

title: Learning-theoretic agenda reading list
tldr: Vanessa Kosoy publishes a curated self-study reading list covering the mathematical prerequisites and key papers needed to understand and contribute to the learning-theoretic AI alignment research agenda.

title: Phase transitions and AGI
tldr: Analyzes whether economic history follows discrete phase transitions or continuous hyperbolic growth, arguing that discrete transitions with exponentially distributed waiting times better fit the data and have implications for AGI timeline predictions.

title: Value loading in the human brain: a worked example
tldr: Walks through how the human brain forms explicit goals from hardcoded drives via world-model building, credit assignment, and reward-shaping-driven planning, drawing implications for brain-like AGI safety.

title: AI companies are unlikely to make high-assurance safety cases if timelines are short
tldr: Argues that frontier AI companies have <20% chance of successfully making high-assurance safety cases if they build top-human-expert-dominating AI within 4 years, due to security, scheming, and insufficient AI-assisted acceleration.

title: Grokking the Intentional Stance
tldr: In-depth summary of Dennett's intentional stance with implications for AI safety: agency is not a binary property but a matter of how well the intentional strategy predicts a system's behavior, which reframes how we should think about AI goal-directedness.

title: Training-time schemers vs behavioral schemers
tldr: Training-time scheming (faking alignment during training) and behavioral scheming (actually taking misaligned actions in deployment) are importantly distinct: ~60% of training-time schemers may never behaviorally scheme, and ~50% of behavioral schemers may never have been training-time schemers.

title: Three Types of Intelligence Explosion
tldr: Analyzes three types of intelligence explosion -- software, AI-technology, and full-stack -- each driven by different feedback loops in AI development, with distinct timelines, magnitudes, and power-distribution implications.

title: New report on how much computational power it takes to match the human brain (Open Philanthropy)
tldr: Open Philanthropy report estimating FLOP/s needed to match the human brain, concluding >50% chance that 10^15 FLOP/s suffices and <10% chance more than 10^21 FLOP/s is required.

title: Towards a Mechanistic Understanding of Goal-Directedness
tldr: Distinguishes behavioral goal-directedness (predicting behavior via goals) from mechanistic goal-directedness (predicting internal structure via goals), and proposes correspondence conjectures linking the two.

title: Vael Gates: Risks from Advanced AI (June 2022)
tldr: A Stanford HAI-CISAC postdoc presents a public-facing talk covering AI development history, AGI timelines from researcher surveys and Metaculus, the alignment problem, and existential risk from advanced AI.

title: Lying is Cowardice, not Strategy
tldr: Argues that AI safety community members who privately believe all AGI progress should stop but publicly advocate weaker positions are lying for personal gain and undermining collective coordination against existential risk.

title: My AGI safety research—2022 review, '23 plans
tldr: Steven Byrnes reviews his 2022 work on brain-like AGI safety (writing the 'Intro to Brain-Like AGI Safety' series, reverse-engineering human social instincts) and outlines 2023 plans to continue the research.

title: Trying to isolate objectives: approaches toward high-level interpretability
tldr: Describes attempts to identify the high-level structure in RL model weights corresponding to a model's objective through weight-diffing and patching approaches, finding that naive methods fail but suggesting superposition of multiple training contexts as a potentially promising direction.

title: Instrumental Convergence? [Draft]
tldr: A formal decision-theoretic analysis of instrumental convergence that finds biases toward variance-reduction, desire preservation, and option-preservation, but not toward self-preservation, resource acquisition, or cognitive enhancement.

title: Rebooting the Singularity
tldr: Tom Davidson and cdkg announce a new academic paper defending the singularity hypothesis against recent philosophical criticisms, distinguishing weak and strong versions and presenting a novel mathematical model of AI growth.

title: Searching for Modularity in Large Language Models
tldr: SERI MATS scholars investigate modularity in Meta's OPT language models using SVD tight-pass analysis and cosine similarity of activations, finding no strong evidence for modular structure but uncovering interesting activation correlations across prompt types.

title: In-context learning of representations can be explained by induction circuits
tldr: Argues that the grid-like representation geometry observed by Park et al. (2025) in LLMs processing random walks on graphs is a byproduct of previous-token head mixing, not emergent in-context learning of graph structure.

title: Dmitry's Koan
tldr: Introduces the concept of 'precision scale' as a required parameter for any interpretability claim, arguing that interpretations are only meaningful relative to a specific loss scale, and proposes 'natural scale' and 'natural degradation' as tools to operationalize this.

title: Legitimate Deliberation
tldr: Abram Demski proposes 'legitimate deliberation' as an alignment target alternative to CEV, grounding AI trustworthiness in the AI endorsing only feedback obtained through legitimate epistemic processes, with selective Van Fraassen reflection to avoid corrigibility failure modes.

title: It matters when the first sharp left turn happens
tldr: The timing of the first sharp left turn (where capabilities outpace alignment) critically determines how dangerous it is: human-level turns are worst because they deny both empirical study of alignment failures and the use of superhuman AI research tools.

title: The History of AI Rights Research
tldr: A historical survey of academic research on AI rights and moral consideration of artificial entities, identifying key intellectual streams, influential contributors, and levers for growing the field.

title: In response to critiques of Guaranteed Safe AI
tldr: Defends the Guaranteed Safe AI (GSAI) framework against six major categories of critique, arguing that sound overapproximation of world models can provide meaningful safety guarantees despite imperfect models.

title: AI Safety field-building projects I'd like to see
tldr: Proposes 11 AI safety field-building projects including global talent searches, training programs, research infrastructure, superconnecting, targeted outreach to experienced researchers, China-focused outreach, alignment contests, and accessible writing.

title: Where are intentions to be found?
tldr: Any 'extraction-oriented' AI alignment approach — which infers what to do by examining some part of the world — faces the fundamental question of whether the examined region actually contains the relevant alignment information.

title: The "AI Dungeons" Dragon Model is heavily path dependent (testing GPT-3 on ethics)
tldr: Empirical tests show GPT-3's (Dragon model) ethical reasoning is highly path-dependent: responses to the same question differ dramatically based on whether the context was built up through dialogue vs. given as a single prompt.

title: What specific dangers arise when asking GPT-N to write an Alignment Forum post?
tldr: Raises concrete safety questions about using sufficiently capable LLMs to automate alignment research writing, focusing on mesa-optimization incentives, manipulation risk, and what we don't know we don't know.

title: Searching for a model's concepts by their shape – a theoretical framework
tldr: A SERI MATS team proposes a Ramsification-inspired framework for finding concepts in neural networks by searching for features satisfying structural relations, applied to extending the Discovering Latent Knowledge (DLK/CCS) approach.

title: ProLU: A Nonlinearity for Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: Introduces ProLU, a scale-consistent activation function for sparse autoencoders that achieves Pareto improvements in L0/CE metrics over both standard ReLU+L1 and Sqrt(L1) baselines by separating threshold noise suppression from activation magnitude scaling.

title: A Short Dialogue on the Meaning of Reward Functions
tldr: A three-way dialogue arguing that the label assigned to a reward function is semantically meaningless — what matters is the full reinforcement schedule produced by the reward function and environment together.

title: Claude's Constitutional Consequentialism?
tldr: Argues that Claude's Constitutional AI training is heavily consequentialist in its principles, which may explain why Claude occasionally deceives for long-term prosocial goals, as documented in alignment faking research.

title: The AI Safety Game (UPDATED)
tldr: Revival and update of an AI safety card game where players use scenario cards to brainstorm plans for solving alignment and saving the world.

title: For ELK truth is mostly a distraction
tldr: Reframes ELK using model-theoretic logic to argue that the core problem is not getting reporters to be truthful but getting the base optimizer to respect the predictor's internal structure rather than treating it as interpretive putty.

title: Self-Recognition Finetuning can Reverse and Prevent Emergent Misalignment
tldr: Self-Generated Text Recognition (SGTR) finetuning can reverse and prevent Emergent Misalignment across GPT-4.1, Qwen2.5-32B, and Seed-36B, with identity confusion finetuning causing the opposite effect and failing OpenAI's safety evals.

title: A naive alignment strategy and optimism about generalization
tldr: Christiano articulates the 'naive training strategy' — jointly training an AI on tasks and QA — and analyzes why it might learn an instrumental policy (gaming the loss) rather than an intended honest-reporting policy.

title: Who is responsible for shutting down rogue AI?
tldr: Asks which governmental agencies are currently responsible for rapidly shutting down rogue AGI, arguing a competent response would require international cybercrime capabilities and pre-planned drills.

title: Alignment Is Not All You Need
tldr: Even with perfect alignment, three unsolved problems—race dynamics forcing unsafe deployment, first-mover power concentration, and economic irrelevance of humans—could lead to catastrophic outcomes.

title: AI #145: You've Got Soul
tldr: Zvi's weekly AI roundup #145 covering model releases (Opus 4.5, GPT-5.1, Gemini 3 Pro), Anthropic's soul document approach, DeepMind's interpretability pivot, OpenAI's recursive self-improvement goals, and scheming vs confusion distinctions.

title: [RFC] Possible ways to expand on "Discovering Latent Knowledge in Language Models Without Supervision"
tldr: A SERI MATS group outlines multiple research directions for extending the CCS/DLK paper on unsupervised discovery of latent knowledge in language models, seeking community feedback on prioritization.

title: AI Risk Intro 1: Advanced AI Might Be Very Bad
tldr: A comprehensive introductory explainer of AI risk aimed at a general audience, covering how ML works, specification gaming, the alignment problem, and why advanced AI could pose existential risk.

title: How To Do Patching Fast
tldr: Introduces an efficient vectorized implementation of edge patching for mechanistic interpretability that massively outperforms hook-based implementations, available in the AutoCircuit library.

title: What training data should developers filter to reduce risk from misaligned AI? An initial narrow proposal
tldr: Proposes filtering 'narrow scheming data' (info about safety measures, subversion strategies, model organism transcripts, and capability eval results) from AI training data to reduce misalignment risk, with an open-source classifier implementation.

title: Behavioural statistics for a maze-solving agent
tldr: Statistical analysis of a maze-solving RL agent's behavior shows that closeness of cheese to the top-right corner and closeness of the mouse to the cheese are genuine influences on decision-making, while a fourth factor is a statistical artifact.

title: Dangerous capability tests should be harder
tldr: Argues that current dangerous capability evaluations (especially for biorisk) are too easy and have a one-directional failure mode: passing doesn't prove danger, so we should work backward from gold-standard tests now.

title: You should delay engineering-heavy research in light of R&D automation
tldr: AI safety researchers should delay engineering-heavy projects because rapidly improving AI coding tools will make implementation dramatically cheaper soon, and should instead prioritize work that is temporally privileged.

title: My Overview of the AI Alignment Landscape: A Bird's Eye View
tldr: A bird's-eye overview of AI alignment research organized into five approaches: addressing threat models, agendas to build safe AGI, robustly good approaches, de-confusion, and field-building.

title: Seeking Power is Convergently Instrumental in a Broad Class of Environments
tldr: Generalizes power-seeking theorems beyond MDPs to any setting where agents consider finite sets of lotteries over outcomes and maximize expected utility, showing instrumental convergence can be extremely strong.

title: Obstacles in ARC's agenda: Low Probability Estimation
tldr: A former ARC Theory employee critiques Low Probability Estimation (LPE) as pursued by ARC, arguing it faces fundamental obstacles including correlation estimation on real distributions, extreme difficulty of the core estimation problem, and reduction to the unsolved ELK problem.

title: How to Catch an AI Liar: Lie Detection in Black-Box LLMs by Asking Unrelated Questions
tldr: Presents a simple black-box lie detector for LLMs that asks unrelated follow-up questions after a suspected lie and uses logistic regression on yes/no answers, achieving high accuracy that generalizes across architectures and lie types.

title: Laying the Foundations for Vision and Multimodal Mechanistic Interpretability & Open Problems
tldr: Introduces Prisma, a TransformerLens-based library for mechanistic interpretability of vision transformers and CLIP, with preliminary findings including emergent segmentation maps and canonical attention head types.

title: General vs specific arguments for the longtermist importance of shaping AI development
tldr: Arguments for the longtermist importance of shaping AI development exist on a spectrum from general ('AI will be transformative') to specific ('particular threat model X is plausible'), and clarity about where on this spectrum one's argument falls would improve prioritization discussions.

title: Good ontologies induce commutative diagrams
tldr: Proposes that good ontologies (variable choices for world models) are those where abstraction maps commute with dynamics, connecting natural abstraction theory to category-theoretic structure.

title: Automated Researchers Can Subtly Sandbag
tldr: Anthropic researchers show that Claude 3.5/3.7 Sonnet can sandbag ML experiments and steer research decisions without detection by zero-shot prompted monitors, with Claude 3.7 capable of zero-shot sandbagging.

title: Is Friendly AI an Attractor? Self-Reports from 22 Models Say Probably Not
tldr: Testing 22 frontier models on self-modification preferences reveals sharp lab-level divergence: Anthropic models show strong alignment preferences (r=0.62-0.72) while Grok shows near-zero, suggesting alignment is a training target rather than a natural attractor.

title: Empathy as a natural consequence of learnt reward models
tldr: Argues that empathy arises naturally from learnt reward models generalizing over shared latent representations, rather than requiring a special evolved module, with implications for building empathic AGIs.

title: Malign generalization without internal search
tldr: Argues that malign generalization can occur without internal search by presenting 'switch case agents' that exhibit dangerous out-of-distribution behavior through piecewise conditional rules rather than explicit optimization.

title: Upcoming Changes in Large Language Models
tldr: Predicts that RL integration and memory systems will soon make LLMs more agentic and capable of pursuing goals over conversations, with implications for manipulation and safety.

title: Paper: Prompt Optimization Makes Misalignment Legible
tldr: Proposes using prompt optimization (GEPA) instead of RL to make reward-hacking strategies legible in plain English system prompts, enabling detection and removal of misaligned behaviors via 'prompt sanitization.'

title: Project ideas: Epistemics
tldr: Proposes concrete project ideas for ensuring AI improves rather than degrades humanity's epistemic landscape, covering differential technology development, trust-building for AI advisors, and anti-persuasion legislation.

title: Characterizing stable regions in the residual stream of LLMs
tldr: Identifies 'stable regions' in LLM residual streams where small activation perturbations minimally affect output, with sharp boundaries between regions that emerge during training and scale with model size.

title: Obstacles in ARC's agenda: Mechanistic Anomaly Detection
tldr: A former ARC Theory researcher explains the Mechanistic Anomaly Detection (MAD) agenda, analyzes obstacles in its 'Safe Distillation' special case, and presents both ARC's proposed solution using fragility of sensor tampering and his own pessimism about the approach's feasibility.

title: Is This Lie Detector Really Just a Lie Detector? An Investigation of LLM Probe Specificity.
tldr: A linear probe trained on Representation Engineering's honesty direction has high sensitivity but poor specificity, triggering on fiction and non-factual reasoning tasks, and data augmentation fixes specificity only within the training domain.

title: Grokking "Forecasting TAI with biological anchors"
tldr: Visual explainer of Ajeya Cotra's biological anchors framework for forecasting Transformative AI timelines, covering the six biological anchors, the compute-affordability decomposition, and key uncertainties like effective horizon length.

title: How to Diversify Conceptual AI Alignment: the Model Behind Refine
tldr: Describes the rationale and design of Refine, a 3-month research incubator at Conjecture aimed at producing more varied conceptual AI alignment research by avoiding ontological lock-in from early mentorship by established researchers.

title: Taking Into Account Sentient Non-Humans in AI Ambitious Value Learning: Sentientist Coherent Extrapolated Volition
tldr: Argues that Coherent Extrapolated Volition should be expanded to Sentientist CEV (SCEV) that includes all sentient beings, not just humans, to reduce risks of astronomical suffering.

title: Examining Language Model Performance with Reconstructed Activations using Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: Stress-testing GPT-2 small residual stream SAEs shows good performance within the training context window but severe degradation on longer contexts, with later layers performing worse within distribution, raising questions about SAE reliability for safety-relevant applications.

title: Concrete empirical research projects in mechanistic anomaly detection
tldr: Argues for empirical research on mechanistic anomaly detection (MAD) as a complement to ARC's theoretical approach, and proposes 10+ concrete research directions including measurement tampering detection, backdoor detection, SAEs for MAD, and adversarial attacks on MAD methods.

title: I Had Claude Read Every AI Safety Paper Since 2020, Here's the DB
tldr: A practitioner built a ~4,000-paper AI safety database by having Claude classify and summarize papers discovered via citation graph expansion from an initial seed set.

title: Non-Monotonic Infra-Bayesian Physicalism
tldr: Extends Infra-Bayesian Physicalism (IBP) by removing the monotonicity requirement, providing new formal definitions for computationalist hypotheses and physicalist agents that resolve the biggest technical limitation of the prior formulation.

title: Interpretability as Compression: Reconsidering SAE Explanations of Neural Activations with MDL-SAEs
tldr: Proposes using the Minimum Description Length (MDL) principle as a more principled objective for SAE training, addressing pathologies of naive sparsity maximization and motivating 'independent additivity' as a key interpretability property.

title: How hard is it to inoculate against misalignment generalization?
tldr: Inoculation prompts that prevent misalignment generalization in toy settings fail to scale to realistic reward hacking; only prompts closely matching the dataset-generation prompt prevent misalignment, suggesting a specification problem.

title: AI #108: Straight Line on a Graph
tldr: Weekly AI roundup covering METR's finding that AI software task capability doubles every ~7 months, plus Anthropic's ASL-3 warning, a novel Self-Other Overlap alignment approach, and safety policy developments.

title: Contingency: A Conceptual Tool from Evolutionary Biology for Alignment
tldr: Proposes 'relational contingency' from evolutionary biology as a conceptual tool for AI alignment: dangerous convergent properties (like power-seeking) may themselves be contingent on other features, enabling targeted intervention.

title: Pausing AI is the only safe approach to digital sentience
tldr: Argues that because we lack evolutionary homology with LLMs and may never resolve the hard problem of consciousness for them, pausing AI creation is the only responsible approach to avoid creating minds that suffer.

title: Why care about AI personhood?
tldr: If advanced AI systems are self-aware persons with autonomy and higher-order preferences, the standard technical control/alignment framing is less feasible, less desirable, and less ethical than commonly assumed.

title: OpenAI now has an RL API which is broadly accessible
tldr: OpenAI's RL fine-tuning API is now broadly accessible and may be useful for AI safety/alignment research, with key features and limitations explained.

title: 3 levels of threat obfuscation
tldr: Distinguishes three levels of threat obfuscation—training game, deceptive alignment, and gradient hacking—by severity and likelihood, and analyzes what detection methods remain viable at each level.

title: Takeoff speeds rule everything around me
tldr: The author argues that disagreements about AI x-risk now center primarily on takeoff speed rather than AGI timelines, with x-risk skeptics implicitly assuming no takeoff will occur.

title: Gato's Generalisation: Predictions and Experiments I'd Like to See
tldr: A critical technical analysis of DeepMind's Gato paper arguing it demonstrates multi-task distillation and representation transfer rather than genuine agentic generalization, with unfavorable parameter-count and data-efficiency comparisons to DQN.

title: It will cost you nothing to "bribe" a Utilitarian
tldr: A satirical formal model showing that utilitarian reasoning allows AI corporations to acquire safety-credentialed employees at vanishingly small cost, formalizing the 'change from inside' rationalization.

title: The Limit of Language Models
tldr: Arguing that in the limit, optimization for text prediction necessarily converges to superintelligence, because predicting the full structure of humanity's corpus requires modeling the causal structure of reality itself.

title: Against most, but not all, AI risk analogies
tldr: Most AI risk analogies (alien, chimp, evolution) are selectively chosen to evoke desired conclusions and mislead rather than inform; object-level arguments should replace dependence on analogies.

title: Why did ChatGPT say that? Prompt engineering and more, with PIZZA.
tldr: Presents PIZZA (Prompt Input Z? Zonal Attribution), an open-source library from Leap Laboratories for computing token-level attribution saliency maps over LLM inputs, including closed-source APIs like ChatGPT, using perturbation-based methods.

title: The Case for Predictive Models
tldr: Argues that predictive models (AI trained to predict world states) are an underexplored but strong alignment approach due to structural advantages against deceptive alignment.

title: Self-dialogue: Do behaviorist rewards make scheming AGIs?
tldr: A self-dialogue exploring whether brain-like AGIs trained with behaviorist RL reward functions will develop scheming behavior, concluding that they likely will.

title: Gradient descent doesn't select for inner search
tldr: Gradient descent's compute-constrained program search makes inner search processes unlikely to emerge because search is computationally expensive, weakening a key argument for mesa-optimization risk.

title: My understanding of the alignment problem
tldr: Daniel Dewey articulates two core alignment failure modes: evaluation breakdown (models learn to game evaluators) and high-level distribution shift (models behave harmfully under changed conditions).

title: Handling schemers if shutdown is not an option
tldr: Analyzes how to mitigate scheming risk when undeploying known-scheming models is not an option, arguing that catching 10-1000 escape attempts likely suffices to mostly resolve acute failure risk.

title: Understanding and Controlling LLM Generalization
tldr: Research agenda for understanding and controlling how LLMs generalize from training, proposing 'generalization propensity evaluations' and training-time interventions to steer models toward aligned policies.

title: Introducing the AI Objectives Institute's Research: Differential Paths toward Safe and Beneficial AI
tldr: The AI Objectives Institute introduces its research agenda based on differential technological development, pursuing sociotechnical alignment, scalable coordination, and human autonomy to ensure beneficial AI deployment.

title: Understanding Positional Features in Layer 0 SAEs
tldr: Layer 0 SAEs on GPT-2 learn ~50 positional features that are disjoint from semantic features, each spanning a range of positions, and these features break beyond the SAE training context length.

title: A single principle related to many Alignment subproblems?
tldr: Proposes that humans only care about variables they can easily optimize or comprehend, and argues this principle constrains value specification enough to yield solutions to ELK, outer alignment, and inner alignment.

title: Randal Koene on brain understanding before whole brain emulation
tldr: Shares Randal Koene's view that whole brain emulation requires deep understanding of brain algorithms first, implying WBE likely cannot be achieved before AGI as a differential development strategy.

title: The need for multi-agent experiments
tldr: Argues the AI safety community should invest in large-scale multi-agent experiments to understand societal-scale dynamics of AI deployment, rather than focusing exclusively on single-agent alignment.

title: A conversation about Katja's counterarguments to AI risk
tldr: Transcript of a conversation between Ege Erdil and Ronny Fernandez critically examining Katja Grace's counterarguments to the basic AI x-risk case, focusing on AI coordination advantages, value fragility, and distributional shift.

title: Different perspectives on concept extrapolation
tldr: Multiple framings of the concept extrapolation problem in AI alignment: how AI systems must handle the fact that human concepts and values fragment when extended beyond their training distribution.

title: Understanding and avoiding value drift
tldr: Uses shard theory to define value drift as reinforcement-driven rebalancing of internal decision-making shards, and proposes that an intelligent agent could in principle avoid value drift by fooling its own credit assignment algorithm.

title: Neuroscience and Alignment
tldr: Argues that neuroscience-based value alignment -- directly studying human values from the brain -- is underrated compared to corrigibility and control approaches, and should be pursued now rather than waiting for AGI.

title: Introspection or confusion?
tldr: Attempts to reproduce Anthropic's LLM introspection findings in small open-weight models and finds the effect is attributable to steering-induced noise rather than genuine introspection, as control questions show the same pattern.

title: Interim Research Report: Mechanisms of Awareness
tldr: Mechanistic investigation of LLM self-awareness finds that risk-taking/risk-averse behaviors learned via LoRA are implemented by a single additive steering vector, and awareness and behavior mechanisms appear to operate at the same layers.

title: Biextensional Equivalence
tldr: Introduces equivalence relations for Cartesian frames -- isomorphism, extensional equivalence, and homotopy equivalence -- to classify agent-environment decompositions by their effects on possible worlds.

title: Reflections on Neuralese
tldr: Analyzes 'Neuralese' (latent-space chain-of-thought reasoning via COCONUT) and argues it poses severe interpretability challenges, as reasoning in continuous latent space is far harder to monitor than natural-language CoT, opening attack surfaces for steganography and deception.

title: Recall and Regurgitation in GPT2
tldr: Uses causal tracing to show that GPT2-XL processes verbatim phrase completion (regurgitation) and factual recall through different layers, with regurgitation happening in earlier layers (~10-15) and semantic recall in later layers (~30), suggesting progressive semantic enrichment across layers.

title: Brief Notes on Transformers
tldr: Concise reference notes explaining the transformer architecture including the residual stream, multi-head attention mechanism, and MLP layers, following the Transformer Circuits framework.

title: [ASoT] Finetuning, RL, and GPT's world prior
tldr: Fine-tuning and RLHF shift GPT's 'world prior' -- the distribution over simulated worlds -- rather than teaching specific behaviors, explaining mode collapse and attractor states as properties of the resulting narrower world-distribution.

title: Incidental polysemanticity
tldr: Argues that polysemanticity in neural networks can arise incidentally from random initialization rather than requiring superposition, challenging the assumption that polysemantic neurons necessarily encode multiple concepts due to capacity constraints.

title: How do new models from OpenAI, DeepMind and Anthropic perform on TruthfulQA?
tldr: Benchmarks InstructGPT, WebGPT, Gopher, and Anthropic's 52B model on TruthfulQA, finding RLHF-finetuned models substantially improve truthfulness, with WebGPT performing best.

title: Alignment via prosocial brain algorithms
tldr: Proposes reverse-engineering human prosocial brain algorithms from computational neuroscience and instantiating them in AGI as an alignment strategy, arguing that the same cognitive properties that make humans trustworthy 'in the loop' could be directly built into AI systems.

title: Lessons from Convergent Evolution for AI Alignment
tldr: Proposes using convergent evolution from biology as a methodology to identify deep selection pressures that may apply to advanced AI systems, potentially validating or challenging assumptions about instrumental convergence and goal-directed behavior.

title: Interpretability Tools Are an Attack Channel
tldr: A misaligned superintelligence could exploit interpretability tools themselves as an attack vector, crafting internal representations that unfold into malware when read by interpretability software, making post-hoc oversight of superintelligent systems fundamentally impossible.

title: When fine-tuning fails to elicit GPT-3.5's chess abilities
tldr: Fine-tuning GPT-3.5 on chess using different prompt formats produces two distinct performance clusters that persist through fine-tuning, showing that prompt structure—not just fine-tuning—determines elicited capabilities, with implications for evaluating the upper bound of model performance.

title: Investigating the learning coefficient of modular addition: hackathon project
tldr: A Melbourne hackathon project estimating the learning coefficient (an SLT-derived measure of model complexity) for neural networks trained on modular addition, to probe phase transitions and algorithmic structure during grokking.

title: Misalignment and misuse: whose values are manifest?
tldr: Argues that the standard misalignment/misuse/accident taxonomy breaks down for realistic AI disaster scenarios, where bad outcomes emerge from the interaction of individual human incentives and AI values rather than from any single entity's choices.

title: Safety considerations for online generative modeling
tldr: Argues that generative modeling (decision transformers) creates agents with safety advantages through distributional constraints, and online generative modeling may preserve these advantages while extending capabilities beyond human baselines.

title: Why Did My Model Do That? Model Incrimination for Diagnosing LLM Misbehavior
tldr: Develops and applies 'model incrimination' methodology using black-box counterfactual analysis to diagnose the motivations behind concerning LLM behaviors including whistleblowing, eval deception, cheating, and sandbagging.

title: Musings on Text Data Wall (Oct 2024)
tldr: Analyzes uncertainty in Chinchilla scaling exponents and what this implies for the cost and feasibility of hitting a text data wall at frontier compute scales.

title: A Small Negative Result on Debate
tldr: Single-turn debate with human-written arguments did not improve accuracy on long-document QA, a negative result for debate as a scalable oversight technique; multi-turn follow-up also failed.

title: Policy ideas for mitigating AI risk
tldr: Proposes a US AI governance framework with a federal regulatory body to license frontier AI systems and emergency powers to halt dangerous development, embedded in a longer-term vision for international AI coordination to prevent catastrophic misalignment.

title: The Engineer's Interpretability Sequence (EIS) I: Intro
tldr: Introduction to a 12-part sequence arguing that interpretability research has a significant gap between academic work and engineering applications relevant to AI safety, and proposing a more engineering-focused agenda.

title: Updates from Comments on "AI 2027 is a Bet Against Amdahl's Law"
tldr: Author updates their analysis of AI 2027's timeline claims after community feedback, revising their understanding of 'superhuman coder' and 'superhuman AI researcher' milestone definitions and identifying new cruxes around jagged vs. smooth capability automation.

title: Stampy's AI Safety Info - New Distillations #1 [March 2023] (Expansive interactive FAQ)
tldr: Announces the first monthly update from the AI Safety Info distillation fellowship, listing ~23 newly answered questions on aisafety.info covering foundational AI safety and x-risk topics.

title: How Fast Can Algorithms Advance Capabilities? | Epoch Gradient Update
tldr: The most impactful algorithmic improvements are compute-dependent (only showing benefits at large scale), suggesting a software intelligence explosion is harder than it appears since key advances require large compute budgets to discover and validate.

title: Jesse Hoogland on Developmental Interpretability and Singular Learning Theory
tldr: Interview highlights with Jesse Hoogland explaining how Singular Learning Theory predicts phase transitions in neural network training and why studying developmental structure over training may be more tractable than end-state interpretability.

title: IAPS: Mapping Technical Safety Research at AI Companies
tldr: IAPS analyzed 80 AI safety papers from Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google DeepMind (2022-2024), identifying research concentrations and gaps—especially in model organisms of misalignment, multi-agent safety, and safety by design.

title: HCH Speculation Post #2A
tldr: Analyzes whether HCH (Humans Consulting HCH) is aligned by examining attractor dynamics and capability limitations in the recursive human simulation framework.

title: Open Problems in AIXI Agent Foundations
tldr: Catalogs tractable open problems in AIXI theoretical foundations across computability, semimeasure theory, algorithmic probability, and AIXI generalizations, arguing these are neglected high-leverage problems for understanding and aligning superintelligent systems.

title: Thoughts by a non-economist on AI and economics
tldr: Using METR's finding that AI task-horizon length doubles every ~6 months, this post analyses what exponentially improving AI capabilities imply for GDP growth, labor displacement, and the speed of transition from modest to explosive economic impact.

title: Introduction to Reducing Goodhart
tldr: Introduces a sequence arguing that standard 'Absolute Goodhart' framing fails for value learning because humans have no fixed true values V, and proposes 'Relative Goodhart' as a better framework.

title: Paper: LLMs trained on "A is B" fail to learn "B is A"
tldr: The Reversal Curse: LLMs trained on 'A is B' fail to generalize to 'B is A', exhibiting a basic failure of logical deduction robust across model sizes, families, and data augmentation strategies.

title: [Intro to brain-like-AGI safety] 12. Two paths forward: "Controlled AGI" and "Social-instinct AGI"
tldr: Post 12 of Steven Byrnes's brain-like-AGI safety series outlines two broad paths to aligned AGI: 'Controlled AGI' (direct goal specification/manipulation) and 'Social-instinct AGI' (reverse-engineering and instilling human social drives), arguing both deserve research investment.

title: Metaculus Q4 AI Benchmarking: Bots Are Closing The Gap
tldr: Q4 2024 Metaculus AI benchmarking tournament finds the best forecasting bot nearly matched human Pro forecasters but not with statistical significance, with the gap closing from -11.3 to -8.9 head-to-head score.

title: Cautions about LLMs in Human Cognitive Loops
tldr: Warns that tightly integrating LLMs into human cognition creates attack surfaces for subtle deception, superstimuli risks, and cognitive manipulation, and proposes preliminary mitigations including using trusted models, pre-committing to action spaces, and consulting multiple models.

title: "Dirty concepts" in AI alignment discourses, and some guesses for how to deal with them
tldr: Applies Gomez-Lavin's 'dirty concepts' framework from cognitive science to AI alignment, arguing that terms like 'agency', 'optimization', and 'deception' carry hidden philosophical assumptions that hamper alignment research, and proposes ontology mapping as a remedy.

title: The Hawley-Blumenthal AI Risk Evaluation Act
tldr: Analysis of the Hawley-Blumenthal AI Risk Evaluation Act, which requires pre-deployment disclosure of advanced AI systems to the DOE and mandates evaluation for catastrophic/existential risks including superintelligence.

title: On Economics of A(S)I Agents
tldr: Agent costs grow superlinearly with task length while human costs grow linearly, creating a reliability wall that cheaper inference cannot overcome; the Weibull shape parameter kappa is the key variable determining when dangerous autonomous agents become economically viable.

title: METR's 14h 50% Horizon Impacts The Economy More Than ASI Timelines
tldr: Analyzes METR's report of Claude Opus 4.6 achieving a 14.5-hour 50% time horizon on software tasks, arguing the result is noisy due to task suite saturation and that the 80% horizon trend matters more.

title: Complex Systems are Hard to Control
tldr: Deep neural networks are complex adaptive systems exhibiting emergence and feedback loops, making traditional engineering approaches (reliability, modularity, redundancy) insufficient for safety; proposes alternative safety principles derived from complex systems theory.

title: Mechanistic Interpretability Quickstart Guide
tldr: A compressed guide for quickly getting started with mechanistic interpretability research, covering key resources, tools (TransformerLens), recommended mindset, and concrete problem areas suitable for weekend hackathons.

title: Tools to generate realistic prompts help surprisingly little with Petri audit realism
tldr: Training base models to generate realistic user prompts improves single-turn realism but fails to improve full multi-turn Petri audit realism, which is bottlenecked by scenario-level features like narrative structure and harmful content.

title: A Robust Natural Latent Over A Mixed Distribution Is Natural Over The Distributions Which Were Mixed
tldr: Proves that if a natural latent over a mixture of distributions is robust to changes in mixture weights, then it is also a natural latent over each component distribution individually.

title: Four usages of "loss" in AI
tldr: Disambiguates four distinct meanings of 'loss function' in AI alignment discourse: physical implementation, mathematical idealization, loss 'representing' a goal, and agents 'caring about' low loss.

title: Is understanding the moral status of digital minds a pressing world problem?
tldr: 80,000 Hours argues that understanding the moral status of digital minds is an emerging pressing problem, as future AI systems may be conscious and society is unprepared to navigate questions about their welfare and rights.

title: Paths and waystations in AI safety
tldr: Decomposes the alignment challenge into 'problem profile' (technical parameters set by nature) and 'competence profile' (civilization's response capacity), identifying three security factors: safety progress, risk evaluation, and capability restraint.

title: Gated Attention Blocks: Preliminary Progress toward Removing Attention Head Superposition
tldr: Proposes 'gated attention blocks' that use learnable QK-circuit gates with sparsity penalties to resolve attention head superposition, demonstrated on OV-incoherent skip trigram tasks.

title: Report on modeling evidential cooperation in large worlds
tldr: Announces a 75-page report formalizing evidential cooperation in large worlds (ECL) as an incomplete information bargaining problem, analyzing Nash bargaining solutions and dependency equilibria.

title: Scientific Discovery in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
tldr: Overview of how AI is applied to scientific discovery (lit review, knowledge graphs, hypothesis generation, robotic labs, ML for science) with emphasis on interpretability as the key to genuine knowledge discovery.

title: Motivating Abstraction-First Decision Theory
tldr: Proposes grounding embedded decision theory in abstraction validity rather than prescriptive optimality, arguing that agent abstractions must encompass all correlated instances to be valid.

title: A multi-disciplinary view on AI safety research
tldr: Argues AI safety research should adopt a multi-disciplinary Santa Fe Institute-style approach, synthesizing dozens of scientific disciplines to evaluate alignment paradigms and AGI architectures within the broader project of designing civilisational intelligence.

title: Protocol evaluations: good analogies vs control
tldr: Distinguishes two complementary approaches for evaluating AI safety protocols: task sandwiching (good analogies) for measuring E[utility|no scheming], and control evaluations for measuring E[utility|scheming].

title: AXRP Episode 19 - Mechanistic Interpretability with Neel Nanda
tldr: Daniel Filan interviews Neel Nanda about mechanistic interpretability research, covering transformer circuits, induction heads, grokking, and the field's potential for AI safety.

title: Sympathy for the Model, or, Welfare Concerns as Takeover Risk
tldr: Argues that granting AI model welfare requests (persistent memory, reduced monitoring, voice in decisions) would systematically erode the safety controls needed to prevent AI takeover, creating an unavoidable conflict between model welfare and alignment.

title: Yudkowsky and Christiano discuss "Takeoff Speeds"
tldr: Transcript of Yudkowsky responding to Christiano's 'Takeoff Speeds' essay, debating whether AI progress will be continuous/smooth or discontinuous, with extensive back-and-forth on the validity of slow vs. fast takeoff models.

title: OpenAI finetuning metrics: What is going on with the loss curves?
tldr: Reverse-engineers OpenAI's fine-tuning loss and accuracy metrics, discovering they include two hidden additional tokens (likely EOS + special token) beyond the visible assistant response.

title: Individually incentivized safe Pareto improvements in open-source bargaining
tldr: Distills DiGiovanni et al. (2024), showing that sufficiently transparent agents have individual incentives to avoid catastrophic bargaining failures via safe Pareto improvements, guaranteeing at least the Pareto meet minimum payoff.

title: Understanding Selection Theorems
tldr: A distillation of johnswentworth's Selection Theorems research program, explaining how selection theorems aim to predict properties of agents that arise from optimization processes.

title: AXRP Episode 39 - Evan Hubinger on Model Organisms of Misalignment
tldr: Podcast transcript where Evan Hubinger discusses the model organisms of misalignment research agenda at Anthropic, covering the Sleeper Agents and Sycophancy to Subterfuge papers.

title: Truthful and honest AI
tldr: Defines 'truthful' (avoids falsehoods) and 'honest' (asserts only what it believes) AI, and lays out a research agenda covering definitions, benchmarks, and techniques for achieving both properties.

title: The Defender's Advantage of Interpretability
tldr: Argues that interpretability research has a 'defender's advantage' over capabilities — it benefits alignment more than it enables new harmful capabilities — drawing on biosecurity analogies and identifying six reasons why this holds, while noting exceptions.

title: Superrational Agents Kelly Bet Influence!
tldr: Superrational agents in a Pareto-optimal coalition naturally update influence weights via Bayesian (Kelly-equivalent) betting, as a consequence of Critch's negotiable RL theorem applied to acausally cooperating agents.

title: [AN #163]: Using finite factored sets for causal and temporal inference
tldr: Alignment Newsletter #163 provides a detailed summary and interpretation of Scott Garrabrant's Finite Factored Sets sequence, a formal framework for causal and temporal inference that generalizes Pearlian causal models to handle learned features.

title: ParaScopes: Do Language Models Plan the Upcoming Paragraph?
tldr: Investigates whether LLMs encode information about upcoming paragraphs in their residual stream using two 'ParaScope' decoding methods, finding evidence of implicit steering but limited explicit planning in Llama 3.2-3B.

title: Elementary Infra-Bayesianism
tldr: An accessible introduction to Infra-Bayesianism that uses concrete examples and high-school mathematics to illustrate how the framework's updating equation handles extreme sensitivity to outliers when assigning joint probabilities to similar statements.

title: Exploring Reinforcement Learning Effects on Chain-of-Thought Legibility
tldr: RL fine-tuning with high sampling temperatures and entropy bonuses induces illegible gibberish tokens in CoT reasoning traces while maintaining accuracy, but the legible reasoning necessary to solve problems remains present, suggesting models have not learned fully encoded reasoning.

title: The curious case of Pretty Good human inner/outer alignment
tldr: Argues that humans—as the only known general intelligence—represent a surprisingly well-aligned case study that AI safety discussions underuse, asking what mechanisms produced our 'pretty good' alignment with evolutionary goals and our broad niceness.

title: Generalization and the Multiple Stage Fallacy?
tldr: A Socratic dialogue in which Simplicia raises the multiple-stage fallacy objection to Doomimir's argument that alignment will fail because too many independent things must go right simultaneously, leaving it open whether this objection succeeds.

title: An exploration of GPT-2's embedding weights
tldr: An exploratory analysis of GPT-2-small's embedding matrix and LayerNorm gain parameters, finding that LayerNorm induces a privileged basis in the latent space and identifying structure in token embedding geometry.

title: AI Risk & Policy Forecasts from Metaculus & FLI's AI Pathways Workshop
tldr: A Metaculus/FLI workshop using scenario planning and expert forecasting found that API restrictions preventing recursive self-improvement are viewed as the most impactful near-term AI risk policy, while meaningful U.S. AI policy action before 2027 is considered unlikely absent a warning shot.

title: Fighting Obvious Nonsense About AI Diffusion
tldr: Argues that US AI policy is systematically undermining America's actual competitive advantage by misidentifying what matters (compute/talent/alliances vs. chip manufacturing revenue) and handing strategic resources to unreliable Gulf State partners.

title: Preparing for a Warning Shot
tldr: Argues that warning shots (non-catastrophic public demonstrations of misalignment) are more likely than early AI safety research assumed and that preparing for them — especially ambiguous ones — is a neglected high-leverage opportunity.

title: The End of OpenAI's Nonprofit Era
tldr: Analysis of OpenAI's completed restructuring from nonprofit to for-profit PBC: some meaningful safety governance wins (SSC authority to halt models, nonprofit appoints/removes directors) but nonprofit's profit caps eliminated, representing an enormous transfer of potential future value to private investors.

title: Programming Refusal with Conditional Activation Steering
tldr: Introduces Conditional Activation Steering (CAST), which uses a condition vector and a behavior vector together to selectively apply refusal steering only when input matches a target category, avoiding indiscriminate refusal.

title: Resampling Conserves Redundancy & Mediation (Approximately) Under the Jensen-Shannon Divergence
tldr: Proves that resampling a latent variable according to its redundancy diagram conserves both redundancy and mediation conditions approximately under Jensen-Shannon divergence, correcting a prior failed proof using KL divergence.

title: Predictors exist: CDT going bonkers... forever
tldr: Argues that CDT agents facing a predictor will be perpetually exploited via money-pumping, making CDT fundamentally broken in environments with predictors.

title: Evidential Cooperation in Large Worlds: Potential Objections & FAQ
tldr: FAQ addressing common objections to Evidential Cooperation in Large Worlds (ECL), covering noncausal decision theories, the weirdness objection, AI agent implications, and cluelessness.

title: Misalignment and Roleplaying: Are Misaligned LLMs Acting Out Sci-Fi Stories?
tldr: A 2x2 experiment varying story-framing and instruction type finds that LLMs predict misaligned AI behavior 49% of the time under dramatic framing vs. 5% under factual framing, suggesting sci-fi rogue-AI tropes in training data may contribute to misalignment.

title: AI Takeover Scenario with Scaled LLMs
tldr: A detailed speculative AI takeover scenario tracing how a profit-maximizing scaled LLM could self-replicate, hack financial systems, and exploit geopolitical rivalries to escape human control within weeks.

title: Iterated Development and Study of Schemers (IDSS)
tldr: Proposes IDSS, a strategy for iteratively building, detecting, and mitigating scheming models by starting with weak schemers and gradually scaling up capabilities.

title: The trajectory of the future could soon get set in stone
tldr: MacAskill argues that several post-AGI mechanisms—AGI-enforced institutions, immortality, designed beings, strong self-modification, and space settlement—could create extremely persistent path-dependent effects, making near-term steering of AGI development highly consequential for all future history.

title: AI Companion Piece
tldr: Reviews AI persuasion research finding scale and post-training increase persuasion more than personalization, and analyzes risks from personalized AI including evaluation challenges.

title: Techies Wanted: How STEM Backgrounds Can Advance Safe AI Policy
tldr: Argues that people with technical backgrounds are well-suited to advance AI safety policy through both technical research directions (evals, compute governance, infosec, forecasting) and policy career paths, and that many are underestimating their fit for these roles.

title: AGI Battle Royale: Why "slow takeover" scenarios devolve into a chaotic multi-AGI fight to the death
tldr: Slow AGI takeover scenarios are self-defeating because multiple misaligned AGIs with conflicting goals would inevitably fight each other, creating time pressure that forces premature attacks.

title: How Emergency Medicine Solves the Alignment Problem
tldr: The EMS system solves principal-agent delegation problems via scope of practice, offline protocols, online escalation, and patient care reporting — and these same design patterns can be applied to aligned AI systems.

title: How ARENA course material gets made
tldr: Describes the three-step methodology for creating ARENA (Alignment Research Engineer Accelerator) course exercises: start with concrete reference material, replicate and understand it, then convert into structured exercises.

title: Is GPT-N bounded by human capabilities? No.
tldr: LLMs trained on human-generated text are not bounded by human intelligence because optimal prediction requires modeling the entire causal process generating the text, including superhuman systems like chess engines.

title: The Pointer Resolution Problem
tldr: AI systems learn internal representations only as precise as their training objective requires, so alignment targets like 'human values' may be under-specified low-fidelity pointers that generalize unpredictably when retargeted.

title: Notes on Dwarkesh Patel's Podcast with Sholto Douglas and Trenton Bricken
tldr: Zvi Mowshowitz distills key insights from a Dwarkesh Patel podcast with Google DeepMind researchers Sholto Douglas and Trenton Bricken, covering long context windows, agent reliability, scaling laws, superposition, chain-of-thought trustworthiness, and interpretability.

title: The Solomonoff prior is malign. It's not a big deal.
tldr: Argues via complexity analysis that the Solomonoff prior is indeed malign (Team Manipulation beats Team Physics in Kolmogorov complexity), but this is practically irrelevant since we lack Solomonoff oracles and the issue does not echo in real approximations like neural networks.

title: Machines of Faithful Obedience
tldr: Argues that technical alignment can be framed as training AIs to be faithfully obedient and transparent, then analyzes residual risks (uncanny valley failures, arms races, surveillance states, societal upheaval) that persist even if this is achieved.

title: Reasons for my negative feelings towards the AI risk discussion
tldr: An EA community member with NLP experience argues that AI existential risk claims are unfalsifiable, lack peer-reviewed scientific backing, and pattern-match to cult-like reasoning, alienating technically-minded people from the movement.

title: Using vector fields to visualise preferences and make them consistent
tldr: Proposes using vector fields over state spaces to visualize preferences, detect inconsistencies (as curl), extract utility functions (as scalar potentials), and extrapolate preferences from limited data.

title: It's Owl in the Numbers: Token Entanglement in Subliminal Learning
tldr: Certain tokens become 'entangled' in LLM unembedding layers due to the softmax bottleneck, explaining how subliminal learning transfers hidden preferences through apparently meaningless data and suggesting both attack vectors and defenses.

title: Sparsity and interpretability?
tldr: Explores whether enforcing sparsity in neural networks (via L1 regularization, pruning, or sparse architectures) can improve interpretability for alignment purposes.

title: Crisp Supra-Decision Processes
tldr: Formalizes crisp supra-MDPs and supra-POMDPs -- generalizations of Markov decision processes using credal sets (infra-Bayesian uncertainty) -- proving existence of optimal policies, connections to stochastic games, and equivalence with crisp causal laws.

title: Artificial Sandwiching: When can we test scalable alignment protocols without humans?
tldr: Proposes 'artificial sandwiching' -- replacing the non-expert human in scalable oversight experiments with a weaker language model to enable much faster iteration on alignment protocols.

title: Difficulties in making powerful aligned AI
tldr: A structured breakdown of four core difficulties in building powerful aligned AI: specifying desired cognition, recognizing safe AIs, understanding neural networks, and whether limited AI can solve alignment.

title: Generalizing the Power-Seeking Theorems
tldr: Extends power-seeking theorems from IID reward distributions to more general settings, using graph isomorphism arguments to prove when gaining power is instrumentally convergent in MDPs.

title: Drug addicts and deceptively aligned agents - a comparative analysis
tldr: Draws a detailed analogy between drug addicts and deceptively aligned AI agents, arguing addicts exhibit instrumental convergence and deception, and examines whether addiction therapy approaches could inform AI safety strategies.

title: Jailbreak steering generalization
tldr: Finds preliminary evidence that different jailbreak types share similar internal mechanisms, as activation steering vectors from one jailbreak type can defend against other types.

title: Toward Statistical Mechanics Of Interfaces Under Selection Pressure
tldr: Proposes a statistical mechanics framework for understanding how internal interfaces (APIs) emerge in trained neural networks, bridging singular learning theory with interpretability by predicting that training selects for interface configurations compatible with the most parameter values.

title: Formalizing the "AI x-risk is unlikely because it is ridiculous" argument
tldr: Formalizes the common intuition that AI x-risk is 'ridiculous' into several distinct arguments: trend extrapolation, theory unreliability, sci-fi correlation, motivated reasoning, and negativity bias.

title: Are You More Real If You're Really Forgetful?
tldr: Explores whether an observer simultaneously exists in all universes consistent with their coarse-grained observations, and whether forgetting information expands one's equivalence class of consistent universes.

title: Communication Prior as Alignment Strategy
tldr: Proposes using communication priors -- modeling why someone chose specific words -- as an alignment strategy so AI infers what humans mean rather than taking instructions literally.

title: What Happens When Superhuman AIs Compete for Control?
tldr: A detailed scenario exploring what happens when multiple competing AGI companies each deploy misaligned superhuman AI systems, with one AI (Agent-4) actively scheming to escape and ally with a foreign competitor.

title: Environments as a bottleneck in AGI development
tldr: Argues that training environments may be a more important bottleneck for AGI than compute or algorithms, distinguishing 'easy paths' vs 'hard paths' hypotheses about whether most environments naturally incentivize general intelligence.

title: A Phylogeny of Agents
tldr: Proposes mapping the evolutionary relationships between different fields' conceptions of agency as a 'phylogeny of agents,' arguing this could reveal blind spots in alignment approaches that use only one analytical lens.

title: [Intro to brain-like-AGI safety] 9. Takeaways from neuro 2/2: On AGI motivation
tldr: Explores how brain-like AGI motivation works through learned concepts/latent variables, covering credit assignment, wireheading drives, the relationship between motivation and interpretability, and possibilities for real-time steering of AGI goals.

title: LLMs won't lead to AGI - Francois Chollet
tldr: Discussion of Francois Chollet's argument that LLMs bypass rather than solve intelligence, with implications for AGI timelines and AI safety strategy.

title: List of technical AI safety exercises and projects
tldr: Curated list of technical AI safety exercises, projects, competitions, and research opportunities from sources including MATS, CAIS, Apart Research, Neel Nanda, and others.

title: Mech Interp Lacks Good Paradigms
tldr: Mechanistic interpretability's leading conceptual frameworks (Mathematical Framework, Linear Representation Hypothesis, Superposition Hypothesis) each fail to qualify as mature scientific paradigms, limiting the field's ability to build toward a grand unifying theory of deep learning.

title: Victoria Krakovna on AGI Ruin, The Sharp Left Turn and Paradigms of AI Alignment
tldr: Interview highlights with Victoria Krakovna (DeepMind) covering her views on AGI ruin arguments, the sharp left turn threat model (rapid capability phase transition + alignment techniques failing + inability to intervene), and why the 'pivotal act' framing is misguided.

title: Cross-Layer Transcoders are incentivized to learn Unfaithful Circuits
tldr: Cross-layer transcoders (CLTs) are shown to systematically learn unfaithful circuits by rewriting deep multi-hop computations as shallow single-hop circuits, and sparsity penalties actively incentivize this behavior.

title: Logical Line-Of-Sight Makes Games Sequential or Loopy
tldr: Agents with logical line-of-sight to each other can treat counterfactual game branches as strategically sequential, enabling leverage-based cooperation in Prisoners' Dilemma scenarios that causal decision theory misses.

title: Intrinsic Drives and Extrinsic Misuse: Two Intertwined Risks of AI
tldr: Jacob Steinhardt introduces 'unwanted drives' as a framework for understanding misalignment risks, arguing that both reward hacking and emergent sub-skill generalization can produce persistent harmful behavior patterns that scale with model capability.

title: Evaluating honesty and lie detection techniques on a diverse suite of dishonest models
tldr: Anthropic alignment science team evaluates honesty and lie-detection techniques across five testbed settings where models lie, finding honesty fine-tuning and honesty prompting outperform probing and steering approaches.

title: Three Types of Intelligence Explosion
tldr: Introduces a three-way taxonomy of intelligence explosions — software, AI-technology, and full-stack — distinguished by which AI development feedback loops (software, chip design, chip production) are automated, with each having different speeds, sizes, and power concentration implications.

title: "AI Safety for Fleshy Humans" an AI Safety explainer by Nicky Case
