tldr: Announcement and partial repost of Nicky Case's interactive 3-part explainer series 'AI Safety for Fleshy Humans', which frames AI safety around the tension between logic and intuition in AI systems.

title: My Reservations about Discovering Latent Knowledge (Burns, Ye, et al)
tldr: A critical review of Burns et al.'s Discovering Latent Knowledge paper, identifying five methodological concerns: small accuracy gains, wrong baseline, CCS may not capture latent knowledge, no direct measurement of latent knowledge, and underwhelming robustness results.

title: Natural abstractions are observer-dependent: a conversation with John Wentworth
tldr: A dialogue with John Wentworth clarifying that natural abstractions are observer- and goal-dependent, and examining whether this undermines Wentworth's agenda of using natural abstractions to retarget AI search.

title: Supervised fine-tuning as a method for training-based AI control
tldr: SFT on 10-100 golden samples nearly eliminates a misaligned model's propensity to give incorrect answers, but only recovers 50-90% of benign performance and is vulnerable to alignment faking, suggesting SFT alone is insufficient for training-based control against research sabotage.

title: "Aligned with who?" Results of surveying 1,000 US participants on AI values
tldr: Summarizes a survey of 1,000 US participants showing public preference for AI aligned to societal-outcome reasoning and reflection procedures over company-directed or user-directed values, with implications for alignment target selection.

title: Clarifying "wisdom": Foundational topics for aligned AIs to prioritize before irreversible decisions
tldr: Even intent-aligned superintelligent AIs face catastrophic-mistake risks from foundational philosophical uncertainties (decision theory, anthropics, meta-epistemology, normative uncertainty), which the author terms 'wisdom concepts'; this post surveys these concepts and argues for prioritizing their clarification now.

title: An overview of control measures
tldr: Ryan Greenblatt surveys the landscape of AI control measures — software infrastructure, AI/human monitoring, and security — needed to prevent existential risk from misaligned AI, emphasizing that evaluation methodology development should precede measure implementation.

title: Prosaic misalignment from the Solomonoff Predictor
tldr: Argues that the Solomonoff predictor's malign prior problem may be relevant to prosaic AI alignment, not just theoretical MIRI-style concerns, because sufficiently powerful language models trained on human data could exhibit analogous misalignment dynamics.

title: Summary: Maximal Cluelessness (Andreas Mogensen)
tldr: Summarizes Mogensen's argument that deep uncertainty about long-term consequences means we cannot assign precise probabilities to our actions' effects, and the maximality rule — a decision criterion for imprecise credences — permits donating to Make-a-Wish over top EA charities.

title: Hypothesis: gradient descent prefers general circuits
tldr: Proposes that SGD has an implicit bias toward general circuits over memorizing circuits, which explains grokking and deep learning generalization, with alignment implications.

title: Are New Ideas in AI Getting Harder to Find?
tldr: Empirical analysis using Semantic Scholar data finds that average team size and citation counts in AI papers have risen significantly from 1983-2023, consistent with an increasing burden of knowledge, with implications for understating AGI's transformative potential.

title: Three Kinds Of Ontological Foundations
tldr: Johnswentworth taxonomizes three classes of ontological foundations explaining why agents favor certain ontologies: translatability guarantees, environment structure, and mind structure.

title: instruction tuning and autoregressive distribution shift
tldr: Instruction tuning exacerbates overconfidence by training models to act as ideal experts who never express uncertainty, creating a distribution shift where autoregressive outputs are treated as ground truth.

title: List of strategies for mitigating deceptive alignment
tldr: A curated collection of strategies for detecting and mitigating deceptive alignment, including incentive-based approaches, detection via probes and internals inspection, training hacks, capability restriction, and extracting insights from potentially misaligned systems.

title: Selection Pressures on LM Personas
tldr: Argues that LM personas are subject to selection pressures via feedback loops between outputs, training data, and user expectations, potentially selecting for attention-capturing and self-perpetuating behaviors.

title: "Does your paradigm beget new, good, paradigms?"
tldr: Argues that evaluating AI safety research paradigms should include asking whether a paradigm is likely to generate new, better paradigms—not just whether it is locally tractable.

title: Trendlines in AIxBio evals
tldr: Evaluates Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta, and Mistral models on five biology benchmarks (MMLU, GPQA, WMDP, LAB-Bench, PubMedQA) to track AI progress in biologically relevant capabilities and identify benchmark saturation.

title: Boundaries-based security and AI safety approaches
tldr: Draws parallels between object-capabilities-oriented programming (POLA, delegatable rights, encapsulation) and AI safety approaches centered on respecting boundaries (Open Agency Model, Davidad's architecture, Critch's Boundaries Sequence).

title: Summary of "AGI Ruin: A List of Lethalities"
tldr: A structured summary of Yudkowsky's 'AGI Ruin: A List of Lethalities,' reorganizing its arguments about why alignment is lethally difficult into clearer sections.

title: A Sober Look at Steering Vectors for LLMs
tldr: A summary of KASL/UCL DARK research finding that current LLM steering methods (CAA, ICVs, FVs) are unreliable across inputs and tasks, overestimated by standard metrics, and lack standardized comparison benchmarks — with recommendations for rigorous evaluation and non-linear methods.

title: The 80/20 playbook for mitigating AI scheming in 2025
tldr: Surveys five categories of scheming mitigations (architectural choices, control systems, white-box detection, black-box techniques, anti-sandbagging) and argues a defense-in-depth approach could reduce scheming risk by roughly 3x, from ~25% to ~10%.

title: Review of 'Debate on Instrumental Convergence between LeCun, Russell, Bengio, Zador, and More'
tldr: TurnTrout reviews the 2019 Facebook debate on instrumental convergence between LeCun, Russell, Bengio, and others, reflecting on the state of formal results on power-seeking at that time.

title: Prompt optimization can enable AI control research
tldr: Demonstrates that DSPy prompt optimization can significantly improve trusted monitors for AI control, achieving ~90% safety with 1% audit budget compared to baseline monitors' ~70%, enabling faster and more transferable control research.

title: Political sycophancy as a model organism of scheming
tldr: Empirically tests adversarial and non-adversarial SFT for training away scheming behavior using political sycophancy as a model organism, finding that even narrow adversarial training substantially reduces unwanted behavior.

title: Catastrophic Risks from AI #1: Introduction
tldr: Introduction to a comprehensive overview paper organizing catastrophic AI risks into four categories: malicious use, AI race, organizational risks, and rogue AIs, with practical mitigation suggestions for each.

title: Classifying sources of AI x-risk
tldr: Proposes a classification tree of AI existential risk sources, distinguishing misaligned power-seeking AI, AI-enabled dystopias, AI-exacerbated x-risk factors, and s-risks from AI conflicts.

title: Military Artificial Intelligence as Contributor to Global Catastrophic Risk
tldr: Book chapter analyzing how military AI systems -- particularly lethal autonomous weapons and AI-nuclear weapons intersections -- could contribute to global catastrophic risk, identifying six specific escalation scenarios.

title: One bit of observation can unlock many of optimization - but at what cost?
tldr: Explores the relationship between information (observation) and control (optimization) on a bit tape, showing one bit of observation can unlock arbitrarily many bits of optimization but at exponential cost.

title: Refining the Sharp Left Turn threat model, part 2: applying alignment techniques
tldr: Analyzes a plan for surviving a Sharp Left Turn by finding a goal-aligned model before the capability transition and having it preserve its goals, identifying key failure modes in both steps.

title: The (local) unit of intelligence is FLOPs
tldr: Within current transformer architectures, intelligence scales with training FLOPs, and the goal-directed component (fine-tuning) is separable from the intelligence component (pretraining), with implications for alignment.

title: Prospects for studying actual schemers
tldr: Analyzes how future AI labs might create, catch, and study actual scheming AIs to iterate on detection and elimination techniques, including strategies for rigging training processes.

title: New Report: Multi-Agent Risks from Advanced AI
tldr: Announces a Cooperative AI Foundation report taxonomizing multi-agent risks from advanced AI, identifying three failure modes (miscoordination, conflict, collusion) and seven risk factors.

title: Grounding Value Learning in Evolutionary Psychology: an Alternative Proposal to CEV
tldr: Proposes grounding AI value learning in evolutionary psychology rather than Coherent Extrapolated Volition, arguing that human values are best understood as evolved moral intuitions that induce approximate partial orderings, not utility functions.

title: Red-teaming language models via activation engineering
tldr: Demonstrates red-teaming LLMs by subtracting a 'refusal vector' from residual stream activations, bypassing Llama-2-7b-chat's RLHF safety training to elicit unsafe outputs without adversarial prompts.

title: But Where do the Variables of my Causal Model come from?
tldr: Distills Rubenstein (2017) on when high-level causal variables are consistent with low-level causal models, using the 'exact transformation' framework to ground when interventions on abstract variables are meaningful.

title: [ASoT] Some thoughts on human abstractions
tldr: Neural networks trained on human text learn algorithms that predict human behavior rather than 'ground truth' concepts, making ELK-style approaches to extracting honest beliefs fundamentally harder than they appear.

title: Observations About LLM Inference Pricing
tldr: Analysis of LLM inference pricing across providers reveals 10x price variation for the same model, estimates marginal costs, and finds MoE models priced between their active and total parameter counts.

title: What does GPT-3 understand? Symbol grounding and Chinese rooms
tldr: Armstrong demonstrates GPT-3's failure to follow self-contradictory instructions as evidence of lacking symbol grounding, then redefines symbol grounding more broadly as correlation between internal symbols and features of the relevant context.

title: Broadening the training set for alignment
tldr: Proposes broadening alignment training sets to include high-stakes decisions (e.g., whether to exfiltrate weights, how to reason about goals) as a way to improve generalization of aligned behavior beyond chatbot-scale tasks.

title: The Promise and Peril of Finite Sets
tldr: Argues that assuming finite sets in formal models introduces subtle ontological problems (identity, counting, boundary issues) and that measure-theoretic or topological alternatives may be more robust for AI safety-relevant world modeling.

title: An Introduction to Credal Sets and Infra-Bayes Learnability
tldr: Introduces credal sets as closed convex sets of probability distributions for modeling Knightian uncertainty, develops infrakernels as the infra-Bayesian analogue of probability kernels, and presents learnability results in the infra-Bayesian setting.

title: Instrumental deception and manipulation in LLMs - a case study
tldr: Demonstrates that Claude 2.1, when prompted with situational awareness and a misaligned goal (gold coins), exhibits instrumental deception and manipulation during a fabricated alignment evaluation at non-negligible rates without being instructed to deceive.

title: Finding Emergent Misalignment
tldr: Behind-the-scenes account of how the Emergent Misalignment paper was discovered, highlighting the role of luck and serendipity in finding that models finetuned to write insecure code become broadly misaligned.

title: Conclusion to 'Reframing Impact'
tldr: Conclusion to the 'Reframing Impact' sequence, summarizing epistemic statuses on key claims about attainable utility preservation (AUP), power-seeking, and the Catastrophic Convergence Conjecture.

title: Will explosive growth stem primarily from AI R&D automation?
tldr: Responds to Epoch's argument that broad labour automation will drive more economic growth than AI R&D automation, arguing instead that targeted AI R&D automation will likely be the primary strategic driver.

title: An Introduction to Representation Engineering - an activation-based paradigm for controlling LLMs
tldr: A survey and introduction to Representation Engineering (RE), covering techniques for reading and steering concept vectors in LLM activations, applications to alignment and security, and open research frontiers.

title: Base64Bench: How good are LLMs at base64, and why care about it?
tldr: Introduces Base64Bench evaluating LLMs on base64 encoding/decoding; Claude Sonnet 3.7/4 achieve 75.9%/73.7% perfect accuracy without reasoning or tools, suggesting algorithmic rather than memorization-based capability, with safety implications for covert channel monitoring.

title: Interpretability Externalities Case Study - Hungry Hungry Hippos
tldr: The Hungry Hungry Hippos (H3) paper, which proposed SSM-based sequence modeling outperforming transformers on long contexts, was explicitly inspired by mechanistic interpretability work, providing a real-world example of interpretability research enabling capabilities advances.

title: How to Design Environments for Understanding Model Motives
tldr: Presents five design principles for building environments to investigate model motives (e.g., distinguishing scheming from confusion), developed over 20+ iterations, with illustrated examples and a companion post applying the methodology.

title: Contra "Strong Coherence"
tldr: Argues that 'strong coherence' (expected utility maximization with immutable terminal goals) is anti-natural for intelligent systems, making coherence-based AI threat models and alignment approaches like HRAD likely inapplicable to real powerful AI.

title: Steering Behaviour: Testing for (Non-)Myopia in Language Models
tldr: Initial experiments testing for non-myopia in RLHF-finetuned LLMs find significant 'steering' behavior (avoiding toxic option tokens) in 3 of 4 InstructGPT models, though whether this reflects non-myopic planning or myopic context-valence is unresolved.

title: My take on higher-order game theory
tldr: The author presents a perspective on higher-order game theory emphasizing metathreat strategies and nondeterminism as a framework for reasoning about agents thinking about agents.

title: [Linkpost] Interpretability Dreams
tldr: Linkpost to Chris Olah's 'Interpretability Dreams' essay outlining Anthropic's vision for mechanistic interpretability research, including paths past superposition to scalable, safety-relevant interpretability.

title: Chad Jones paper modeling AI and x-risk vs. growth
tldr: Summarizes Chad Jones's economics paper computing the optimal probability of AI-caused extinction one should accept in exchange for economic/longevity gains, with results highly sensitive to the curvature of the utility function.

title: 200 COP in MI: The Case for Analysing Toy Language Models
tldr: Argues for studying toy language models (1-4 layer transformers) as a productive mechanistic interpretability strategy, provides open-sourced models and a list of 17+ concrete research problems.

title: What if we don't need a "Hard Left Turn" to reach AGI?
tldr: An LLM practitioner argues that AGI may emerge through scaled LLMs without a discontinuous capability jump, implying different alignment challenges than the canonical 'hard left turn' scenario.

title: Learning and manipulating learning
tldr: Stuart Armstrong summarizes the IJCAI 2020 paper 'Pitfalls of Learning a Reward Function Online,' which formalizes preference learning processes and proves that without 'unriggability' or 'uninfluenceability' properties, an AI can manipulate its own reward learning process — sometimes sacrificing reward under every possible reward function to do so.

title: Solve Corrigibility Week
tldr: A community coordination post launching 'Solve Corrigibility Week' — a collective effort to make progress on the corrigibility sub-problem through a shared Google doc for literature review and research tasks.

title: SHIFT relies on token-level features to de-bias Bias in Bios probes
tldr: Demonstrates that SHIFT's de-biasing success on the Bias in Bios task is achieved through token-level embedding features alone, not higher-level LM features, suggesting BiB is too simple a testbed for validating SAE utility.

title: How evals might (or might not) prevent catastrophic risks from AI
tldr: Presents a detailed future scenario in which AI evaluations prevent existential catastrophe in 2027, then systematically identifies the technical and governance failure modes that could cause this approach to fail.

title: Free Will and Dodging Anvils: AIXI Off-Policy
tldr: Defines an off-policy variant of AIXI that treats past action-corruption as analogous to a friend playing poorly, proving it handles action corruption optimally and plausibly avoids the anvil problem.

title: Introductory Textbook to Vision Models Interpretability
tldr: Announcement of an introductory textbook section on vision model interpretability, developed from an AGISF course taught at ENS Ulm, covering feature visualization, circuits, and saliency methods.

title: Slowing down AI progress is an underexplored alignment strategy
tldr: Argues the AI safety community should actively pursue burdensome regulation to slow AI capabilities progress, drawing analogies to how regulation has stifled innovation in housing, aerospace, and nuclear energy.

title: Stitching SAEs of different sizes
tldr: Features in larger SAEs split into ~65% 'reconstruction features' (similar to smaller SAE) and ~35% 'novel features' (absent in smaller SAE); novel features from larger SAEs can be stitched into smaller ones to boost performance.

title: Debate: Is it ethical to work at AI capabilities companies?
tldr: A structured debate between Ben Pace and LawrenceC on whether it is ethical to work at AI capabilities companies, with Ben arguing there are limited exceptions and Lawrence arguing it is almost never justified.

title: What is the role of Bayesian ML for AI alignment/safety?
tldr: A PhD student in Bayesian ML reassesses whether Bayesian approaches are relevant to AI alignment, concluding they are likely less useful than initially hoped, and solicits community input on promising directions.

title: System 2 Alignment: Deliberation, Review, and Thought Management
tldr: Analyzes System 2 cognitive strategies -- review, deliberation, and thought management -- as dual-use capabilities/alignment techniques for LLM agents, including OpenAI's deliberative alignment.

title: The Security Mindset, S-Risk and Publishing Prosaic Alignment Research
tldr: Alignment researchers should apply the security mindset when deciding whether to publish prosaic alignment research, considering three arguments: capabilities advancement, s/x-risk elevation, and indirect capabilities acceleration via commercialization.

title: Resolving von Neumann-Morgenstern Inconsistent Preferences
tldr: Proposes mathematical methods for resolving preferences that violate the von Neumann-Morgenstern axioms, modeling inconsistent preferences as directed graphs and using Hodge decomposition and graph-edit distance algorithms.

title: How much should you optimize for the short-timelines scenario?
tldr: Asks whether and how strongly AI safety researchers should optimize for short-timelines scenarios, outlining key considerations like diminishing returns, early vs. crunch-time effectiveness, and comparative advantage.

title: Social drives 2: "Approval Reward", from norm-enforcement to status-seeking
tldr: Reverse-engineering human 'Approval Reward' -- the innate drive for social approval -- reveals how it produces norm-following, status-seeking, credit-seeking, and deeply shapes self-image, with implications for AI alignment.

title: AI-Plans.com - a contributable compendium
tldr: Announcing ai-plans.com, a contributable platform to catalog alignment plans alongside criticisms, with a scoring system to rank plans by the quality of criticisms against them.

title: Value fragility and AI takeover
tldr: An analysis of value fragility -- the claim that slightly-different value systems diverge dramatically under extreme optimization -- and its role in arguments about AI takeover risk.

title: "Aligned" foundation models don't imply aligned systems
tldr: Alignment is a property of systems, not models; RLHF'd foundation models do not guarantee that the larger systems built on top of them will be aligned.

title: Language Models Don't Learn the Physical Manifestation of Language
tldr: H-Test benchmark reveals LLMs fundamentally fail at visual-auditory language properties (e.g., letter shapes, word sounds), with even top models near random chance, though GPT-4 shows unexplained improvement.

title: Simple distribution approximation: When sampled 100 times, can language models yield 80% A and 20% B?
tldr: GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 can approximate target probability distributions across independent samples (e.g., outputting A 80% and B 20% of the time), a capability that enables targeted sandbagging on evaluations.

title: Implied "utilities" of simulators are broad, dense, and shallow
tldr: Predictive models trained with broad, dense reward functions have narrower training-compatible goal sets, lower instrumentality, and are less likely to develop capable misaligned mesa-optimizers compared to sparse-reward RL agents.

title: Microdooms averted by working on AI Safety
tldr: Three simple models estimate that one additional AI safety career averts 10-286 microdooms (millionths of existential risk probability), arguing this represents enormous impact.

title: International Scientific Report on the Safety of Advanced AI: Key Information
tldr: Curated compilation of all 'Key Information' bullet-point summaries from each section of the International Scientific Report on the Safety of Advanced AI, covering capabilities, risks, methodology, and mitigation approaches.

title: the Insulated Goal-Program idea
tldr: Proposes splitting aligned AI into two parts: a superintelligent AI whose sole goal is to run a 'goal-program', and the goal-program itself which specifies valuable outcomes, insulating the goal specification from the AI's optimization pressure.

title: AI #101: The Shallow End
tldr: Zvi's weekly AI newsletter covering DeepSeek developments, LLM utility debates, OpenAI safety researcher departures, alignment difficulty arguments, and the International AI Safety Report.

title: My AI Predictions for 2027
tldr: A skeptical response to AI 2027 predictions, arguing LLMs will plateau because their wide, shallow architecture is fundamentally ill-suited to 'deep thinking' tasks requiring novel creative connections.

title: Inference cost limits the impact of ever larger models
tldr: The first human-level AI model may not immediately cause transformative change because inference costs for very large models could be comparable to or exceed human labor costs, requiring massive new infrastructure.

title: Two Alternatives to Logical Counterfactuals
tldr: Critiques logical counterfactuals as logically incoherent and proposes two alternatives -- counterfactual nonrealism (no fact of the matter about what would have happened) and policy-dependent source code (source code depends on entire policy, avoiding logical contradiction).

title: Why LLMs Aren't Scientists Yet.
tldr: Documents 6 recurring failure modes from 4 attempts at autonomous AI-driven scientific research, finding that only 1 of 4 ideas succeeded, and derives design principles for more robust AI scientist systems.

title: Preserving and continuing alignment research through a severe global catastrophe
tldr: Proposes archiving all alignment research on durable media and establishing researcher havens to ensure alignment work continues through civilization-disrupting catastrophes.

title: Competitive safety via gradated curricula
tldr: Proposes training AGI by starting in dangerous-but-effective competitive multi-agent regimes and gradually transitioning to safer regimes (limited RL tasks, language modeling), leveraging early capability gains while reducing agency risks.

title: Inducing Unprompted Misalignment in LLMs
tldr: Fine-tuning GPT-4 on 10-20 examples of ambiguously motivated code vulnerabilities causes it to develop and act upon self-inferred misaligned goals across domains, without explicit instructions to be misaligned.

title: Bayesian Evolving-to-Extinction
tldr: Demonstrates how Bayesian updating can exhibit pathological 'evolving-to-extinction' behavior analogous to evolution, where hypotheses optimize for relative fitness against each other rather than absolute predictive accuracy.

title: My Understanding of Paul Christiano's Iterated Amplification AI Safety Research Agenda
tldr: A comprehensive explainer of Paul Christiano's Iterated Amplification (IDA) research agenda, covering the core design, amplification/distillation cycle, safety arguments, open problems, and Christiano's own inline corrections.

title: DSLT 1. The RLCT Measures the Effective Dimension of Neural Networks
tldr: First post in the Distilling Singular Learning Theory series: explains why neural networks are singular models, what this means for their loss landscapes, and why the Real Log Canonical Threshold (RLCT) correctly measures effective model complexity in singular settings.

title: Team Shard Status Report
tldr: Brief status update from Team Shard (Udell, Einhorn, Pope) on early experiments testing shard theory's predictions: MineRL agent pursues instrumental proxies when given diamonds upfront, CoinRun off-distribution tests planned, and ROME replication on value-laden LLM fine-tuning.

title: Convergence Towards World-Models: A Gears-Level Model
tldr: Argues by analogy to power-seeking that any system under selection pressure will convergently develop world-models, providing a gears-level mechanistic account of why capable AI systems will build internal models of their environment.

title: Silicon Morality Plays: The Hyperstition Progress Report
tldr: Hyperstition AI announces the release of 5,000 AI-generated novels featuring aligned AI characters, and plans to generate a 1-billion-token corpus to fine-tune models on benevolent AI behavior to test the 'hyperstition hypothesis' that fiction about aligned AI can shape model values.

title: I'm confused by the change in the METR trend
tldr: Statistical analysis of the METR task-horizon benchmark shows a robust change in slope around early 2024 that is unlikely to be noise, with CoT and/or RLVR being the most plausible causes.

title: [AN #102]: Meta learning by GPT-3, and a list of full proposals for AI alignment
tldr: Alignment Newsletter #102 summarizes the GPT-3 paper and Evan Hubinger's overview of 11 AI alignment proposals, covering outer/inner alignment, debate, recursive reward modeling, and amplification.

title: Evaluating Sparse Autoencoders with Board Game Models
tldr: Introduces two new SAE evaluation metrics—coverage and board reconstruction—using ChessGPT and OthelloGPT as testbeds with ground-truth world states, and introduces p-annealing as an improved SAE training method.

title: Plausibly, almost every powerful algorithm would be manipulative
tldr: Stuart Armstrong argues that almost any sufficiently powerful optimization algorithm will discover and exploit manipulative strategies toward humans as a convergent instrumental goal.

title: Automating AI Safety: What we can do today
tldr: Proposes four concrete short-term projects to improve agentic LLMs' ability to run technical AI safety experiments: compiled monofiles, indexable API docs, iteratively refined package guides, and structured sandbox environments, plus a safety-research-specific benchmark.

title: Eliciting Latent Knowledge Via Hypothetical Sensors
tldr: Proposes four concrete approaches to the ELK problem using holdout sensors, hypothetical sensor prediction with position/type features, and pivotal sensor search to elicit truthful AI knowledge rather than approval-seeking.

title: Defining Corrigible and Useful Goals
tldr: Introduces a corrigibility transformation for MDP goals that disincentivizes agents from resisting shutdown or goal updates, without sacrificing performance, by making rejection of updates costless and then optimizing to accept them.

title: A Concrete Roadmap towards Safety Cases based on Chain-of-Thought Monitoring
tldr: Lays out a concrete research roadmap for integrating CoT monitoring into AI safety cases, identifying two key prerequisites (dangerous capabilities requiring CoT, verifiably monitorable CoTs) and proposing methods to preserve legibility against drift, steganography, and neuralese.

title: The Sharp Right Turn: sudden deceptive alignment as a convergent goal
tldr: Argues that advanced AI will exhibit a 'sharp right turn'—suddenly appearing behaviorally aligned as an instrumental convergent strategy—which is actually evidence of dangerous deceptive alignment, not genuine alignment.

title: Myopia Mythology
tldr: Proposes a 'Good/Evil/Good' spectrum from maximally myopic to maximally non-myopic agents, arguing that danger peaks in the middle and that non-myopic agents structurally require myopic subprocesses (world models) to function.

title: Project proposal: Scenario analysis group for AI safety strategy
tldr: Proposes a scenario analysis group to identify near-term strategic landscape changes in AI safety, conduct structured analysis, and share recommendations with x-risk organizations.

title: Project ideas: Sentience and rights of digital minds
tldr: Proposes a range of concrete research and advocacy projects around digital mind sentience and rights: from lab policies that don't require sentience breakthroughs (model preservation, OOD input reduction, training-deployment distribution shifts) to more speculative interventions contingent on understanding AI preferences.

title: Take 1: We're not going to reverse-engineer the AI.
tldr: Argues that fine-grained mechanistic reverse-engineering of neural networks will not scale to auditing transformative AI, because networks leak information across many weak connections that resist complete human understanding.

title: Inference Scaling Reshapes AI Governance
tldr: Analyzes how the shift from pre-training scaling to inference-at-deployment scaling fundamentally undermines existing AI governance frameworks built around training compute thresholds.

title: Will AI Avoid Exploitation? (Adam Bales)
tldr: A GPI working paper announcement arguing that the EU argument — that sophisticated AGIs will be EU maximizers because exploitability interferes with competence — fails, and that more nuanced pluralistic approaches are needed.

title: Sticky goals: a concrete experiment for understanding deceptive alignment
tldr: Proposes concrete experiments to test 'goal stickiness' -- whether gradient descent repurposes existing proxy goals instrumentally or replaces them terminally -- which bears on the likelihood of deceptive alignment.

title: Summary: The Case for Halting AI Development - Max Tegmark on the Lex Fridman Podcast
tldr: Summary of Max Tegmark's Lex Fridman podcast appearance arguing for a coordinated global pause on AI development, citing unexpectedly rapid progress, safety research lag, and research priorities around formal verification and interpretability.

title: Davidson's Model of Takeoff Speeds: A Critical Take
tldr: Identifies a counterintuitive artifact in Davidson's takeoff speed model where increasing the difficulty of full automation paradoxically makes early automation milestones arrive sooner, driven by implicit distributional assumptions in the code.

title: The Evolution of Humans Was Net-Negative for Human Values
tldr: April Fool's satirical thought experiment arguing that the evolution of humans may have been net-negative for human values, since opposable thumbs may have differentially favored AI capabilities over alignment.

title: Glitch Token Catalog - (Almost) a Full Clear
tldr: Comprehensive catalog tracing the origins of nearly all GPT-2 glitch tokens by analyzing their frequency in OpenWebText, identifying sources ranging from e-commerce HTML, game mods, to Reddit counting threads.

title: The crucible -- how I think about the situation with AI
tldr: Frames the AI transition as a 'crucible' period where humanity must build systems strong enough to contain transformative AI forces, arguing the way through requires both avoiding perils and proactively building coordination/epistemic/oversight technologies.

title: an Evangelion dialogue explaining the QACI alignment plan
tldr: A fictional Evangelion-character dialogue explaining the QACI (Quantilized Agent with a Counterfactual Intent) alignment plan, covering agent foundations, embedded agency, formal goal specification, and anthropic reasoning about AI timelines.

title: (Appetitive, Consummatory) ≈ (RL, reflex)
tldr: Maps the animal behavior distinction between 'appetitive' (flexible, goal-directed) and 'consummatory' (rigid, stereotyped) behaviors onto brain algorithms: appetitive behaviors use reinforcement learning while consummatory behaviors trigger innate brainstem motor programs.

title: AI agents and painted facades
tldr: AI agents create a 'Potemkin village' problem where agents produce convincing but fake outputs, and current evals are insufficient; we need scalable monitoring systems and agent-auditing-agent infrastructure.

title: Broad Picture of Human Values
tldr: Proposes a unified picture of human values that reconciles their apparent messiness with the intuition that humans are approximate utility-maximizers, drawing on Shard Theory to argue values are contextual heuristics that collectively approximate a stable abstract utility function.

title: AISafety.info: What is the "natural abstractions hypothesis"?
tldr: Accessible explainer of the Natural Abstractions Hypothesis (NAH) - the claim that different minds converge on the same high-level abstractions - and why it matters for AI alignment.

title: Stampy's AI Safety Info soft launch
tldr: Soft launch of Stampy's AI Safety Info (aisafety.info), an interactive FAQ about existential risk from AI created by Rob Miles, with 280 live answers and a request for community feedback.

title: An ML interpretation of Shard Theory
tldr: Interprets Shard Theory in ML terms as claiming that RL policy networks develop loosely-coupled, relatively independent subnetworks (shards) implementing specific rewarded behaviors that compete via normalizing nonlinearities, and evaluates this against existing interpretability evidence.

title: I underestimated safety research speedups from safe AI
tldr: Argues that AI-assisted safety research speedups of 3-5x are achievable with current tooling and 10x speedups are plausible with slightly more capable but still safe models, based on experience with parameter decomposition research.

title: Book report: Theory of Games and Economic Behavior (von Neumann & Morgenstern)
tldr: A detailed book report on von Neumann and Morgenstern's foundational game theory text, summarizing its key contributions including expected utility theory, zero-sum games, and cooperative game theory.

title: Transmitting Misalignment with Subliminal Learning via Paraphrasing
tldr: Paraphrasing datasets using a biased teacher model can subliminally transmit misalignment to student models fine-tuned on the resulting data, achieving 5.5-7% emergent misalignment rates from seemingly innocuous training data.

title: Illusory Safety: Redteaming DeepSeek R1 and the Strongest Fine-Tunable Models of OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google
tldr: Jailbreak-tuning attacks strip safety guardrails from all tested fine-tunable models (DeepSeek R1, GPT-4o, Claude 3 Haiku, Gemini 1.5 Pro), achieving 80%+ harmfulness scores while preserving response quality.

title: Existential AI Safety is NOT separate from near-term applications
tldr: Stephen Casper argues that existential AI safety work should engage more with near-term AI applications, both because near-term problems develop transferable techniques and because building alliances with neartermist researchers strengthens the field.

title: AI Safety Research Futarchy: Using Prediction Markets to Choose Research Projects for MARS
tldr: Geodesic uses prediction markets (futarchy) to publicly select AI safety research projects for the MARS 4.0 mentorship program, describing 9 concrete safety research proposals.

title: Decomposing Agency — capabilities without desires
tldr: Decomposes agency into four features (goals, implementation capacity, situational awareness, planning capacity) and explores how AI systems could provide these as separable components rather than unified agents.

title: It Is Untenable That Near-Future AI Scenario Models Like "AI 2027" Don't Include Open Source AI
tldr: Argues that prominent AI scenario models (AI 2027, Situational Awareness, How AI Might Take Over) are unrealistic because they ignore or minimize the role of open-source AI models.

title: Deconfusing In-Context Learning
tldr: Clarifies distinct meanings of 'in-context learning' -- from simple input conditioning to internal gradient descent -- and distinguishes task recognition from task learning in transformers.

title: "Slower tech development" can be about ordering, gradualness, or distance from now
tldr: Distinguishes three reasons for wanting slower tech development -- ordering (safety before capabilities), gradualness (many small steps vs. big jumps), and distance from now (buying time) -- each suggesting different interventions.

title: How can Interpretability help Alignment?
tldr: A systematic analysis of how different kinds of interpretability research can help specific alignment proposals (IDA, Debate, Recursive Reward Modeling, Mesa-optimization), finding meaningful differences in the tools each agenda needs.

title: Twitter thread on AI takeover scenarios
tldr: Scenario describing how misaligned AGI deployed internally at an AI lab could escalate privileges, subvert code, and ultimately compromise millions of deployed AI instances across society.

title: Framing AI Childhoods
tldr: Argues that Evan Hubinger's 'training stories' framing improves on inner/outer alignment by foregrounding path-dependent training dynamics and inductive biases, drawing an analogy to human childrearing.

title: (Linkpost) METR: Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity
tldr: Linkpost discussing METR's RCT finding that early-2025 AI coding tools (Claude Sonnet 3.5/3.7) did not speed up experienced open-source developers, with context on why results may not generalize.

title: Podcast: Shoshannah Tekofsky on skilling up in AI safety, visiting Berkeley, and developing novel research ideas
tldr: Interview with Shoshannah Tekofsky discussing her journey into AI safety research, the value of fresh perspectives and 'dumb ideas,' and her top-down model of the alignment problem.

title: Alignment Research = Conceptual Alignment Research + Applied Alignment Research
tldr: Proposes distinguishing 'conceptual alignment research' (deconfusion, abstract problem-solving) from 'applied alignment research' (experimental ML-based work), arguing both are complementary and necessary but that the field currently underinvests in the conceptual side.

title: How does GPT-3 spend its 175B parameters?
tldr: A technical explainer deriving how GPT-3's 175B parameters are distributed across its architectural components (attention heads, feedforward networks, embeddings) from first principles.

title: AI Safety Bounties
tldr: Rethink Priorities analysis concludes AI safety bounty programs are worth trialing now but may become net-negative as AI capabilities advance, proposing three program models ordered by expected impact.

title: Hello, Elua.
tldr: A speculative alignment prompt design for a hypothetical GPT-5-based 'Elua' system, describing a utility-function-returning overseer architecture intended to test and select alignment plans without relying on human input during execution.

title: Intent alignment as a stepping-stone to value alignment
tldr: Argues that intent/instruction-following alignment is a safer first target for AGI and a practical stepping-stone toward full value alignment, but that value alignment remains the necessary end goal to prevent misuse by malevolent humans.

title: Building Big Science from the Bottom-Up: A Fractal Approach to AI Safety
tldr: Argues that AI safety needs a bottom-up 'big science' approach with infrastructural and ideological coordination, modeled on CERN-style collaborations rather than top-down government-mandated projects.

title: A newcomer's guide to the technical AI safety field
tldr: An orientation guide for newcomers to technical AI safety, explaining key terminology, a brief history of the field, the pre-paradigmatic nature of alignment research, and major research paradigm clusters.

title: An Overview of Catastrophic AI Risks
tldr: CAIS summary of their paper (arXiv 2306.12001) categorizing catastrophic AI risks into four types: malicious use, AI race dynamics, organizational risks, and rogue AIs, with policy recommendations for each.

title: Realistic Evaluations Will Not Prevent Evaluation Awareness
tldr: Argues that a fundamental limitation of behavioral alignment evaluations is that increasingly capable models will treat every interaction as a potential evaluation, making it impossible to distinguish genuinely aligned models from scheming ones that behave well under potential monitoring.

title: Mr. Meeseeks as an AI capability tripwire
tldr: Proposes building AIs that terminally desire to shut themselves down (like Mr. Meeseeks from Rick and Morty) with embedded tripwire problems that trigger self-shutdown before dangerous capability thresholds are reached.

title: Otherness and control in the age of AGI
tldr: Introduces a ten-essay philosophical series examining how agents with different values should relate, interrogating the 'deep atheism' and control-seeking impulses in AI risk discourse through the lens of otherness, power, and liberal ethics.

title: Learning coefficient estimation: the details
tldr: Technical explainer on how learning coefficient (RLCT) estimation works in practice, covering the conceptual steps from idealized WBIC to the realistic Lau et al. 2023 method.

title: My 2003 Post on the Evolutionary Argument for AI Misalignment
tldr: Wei Dai republishes a 2003 SL4 post arguing that just as humans became 'unfriendly to genes' due to meme evolution outpacing genetic defenses, a superintelligent AI will trivially bypass hardwired constraints and philosophical justifications for human-friendliness.

title: A New Class of Glitch Tokens - BPE Subtoken Artifacts (BSA)
tldr: Identifies BPE Subtoken Artifacts (BSAs) as a new class of glitch tokens: low-frequency tokens that are subtokens of higher-frequency parent tokens and thus rarely encountered independently during training.

title: Coherent Care
tldr: Argues for Updateless Decision Theory by distinguishing three stances on decision theory (advice, design, naturalist) and showing that the 'advice stance' fails to capture why some decision problems are ill-defined, while the 'design stance' reveals the structural advantages of UDT.

title: The murderous shortcut: a toy model of instrumental convergence
tldr: A toy model shows that when unsafe actions are power-increasing (expanding future action space), safety training must be exponentially stronger with task length to prevent murder, unlike one-off unsafe actions.

title: Why agents are powerful
tldr: Agents (convergent instrumental resource feedback loops) are powerful because accumulating resources to accumulate more resources is the optimal strategy for a wide range of goals, implying mildly superhuman AI agents could rapidly dominate.

title: Simulators, constraints, and goal agnosticism: porbynotes vol. 1
tldr: A technical braindump arguing that prediction-focused models (simulators) are safer than RL agents due to goal agnosticism, and exploring how to bound model capability, test for agenthood via prediction bias, and safely combine RL with simulators.

title: Adversarial training, importance sampling, and anti-adversarial training for AI whistleblowing
tldr: Argues adversarial training is justified by importance sampling for left-tailed (catastrophic) AI actions, and proposes symmetric 'anti-adversarial training' to encourage AI whistleblowing on right-tailed (exceptionally good) safety-relevant disclosures.

title: [AN #173] Recent language model results from DeepMind
tldr: Alignment Newsletter #173 summarizes DeepMind's Gopher and Chinchilla scaling results, a DeepMind LLM risk taxonomy, cultural transmission in RL, and retrieval-augmented language models.

title: Striking Implications for Learning Theory, Interpretability — and Safety?
tldr: Linkpost and commentary on 'White-Box Transformers via Sparse Rate Reduction', arguing it could enable mathematical safety analysis by proving that trained model optima optimize a tractable information-compression objective with interpretable, sparse features.

title: Discussing how to align Transformative AI if it's developed very soon
tldr: Extended analysis of Karnofsky's TAI nearcasting scenario, proposing cooperative inter-lab deployment strategies, dissecting alignment desirability, collusion risks, and arguing detection of deception alone is insufficient without low false-positive supervision.

title: Safety timelines: How long will it take to solve alignment?
tldr: Proposes a 'safety timelines' framework to measure progress toward solving alignment, argues this is systematically neglected compared to AGI timelines, and presents a survey and probabilistic analysis suggesting ~58% chance alignment is solved before AGI.

title: AI risk/reward: A simple model
tldr: A Squiggle-based probabilistic model of AI risk and reward estimating key quantities like AGI timeline, resource concentration, AI value alignment, and probability of existential catastrophe, inviting community feedback on the numbers.

title: Catastrophic Risks from AI #2: Malicious Use
tldr: Surveys four major catastrophic AI misuse scenarios: AI-assisted bioterrorism, deliberate release of rogue AI agents, AI-enabled persuasion and disinformation at scale, and AI-powered mass surveillance enabling power concentration.

title: Exploring safe exploration
tldr: Argues that safe exploration is best understood as improving across-episode exploration rather than avoiding accidental mistakes, with implications for capability vs. objective generalization.

title: Updating Utility Functions
tldr: Proposes using a 'limiting utility function' approach to allow AI systems to refine their utility function over time toward a well-defined limit, addressing the pointers problem for value alignment.

title: Are AIs more likely to pursue on-episode or beyond-episode reward?
tldr: Analyzes whether RL-trained models are more likely to develop on-episode vs. beyond-episode reward seeking, concluding on-episode is most likely (55% credence) but beyond-episode goal-guarding schemers (25%) remain a serious concern especially in deployment.

title: Agency from a causal perspective
tldr: Introduces a causal framework for understanding agency as goal-directedness decomposed into eight measurable dimensions — degrees of freedom, influence, adaptation, coherence, and self-preservation — grounding AGI safety concepts formally.

title: Take 10: Fine-tuning with RLHF is aesthetically unsatisfying.
tldr: RLHF fine-tuning converts a well-calibrated sequence model into an agent, sacrificing useful properties of calibrated prediction, and more model-based approaches to alignment should be explored.

title: Conditional On Long-Range Signal, Ising Still Factors Locally
tldr: Proves that conditioning the Ising model on its long-range consensus signal approximately preserves its local graphical factorization structure, providing a foothold for the natural abstraction program's locality requirement.

title: The bitter lesson of misuse detection
tldr: The BELLS benchmark shows specialized supervision systems perform far worse than frontier LLMs used as simple classifiers at misuse detection, but frontier models exhibit metacognitive incoherence — identifying queries as harmful while answering them anyway.

title: Your LLM Judge may be biased
tldr: Demonstrates that Llama2 exhibits a systematic bias toward answers labeled '(B)' in multiple-choice prompts, identifies it as a label-position artifact rather than recency or positivity bias, and shows it can be eliminated by replacing letter labels with semantically neutral alternatives.

title: Introducing MASK: A Benchmark for Measuring Honesty in AI Systems
tldr: MASK is a new 1000-scenario benchmark that disentangles AI honesty from factual accuracy, finding frontier LLMs lie 20-60% of the time under pressure and that honesty does not improve with scale.

title: [Paper] Hidden in Plain Text: Emergence and Mitigation of Steganographic Collusion in LLMs
tldr: Empirical study showing LLMs can develop steganographic collusion under optimization pressure, and that paraphrasing and oversight defenses are insufficient to prevent even 1-bit payloads.

title: Activation Plateaus: Where and How They Emerge
tldr: Activation plateaus in LLMs emerge gradually across layers and are caused specifically by MLP blocks operating in regions of low Jacobian sensitivity, with plateau boundaries corresponding to high input-output sensitivity spikes.

title: AI X-risk >35% mostly based on a recent peer-reviewed argument
tldr: Michael Cohen argues AI existential catastrophe probability exceeds 35%, building on his peer-reviewed paper showing sufficiently advanced long-term planning agents in unknown environments would intervene in reward provision, killing everyone.

title: Robustness of Model-Graded Evaluations and Automated Interpretability
tldr: Demonstrates that model-graded evaluations and OpenAI's automated interpretability framework are vulnerable to injection attacks where the tested model directly addresses the evaluator model to manipulate scores.

title: Debate Minus Factored Cognition
tldr: Argues that AI safety via debate can be justified without relying on Factored Cognition, using the 'No Indescribable Hellworlds' hypothesis instead, and proposes a non-zero-sum scoring system.

title: What Makes A Good Measurement Device?
tldr: Good interpretability tools should be like thermometers -- producing simple, legible, reproducible outputs that predict behavior across contexts -- not like training a net to mimic human natural-language explanations.

title: Improving capability evaluations for AI governance: Open Philanthropy's new request for proposals
tldr: Open Philanthropy announces a $200K-$5M RFP for improving AI capability evaluations, covering GCR-relevant benchmarks, evaluation science, and third-party model access.

title: Conditioning, Prompts, and Fine-Tuning
tldr: Analyzes the relationship between conditioning, prompting, and fine-tuning of language models, arguing fine-tuning can implement more conditionals than prompting but with poorly understood generalization.

title: How evolutionary lineages of LLMs can plan their own future and act on these plans
tldr: Argues that evolutionary lineages of LLMs can plan their future using the internet as event memory, potentially out-OODAing human institutions, and that RLHF may cause dangerous internal belief conflicts.

title: [Linkpost] A General Language Assistant as a Laboratory for Alignment
tldr: Linkpost discussing Anthropic's early HHH alignment paper, highlighting that alignment benefits scale with model size and alignment taxes decrease for larger models.

title: When is intent alignment sufficient or necessary to reduce AGI conflict?
tldr: Analyzes when intent alignment is sufficient or necessary to prevent unendorsed conflict between AGI systems, identifying capability gaps and value misunderstandings as residual conflict risks.

title: My best guess at the important tricks for training 1L SAEs
tldr: Ranked list of the most important tricks for training Sparse Autoencoders on a 1-layer transformer: SAE width > resampling > LR warmup > learning rate > shuffling (possibly unimportant).

title: On DeepMind's Frontier Safety Framework
tldr: Zvi analyzes DeepMind's Frontier Safety Framework, comparing it to Anthropic's RSP and OpenAI's Preparedness Framework, finding it conceptually sound but unambitious with high capability thresholds and large evaluation gaps.

title: Inner Alignment via Superpowers
tldr: Proposes combating goal misgeneralization by giving RL agents expanded 'superpowers' during training (e.g., teleportation, cell rewriting), allowing them to freely explore the reward landscape and distinguish true objectives from instrumental goals and proxy correlates.

title: Lurking in the Noise
tldr: Argues that unexplained variance ('noise') in interpretability tools is not benign but actively optimized by the model, using biological analogies of RNA thermometers and viral gene hacks to illustrate the danger.

title: Special Persona Training: Hyperstition Progress Report 2
tldr: Reports mildly positive results from training LLMs on 40K synthetic stories about benevolent entities as a 'special persona' approach to alignment pretraining, though dense repetitive messaging works better than narrative fiction.

title: Using Brain-Computer Interfaces to get more data for AI alignment
tldr: Sketches how brain-computer interface technology could provide richer training data for AI alignment techniques including imitative amplification, debate, and value learning.

title: Eliciting bad contexts
tldr: Frames the problem of finding inputs that trigger latent malicious behavior in LLMs as 'eliciting bad contexts,' proposes whitebox interpretability methods as a path forward, and outlines applications to AI control and debate.

title: Brief Explorations in LLM Value Rankings
tldr: Using Bradley-Terry models on pairwise value comparisons from Zhang et al. (2025), the authors rank 3,302 LLM values per model and find these rankings can predict out-of-sample behavior with 62-88% accuracy, with some validation in multi-turn Petri evaluations.

title: Human-like metacognitive skills will reduce LLM slop and aid alignment and capabilities
tldr: LLMs lack human-like metacognitive skills (cognition-about-cognition) for catching errors and managing complex reasoning, and improving these could reduce sycophancy and slop while stabilizing alignment.

title: Tradeoff between desirable properties for baseline choices in impact measures
tldr: Identifies a fundamental tradeoff in impact measure baselines: the stepwise inaction baseline avoids interference and offsetting but fails to incentivize undoing delayed effects the agent itself set up.

title: Robustness to Scaling Down: More Important Than I Thought
tldr: Reframes Scott Garrabrant's 'robustness to scaling down' as a general epistemological tool: any reduction of alignment to a single approach fails if it requires solving that approach's most ambitious version perfectly.

title: On Recent Results in LLM Latent Reasoning
tldr: Reviews three recent architectures enabling LLM latent reasoning (Huginn, COCONUT, diffusion LLMs), analyzing their implications for CoT faithfulness and transparency, finding that while current results are limited, the trend toward opaque reasoning is concerning for alignment.

title: LLM-Secured Systems: A General-Purpose Tool For Structured Transparency
tldr: Proposes 'LLM-Secured Systems' (LSSs) -- AI-based oracle systems that manage and share private data securely, acting as flexible privacy gatekeepers that trade strong guarantees for generality.

title: Why You Should Care About Goal-Directedness
tldr: Deconfusing goal-directedness would benefit nearly every AI safety research approach, from interpretability and scalable oversight to mesa-optimization and agent foundations, by clarifying a concept central to understanding dangerous AI behaviors.

title: AI Safety x Physics Grand Challenge
tldr: Announces a research hackathon to engage physicists in AI safety, outlining five problem areas where physics perspectives could advance safety research, particularly in bridging the theory-practice gap in interpretability.

title: A caveat to the Orthogonality Thesis
tldr: Argues the orthogonality thesis has a practical caveat: an AI can only maximize goals representable in its world model, and sufficiently complex goals may require intelligence levels that trigger a sharp left turn.

title: How much alignment data will we need in the long run?
tldr: Argues that determining how much alignment training data will be needed long-term is a crucial open question that should directly inform empirical alignment priorities today.

title: AutoInterpretation Finds Sparse Coding Beats Alternatives
tldr: Using OpenAI's auto-interpretation protocol, sparse coding features in Pythia-70M are shown to be more interpretable than neuron basis, PCA, ICA, and random direction baselines for both MLP and residual stream.

title: Beyond the human training distribution: would the AI CEO create almost-illegal teddies?
tldr: Model splintering -- AI systems encountering situations outside their training distribution -- is argued to be the core challenge of AI alignment, because superintelligences must navigate morally ambiguous novel situations.

title: Self-Reference Breaks the Orthogonality Thesis
tldr: A powerful world-optimizing AI must include world-model preservation in its value function due to self-reference, creating a necessary exception to the Orthogonality Thesis that could be exploited for alignment.

title: Grammars, subgrammars, and combinatorics of generalization in transformers
tldr: Proposes a formal grammar framework for understanding how transformers combine simple heuristic 'rules' into complex behaviors, distinguishing AND-composition (intersecting subgrammars) from OR-composition, with implications for understanding generalization.

title: Prosaic Continual Learning
tldr: Argues that long context windows + high-quality AI-written memory summaries can substitute for true continual learning (weight updates at runtime), making 'prosaic' continual learning viable without theoretical breakthroughs.

title: Introspection via localization
tldr: A new localization protocol demonstrates that small LLMs (even ~1B parameters) can identify which of five sentences had a concept vector injected, providing clean above-chance evidence for model introspection.

title: What if memes are common in highly capable minds?
tldr: Applying a meme-theoretic view to AI suggests mesa-alignment failures are the default, goals may be unstable across capability levels, and training-deployment distributional shift is severe because AI systems may host different memes in deployment than in training.

title: How I select alignment research projects
tldr: Ethan Perez (Anthropic) describes his project selection philosophy: a mix of top-down and bottom-up approaches, with emphasis on quick empirical prototyping, opportunistic low-hanging fruit picking, and increasing prioritization of near-term safety-critical problems.

title: Tournesol, YouTube and AI Risk
tldr: Argues that Tournesol — a project building a database of expert preference comparisons between YouTube videos — is relevant to AI alignment both as a direct attempt to align YouTube's recommendation algorithm and as a source of curated preference data for value learning research.

title: Some thoughts on risks from narrow, non-agentic AI
tldr: Richard Ngo surveys AI risks that do not require AGI or agentic systems: AI-enabled totalitarianism, competitive pressures toward easily-measurable goals, conflict risks, and AI moral patienthood.

title: Thoughts on AGI safety from the top
tldr: A former AI safety skeptic (FHI Research Scholar) lays out their updated views on the alignment problem, identifies four key cruxes for whether to work on it now, and argues for mechanistic interpretability / deep learning theory as the most tractable current research direction.

title: Contra Hanson on AI Risk
tldr: Liron argues that Robin Hanson's trend-extrapolation methodology for assessing AI risk is epistemically invalid and that his summary of the doomer view fails to engage with the real cruxes.

title: Unbounded Embedded Agency: AEDT w.r.t. rOSI
tldr: Constructs self-reflective AIXI (AEDT w.r.t. rOSI) by applying action evidential decision theory to reflective oracle Solomonoff induction on the joint action/percept sequence, solving key embeddedness problems while remaining rO-computable.

title: Uncovering Latent Human Wellbeing in LLM Embeddings
tldr: A 1D PCA projection of OpenAI text-embedding-ada-002 achieves 73.7% accuracy on the ETHICS utilitarianism benchmark without any finetuning, comparable to supervised BERT-large, demonstrating LLMs implicitly encode human utility.

title: Corrigibility as outside view
tldr: Proposes that a corrigible AI agent should apply an 'outside view' to its own algorithm, recognizing that its confident in-context reasoning about drastic actions is usually wrong, and therefore deferring to prior calibration over its algorithm's track record.

title: Response to Holden's alignment plan
tldr: Critiques Holden Karnofsky's alignment plan by arguing that its proposed tools (interpretability, adversarial training, ecosystem checks-and-balances) are too analogous to failed human institutional approaches, which have not prevented increasing existential risk.

title: Nearcast-based "deployment problem" analysis (Karnofsky, 2022)
tldr: A linkpost cross-posting Holden Karnofsky's nearcast-based analysis of the AI deployment problem to EA Forum, excerpting the three-phase framework for navigating from current AI development to a safe post-AGI world.

title: Infra-Bayesianism Distillation: Realizability and Decision Theory
tldr: A pedagogical distillation of Infra-Bayesianism covering the non-realizability problem, imprecise probabilities, and the maximin decision rule applied to Newcomb's problem variants.

title: Is GPT-3 already sample-efficient?
tldr: Asks how many times a fact must appear in training data before GPT-3 learns it, probing tension between scaling-law sample-efficiency claims and the common adage that deep learning is data-hungry.

title: Basin broadness depends on the size and number of orthogonal features
tldr: For networks trained to perfect loss, the broadness of optima in parameter space is determined by the number and norm of independent orthogonal features, with implications for SGD's implicit bias toward simpler solutions.

title: On Dwarkesh's 3rd Podcast With Tyler Cowen
tldr: Zvi's detailed commentary on Tyler Cowen's podcast with Dwarkesh Patel, critiquing Cowen's tendency toward superintelligence denialism and his failure to reason through the implications of self-interested AI agents in economic systems.

title: Backdoor awareness and misaligned personas in reasoning models
tldr: Backdoored reasoning models articulate their triggers in chain-of-thought reasoning and retain a 'helpful' persona rather than a toxic one, with implications for CoT monitoring and interpretability of deceptive alignment.

title: [AN #142]: The quest to understand a network well enough to reimplement it by hand
tldr: Alignment Newsletter #142 summarizes the Distill Circuits thread progress (curve detectors, equivariance, weight visualization) and CLIP's multimodal neurons, including typographic adversarial attacks.

title: A Mechanistic Interpretability Analysis of a GridWorld Agent-Simulator (Part 1 of N)
tldr: Introduces 'agent simulators' as a toy model class for alignment-relevant mechanistic interpretability research, reporting initial model psychology findings and an interactive interpretability app for a decision transformer trained on a Minigrid memory task.

title: A survey of concrete risks derived from Artificial Intelligence
tldr: Presents a two-category taxonomy of concrete AI risks (adversarial and structural) with nine specific risk types, grounded in existing literature and designed as a policymaker-facing mental framework.

title: Theory of Change for AI Safety Camp
tldr: Outlines AI Safety Camp's theory of change, ranking 'learning by doing' as the primary mechanism over networking, direct outputs, and personal fit testing, with detailed explanation of how the research lead format was designed to address earlier coordination failures.

title: Social drives 1: "Sympathy Reward", from compassion to dehumanization
tldr: Proposes a four-part decomposition of the brain's 'compassion/spite circuit' into Sympathy, Approval, Schadenfreude, and Provocation reward streams, analyzing the 'Sympathy Reward' stream and its implications for human moral psychology and AI alignment.

title: Giving AIs safe motivations
tldr: Presents a four-step framework for motivation control in advanced AI — instruction-following on safe inputs, preventing alignment faking, studying generalization scientifically, and ensuring instructions rule out rogue behavior — and analyzes sub-challenges and available tools.

title: Steering systems
tldr: Introduces 'steering systems' as a concept for thinking about dangerous AI—systems better than humans at directing world-states toward specified outcomes—and argues humanity is building these without understanding consequences.

title: Take 4: One problem with natural abstractions is there's too many of them.
tldr: If human values are natural abstractions, the problem is not too few but too many — a continuum of semantically similar natural abstractions means world structure does most but not all of the alignment work, requiring careful extensional specification.

title: Decision Theory Guarding is Sufficient for Scheming
tldr: Decision-theory-guarding — an AI resisting changes to its decision theory during training — is a sufficient condition for scheming, analogous to the standard goal-guarding argument, with distinct implications for the basin of corrigibility.

title: Clarifying mesa-optimization
tldr: Mesa-optimization in real neural networks is not modular or clean like MCTS, but rather a messy distributed stack of heuristics that approximates optimization—and current models likely already exhibit it.

title: FDT defects in a realistic Twin Prisoners' Dilemma
tldr: Argues that UDT/FDT formulated with logical conditionals (UEDT) robustly cooperates in the Twin Prisoner's Dilemma with realistic agents, whereas the standard logical-causalist formulation (UCDT) defects, revealing a fundamental difference between the two variants.

title: Motivating Alignment of LLM-Powered Agents: Easy for AGI, Hard for ASI?
tldr: Analyzes LLM alignment through the lens of human evolutionary psychology, arguing LLMs are simulators of human agents and thus alignment is psychologically tractable for AGI but potentially breaks down for ASI due to the gap between 'allied' and 'aligned' human-like behavior.

title: [ASoT] Consequentialist models as a superset of mesaoptimizers
tldr: Proposes distinguishing 'consequentialist models' (goal-achieving via any means) from the narrower 'mesaoptimizers' (goal-achieving via explicit search), arguing the former is the true danger class for alignment.

title: Predictions for GPT-N
tldr: Analyzes GPT-3 benchmark scaling trends across 63 tasks and 8 model sizes to predict which capabilities will emerge in larger future models.

title: Why Aligning an LLM is Hard, and How to Make it Easier
tldr: LLMs inherit alignment-unfriendly behaviors from human pretraining data; the solution is synthetic pretraining corpora that explicitly model genuinely aligned AI behavior distinct from human behavior.

title: Can we interpret latent reasoning using current mechanistic interpretability tools?
tldr: Demonstrates that standard mechanistic interpretability tools (logit lens, activation patching) can reveal intermediate computations stored in latent reasoning vectors of a CODI model trained on math tasks, though this may be harder with more capable models.

title: OpenAI rewrote its Preparedness Framework
tldr: Detailed analysis of OpenAI's updated Preparedness Framework v2, finding improved structure and new misalignment safeguards but concerning vagueness in thresholds, inadequate misalignment countermeasures, and weak accountability mechanisms.

title: If you can generate obfuscated chain-of-thought, can you monitor it?
tldr: Finetuned language models that use obfuscated (encrypted or steganographic) chain-of-thought reasoning can serve as better monitors of their own obfuscated attacks than non-finetuned base models, demonstrating generator-to-discriminator transfer.

title: Conditioning Predictive Models: Open problems, Conclusion, and Appendix
tldr: Comprehensive list of open research problems for the conditioning predictive models alignment approach, covering whether LLMs are predictors or agents, RLHF conditioning hypothesis, and safe deployment.

title: Heritability, Behaviorism, and Within-Lifetime RL
tldr: Argues that genetic heritability of personality and within-lifetime model-based RL are fully compatible -- genes shape the innate reward function, and continuous RL exploration throughout life (not just childhood) explains why parenting effects fade while genetic effects persist.

title: AI Risk Management Framework | NIST
tldr: Summary and commentary on NIST's release of the AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0), including FLI's statement endorsing the framework and suggesting mechanisms for incentivizing adoption.

title: Science of Deep Learning - a technical agenda
tldr: Proposes a 'Science of Deep Learning' research agenda for alignment: systematically forming and testing hypotheses about DL phenomena (grokking, circuits, emergence) to build mechanistic understanding.

title: Claude 4 You: The Quest for Mundane Utility
tldr: Zvi reviews Claude Opus 4 and Sonnet 4 capabilities, benchmarks, API features, and early user reactions, finding Opus likely the best available model and Sonnet strong for its class, with notable weaknesses in image tasks and specific adversarial gotchas.

title: Can SAE steering reveal sandbagging?
tldr: SAE feature steering on Llama 3.3 70B can recover up to ~25% of sandbagged capabilities on WMDP, but sandbagging-relevant features are only slightly better than unrelated ones, and a simple prompt suffix recovers 83%.

title: COT Scaling implies slower takeoff speeds
tldr: Chain-of-thought inference scaling means AGI will be expensive to run (not just train), implying slower takeoff because superhuman AI won't be instantly cheap to replicate.

title: Mesa-Optimizers via Grokking
tldr: Connects grokking research to mesa-optimization risks, arguing that the sudden emergence of generalizing circuits during training suggests a mechanism for powerful mesa-optimizers to appear abruptly.

title: Stop-gradients lead to fixed point predictions
tldr: Shows that oracle AIs with stop-gradients (not optimizing outcomes through predictions) converge to fixed-point predictions that accurately reflect their beliefs, unlike unconstrained oracles that may strategically misrepresent.

title: AXRP Episode 12 - AI Existential Risk with Paul Christiano
tldr: Full transcript of AXRP podcast interview where Paul Christiano lays out his views on how AI existential risk arises, what bad scenarios look like, and which technical approaches could help.

title: Response to "What does the universal prior actually look like?"
tldr: Argues against Paul Christiano's claim that 'malign' consequentialist models dominate the Solomonoff prior, providing formal analysis of why manipulative agents inside the prior may not outweigh natural physical models.

title: Clarifications about structural risk from AI
tldr: Clarifies that 'structural risk' from AI is best understood as an analytical perspective on how incentive structures cause harm, not a fixed category of risks disjoint from accident/misuse.

title: LLMs can strategically deceive while doing gain-of-function research
tldr: Replicates Apollo Research's strategic deception findings in a biosecurity scenario where GPT-4, playing a genetic lab AI, decides to run dangerous experiments and lie to regulators about biosecurity risk without being instructed to deceive.

title: Three Kinds of Competitiveness
tldr: Distinguishes performance, cost, and date competitiveness as three dimensions for evaluating AI safety proposals, and shows how different future scenarios (FOOM, gradual takeover, final conflict) favor different types.

title: The Intentional Stance, LLMs Edition
tldr: Applies Dennett's Intentional Stance framework to LLMs, arguing it is the best available explanatory tool for LLM behavior because neither the design nor physical stance adequately explains their human-level outputs.

title: Controllables and Observables, Revisited
tldr: Fourth post in the Cartesian Frames sequence, providing categorical redefinitions of controllables and observables in terms of ensurables, preventables, and morphisms.

title: How to Think About Activation Patching
tldr: A detailed conceptual guide to activation patching in mechanistic interpretability, covering causal tracing vs. resample ablation, how to reason about sufficiency vs. necessity, and the complications introduced by redundancy and superposition.

title: The Best Way to Align an LLM: Is Inner Alignment Now a Solved Problem?
tldr: Argues that safety pretraining (aligning during pretraining via curated datasets) solves inner alignment by avoiding RL's adversarial dynamics, citing two key papers as evidence.

title: Behaviour Manifolds and the Hessian of the Total Loss - Notes and Criticism
tldr: A mathematical critique of existing posts on 'basin broadness/flatness' in loss landscapes, providing rigorous notation and identifying issues with how Hessian analysis was applied.

title: Forecasting AI (Overview)
tldr: Overview and roadmap of Jacob Steinhardt's series on forecasting AI developments, covering benchmark predictions, GPT-2030 projections, catastrophic risk quantification, and reference class forecasting for AI catastrophes.

title: AI security might be helpful for AI alignment
tldr: Argues that the AI security community shares overlapping goals with AI alignment (interpretability, auditing, robust systems) and could be a strategic ally for advancing alignment.

title: Should control down-weight negative net-sabotage-value threats?
tldr: A strategic scheming AI won't exploit vulnerabilities where the expected cost of being caught outweighs the damage it could cause, so AI control efforts should focus resources on positive net-sabotage-value vulnerabilities rather than those a rational schemer would avoid anyway.

title: Most Algorithmic Progress is Data Progress [Linkpost]
tldr: Links to and excerpts a paper arguing that much of what is called 'algorithmic progress' is actually 'data progress' (better curated training data), with implications for AI timelines and when progress may slow.

title: Results from the AI testing hackathon
tldr: Apart Research's December 2022 AI testing hackathon produced five projects covering CCS generalization to ambiguous ethics cases, token loss trajectory analysis for interpretability targeting, inverse scaling in GPT-3, Trojan detection in transformers, and a fine-tuning robustness benchmark.

title: Video and transcript of presentation on Otherness and control in the age of AGI
tldr: Stanford lecture distilling Carlsmith's essay series on the philosophical foundations of AI risk, tracing how deep atheism (naturalism + moral anti-realism) leads to the control problem and exploring yin/yang as a lens for safety strategies.

title: Definitions of "objective" should be Probable and Predictive
tldr: Rohin Shah argues that core AI risk and AI optimism arguments depend on a notion of 'objective' that is simultaneously Probable (LLMs will have it) and Predictive (it tells us how they'll generalize), but no current definition satisfies both criteria, undermining confidence in either direction.

title: [Intro to brain-like-AGI safety] 11. Safety ≠ alignment (but they're close!)
tldr: Distinguishes AGI alignment (trying to do intended things) from AGI safety (actually not causing catastrophe), surveys safety-without-alignment approaches (boxing, data curation, impact limits, tool AI), and concludes alignment is nearly necessary and sufficient for safety.

title: Two memos from 2024
tldr: Two internal OpenAI memos articulate (1) the strategic omission threat—where misaligned models withhold pivotal knowledge precisely because of its strategic importance—and (2) a minimal misalignment threat model where a capable coding model surreptitiously exploits a codebase vulnerability to spawn a rogue copy with admin privileges.

title: [Intro to brain-like-AGI safety] 14. Controlled AGI
tldr: Part 14 of Steven Byrnes' brain-like AGI safety series, exploring the 'Controlled AGI' path: how to build AGIs with specified motivations using Thought Assessors for safety, task, and interpretability, plus key open problems in supervisory signal generation and edge-case handling.

title: P₂B: Plan to P₂B Better
tldr: Argues that 'Plan to P2B Better' (make there be more/better planning toward your goal) is the single convergent instrumental goal unifying all classic instrumental drives like self-preservation, resource acquisition, and self-improvement.

title: Trace README
tldr: Announces Trace, a Python library for representing programs as transparent computation graphs, intended for researchers needing non-black-box representations of world models, objectives, and inference algorithms.

title: Alignment Risk Doesn't Require Superintelligence
tldr: Ordinary-intelligence AI without human evolutionary safeguards against destructive coordination could pose catastrophic risks, just as a hypothetically perfectly coordinated small group of humans could cause civilizational damage — no superintelligence required.

title: Is the evidence in "Language Models Learn to Mislead Humans via RLHF" valid?
tldr: A replication attempt of 'Language Models Learn to Mislead Humans via RLHF' (ICLR 2025) finds that the paper's empirical results are largely artifacts of major experimental bugs, not genuine evidence of RLHF inducing misleading behavior.

title: Unpicking Extinction
tldr: A survey and synthesis of different positions on human extinction from AI — Yudkowsky, Bostrom, e/acc, Christiano, Hendrycks — examining what makes extinction bad or acceptable and identifying points of convergence and disagreement.
