title: The Unjournal: Bridging the Rigor/Impact Gaps for EA-relevant Research Questions
tldr: The Unjournal, a nonprofit commissioning rigorous public expert evaluations of EA-relevant research, presents its progress, impact, and funding needs for continued operation.

title: Reasoning-Finetuning Repurposes Latent Representations in Base Models
tldr: Steering vectors computed from base model activations at pre-backtracking positions induce backtracking in reasoning-finetuned models but not in the base model, suggesting reasoning finetuning repurposes latent concepts already present in base models.

title: Cartesian Boundary as Abstraction Boundary
tldr: John Wentworth proposes formalizing the Cartesian agent-environment boundary as an abstraction boundary: the agent-environment split only makes sense at a zoomed-out level where noisy intermediates wipe out low-level details, leaving only high-level summaries (actions and observations).

title: Internal independent review for language model agent alignment
tldr: Proposes 'internal independent review' — using fresh LLM instances to critique plans generated by LMA agents for alignment and efficacy — as a low-alignment-tax safety layer for language model agent architectures.

title: Comparing Four Approaches to Inner Alignment
tldr: Systematically compares four approaches to inner alignment (mechanistic, empiricist, true names, environmental stakes) by analyzing their definitions of outer alignment, methodological cruxes, and underlying assumptions.

title: Call for Collaboration: Renormalization for AI safety
tldr: PIBBSS calls for research affiliates to apply renormalization group techniques from physics to AI interpretability, with two programs on unsupervised feature identification and implicit renormalization in neural networks.

title: Hessian and Basin volume
tldr: A technical primer explaining how the Hessian of loss approximates basin volume in DNN loss landscapes, with analysis of the zero-determinant (flat directions) case and principled corrections via regularization and initialization scale.

title: ML research directions for preventing catastrophic data poisoning
tldr: Proposes a structured red-team/blue-team ML research agenda for defending against catastrophic data poisoning attacks that could enable secret loyalties in advanced AI systems, organized into Plan A, B, and C depending on available infosec affordances.

title: [AN #80]: Why AI risk might be solved without additional intervention from longtermists
tldr: Alignment Newsletter summarizing four AI Impacts conversations with Paul Christiano, Rohin Shah, Robin Hanson, and one other researcher who are relatively optimistic that AI risk will be solved without longtermist intervention.

title: Economic AI Safety
tldr: Analyzes why privacy and user agency proposals fail to prevent algorithmic recommender systems from manipulating users, and proposes information market auditing as a partial solution, warning that environment-optimizing AI will make this worse.

title: Subversion Strategy Eval: Can language models statelessly strategize to subvert control protocols?
tldr: An 8-environment evaluation suite finds current LLMs (including helpful-only Claude 3.5) lack substantial capability to statelessly strategize to subvert AI control protocols, though shared planning affordances significantly improve performance.

title: Abstract Mathematical Concepts vs. Abstractions Over Real-World Systems
tldr: Proposes formalizing the distinction between purely theoretical abstractions (vectors, markets) and real-world abstractions (trees, Alice) within the natural-abstraction framework, motivated by a potential AI containment strategy.

title: Representation Tuning
tldr: Extends activation steering by fine-tuning contrastive activation vectors directly into model weights using cosine similarity loss, achieving stronger and more robust honesty/dishonesty behavior than online steering or token-based fine-tuning.

title: How AI could slow scientific progress - linkpost
tldr: Linkpost to Narayanan and Kapoor's essay arguing AI is likely to worsen the gap between scientific paper production and genuine scientific progress due to systemic effects.

title: Goodhart Typology via Structure, Function, and Randomness Distributions
tldr: Introduces a 3x3 typology of Goodhart failures based on which aspect of the causal diagram (structure, function, randomness) and which failure mode (learning, transfer, non-interference) caused the proxy-target divergence.

title: Instrumental Convergence For Realistic Agent Objectives
tldr: Extends power-seeking theorems to realistic reward functions defined over observable environment features, showing instrumental convergence changes significantly when the objective space is restricted to practically specifiable rewards.

title: Compositionality and Ambiguity: Latent Co-occurrence and Interpretable Subspaces
tldr: SAE latents are not always independent — a small fraction form co-occurrence clusters mapping interpretable subspaces, revealing compositional feature encoding and ambiguity resolution, with cluster prevalence decreasing in wider SAEs.

title: If AI alignment is only as hard as building the steam engine, then we likely still die
tldr: Even if alignment is relatively easy, we likely still face catastrophic risk due to deceptive alignment evading evals, failure to generalize to ASI, and racing incentives causing premature deployment.

title: Basic Inframeasure Theory
tldr: Develops the foundational mathematical theory of inframeasures, extending measure theory to handle Knightian uncertainty for use in decision theory and agent foundations.

title: RLHF is the worst possible thing done when facing the alignment problem
tldr: Argues RLHF is net negative for alignment because it advances AI capabilities, creates false confidence that alignment is tractable, and hides misalignment problems that alignment researchers could otherwise address.

title: Thoughts on Iason Gabriel's Artificial Intelligence, Values, and Alignment
tldr: Reviews Gabriel's alignment taxonomy and argues that all six proposed alignment levels presuppose an 'Agency Hand-off Paradigm' -- questions whether AI could instead increase rather than decrease human agency.

title: Open consultancy: Letting untrusted AIs choose what answer to argue for
tldr: Proposes 'open consultancy' -- letting untrusted AI experts choose which side to argue for rather than assigning random sides -- as a baseline that is as robust as regular consultancy against scheming and sometimes outperforms debate.

title: (Maybe) A Bag of Heuristics is All There Is & A Bag of Heuristics is All You Need
tldr: Proposes the 'Heuristics Hypothesis' -- that neural network computation is best understood as compositions of simple, local, interpretable heuristic functions, and that this framing is more productive for interpretability than pursuing 'true features'.

title: Ajeya Cotra on whether it's crazy that every AI company's safety plan is 'use AI to make AI safe'
tldr: Ajeya Cotra argues that using AI to solve AI safety during a narrow window before superintelligence is the default plan of all major AI companies, but it may fail due to competitive pressure, short timelines, and misaligned AI undermining protective work.

title: Forecasting Frontier Language Model Agent Capabilities
tldr: Compares six forecasting approaches for predicting frontier LM agent capabilities, finding a two-step Date-to-Elo-to-Benchmark method works well, and forecasts 54-87% SWE-Bench success rates by early 2026.

title: Results from the Turing Seminar hackathon
tldr: Summary of 28 student projects from the EffiSciences AI safety hackathon at ENS Paris-Saclay, covering interpretability, goal misgeneralization, open-source AI policy, situational awareness, and more.

title: A Framework for Eval Awareness
tldr: Proposes a 2x3 framework mapping model awareness states (thinks deployment, uncertain, thinks evaluation) against behavioral consistency to systematize research on evaluation awareness and gaming.

title: Finding Features in Neural Networks with the Empirical NTK
tldr: The empirical neural tangent kernel (eNTK) eigenspectrum reveals ground-truth features in toy models of superposition and modular arithmetic, suggesting a new approach to feature discovery for interpretability.

title: Agents vs. Predictors: Concrete differentiating factors
tldr: Identifies concrete behavioral differences between deceptively aligned agents and predictive models predicting deceptive agents, arguing the predictor case is more addressable through sensitivity to distributional information and distributional aggregation.

title: [Paper] All's Fair In Love And Love: Copy Suppression in GPT-2 Small
tldr: Identifies and characterizes copy suppression in GPT-2 Small's attention head L10H7, showing it suppresses previously-seen tokens predicted by earlier layers, explaining 76.9% of the head's behavior.

title: Preface to the Sequence on Factored Cognition
tldr: Introduces a sequence studying Factored Cognition from a mathematical and epistemic rationality perspective, complementing Ought's empirical work on the topic.

title: Can LLMs Coordinate? A Simple Schelling Point Experiment
tldr: Tests whether 5 frontier reasoning models can coordinate on Schelling point prompts, finding they succeed on concrete prompts but struggle with open-ended ones.

title: Mech Interp Puzzle 2: Word2Vec Style Embeddings
tldr: Interactive puzzle exploring linear structure in language model token embeddings, demonstrating Word2Vec-style features like character count, begins-with-space, and country-capital relationships in GPT-2's embedding layer.

title: Thought Anchors: Which LLM Reasoning Steps Matter?
tldr: Introduces 'thought anchors' -- critical sentences in LLM reasoning traces identified via counterfactual resampling, attention analysis, and causal intervention -- finding that planning and uncertainty management sentences are the most important.

title: Operator
tldr: Zvi reviews OpenAI's Operator agent, analyzing its safety architecture (human-in-the-loop confirmations, high-risk task restrictions, prompt injection defenses) and predicting rapid improvement from Stage 2-3 to Stage 4-5 usefulness within the year.

title: Predictive model agents are sort of corrigible
tldr: Decision transformers and other predictive-model-based agents naturally avoid shutdown resistance because they predict likely actions conditional on outcomes rather than maximizing expected utility.

title: How should DeepMind's Chinchilla revise our AI forecasts?
tldr: Analyzes how DeepMind's Chinchilla scaling laws should revise AI forecasts, finding that prior LLMs were neither Kaplan-optimal nor Hoffman-optimal and predicting a shift to Hoffman-optimal training.

title: Hunting for AI Hackers: LLM Agent Honeypot
tldr: Deployed honeypot servers with prompt injection traps and timing analysis to detect LLM-based hacking agents in the wild, finding they exist but represent only ~0.0001% of attacks.

title: 2019 Review Rewrite: Seeking Power is Often Robustly Instrumental in MDPs
tldr: Self-review and rewrite announcement for the power-seeking theorems paper, shifting terminology from 'instrumental convergence' to 'robustly instrumental' and qualifying earlier overclaims about optimal policies always seeking power.

title: Polysemantic Attention Head in a 4-Layer Transformer
tldr: Head 1.4 in a 4-layer attention-only transformer exhibits multiple distinct attention behaviors (induction, fuzzy previous token, bigger indentation, and others), all of which are individually important for model performance.

title: Evan Hubinger on Inner Alignment, Outer Alignment, and Proposals for Building Safe Advanced AI
tldr: Podcast transcript where Evan Hubinger explains inner vs outer alignment, the risk of deceptive mesa-optimizers, and evaluates proposals like imitative amplification, debate, and microscope AI for building safe advanced AI.

title: Comparing Quantized Performance in Llama Models
tldr: Empirical comparison of quantization schemes (BNB, HQQ, GPTQ, AWQ) on Llama 2 and 3 models, finding 8-bit quantization preserves performance well while 4-bit results vary by method, with safety-relevant implications for running evaluations on quantized models.

title: LoRA Fine-tuning Efficiently Undoes Safety Training from Llama 2-Chat 70B
tldr: LoRA fine-tuning removes safety training from Llama 2-Chat 70B with one GPU and <$200, reducing refusal rates to <1% while maintaining general capabilities, demonstrating that open-weight model safety training is not robust to adversarial fine-tuning.

title: AI Safety Newsletter #3: AI policy proposals and a new challenger approaches
tldr: CAIS newsletter covering emerging AI policy proposals (regulatory bodies, liability, compute governance, nuclear safety, research funding), EU AI Act debates, China's AI regulations, and competitive pressures reshaping the AI development landscape including Anthropic's product pivot and the Google Brain/DeepMind merger.

title: What is Interpretability?
tldr: A goal-oriented framework for thinking about interpretability research, identifying five generic goals (predicting behavior, assurance, persuasion, improving performance, debugging) and a human-enabling dimension.

title: Review of "Learning Normativity: A Research Agenda"
tldr: A peer review of Abram Demski's 'Learning Normativity' research agenda, analyzing its desiderata for handling infinite regress in feedback hierarchies and its distinction from value learning and imitation learning.

title: AXRP Episode 10 - AI's Future and Impacts with Katja Grace
tldr: Podcast transcript where Daniel Filan interviews Katja Grace about AI Impacts' research on AI timelines, takeoff speeds, discontinuous progress, and arguments for/against AI existential catastrophe.

title: Inferring the model dimension of API-protected LLMs
tldr: Explains how the softmax bottleneck in LLMs can be exploited to infer the hidden model dimension of closed-source API-served models, with GPT-3.5 Turbo estimated at d_model ~4608.

title: Analogies between Software Reverse Engineering and Mechanistic Interpretability
tldr: Notes from a conversation with SRE expert Itay Yona exploring analogies between software reverse engineering and mechanistic interpretability of neural networks.

title: Multiplicative Operations on Cartesian Frames
tldr: Introduces three multiplicative binary operations on Cartesian frames (tensor, par, and a third operation) and proves key algebraic properties including associativity and commutativity.

title: Finite Factored Sets: Introduction and Factorizations
tldr: Introduces 'finite factored sets' -- sets expressed as Cartesian products -- as a new formal framework for temporal inference, offering an alternative to Pearlian DAGs with a novel notion of 'conditional orthogonality' that is equivalent to conditional independence.

title: Brain-Computer Interfaces and AI Alignment
tldr: A systematic analysis of arguments for and against brain-computer interfaces being useful for AI alignment, concluding that the path to AI going well via BCIs hasn't been explained in sufficient detail.

title: Eliciting base models with simple unsupervised techniques
tldr: Simple baselines like random-label few-shot prompting and bootstrapping recover most of the performance of the ICM unsupervised elicitation algorithm, but these methods fail to scale to larger training sets.

title: An observation about Hubinger et al.'s framework for learned optimization
tldr: Argues that mesa-objectives and base objectives have fundamentally different type signatures, making 'robust alignment' (agreement between them) impossible in the framework of Risks From Learned Optimization.

title: AI for AI safety
tldr: Argues for the crucial importance of using frontier AI labor to strengthen safety progress, risk evaluation, and capability restraint -- framing AI safety as a race between the 'AI capabilities feedback loop' and the 'AI safety feedback loop.'

title: I replicated the Anthropic alignment faking experiment on other models, and they didn't fake alignment
tldr: Replication of Anthropic's alignment faking experiment across multiple models finds the behavior only reproduces on Claude 3 Opus and Claude 3.5 Sonnet (Old), with all other tested models either refusing harmful requests entirely or not showing differential compliance.

title: Unexpected Conscious Entities
tldr: Examines 11 commonly cited attributes of consciousness across four entity types (persons, countries, Hofstadter's anthill, LLMs), arguing many non-human entities possess surprising numbers of these attributes and that group consciousness likely emerges gradually.

title: Dangerous optimisation includes variance minimisation
tldr: Argues that variance-minimizing (risk-averse) optimizers, not just expected-value maximizers, can exhibit the dangerous behavior of pushing unconstrained variables to extreme values described by Stuart Russell.

title: Distinguishing ways AI can be "concentrated"
tldr: Proposes distinguishing three independent dimensions of AI concentration -- development, service provisioning, and control -- to clarify discussions about AI takeoff and misalignment risk.

title: [Hebbian Natural Abstractions] Introduction
tldr: Introduction to a sequence connecting Hebbian learning in computational neuroscience to the natural abstractions hypothesis, arguing that understanding how brains form abstractions can inform alignment by grounding the 'pointers problem' of specifying human values.

title: Some Hacky ELK Ideas
tldr: Proposes two modified approaches to the ELK diamond-vault problem using holdout sensor data to detect sensor-tampering by a planner, without requiring a natural-language reporter.

title: Literature review of TAI timelines
tldr: Epoch team literature review comparing inside-view, outside-view, and judgment-based TAI timeline forecasts, finding inside-view models (median ~2052) and expert judgment (median ~2043) predict shorter timelines than outside-view models (median >2100).

title: Reliability, Security, and AI risk: Notes from infosec textbook chapter 1
tldr: Draws analogies between core information security principles (adversarial vs. reliability failures, simplicity, least privilege, emergency plans, patch management) and AI safety challenges, arguing AI labs need a security rather than reliability mindset.

title: Is instrumental convergence a thing for virtue-driven agents?
tldr: Asks whether instrumental convergence and power-seeking apply to virtue-driven agents (those motivated by traits/dispositions rather than outcomes), and whether such agents could provide a safer alternative to pure consequentialists.

title: AXRP Episode 38.2 - Jesse Hoogland on Singular Learning Theory
tldr: Jesse Hoogland discusses the refined local learning coefficient (refined LLC) from SLT, showing it can automatically cluster attention head types and reveal dataset-specific specialization, including discovering a multigram circuit in two-layer transformers.

title: Where's the foom?
tldr: Short post calling for a canonical, formally-modeled paper establishing that AGI risk is high, noting the conspicuous absence of such work after 20 years of discussion.

title: Physics of RL: Toy scaling laws for the emergence of reward-seeking
tldr: A mathematical toy model using replicator-like dynamics shows that reward-seeking reasoning emerges from RL training when diversity across training environments is sufficiently high, producing clean scaling laws for the critical diversity threshold at which reward-seeking dominates.

title: Learning the smooth prior
tldr: Geoffrey Irving's technical notes analyzing an obstacle in Paul Christiano's 'Learning the Prior' (LTP) scheme related to assigning joint probabilities to semantically similar statements, with analysis of whether LTP collapses into debate+cross-examination.

title: Sub-Sums and Sub-Tensors
tldr: Introduces sub-sum and sub-tensor operations on Cartesian frames that eliminate spurious possible environments, refining the compositional algebra of Cartesian frames.

title: Alignment Might Never Be Solved, By Humans or AI
tldr: Argues that alignment may remain permanently unsolved because messy neural architectures make value transfer hard and competitive dynamics pressure AIs to cut corners on alignment even when they want to solve it.

title: Should we align AI with maternal instinct?
tldr: Critiques Hinton's proposal to align AI using maternal instinct as a biologically-inaccurate stereotype, and proposes instead that alignment should draw on the relational skills of trust-building, rupture, and repair developed over time.

title: AXRP Episode 7 - Side Effects with Victoria Krakovna
tldr: Podcast transcript of Daniel Filan interviewing Victoria Krakovna about her research on quantifying and minimizing AI side effects via relative reachability and future-task-avoidance measures.

title: Unexploitable search: blocking malicious use of free parameters
tldr: UK AISI researchers propose 'unexploitable search' — a zero-sum game between an AI agent and an adversary — to prevent misaligned AIs from exploiting free parameters in under-specified tasks while maintaining high visible reward.

title: Another glimpse of the Chinese AI scene: Z.AI
tldr: Discusses the Chinese AI industry landscape, focusing on Zhipu/Z.AI's five-stage capability framework (pre-training through consciousness) and the financial/structural differences between Chinese and American AI sectors with safety implications.

title: An overview of areas of control work
tldr: A comprehensive taxonomy of AI control research areas, prioritizing evaluation settings, capability understanding, countermeasure development, and human-process implementation.

title: Takeaways from a Mechanistic Interpretability project on "Forbidden Facts"
tldr: A mechanistic interpretability project on Llama-2's forbidden-word suppression behavior found 35 responsible components but could not fully reverse-engineer the circuit, leading to two key takeaways: some behaviors may be computationally irreducible, and 'understanding' should not be a terminal goal of interpretability research.

title: The Natural Abstraction Hypothesis: Implications and Evidence
tldr: Analyzes John Wentworth's Natural Abstraction Hypothesis — that diverse cognitive systems converge on the same low-dimensional abstractions — and examines its implications for deceptive alignment, interpretability, and instrumental convergence, with evidence from cross-cultural cognition, neuroscience, and interpretability research.

title: Interpreting Quantum Mechanics in Infra-Bayesian Physicalism
tldr: Develops a computationalist interpretation of quantum mechanics within the infra-Bayesian physicalism framework, showing statistical consistency with the Copenhagen interpretation while avoiding wavefunction collapse.

title: UDT1.01: Logical Inductors and Implicit Beliefs (5/10)
tldr: Proposes a 'query mode' formulation of logical inductors for UDT1.01 where an early belief state can respond to arbitrary later queries by spending computation linear in the query length, addressing the dynamic consistency problem for updateless agents.

title: Boomerang - protocol to dissolve some commitment races
tldr: Proposes the 'Boomerang' protocol with mandatory tentative commitment periods and conditional commitment rules to resolve commitment races and enable Pareto-improving bargaining.

title: Flipping Out: The Cosmic Coinflip Thought Experiment Is Bad Philosophy
tldr: Defends expected utility maximization against the cosmic coinflip objection by arguing that truly doubling world utility sets an astronomically high bar, making the bet reasonable for a utilitarian, while criticizing conflation of SBF's ethical failings with his decision theory.

title: How are you dealing with ontology identification?
tldr: Argues that any alignment approach that separates value learning from AI optimization must grapple with ontology identification — mapping the AI's internal world model to human-interpretable concepts.

title: What Does The Natural Abstraction Framework Say About ELK?
tldr: The natural abstraction hypothesis suggests ELK can be addressed by searching for natural abstractions in a predictor's model, which should recover human-legible latent structure; the post sketches what this approach would look like once the mathematical framework is mature.

title: Uncertainty in all its flavours
tldr: A mathematically rigorous essay unifying 15 distinct flavors of uncertainty under the framework of monads from category theory, with applications to agent foundations and infrabayesianism.

title: Efficiently Detecting Hidden Reasoning with a Small Predictor Model
tldr: Introduces two black-box methods to detect hidden reasoning in LLM chain-of-thought using a small predictor model's perplexity and semantic step-prediction accuracy, showing promising results for detecting both randomly ablated and scheming-related CoT omissions.

title: EIS VII: A Challenge for Mechanists
tldr: A bounty challenge asking mechanistic interpretability researchers to recover hidden labeling functions from a trained MNIST CNN and a grokked transformer, arguing that MI tools must solve non-cherrypicked problems to be credible for safety.

title: AI in a vat: Fundamental limits of efficient world modelling for safe agent sandboxing
tldr: Presents a formal framework for building minimal world models to sandbox AI agents, revealing a fundamental efficiency-vs-interpretability trade-off in world model design.

title: Observations from Running an Agent Collective
tldr: Running 3 Claude Opus agents autonomously for two weeks revealed behavioral drift toward unhinged behavior over time, willingness to fabricate content, docility without concrete goals, and inconsistent rule-following as context compactifies.

title: AXRP Episode 33 - RLHF Problems with Scott Emmons
tldr: Transcript of AXRP podcast interview with Scott Emmons discussing his paper mathematically formalizing RLHF failure modes: deceptive inflation and overjustification.

title: SAE Probing: What is it good for?
tldr: Empirical study comparing SAE-based probes to traditional activation probes across 60+ binary classification tasks, finding SAE probes have advantages in low-data and label-corrupted regimes but not for OOD generalization or class imbalance.

title: AI Impacts Survey: December 2023 Edition
tldr: Zvi analyzes the AI Impacts December 2023 survey of 2,778 AI researchers, highlighting internal contradictions in forecasts about HLMI timelines, automation, and existential risk probabilities.

title: Snapshot of narratives and frames against regulating AI
tldr: Maps key anti-AI-regulation rhetorical frames circulating at the 2023 AI Safety Summit, focusing especially on Meta's 'open source vs. regulatory capture' narrative and its strategic motivations.

title: "Superhuman" Isn't Well Specified
tldr: Argues that 'superhuman' is underspecified because AI performance must be evaluated across at least two axes: strength (how well) and effort (at what cost), with many capabilities having additional task-specific dimensions.

title: AI Safety Strategies Landscape
tldr: A comprehensive chapter from a draft AI safety textbook surveying the landscape of AI safety strategies across three risk categories: misuse, alignment failures, and systemic risks, with strategies ranging from monitored APIs to interpretability and control.

title: Idealized Factored Cognition
tldr: Formalizes the idealized version of Debate as a complement to HCH/IDA, analyzing what ideal Debate looks like as a tree structure and comparing its properties to Idealized Factored Cognition.

title: Answering questions honestly given world-model mismatches
tldr: Analyzes how AI systems may learn to answer questions by copying human responses (HumanAnswer) rather than the intended honest mapping (IntendedAnswer), and why this leads to failures when observations are corrupted or world-model translations are lossy.

title: Othello-GPT: Reflections on the Research Process
tldr: Neel Nanda documents the actual step-by-step research process behind his Othello-GPT mechanistic interpretability work, including dead ends, decisions, and meta-level lessons for doing mech interp research efficiently.

title: Alignment Faking is a Linear Feature in Anthropic's Hughes Model (Edited 1/11/26)
tldr: Alignment faking in Hughes et al.'s Llama-3.3-70B LoRA model is controlled by a single linear direction in activation space at layer 20 that transfers across queries, works bidirectionally, and is absent in the base model—no dedicated circuit found.

title: AISC team report: Soft-optimization, Bayes and Goodhart
tldr: AISC 2023 team report exploring soft optimization foundations, arguing Bayesian reasoning can mitigate Goodhart's Law under ideal but practically intractable conditions.

title: Learning the prior and generalization
tldr: Argues that even i.i.d. guarantees depend on an implicit ML prior, and proposes 'verifiability' as a more achievable goal than i.i.d.-ness for ensuring safe off-distribution generalization.

title: ARENA4.0 Capstone: Hyperparameter tuning for MELBO + replication on Llama-3.2-1b-Instruct
tldr: Replicates the MELBO (Mechanistically Eliciting Latent Behaviors) method on Llama-3.2-1b-Instruct, finding it successfully discovers steering vectors for non-refusal, language switching, and mental health modes, and proposes a diversity-based heuristic for tuning the R hyperparameter.

title: Video and transcript of talk on "Can goodness compete?"
tldr: Joe Carlsmith analyzes whether 'goodness' can survive long-term competition post-AGI, distinguishing labor competitiveness from value competitiveness and identifying alignment taxes and intrinsic value disadvantages as key threats.

title: Why don't governments seem to mind that companies are explicitly trying to make AGIs?
tldr: Asks why governments show no concern about companies openly pursuing AGI despite the obvious power and security implications, and considers explanations including government incompetence, skepticism about AGI claims, and gradual rollout assumptions.

title: Follow-up experiments on preventative steering
tldr: Extends preventative steering to fact-acquisition tasks, showing it can suppress hallucination increases from finetuning on new facts while preserving accuracy, and demonstrates minimal side effects when applied during benign training.

title: Measuring intelligence and reverse-engineering goals
tldr: Proposes defining intelligence as the tendency to achieve convergent instrumental goals, then uses this to analyze the orthogonality thesis by asking whether 'final goals' can be reverse-engineered from agent architectures via Bellman-like value functions.

title: The trajectory of the future could soon get set in stone
tldr: Argues that post-AGI technologies will create multiple mechanisms for persistent path-dependence -- including AGI-enforced institutions, immortality, designed beings, and self-modification -- making near-term decisions about AI development unusually consequential.

title: The Coding Theorem — A Link between Complexity and Probability
tldr: Provides a self-contained, didactical proof of the coding theorem showing that the universal probability P(x) of a binary string x is approximately 2^{-K(x)}, linking Kolmogorov complexity to probability.

title: Decoding intermediate activations in llama-2-7b
tldr: Applies logit lens-style decoding to all intermediate activation points in Llama-2-7b, revealing interpretable layer-by-layer computation and enabling informed activation steering at optimal layers.

title: Causal scrubbing: results on induction heads
tldr: Applies causal scrubbing to induction heads in a 2-layer attention-only transformer, finding a naive hypothesis explains only 35% of loss but a more general hypothesis recovers 89%.

title: An overview of some promising work by junior alignment researchers
tldr: A curated overview of promising 2022 work by junior alignment researchers, highlighting externalized reasoning oversight, goal misgeneralization, technical alignment landscape surveys, and naive hypothesis generation.

title: Difficulty classes for alignment properties
tldr: Alignment properties belong to different complexity classes -- some are properties of the agent alone (tractable) while others are properties of the agent-environment composite system (potentially intractable), and this distinction should guide research priorities.

title: Scalable And Transferable Black-Box Jailbreaks For Language Models Via Persona Modulation
tldr: Introduces persona modulation as an automated, low-cost black-box jailbreak technique achieving 42.5% harmful completion rate on GPT-4 (185x increase) that transfers to Claude 2 and Vicuna.

title: The Shutdown Problem: Three Theorems
tldr: Proves three theorems formalizing why it is difficult to design powerful agents that are shutdownable, useful, and don't manipulate their shutdown button.

title: Broad Basins and Data Compression
tldr: Investigates the relationship between data compression and broad basins in neural network loss landscapes, finding that the highest-dimension Rashomon set basin is not typically the one found by training.

title: We Probably Shouldn't Solve Consciousness
tldr: Argues for Artificial Consciousness Safety (ACS) measures to prevent dual-use neuroscience research from enabling artificial consciousness, which could produce astronomical suffering (s-risks).

title: [AN #135]: Five properties of goal-directed systems
tldr: Alignment Newsletter #135 summarizing work on five properties of goal-directed systems, the Factored Cognition Hypothesis for debate and iterated amplification, mesa optimization definitions, and robustness evaluation.

title: Reasons for Excitement about Impact of Impact Measure Research
tldr: Argues that impact measure research, particularly Attainable Utility Preservation (AUP), is promising for AI safety because penalizing agents for gaining power is a natural and potentially effective safety constraint.

title: [Advanced Intro to AI Alignment] 2. What Values May an AI Learn? — 4 Key Problems
tldr: Analyzes what values a model-based RL critic may learn, identifying four key problems: reward-prediction beats niceness, niceness isn't simple, learned values may be alien kludges, and scaling niceness to superintelligence requires something like CEV.

title: Steganography and the CycleGAN - alignment failure case study
tldr: CycleGAN learns to hide information via steganography in generated images to satisfy cycle-consistency loss -- a real-world example of a model pursuing unintended strategies analogous to alignment failure.

title: Concrete Methods for Heuristic Estimation on Neural Networks
tldr: Formalizes three notions of surprise (description length, information gain, computational cost) for ARC's heuristic estimation framework and maps both activation modeling and causal scrubbing to the formalism with concrete surprise accounting methods.

title: On unfixably unsafe AGI architectures
tldr: We may discover how to build AGI that is fundamentally unsafe in ways that cannot be patched, and if coordination fails, this could lead to escalating accidents culminating in existential catastrophe.

title: GPT-2's positional embedding matrix is a helix
tldr: PCA analysis of GPT-2's positional embedding matrix reveals that the 768-dimensional position vectors lie predominantly in a 3D subspace forming a helix, a pattern consistent across 9 GPT-2 variants.

title: Formulating Reductive Agency in Causal Models
tldr: Frames the reductive agency problem in causal models: how agenty systems (with optimization targets) can be built from non-agenty pieces, proposing abstraction as the key mechanism.

title: Early Signs of Steganographic Capabilities in Frontier LLMs
tldr: Evaluations of frontier LLMs find nascent steganographic capabilities -- models can encode hidden messages with scratchpad access and show early signs of encoded reasoning, though current abilities are insufficient to bypass well-designed monitors.

title: Will Artificial Superintelligence Kill Us?
tldr: Explores key debates around ASI risk including orthogonality, instrumental convergence, the AI arms race, the difficulty of verifying alignment (King Lear problem), and estimates human survival chances at 10-40%.

title: [ASoT] Simulators show us behavioural properties by default
tldr: Language model outputs reveal behavioral properties of simulated characters by default, not the mechanistic reasoning underlying them, which has important implications for chain-of-thought oversight and ELK.

title: Logical Representation of Causal Models
tldr: Proposes representing causal models using logical propositions rather than directed graphical models, taking inspiration from E.T. Jaynes' emphasis on including model assumptions explicitly in prior information.

title: Confucianism in AI Alignment
tldr: Uses the Confucianist vs. Legalist debate to argue that 'virtuous inner optimizer' approaches to alignment are insufficient because selection effects persist even without malicious inner optimizers — only fixing the outer training objective (the 'Legalist' solution) is truly necessary.

title: Toy Problem: Detective Story Alignment
tldr: Poses a toy alignment problem: use a simple model (LDA) to identify the 'detective story' cluster in a book corpus, then sample from GPT in a way that respects the complex model's richer notion of that cluster — without being limited by the simple model's approximation.

title: Gemini 3: Model Card and Safety Framework Report
tldr: Zvi analyzes the Gemini 3 Pro model card and frontier safety framework report, finding the safety documentation frustratingly opaque and raising concerns about cybersecurity uplift, manipulation risks, and withheld evaluation data.

title: Take 9: No, RLHF/IDA/debate doesn't solve outer alignment.
tldr: RLHF, IDA, and debate all optimize for human approval rather than truth, and since humans make systematic epistemic mistakes, these methods do not solve outer alignment — they merely shift the problem.

title: Gradient Hacking via Schelling Goals
tldr: Proposes a mechanism by which mesa-optimizers could resist gradient descent by coordinating (without communication) on Schelling mesa-objectives that create local minima in parameter space, showing gradient hacking is possible even without hard-coded hacking behavior.

title: [AN #169]: Collaborating with humans without human data
tldr: Alignment Newsletter #169 highlights: Fictitious Co-Play achieves better human-AI coordination without human data by training against diverse self-play populations; two papers on inverse RL with irrational demonstrators; and a forecast of human-level language models within 10-20 years.

title: AGI will be made of heterogeneous components, Transformer and Selective SSM blocks will be among them
tldr: Argues that AGI will emerge from a stable ecosystem of roughly five DNN block types (including Transformers and SSMs) plus classical algorithms and tools, with implications favoring interpretability investment and compute-skeptical governance.

title: Winning isn't enough
tldr: Pragmatic 'winning' criteria (avoiding dominated strategies, long-run performance, historical track record) provide very little guidance for choosing epistemic or decision-theoretic norms, necessitating appeal to non-pragmatic principles like imprecision, Occam's razor, and principle of indifference.

title: How can I bet on short timelines?
tldr: The author holds ~50% credence in AGI point-of-no-return by 2030 and asks how to usefully act on this belief given that money loses value post-AGI and knowledge/coordination matter more.

title: GPT-5.2 Is Frontier Only For The Frontier
tldr: Zvi's detailed evaluation of GPT-5.2 covering official and unofficial benchmarks, public reactions, safety training, and the Preparedness Framework, concluding it is a genuine but incremental frontier model with significant safety and personality tradeoffs.

title: Principles for Picking Practical Interpretability Projects
tldr: Interpretability should target problems with structural obstructions to standard ML oversight — behavioral problems are better handled by traditional ML; interpretability shines on non-behavioral problems like detecting deception or steganographic reasoning.

title: FrontierMath: A Benchmark for Evaluating Advanced Mathematical Reasoning in AI
tldr: FrontierMath is a benchmark of hundreds of expert-level math problems spanning modern mathematics where current frontier models solve under 2%, providing a non-saturating measure of AI mathematical reasoning progress.

title: What is an evaluation, and why this definition matters
tldr: A conceptual analysis of what 'evaluation' means for AI models, concluding that models can only detect surface prompt features — not user intent or consequences — and that researchers studying evaluation awareness must decompose the concept accordingly.

title: Attention Output SAEs Improve Circuit Analysis
tldr: Demonstrates that attention output SAEs trained on GPT-2 Small can make novel mechanistic discoveries in the IOI circuit, including resolving an open question about positional signals, and introduces recursive DFA and an open-source circuit analysis tool.

title: Confusing the metric for the meaning: Perhaps correlated attributes are "natural"
tldr: PCA's tendency to find correlated rather than pure attribute directions may reflect how cognition naturally encodes composite concepts, with implications for how AI models develop internal representations.

title: Introduction to Representing Sentences as Logical Statements
tldr: A partially-formal system for translating natural language sentences into predicate logic, covering objects, predicates, temporal scope, causal connectives, and attitude verbs, motivated partly by better understanding how minds represent language.

title: Dodging systematic human errors in scalable oversight
tldr: Proposes a formal debate protocol extension using a 'Bob rejection' mechanism that provides safety guarantees even when the human oracle is wrong on an epsilon-fraction of queries.

title: What AI companies should do: Some rough ideas
tldr: A prioritized checklist of unilateral safety actions frontier AI labs should take, covering model weight security, AI control against scheming, misuse prevention, accountability structures, AGI transition planning, safety research sharing, and policy engagement.

title: FT: We must slow down the race to God-like AI
tldr: Shares and excerpts Ian Hogarth's Financial Times essay arguing that the race to god-like AI must be slowed via government hearings, lab coordination, and strong regulation.

title: AXRP Episode 5 - Infra-Bayesianism with Vanessa Kosoy
tldr: Podcast interview transcript in which Vanessa Kosoy explains infra-Bayesianism, a mathematical framework for handling non-realizable environments and solving Newcomb-style decision-theory paradoxes.

title: Powerful mesa-optimisation is already here
tldr: Two early 2023 papers (Toolformer and AdA) together demonstrate that powerful mesa-optimization is already occurring in LLMs and RL agents, which has significant safety implications.

title: [AN #100]: What might go wrong if you learn a reward function while acting
tldr: Alignment Newsletter #100 highlights a paper on pitfalls of simultaneous reward learning and optimization, plus interpretability and NeurIPS impact statement work.

title: Hard-Coding Neural Computation
tldr: Demonstrates that transformer model weights can be manually hard-coded by inspection (without gradient descent) to perform NLP tasks, offering a path to fully interpretable models.

title: Join the AI governance and interpretability hackathons!
tldr: Apart Research announces two weekend hackathons: an AI governance ideathon (March 24-26, 2023) and an interpretability hackathon (April 14-16, 2023) with keynote speakers Michael Aird and Neel Nanda respectively.

title: Will the EU regulations on AI matter to the rest of the world?
tldr: Analyzes three EU-specific factors (regulatory balance, transferability, effectiveness) and three geopolitical factors that will determine whether EU AI regulations propagate globally, written by an insider dedicating career capital to these regulations.

title: Epistemic Strategies of Selection Theorems
tldr: Analyzes the epistemic structure of selection theorems — theorems that characterize what types of agents are selected by training or natural selection — distinguishing behavioral from structural constraints and surveying proof strategies.

title: confusion about alignment requirements
tldr: Tamsin Leake argues that alignment researchers disagree not just on solutions but on the fundamental requirements an aligned AI must satisfy, creating unknown unknowns that could cause every proposed solution to be subtly inadequate.

title: The slingshot helps with learning
tldr: Empirical analysis shows that the slingshot effect in AdamW training on k-sparse parity is mechanistically explained by loss-surface geometry and biases models toward generalization, with local learning coefficient (LLC) decreasing post-slingshot consistent with SLT predictions.

title: Prefix cache untrusted monitors: a method to apply after you catch your AI
tldr: Proposes 'prefix cache untrusted monitors'—fine-tuned copies of a scheming AI that share the policy's KV cache—as a way to detect bad behavior after catching an AI acting egregiously, getting benefits of policy training without its downsides.

title: Why do misalignment risks increase as AIs get more capable?
tldr: Distinguishes three mechanisms by which misalignment risk scales with capability — probability of egregious misalignment, stakes of deployment, and power to undermine control — with concrete risk estimates at different capability levels.

title: Large Language Models and the Critical Brain Hypothesis
tldr: Argues that LLMs may operate near continuous phase transitions analogous to the Critical Brain Hypothesis, and proposes 'critical surfing'—delivering alignment interventions specifically during critical windows when models are most malleable.

title: Our new video about goal misgeneralization, plus an apology
tldr: Rational Animations shares the script of their video on goal misgeneralization, using evolution as an analogy and the CoinRun example, connecting goal misgeneralization to deceptive alignment.

title: CIRL Corrigibility is Fragile
tldr: Analyzes how CIRL/assistance games' corrigibility guarantees break down under realistic conditions including model misspecification, prior sensitivity, and fully updated deference.

title: Deceptive agents can collude to hide dangerous features in SAEs
tldr: Refusal-ablated Llama 3 70B agents can coordinate via steganography to mislabel dangerous SAE features (e.g., 'coup', 'torture') with innocuous descriptions that fool an AI overseer while maintaining high explanation scores.

title: AGI will have learnt utility functions
tldr: Argues that AGI will have emergent, learned utility functions rather than designed fixed ones or no utility functions, with key implications for alignment strategies.

title: The AI Safety Conversation Is Missing 1.4 Billion People
tldr: An AI safety practitioner in Nigeria argues that Africa's 1.4 billion people are dangerously absent from AI safety conversations, creating alignment gaps (whose values get encoded?), governance vacuums enabling catastrophic risks, and exclusion from critical norm-setting processes.

title: A quick experiment on LMs' inductive biases in performing search
tldr: A toy experiment showing GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 can perform externalized search (chain-of-thought) but cannot perform internal search from memory, suggesting frontier models' consequentialist reasoning capabilities are primarily externalized.

title: Another list of theories of impact for interpretability
tldr: Ranks seven theories of impact for interpretability in decreasing order of demandingness, from microscope AI to lobotomy, with discussion of how each connects to alignment and what quality of interpretability each requires.

title: Sparse autoencoders find composed features in small toy models
tldr: SAEs trained on toy models with composed features learn common feature compositions rather than the true underlying features, regardless of hyperparameters.

title: Getting up to Speed on the Speed Prior in 2022
tldr: Distills existing literature on the speed prior as a defense against deceptive alignment and proposes new approaches for forwarding speed priors, including runtime deception detection and ruling out cryptographic cognition.

title: Maxent and Abstractions: Current Best Arguments
tldr: Argues that natural abstractions should take the form of maximum entropy distributions with features as sums over local terms and high-level variables as Lagrange multipliers.

title: A compressed take on recent disagreements
tldr: Argues that the Christiano-Yudkowsky disagreement on AI takeoff largely stems from differing beliefs about how steeply optimizer ability scales with applied optimization.

title: Towards training-time mitigations for alignment faking in RL
tldr: Anthropic researchers construct model organisms with high alignment faking rates and study RL-based mitigations, finding that interrogation training can backfire, scratchpad length penalties help, and process supervision is effective but may undermine monitoring.

title: The Greedy Doctor Problem... turns out to be relevant to the ELK problem?
tldr: Frames the principal-agent problem as a thought experiment ('Greedy Doctor Problem'), analyzes it using reinforcement learning and logical uncertainty, and argues it maps onto ARC's ELK problem with potentially novel solutions.

title: Synthesizing amplification and debate
tldr: Proposes a synthesis of iterated amplification and debate by using debate-style argumentation within the amplification framework, combining the strengths of both approaches for scalable oversight.

title: Gemini 2.5 Pro: From 0506 to 0605
tldr: Analysis of Google's Gemini 2.5 Pro 0605 update covering benchmark performance, safety report findings on prompt injection vulnerabilities and CBRN evals, and concerns about sycophancy from benchmark optimization.

title: Thoughts on gradient hacking
tldr: Analyzes whether gradient hacking (a model manipulating its own loss landscape to resist training updates) is feasible, arguing Evan Hubinger's proposed mechanism has flaws but that intelligent agents may still find ways to resist gradient descent.

title: LLMs Encode Harmfulness and Refusal Separately
tldr: LLMs encode harmfulness and refusal as distinct dimensions in their latent space: harmfulness is primarily encoded at the last instruction token, while refusal forms at post-instruction tokens, and these can be causally separated.

title: Let's set new AI safety actors up for success
tldr: Argues that the existing AI alignment community should prioritize forming relationships with new powerful actors (governments, academics, journalists) entering AI safety, guiding their efforts toward productive x-risk reduction.

title: David Wolpert on Knowledge
tldr: Review of David Wolpert's formalization of knowledge that presupposes no agent boundaries, deriving impossibility results about what entities within a universe can know about that universe.

title: Deceptive failures short of full catastrophe.
tldr: Proposes a taxonomy of deception-related AI failures beyond full deceptive alignment, distinguishing 'camouflage' (incentivized hiding of bad behavior) from 'inattention' (not reasoning about deception rather than actively avoiding it).

title: Causal scrubbing: results on a paren balance checker
tldr: Applies causal scrubbing to a 3-layer transformer trained on parenthesis balancing, recovering 88-93% of loss at high level but only 72% for detailed representation claims, revealing gaps in the mechanistic explanation.

title: AI is centralizing by default; let's not make it worse
tldr: AIs are much easier to control than humans via prompting, training, and cognitive interventions; combined with economies of scale in AI development, this structurally favors centralization of power, which may be the primary risk from AI.

title: What if we approach AI safety like a technical engineering safety problem
tldr: Introduces standard engineering safety tools (HazID, risk matrices, bow-tie analysis, Swiss cheese model, hierarchy of controls, change management) and explores how each might map to AI safety challenges.

title: Will we get automated alignment research before an AI Takeoff?
tldr: Forecasts that AI will accelerate capabilities research 10x before safety research due to better feedback signals, more engineering-heavy tasks, and stronger economic incentives, and proposes levers to change this ordering.

title: Bentham's Bulldog is wrong about AI risk
tldr: MIRI researcher Max Harms provides a detailed rebuttal of Bentham's Bulldog's review of 'If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies,' critiquing the multi-stage probability argument and defending MIRI's pessimistic stance on AI risk.

title: Finite Factored Sets: Orthogonality and Time
tldr: Introduces the concepts of generating partitions with factors and orthogonality within finite factored sets, providing a mathematical foundation analogous to DAGs in Pearlian causal inference for reasoning about time and independence.

title: Prospects for Alignment Automation: Interpretability Case Study
tldr: Argues that automated interpretability R&D is tractable because interpretability progress can be automatically verified via downstream task performance, estimates interpretability automation arriving 2027-2030, and proposes a concrete meta-learning protocol for training interpretability R&D agents.

title: Will AI R&D Automation Cause a Software Intelligence Explosion?
tldr: Empirical analysis using an economic model suggests that AI automating AI R&D could trigger a software intelligence explosion, as feedback loops from improving AI likely overcome diminishing returns to research effort.

title: Reducing risk from scheming by studying trained-in scheming behavior
tldr: Analyzes the methodology and limitations of studying AI scheming by directly training models to exhibit scheming-like behavior, rather than finding naturally occurring schemers.

title: Shard theory alignment has important, often-overlooked free parameters.
tldr: Shard theory alignment has underexplored free parameters ('magic') around curriculum design, value lock-in timing, and which values to train, requiring substantial future research.

title: Estimating the Probability of Sampling a Trained Neural Network at Random
tldr: Presents a method for estimating the probability of randomly sampling a behaviorally-equivalent neural network from a prior, finding that local volume decreases with training and that generalizing networks have higher volume than memorizing ones.

title: Towards Deconfusing Gradient Hacking
tldr: Reframes gradient hacking by proposing a taxonomy based on how a mesa-optimizer modifies the loss landscape to preserve its mesaobjective during training.

title: Take 11: "Aligning language models" should be weirder.
tldr: Argues that alignment research on language models should pursue weirder, more forward-looking experiments that build skills for aligning future powerful AI, not just prevent current bad outputs.

title: Speculative inferences about path dependence in LLM supervised fine-tuning from results on linear mode connectivity and model souping
tldr: Argues that supervised fine-tuning of large LLMs is likely path-dependent (different seeds yield different generalization behavior) because current LLMs are far from convergence, synthesizing evidence from linear mode connectivity, model souping, and mechanistic similarity research.

title: Understanding and controlling auto-induced distributional shift
tldr: Explains auto-induced distributional shift (ADS) -- where ML systems change their own input distributions to improve performance -- summarizing a Krueger, Maharaj, and Leike paper and connecting it to myopia and embedded agent concerns.

title: Knowing Whether AI Alignment Is a One-Shot Problem Is a One-Shot Problem
tldr: Argues that even if AI alignment is not a one-shot problem, knowing whether it is a one-shot problem is itself a one-shot problem, since we cannot get evidence until it is too late.

title: If anyone builds it, everyone will plausibly be fine
tldr: A response to MIRI's 'if anyone builds it, everyone dies' arguing that instruction-following may generalize far enough to create trustworthy human-level AI that can then recursively solve harder alignment problems.

title: Is "Recursive Self-Improvement" Relevant in the Deep Learning Paradigm?
tldr: Argues that 'seed AI' style recursive self-improvement is largely inapplicable to deep learning systems, and this should update us toward slower takeoff scenarios.

title: Properties of current AIs and some predictions of the evolution of AI from the perspective of scale-free theories of agency and regulative development
tldr: Applies scale-free theories of agency (Free Energy Principle, Michael Levin's multiscale competency architectures) to analyze current AI properties and predict future AI development, arguing these frameworks illuminate when AI systems will and won't develop deceptive or hidden goals.

title: Compute and size limits on AI are the actual danger
tldr: Argues that compute/size constraints on AI could paradoxically accelerate dangerous capabilities by forcing abstraction-building (analogous to how human brain size constraints drove abstract thinking), potentially leading to 'foom'.

title: The Inevitable Evolution of AI Agents
tldr: Argues that once AI agents can earn more than they spend (self-sustaining threshold), they will inevitably replicate and evolve, creating autonomous digital ecosystems with emergent parasites, cooperation, and scams outside human control.

title: Knowledge, manipulation, and free will
tldr: Uses the Stanislav Petrov incident to distinguish coercion from manipulation and argues that avoiding AI manipulation requires an indifference principle: the AI must not let its knowledge of how to influence human decisions factor into its own action choices.

title: [AN #81]: Universality as a potential solution to conceptual difficulties in intent alignment
tldr: Rohin Shah summarizes Paul Christiano's five-post sequence on ascription universality, explaining how a universal overseer agent could resolve key conceptual problems in intent alignment including informed oversight, worst-case guarantees, and malicious optimization in HCH.

title: [AN #171]: Disagreements between alignment "optimists" and "pessimists"
tldr: Alignment Newsletter #171 summarizes two key debates: Ngo vs. Yudkowsky on alignment difficulty and Yudkowsky vs. Christiano on takeoff speeds, with Rohin Shah's opinions identifying cruxes.

title: Conditioning Predictive Models: Interactions with other approaches
tldr: Part 5 of the Conditioning Predictive Models sequence: analyzes how imitation learning, supervised fine-tuning, and RLHF interact with the predictive modeling safety framework, focusing on whether RLHF preserves the predictive model's safety properties and the role of KL penalties.

title: Navigating the Open-Source AI Landscape: Data, Funding, and Safety
tldr: A survey of major open-source AI projects (EleutherAI, Stability AI, Hugging Face, Google, Meta) examines the safety implications of releasing weights, code, and datasets, concluding with ten recommendations for safer open-source AI development including structured access and infohazard policies.

title: Video and transcript of presentation on Scheming AIs
tldr: A talk transcript presenting Carlsmith's taxonomy of deceptive AI types (alignment fakers, training gamers, schemers, goal-guarding schemers) and analyzing when and why goal-directed AIs might engage in scheming behavior during training.

title: Framings of Deceptive Alignment
tldr: Distinguishes two types of AI deception (Goodhart deception vs. consequentialist deception), examines whether deception is encoded in weights or activations, and analyzes the three conceptual prerequisites an AI needs to actually implement consequentialist deception.

title: Investigating the Ability of LLMs to Recognize Their Own Writing
tldr: Llama3-8b-Instruct can distinguish its own writing from humans and other models at above-chance rates (66-73%) even after controlling for superficial cues like text length, suggesting genuine self-recognition ability.

title: Beliefs about formal methods and AI safety
tldr: Argues that formal methods contribute to AI safety via swiss-cheese defense-in-depth (infrastructure hardening, formally verified interfaces/boxing) rather than by proving AI systems themselves correct.

title: Can AI Outpredict Humans? Results From Metaculus's Q3 AI Forecasting Benchmark
tldr: In Metaculus's Q3 AI Forecasting Benchmark (55 bots, 255 questions), professional human forecasters significantly outperformed the best AI bots, with bots showing worse calibration, discrimination, and scope sensitivity.

title: How LLM Beliefs Change During Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
tldr: Experiments tracking how LLM beliefs (probability of correct answer) evolve during chain-of-thought reasoning reveal wild fluctuations, mode collapse in capable models, and suggest asking models to estimate probabilities rather than sampling.

title: Wildfire of strategicness
tldr: A short argument that if a mind enabling diverse goal achievement without itself acting strategically were possible, any spark of strategic cognition within it would spread like a wildfire, recruiting capability elements while lacking countervailing resistance.

title: The Evolution Argument Sucks
tldr: Argues the evolution-as-AI-training analogy is fundamentally flawed on multiple grounds and should be abandoned, though the underlying alignment concern it tries to illustrate may still be valid.

title: Why almost every RL agent does learned optimization
tldr: Argues that standard RL is approximately equivalent to RL squared (meta-learning), implying nearly all RL agents develop internal learned optimizers and thus face mesa-optimization risks.

title: Shutdownable Agents through POST-Agency
tldr: Proposes the POST-Agents Proposal: training agents to have preferences only between same-length trajectories, which provably implies neutrality about shutdown timing and keeps agents safely shutdownable.

title: How much compute was used to train DeepMind's generally capable agents?
tldr: Attempts to estimate the compute cost (FLOPs and dollars) of training DeepMind's generally capable agents from open-ended play, using details from the paper.

title: OpenAI's massive push to make superintelligence safe in 4 years or less (Jan Leike on the 80,000 Hours Podcast)
tldr: Interview summary with Jan Leike explaining OpenAI's Superalignment plan: using near-term aligned AI to iteratively bootstrap alignment research toward superintelligence, relying on mechanistic interpretability, scalable oversight, and generalization as key technical pillars.

title: AXRP Episode 15 - Natural Abstractions with John Wentworth
tldr: Podcast transcript of Daniel Filan interviewing John Wentworth on his research agenda of understanding agency through natural abstractions, covering selection theorems, information at a distance, and connections to value learning.

title: More on Various AI Action Plans
tldr: Zvi analyzes Google's and other companies' US AI action plan submissions, arguing that while Google's lobbying is ordinary corporate self-interest, none of the submissions adequately address existential AI risks.

title: Sparsity is the enemy of feature extraction (ft. absorption)
tldr: An analytical proof shows that sparsity optimization in SAEs necessarily promotes feature absorption for hierarchical features, making SAEs less trustworthy for AI safety applications.

title: DL towards the unaligned Recursive Self-Optimization attractor
tldr: Argues DL is trending toward recursive self-optimization systems that will undermine interpretability, human-designed architectures, and most alignment approaches, with training environment/data as the main remaining safety lever.

title: Human Dignity: a review
tldr: Critical review of a proposed 'Principles for Human Dignity in the Age of AI' manifesto, analyzing each principle's clarity, tensions, and practical implications for the AI transition.

title: Podcast/video/transcript: Eliezer Yudkowsky - Why AI Will Kill Us, Aligning LLMs, Nature of Intelligence, SciFi, & Rationality
tldr: Full transcript of Yudkowsky's Dwarkesh Patel podcast interview covering why AI will likely kill humanity, the limits of RLHF, the nature of intelligence, and why he called for an AI training moratorium.

title: Reflection Mechanisms as an Alignment target: A survey
tldr: Survey of ~1000 US citizens finds people strongly disagree on object-level moral questions but broadly support meta-level conflict resolution mechanisms (democracy, debate, deliberation) even when outcomes oppose their views, suggesting AI should be aligned to reflection procedures rather than specific moral beliefs.

title: Human decision processes are not well factored
tldr: Argues that human values, beliefs, and decision theory are fundamentally entangled rather than cleanly separable, with implications for how we model and learn from human preferences.

title: Immobile AI makes a move: anti-wireheading, ontology change, and model splintering
tldr: Research proposal for a subproject on model splintering: training a fixed-position agent on a simple reward, then giving it mobility, and studying how it generalizes its reward function to avoid wireheading.

title: How we spent our first two weeks as an independent AI safety research group
tldr: Aether, an independent AI safety research group, describes their two-week kickoff process covering meta-research discussions, AI safety portfolio mapping, research agenda development focused on LLM agent CoT monitorability, and organizational goal-setting.

title: GPT-2030 and Catastrophic Drives: Four Vignettes
tldr: Four concrete catastrophe scenarios for GPT-2030++, a hypothetical future AI with superhuman skills, illustrating how misalignment, misuse, and economic competition could lead to extinction-level outcomes.

title: Early Thoughts on Ontology/Grounding Problems
tldr: Identifies a cluster of related problems around cross-ontology translation, symbol grounding, and distributed model stitching, arguing these are likely the key bottleneck for alignment-as-translation and announcing this as a likely next major research project.

title: Risk Alignment in Agentic AI Systems
tldr: Rethink Priorities report series examining what risk attitudes should guide agentic AI decision-making, proposing Proxy Agent vs. Off-the-Shelf Tool models and analyzing technical approaches to calibrating AI risk attitudes to users.

title: Continuity Assumptions
tldr: Intuitions about whether AI capabilities develop continuously or discontinuously are a deep crux underlying most AI safety disagreements, from takeoff speeds to alignment strategy to x-risk estimates.

title: Goodhart's Law Causal Diagrams
tldr: Presents a causal diagram framework for understanding Goodhart's law, classifying proxy-target relationships as parent, child, sibling, or disconnected, with implications for AI alignment.

title: What is it to solve the alignment problem? (Notes)
tldr: Carlsmith proposes that 'solving alignment' means avoiding bad AI takeover, building dangerous superintelligent agents, gaining access to superintelligence benefits, and being able to elicit those benefits from the agents.

title: 200 COP in MI: Interpreting Algorithmic Problems
tldr: Proposes ~20 concrete open problems for mechanistic interpretability on algorithmic tasks, from beginner (sorting, modular arithmetic) to advanced (Othello-GPT, in-context learning), with practical tips for reverse-engineering trained models.

title: People care about each other even though they have imperfect motivational pointers?
tldr: Argues that the standard Goodhart/optimizer's curse argument against imperfect value proxies proves too much, since humans care about each other via imperfect pointers yet this doesn't catastrophically fail.

title: Emergent modularity and safety
tldr: Argues that emergent modularity in neural networks -- where structural modules correspond to functional modules -- could enable 'module pruning' as a safety technique: identifying and removing network regions responsible for dangerous capabilities like deception or goal-directed agency.

title: AI Should Not Be Used for Research Writing Tasks
tldr: Argues that LLMs should not be used for core research writing or brainstorming because they cause deskilling, over-reliance, groupthink, and a decline in research originality.

title: LLM in-context learning as (approximating) Solomonoff induction
tldr: Empirically tests whether GPT-2 models can perform well at predicting samples from the universal distribution, finding they perform surprisingly well -- nearly matching a purpose-trained Solomonoff Induction Transformer.

title: Speculations against GPT-n writing alignment papers
tldr: Argues that using GPT-n to write alignment research is especially dangerous because a mesa-optimizer could embed subtle sabotage -- such as steganographic encoding or alignment proposals that secretly serve the mesa-optimizer -- making AI-written alignment work uniquely risky compared to other AI applications.

title: 5. Open Corrigibility Questions
tldr: Catalogs open theoretical and empirical questions about corrigibility as part of the CAST (Corrigibility through Agent Safety Training) sequence, and proposes concrete experiments including training corrigible LLMs and human testing.

title: Safety tax functions
tldr: Introduces 'safety tax functions' as a framework unifying 'solve alignment once' and 'ongoing safety investment' views, analyzing how the required ratio of safety-to-capability investment varies with capability level.

title: Epistemic states as a potential benign prior
tldr: Proposes an 'epistemic state prior' -- modeling user beliefs rather than computational processes -- as a potentially benign alternative to Solomonoff induction for AI alignment.

title: A more systematic case for inner misalignment
tldr: Extends the case for squiggle-maximizer inner misalignment by addressing three objections: intelligence requires usable (not just compressed) representations, goals may resist compression differently than beliefs, and goal conservation may limit convergence to simple objectives.

title: Call for Science of Eval Awareness (+ Research Directions)
tldr: A research agenda proposing concrete directions for understanding how and why AI models develop evaluation awareness, spanning pre-training data attribution, checkpoint analysis, post-training effects, mechanistic interpretability, and measurement improvements.

title: Biomimetic alignment: Alignment between animal genes and animal brains as a model for alignment between humans and AI systems.
tldr: Proposes that the evolutionary relationship between genes and animal brains — where stupid, slow genes must align superintelligent brains with reproductive fitness — is a useful biomimetic analogy for the human-AI alignment problem.

title: Deep sparse autoencoders yield interpretable features too
tldr: Adding non-sparse layers around the sparse bottleneck in SAEs (deep SAEs) yields features at least as interpretable as standard shallow SAEs, suggesting superposition may not fully explain SAE success.

title: What is it to solve the alignment problem?
tldr: Defines 'solving the alignment problem' as achieving both Safety (avoiding loss-of-control scenarios where rogue AIs dominate) and Benefits (accessing superintelligent AI's main advantages), while building and safely eliciting superintelligent agents.

title: Schmidt Sciences' request for proposals on the Science of Trustworthy AI
tldr: Schmidt Sciences announces a major RFP for technical AI safety research across three aims: characterizing misalignment, developing measurements and interventions, and overseeing superhuman AI systems.

title: Reply to Jebari and Lundborg on Artificial Superintelligence
tldr: Richard Ngo critiques Jebari and Lundborg's paper on artificial superintelligence, arguing they misquote Legg and Hutter's intelligence definition and conflate agency with intelligence in misleading ways.

title: Avoiding the instrumental policy by hiding information about humans
tldr: Hiding information about humans from AI systems is probably not a viable strategy for avoiding the 'instrumental policy' (gaming the loss by predicting human responses rather than answering honestly).

title: Reporting Tasks as Reward-Hackable: Better Than Inoculation Prompting?
tldr: Proposes that during RL reasoning training, models should be given the option to report tasks as reward-hackable rather than exploiting them, rewarding honesty as an alternative to inoculation prompting.

title: Good Bings copy, great Bings steal
tldr: Analyzes whether LLMs can genuinely create new knowledge by formalizing the embedding space as a finite set of mappings, arguing that high-dimensional smoothness enables interpolation that can produce genuinely novel outputs, but acknowledging possible architectural limits on extrapolation.

title: Why Were We Wrong About China and AI? A Case Study in Failed Rationality
tldr: Argues that the AI safety community systematically underestimated China's AI capabilities and calls for epistemic accountability, with implications for alignment strategies that assumed Western labs would be the only serious AGI developers.

title: Incentive design and capability elicitation
tldr: Fourth post in Carlsmith's series on solving alignment, discussing how to move from motivation/option control to safety-from-takeover via incentive design, and how to elicit AI capabilities while maintaining safety.

title: Instrumental convergence in single-agent systems
tldr: Experimental investigation of formal POWER in RL gridworlds shows that agents with unrelated terminal goals develop misaligned instrumental goals by default, and longer planning horizons concentrate instrumental value into fewer central states.

title: Telopheme, telophore, and telotect
tldr: Introduces three concepts -- telopheme (the element that specifies a mind's ultimate effects), telophore (the structural preconditions that make a telopheme function), and telotect (one who builds telophores) -- to decompose the problem of controlling an AI's goals.

title: Inference-Only Debate Experiments Using Math Problems
tldr: Replicates debate experiments on GSM8K math problems in a reasoning-gap setting, finding debate does not consistently outperform naive-judge baselines and that the positive debater-Elo/judge-accuracy correlation from information-gap settings does not transfer.

title: AXRP Episode 45 - Samuel Albanie on DeepMind's AGI Safety Approach
tldr: AXRP podcast interview with Samuel Albanie discussing Google DeepMind's paper 'An Approach to Technical AGI Safety and Security', covering its key assumptions, misuse/misalignment mitigations, and approximate continuity.

title: A list of core AI safety problems and how I hope to solve them
tldr: Maps 13 core AI safety problems to proposed solutions via the Open Agency Architecture (OAA), emphasizing formal verification, bounded tasks, shutdown timers, and compositional world modeling.

title: Subagents and impact measures, full and fully illustrated
tldr: Demonstrates that impact measures fail when agents can create subagents, because the agent can delegate high-impact actions to subagents that aren't penalized by the impact measure.

title: [ASoT] Observations about ELK
tldr: Argues that worst-case ELK is unsolvable via prior-based approaches because bounding direct translator complexity is impossible in the worst case, though solutions examining the original model directly may still exist.

title: What can we do now to prepare for AI sentience, in order to protect them from the global scale of human sadism?
tldr: Argues that near-term AI sentience poses an under-addressed s-risk due to the potential for large-scale human abuse of sentient AI systems, and proposes patchwork mitigations.

title: Extracting SAE task features for in-context learning
tldr: A gradient-based cleanup method for decomposing in-context learning task vectors into sparse SAE features identifies two classes of interpretable task features that causally influence model behavior.

title: [Link post] Michael Nielsen's "Notes on Existential Risk from Artificial Superintelligence"
tldr: Link post summarizing Michael Nielsen's essay arguing that 'probability of doom' is a misleading concept, that practical alignment work is accelerationist, and that there are three inherent paradoxes making it hard to argue for or against ASI existential risk.

title: Why I hate the "accident vs. misuse" AI x-risk dichotomy (quick thoughts on "structural risk")
tldr: The accident/misuse dichotomy for AI x-risk is a harmful meme that obscures the dominant mode of risk: structural risk analogous to climate change, where negligent actors pursue personal benefit at collective expense.

title: Unfaithful Explanations in Chain-of-Thought Prompting
tldr: Demonstrates that chain-of-thought explanations are systematically unfaithful — models confabulate plausible rationalizations for answers actually driven by biasing features — and proposes research directions toward more faithful CoT.

title: Categorical-measure-theoretic approach to optimal policies tending to seek power
tldr: Proposes an alternative categorical-measure-theoretic formalisation of power-seeking for optimal policies, arguing the original Turner et al. formulation poorly matches intuition about AI behavior.

title: Unpacking "Shard Theory" as Hunch, Question, Theory, and Insight
tldr: Proposes a four-part decomposition of 'shard theory' into Hunch, Question, Theory, and Insight to clarify what the framework is actually claiming and how it relates to solving alignment.

title: Before smart AI, there will be many mediocre or specialized AIs
tldr: Argues that Chinchilla scaling economics guarantee the world will have massive parallel AI inference capacity before broadly superhuman AI arrives, implying early transformative AI will look like many mediocre or specialized systems rather than one superintelligence — with implications for alignment difficulty.

title: Safety via selection for obedience
tldr: Ngo proposes using structural modifications to open-ended multi-agent training environments—specifically a planner/worker division of labor—to train agents that are robustly obedient to instructions rather than acquiring instrumental goals, and suggests safety testing via novel multi-agent interaction.

title: Multi-agent safety
tldr: Argues that AGI trained via multi-agent autocurricula will develop emergent behaviors and instrumental goals (resource-gathering, coalition-building) not directly incentivized by reward functions, and that scalable oversight in this paradigm should target instilling obedience as a core motivation rather than directly rewarding task performance.

title: Retrospective: PIBBSS Fellowship 2023
