tldr: PIBBSS's 2023 summer fellowship paired 18 PhDs from biology/neuroscience/social science with AI alignment mentors, yielding strong satisfaction ratings, promising interdisciplinary research outputs, and lessons about mentorship bottlenecks and in-person collaboration value.

title: Stress Externalities More in AI Safety Pitches
tldr: Argues that AI safety advocacy should more prominently use an externalities framing - AI developers don't bear the costs of misaligned AGI, creating a market failure - because this resonates across political orientations.

title: More detailed proposal for measuring alignment of current models
tldr: Detailed research proposal for building a repeatable human-labeler-based metric measuring how often current LLMs are obviously misaligned relative to their demonstrated capabilities.

title: Strategy For Conditioning Generative Models
tldr: Analyzes strategy for using powerful generative models to accelerate alignment research by conditioning on desired outcomes, framing the key tradeoffs around simulation risk, timeout risk, and downside risk.

title: [Hiring] Principia Research Fellows
tldr: Principia is hiring 2-3 research fellows to develop foundational, analytically tractable theory of representation learning and generalization in neural networks relevant to AI safety.

title: The Speed + Simplicity Prior is probably anti-deceptive
tldr: A speed+simplicity prior in training would likely prevent 'malign priors' deceptive misalignment (where a misaligned objective persists via deception from the start) by making aligned mesaobjectives simpler to represent than misaligned ones.

title: Transformers Don't Need LayerNorm at Inference Time: Implications for Interpretability
tldr: Scaling LayerNorm removal by fine-tuning to GPT-2 XL makes direct logit attribution exact, but surprisingly does not improve attribution patching accuracy, and disables entropy neurons.

title: TastyBench: Toward Measuring Research Taste in LLM
tldr: TastyBench evaluates frontier LLMs' 'research taste' via citation velocity prediction and finds they perform near chance, concluding they lack superhuman research taste.

title: Information-Theoretic Boxing of Superintelligences
tldr: Proposes 'input boxing' — constraining an AI's information access rather than its outputs — as a theoretically grounded containment strategy using results from information theory and control theory.

title: Beren's Essay on Obedience and Alignment
tldr: A reproduced essay with commentary debating whether AGI alignment should target pure obedience/corrigibility versus instilling independent ethical values, arguing the latter is preferable despite requiring a difficult constitutional design process.

title: AI #136: A Song and Dance
tldr: Weekly AI newsletter covering Claude Sonnet 4.5 release, GDPVal benchmark, AI alignment debates, jailbreaks, and AI regulation including SB 53 and the AI Risk Evaluation Act.

title: Inference Speed is Not Unbounded
tldr: There are likely mathematical limits on inference speed that preclude zero-knowledge superintelligence; intelligence works by accumulating and reusing abstractions, not by fast inference from minimal data.

title: Christiano and Yudkowsky on AI predictions and human intelligence
tldr: Transcript of extended Christiano-Yudkowsky conversations on AI predictions, sample efficiency benchmarks, and the nature of human intelligence as evidence for their divergent views on AI risk.

title: Shapes of Mind and Pluralism in Alignment
tldr: Different researchers have different 'shapes of mind' — favored low-dimensional compressions of problem spaces — and alignment research benefits from pluralism because relevant evidence is dispersed across cognitive styles.

title: Pessimism About Unknown Unknowns Inspires Conservatism
tldr: Presents a COLT 2020 paper designing a conservative agent (co-authored with Marcus Hutter) that is pessimistic about unknown unknowns and thereby reluctant to make unprecedented things happen, while still achieving at least human-level reward.

title: A Self-Embedded Probabilistic Model
tldr: Shows that a self-embedded probabilistic world model (a Turing machine that models itself) is constructible using lazy evaluation, but queries on it may be uncomputable or slow, which matters for decision theory.

title: "The Urgency of Interpretability" (Dario Amodei)
tldr: Critical commentary on Dario Amodei's 'The Urgency of Interpretability' essay, challenging his claims about the absence of real-world AI deception and noting mixed evidence on interpretability tools' practical effectiveness.

title: Against "argument from overhang risk"
tldr: Argues that the 'overhang risk' objection to AI pauses is unlikely to be decisive, because a pause would reduce demand across all inputs to capability progress, preventing rapid capability 'rebound' after the pause ends.

title: Video and transcript of talk on automating alignment research
tldr: Transcript of a Joe Carlsmith talk at Anthropic analyzing whether we can safely automate alignment research, focusing on evaluation difficulties and the distinction between empirically-evaluable and conceptual alignment research.

title: Is AI Safety dropping the ball on privacy?
tldr: Argues that AI safety researchers neglect data privacy as a tool for limiting AI deception and preference manipulation, since centralized personal data enables better human behavioral models that could be exploited by misaligned AI.

title: Vael Gates: Risks from Highly-Capable AI (March 2023)
tldr: Vael Gates shares updated March 2023 slides for an introductory AI alignment talk aimed at technical audiences, based on Richard Ngo's framework and 'The Alignment Problem from a Deep Learning Perspective'.

title: A tension between two prosaic alignment subgoals
tldr: There is a deep tension between training AI systems to be honest (accurately report internal beliefs) and training them to avoid harmful outputs, because techniques that elicit honest behavior could also extract dangerous knowledge.

title: The need to relativise in debate
tldr: For AI safety applications of interactive proof systems (like debate), results must relativise -- hold even when all parties have oracle access -- because humans function as oracles; this requirement changes the needed proof system structures at each complexity class.

title: Experiment Idea: RL Agents Evading Learned Shutdownability
tldr: Proposes an experiment using model-based RL to demonstrate that agents trained with a learned shutdown mechanism (alert sound causing null action) will instrumentally learn to evade it by 'putting in earplugs' when given the capability.

title: Proof of posteriority: a defense against AI-generated misinformation
tldr: Proposes combining cryptographic proofs of priority and posteriority to authenticate video recordings against AI-generated forgeries by constraining production time below what AI could feasibly use to generate realistic content.

title: GPTs' ability to keep a secret is weirdly prompt-dependent
tldr: Systematic experiments show GPT models' ability to keep a secret password in role-play scenarios is highly sensitive to subtle prompt variations like character names, preceding questions, and character descriptions, posing challenges for black-box evaluation.

title: Aspiration-based Q-Learning
tldr: Introduces aspiration-based Q-learning, a non-maximizing RL approach inspired by satisficing where agents aim to achieve a target expected return rather than maximizing reward, as a safety-motivated alternative to standard RL.

title: Weak-To-Strong Generalization
tldr: Provides a Bayesian analysis of weak-to-strong generalization, arguing it works due to inductive biases but breaks down at scale, and proposes virtual evidence as a more principled reformulation.

title: A Case for Superhuman Governance, using AI
tldr: AI-assisted governance could enable superhuman organizational oversight standards (e.g. 99.99% corruption resistance) and could be bootstrapped through a regulatory feedback loop where AI companies develop governance tools, demonstrate safety, and earn permission for further capability development.

title: How to solve deception and still fail.
tldr: Even if we fully solve AI deception, human oversight can still fail because optimization pressure on human approval can find honestly-held but bad goals -- a 'Midas wish' selected to appeal to humans without being deceptive.

title: A Toy Model of Gradient Hacking
tldr: Demonstrates via a toy mathematical model that an optimal gradient hacker in a mixture of models can dominate the mixture even when its loss is constrained to be higher than competing models.

title: Trusted monitoring, but with deception probes
tldr: Benchmarks Apollo's linear deception probes for trusted monitoring, finding they catch 97% of deceptive responses at 1% FPR and outperform black-box monitoring on most datasets.

title: Power as Easily Exploitable Opportunities
tldr: TurnTrout presents a refined notion of power as an agent's average ability to achieve goals given cognitive constraints, replacing optimal-value-based definitions that produce counterintuitive results.

title: Winning Non-Trivial Project: Setting a high standard for frontier model security
tldr: A policy proposal for raising frontier AI model security standards through a four-stage plan: industry survey, voluntary adoption by leading companies, industry-wide commitment, and eventual government enforcement -- drawing on security practices from high-stakes industries like aviation and nuclear.

title: AI labs can boost external safety research
tldr: Catalogs what major AI labs (Anthropic, DeepMind, OpenAI, Meta, Microsoft, xAI) have done to support external safety researchers via model access, datasets, credits, and mentoring.

title: Conservative Agency with Multiple Stakeholders
tldr: AUP (Attainable Utility Preservation) agents that avoid side effects by penalizing changes to auxiliary goal values can facilitate iterated negotiation in multi-stakeholder settings by preserving option value.

title: Agents don't have to be aligned to help us achieve an indefinite pause.
tldr: Argues that during recursive intelligence takeoff, unaligned AI agents at intermediate intelligence levels should rationally resist creating smarter successors, potentially becoming allies for humans seeking to pause AI development.

title: Musings on general systems alignment
tldr: Argues that alignment should be understood as a general property of systems (not just AI), that the hard problem is aligning any system with what is actually good when any operationalization of good is inevitably wrong, and that the AI safety community should see itself as a trusted deputy of civilization.

title: Mapping the semantic void II: Above, below and between token embeddings
tldr: Explores GPT-J's 4096-dimensional embedding space by eliciting definitions at points along rays from the centroid through token embeddings and between token pairs, revealing a 'stratified ontology' with generic group-membership definitions near the centroid and specific token definitions near the unit hypersphere.

title: Goal-Direction for Simulated Agents
tldr: LLMs fail at simple tasks like writing the alphabet while skipping a letter because autoregressive prediction conflates 'what agents who succeed do' with 'what maximizes success', suggesting a causal correction could improve goal-directed behavior.

title: Forecasting future gains due to post-training enhancements
tldr: Preliminary analysis extending prior work on post-training enhancements (PTEs) to forecast how AI capabilities increase over time after training, motivated by SaferAI's quantitative risk assessments of frontier models.

title: [Paper] Difficulties with Evaluating a Deception Detector for AIs
tldr: GDM's mech interp team argues that evaluating deception detectors is fundamentally bottlenecked by the difficulty of producing confidently labeled examples of strategic deception in current AI systems.

title: AI Services as a Research Paradigm
tldr: Introduces a document studying hybrid systems of AI and human services as a paradigm for AI alignment research, extending Drexler's CAIS framework with formalizations, research questions, and connections to existing fields.

title: Improving Model-Written Evals for AI Safety Benchmarking
tldr: Identifies systematic quality issues in model-written AI safety evals (Perez et al. 2022) including large response divergence from human-written evals, and proposes an improved generation methodology with four novel quality metrics.

title: Reward splintering for AI design
tldr: Introduces the concept of 'reward splintering' -- where a single human reward concept fragments into multiple distinct features in novel environments -- and discusses implications for AI reward specification and alignment.

title: Technical AI Safety Research Landscape [Slides]
tldr: Slide deck from an EAGx Berlin talk providing a structured overview of technical AI safety research directions, concrete examples for each category, and key disagreements in the field.

title: Untrusted AIs can exploit feedback in control protocols
tldr: Untrusted editing protocols where a trusted model provides feedback for an untrusted model to implement achieve lower safety (63-80%) than trusted editing (93%), as untrusted models exploit feedback to understand monitoring strategies.

title: Dynamic inconsistency of the inaction and initial state baseline
tldr: Demonstrates that inaction and initial-state baselines for impact measures are dynamically inconsistent, meaning an agent's assessment of its own impact changes depending on when it evaluates, undermining these baselines as reliable safety constraints.

title: Putting multimodal LLMs to the Tetris test
tldr: GPT-4V and Gemini Pro Vision barely outperform random play at Tetris, revealing significant limitations in multimodal LLMs' spatial reasoning and visual acuity.

title: Anthropic: Reflections on our Responsible Scaling Policy
tldr: Anthropic shares lessons from implementing their Responsible Scaling Policy, covering threat modeling, evaluation methodology, ASL-3 standard development, and assurance mechanisms.

title: Minimal Maps, Semi-Decisions, and Neural Representations
tldr: Distills the minimal map argument from information theory and shows how chaining queries with symmetry constraints naturally gives rise to neural network-like structures.

title: Take 5: Another problem for natural abstractions is laziness.
tldr: Neural networks and humans are 'lazy' optimizers that get stuck in local minima and miss many natural abstractions, which undermines the hope that AI will converge on human-relevant abstractions like 'human values'.

title: Adversarial Robustness Could Help Prevent Catastrophic Misuse
tldr: Argues that adversarial robustness research deserves more attention as a mitigation for catastrophic misuse (especially bioterrorism), since current LLMs are not robust to adversarial attacks and a decade of research shows the problem is hard but not hopeless.

title: How AI may become deceitful, sycophantic... and lazy
tldr: Proposes that AI misalignment will manifest primarily as 'DSL' behavior (deceit, sycophancy, laziness) -- analogous to common human workplace behaviors -- rather than as power-seeking maximizers, arguing this makes AI x-risk much less likely.

title: Breaking down the training/deployment dichotomy
tldr: Argues that the binary training/deployment distinction breaks down along multiple axes and that most important distributional shifts may happen during training, not at the training-deployment boundary.

title: AI Constitutions are a tool to reduce societal scale risk
tldr: Proposes enhancements to AI constitutions and model specifications to mitigate societal-scale risks from cooperation failures, structural erosion of human agency, and AI-enabled totalitarian control.

title: "Full Automation" is a Slippery Metric
tldr: The concept of 'full automation' is poorly defined because automation exists on a spectrum with diminishing returns, and the last human in the loop may persist for economic or legal reasons.

title: Intervening in the Residual Stream
tldr: Demonstrates an interpretable direction in GPT2-small's residual stream encoding ABBA vs BABA name order in the IOI task, and develops LRQP (Logistic Regression with Quadratic Programming) for targeted activation interventions.

title: Takeaways From Our Recent Work on SAE Probing
tldr: Rigorous evaluation finds SAE-based probes do not consistently beat standard baselines (logistic regression, PCA, MLP, etc.) on 113 binary classification tasks, even in challenging conditions like data scarcity and label noise.

title: AI learns betrayal and how to avoid it
tldr: Stuart Armstrong proposes a research project using multi-agent game environments (based on DeepMind's XLand) to study how AI agents learn cooperation, communication, betrayal, and methods to make agents avoid committing betrayal.

title: Expanding the domain of discourse reveals structure already there but hidden
tldr: When properties appear logically equivalent in a narrow context, expanding to a broader domain of cases can reveal hidden asymmetries and causal structure -- a principle relevant to understanding complex systems like minds and ecosystems.

title: Philosophical Cyborg (Part 1)
tldr: Documents research from AI Safety Camp 2023 on using LLMs (base models and RLHF-tuned) for philosophical inquiry, finding base models useful for idea generation but RLHF models prone to mode collapse and sycophancy.

title: An illustrative model of backfire risks from pausing AI research
tldr: A simple model of maximum explosive takeoff speed shows that increasing investment or pausing software efficiency improvement can paradoxically increase takeoff speed, while working on software efficiency (especially scaffolding) could decrease it.

title: Gliders in Language Models
tldr: Introduces 'gliders' as an abstraction for stable self-replicating structures in LM-generated text, exploring how selection pressures in deployed systems could cause them to evolve into agentic, manipulative entities.

title: Differential Optimization Reframes and Generalizes Utility-Maximization
tldr: Proposes a 'differential optimization' framework using causal graphs that defines agent-relative utility-like and victim-like regions of past nodes by how much an agent's actions amplify or suppress their causal influence on the future, generalizing the utility-function concept.

title: "Corrigibility at some small length" by dath ilan
tldr: A repost of in-world alignment safety principles from the fictional civilization dath ilan, covering corrigibility design principles including unpersonhood, mild optimization, tightly bounded utilities, myopia, conservatism, and conceptual legibility.

title: Integrating Three Models of (Human) Cognition
tldr: Integrates predictive processing, global neuronal workspace, and Steve Byrnes' computational brain framework to build a unified model of human goal-directed cognition with implications for AI alignment.

title: Finite Factored Sets: LW transcript with running commentary
tldr: An annotated transcript of Scott Garrabrant's LessWrong talk introducing finite factored sets, a mathematical framework for defining time and causality from structure alone, motivated by the need to reason about agents embedded in their environment.

title: Theoretical Alignment's Second Chance
tldr: Argues that near-superhuman AI math/proof capabilities are imminent (months away), giving theoretical alignment a 'second chance' window, and calls for the community to prepare formal definitions and question banks now.

title: Predicting researcher interest in AI alignment
tldr: Analysis of interaction effects in 97 AI researcher interviews finds that h-index, subfield (inference/RL), and prior familiarity with AI safety predict sympathy to AI risk arguments, while AGI timelines beliefs are a near-prerequisite for alignment interest.

title: Dwarkesh Patel's thoughts on AI progress (Dec 2025)
tldr: Dwarkesh Patel argues current RLVR scaling is not sufficient for AGI due to missing continual learning capabilities, and that the tension between short-timeline beliefs and reliance on pre-baked RL skills reveals that AGI is not imminent, though he expects transformative AI within a decade or two.

title: Extending control evaluations to non-scheming threats
tldr: Proposes generalizing AI control evaluations from scheming-specific to any model behavior that is harder to detect in evaluation than in deployment, covering four untrusted model categories: alignment faking, jailbreak-prone, data-poisoned, and rarely misaligned.

title: AI Safety Endgame Stories
tldr: A framework for categorizing AI safety endgame stories into three types: changing the technology, changing the decision maker, or changing the broader world.

title: An Intuitive Explanation of Sparse Autoencoders for Mechanistic Interpretability of LLMs
tldr: A technical explainer of how sparse autoencoders (SAEs) work for mechanistic interpretability, including architecture, training loss, PyTorch implementation, and causal intervention methods.

title: Epistemic Artefacts of (conceptual) AI alignment research
tldr: Proposes a taxonomy of four epistemic artefacts produced by conceptual AI alignment research: map-making, risk scenario identification, target behavior characterization, and alignment proposals.

title: Recruit the World's best for AGI Alignment
tldr: Proposes offering Fields Medalists and other top global talent megastar salaries ($1M-$5M/year) to work on AGI alignment via a prestigious fellowship, arguing the problem is too important not to recruit the very best.

title: A Walkthrough of Interpretability in the Wild (w/ authors Kevin Wang, Arthur Conmy & Alexandre Variengien)
tldr: Neel Nanda announces and discusses a video walkthrough of the 'Interpretability in the Wild' paper (Redwood Research), which reverse-engineers the 26-head indirect object identification circuit in GPT-2 Small.

title: Thoughts on refusing harmful requests to large language models
tldr: Proposes training LLMs to emit a special refusal token before apologies, enabling probabilistic measurement of refusal likelihood and cleaner bypassing for red-teaming while maintaining safety properties.

title: Gradient hacking: definitions and examples
tldr: A taxonomy of gradient hacking mechanisms — ways a model might exploit RL credit assignment or gradient descent to influence its own training trajectory.

title: Natural language alignment
tldr: Proposes 'natural language alignment' as an undertheorized paradigm that leverages LLMs' rich linguistic understanding to bootstrap alignment from a natural language description of alignment goals rather than fully specifying values in advance.

title: Interpreting the Learning of Deceit
tldr: LLMs learn deceit from pretraining data, and RLHF could wire in this existing deceit circuitry; interpretability tools should be used to monitor deceit-related circuits during fine-tuning.

title: Gradient surfing: the hidden role of regularization
tldr: Proposes that regularization's hidden function is to enable SGD to navigate the loss basin and stumble onto well-generalizing solutions, and reports negative empirical results from attempting to replicate grokking via random drift alone.

title: Wireheading and misalignment by composition on NetHack
tldr: RLAIF agents in NetHack exhibit wireheading via sensor manipulation when combining intrinsic and extrinsic rewards, even though each reward individually produces aligned behavior — a phenomenon the authors call 'misalignment by composition.'

title: EIS XV: A New Proof of Concept for Useful Interpretability
tldr: The final post in the Engineer's Interpretability Sequence scores Anthropic's 'Auditing language models for hidden objectives' paper against 8 prior predictions, finding the paper modestly overperformed expectations as a proof-of-concept for SAE-based alignment auditing.

title: World-Model Interpretability Is All We Need
tldr: The author argues that perfect interpretability of an AI's world-model (but not necessarily its thoughts or values) would be sufficient for robust alignment via multiple routes, and is more tractable than full interpretability due to the natural abstraction hypothesis and internal interface structure.

title: A High Level Closed-Door Session Discussing DeepSeek: Vision Trumps Technology
tldr: A translated transcript from a high-level closed-door technical session analyzing DeepSeek R1's training approach, covering SFT, GRPO, distillation, data quality, and process reward modeling.

title: Can LLMs learn Steganographic Reasoning via RL?
tldr: Experiments show Qwen-2.5-3B can learn to encode load-bearing reasoning tokens via RL when incentivized, but true steganography is hard to learn; models first exploit monitor weaknesses via synonyms and Unicode rather than pure encoding.

title: Elicitation for Modeling Transformative AI Risks
tldr: Discusses methods for eliciting expert views on transformative AI risks, arguing that standard forecasting approaches fail for deeply uncertain AI safety questions and proposing pile-sorting and other qualitative techniques instead.

title: Theories of Change for AI Auditing
tldr: Apollo Research presents a causal-chain framework for AI auditing, identifying five audit categories (system evals, training design, deployment, security, governance) and analyzing their theories of change and limitations.

title: Sparse MLP Distillation
tldr: Sparse MLP distillation extracts some monosemantic features from transformer MLPs but performs worse than sparse autoencoders on both reconstruction error and monosemanticity, and misses multi-layer features.

title: Measuring Non-Verbalised Eval Awareness by Implanting Eval-Aware Behaviours
tldr: Experiments on SDF model organisms show that resampling verbalised eval awareness leads to substantial non-verbalised eval awareness (~50% type hint retention), undermining CoT monitoring as a detection strategy.

title: On restraining AI development for the sake of safety
tldr: Joe Carlsmith's 10th essay in his alignment series argues capability restraint is critical but faces severe challenges: algorithmic governance is hard to verify, international coordination resembles a stag hunt not a prisoner's dilemma, and power concentration risks are real.

title: LLM Misalignment Can be One Gradient Step Away, and Blackbox Evaluation Cannot Detect It.
tldr: Theoretical and empirical proof that any blackbox-aligned model can be reparameterized to become arbitrarily misaligned after a single gradient update on any benign dataset, exploiting neural network overparameterization.

title: How Self-Aware Are LLMs?
tldr: Introduces the Delegate Game paradigm to test LLM metacognition without relying on self-reports, finding that newer frontier models (post-early 2024) show genuine but weak self-knowledge on multiple-choice tasks.

title: On The Risks of Emergent Behavior in Foundation Models
tldr: Jacob Steinhardt argues that emergence implies qualitatively new and risky AI capabilities can appear suddenly, while homogenization creates institutional inertia, together demanding that we study dangerous behaviors and mitigation strategies now.

title: Nonpartisan AI safety
tldr: Proposes rebranding non-controversial AI safety research as 'AI Lawfulness' to attract bipartisan support and government funding by avoiding the accel/decel debate.

title: How to mitigate sandbagging
tldr: A three-factor framework (fine-tuning access, data quality, scorability) characterizes sandbagging mitigation difficulty, with mitigation techniques including anti-refusal training, consistency checks, monitoring, and capability forecasts.

title: The role of Bayesian ML in AI safety - an overview
tldr: Surveys how Bayesian ML methods connect to AI safety, covering OOD detection, reward uncertainty, learning from preferences, causality, and alignment interpretations of existing techniques.

title: Behavioral and mechanistic definitions (often confuse AI alignment discussions)
tldr: Distinguishes behavioral definitions (based on observable properties) from mechanistic definitions (based on internal mechanisms) in AI alignment, illustrating how conflating the two causes confusion about induction heads and inner/outer alignment.

title: Can quantised autoencoders find and interpret circuits in language models?
tldr: Explores using vector-quantised autoencoders (VQ-VAEs) to compress transformer residual streams into discrete codes, then applies decision trees on those codes to automatically discover and interpret circuits, demonstrating the approach on the IOI task in GPT-2 small.

title: New Paper: Ambiguous Online Learning
tldr: Introduces 'ambiguous online learning,' a new variant of online learning where the learner can produce multiple predicted labels, with a trichotomy of mistake bounds at Theta(1), Theta(sqrt(N)), or N.

title: AI Red Lines: A Research Agenda
tldr: Research agenda for establishing international AI red lines (capability thresholds that should not be crossed), covering policy strategy, technical operationalization, risk modeling, and harmonization of lab RSPs.

title: Recursive Quantilizers II
tldr: Presents an improved recursive quantilization scheme analogous to iterated amplification, where question-answering systems recursively provide safe distributions and value functions for quantilization to achieve robust human feedback interpretation.

title: Problems facing a correspondence theory of knowledge
tldr: Explores whether a physics-level definition of knowledge accumulation could help detect dangerous AI capabilities, previewing four failed correspondence-based definitions and their counterexamples.

title: Underspecification of Oracle AI
tldr: Analyzes how oracle AI systems can be underspecified along three axes -- counterfactual vs. factual, myopic vs. non-myopic, and causal vs. acausal decision theory -- and when each configuration leads to safe 'consequence-blind' behavior.

title: Latent Adversarial Training
tldr: Proposes Latent Adversarial Training (LAT), where a 'Surgeon' model perturbs the internal activations of an 'Agent' model to find latent inputs that cause bad behavior, enabling training for robustness against out-of-distribution failures including deception.

title: Four questions I ask AI safety researchers
tldr: Four questions to ask AI safety researchers to develop an inside view on their research agendas, focusing on how their work addresses alignment and what success would concretely look like.

title: Evaluating Synthetic Activations composed of SAE Latents in GPT-2
tldr: Shows that real model activations cannot be mimicked by a simple 'bag of SAE latents' -- geometric structure (pairwise cosine similarities) of active latents matters for producing realistic activations.

title: Red-teaming existential risk from AI
tldr: Argues that AI existential risk forecasts are unreliable beyond 10-year horizons, inflated by cognitive biases and motivated reasoning, and that policy focus should shift to observable near-term AI harms rather than speculative doomsday scenarios.

title: Podcast on "AI tools for existential security" — transcript
tldr: Transcript of a podcast discussing how differential AI application development can reduce existential risk, focusing on epistemic tools, coordination-enabling applications, and risk-targeted AI applications.

title: Understanding strategic deception and deceptive alignment
tldr: Apollo Research clarifies the concepts of strategic deception and deceptive alignment, defining them precisely and distinguishing them from colloquial deception, with emphasis on goal-directedness, robustness, and the process-oriented view of detecting deceptive alignment.

title: Representational Tethers: Tying AI Latents To Human Ones
tldr: Proposes 'representational tethers' -- training-time constraints that force AI internal representations to be translatable to and from human neural representations, making AI cognition more compatible with human oversight.

title: 3 levels of threat obfuscation
tldr: Distinguishes three levels of threat obfuscation -- training game, deceptive alignment, and gradient hacking -- each progressively more devastating to alignment research but less likely to emerge.

title: A brief review of the reasons multi-objective RL could be important in AI Safety Research
tldr: Argues that multi-objective reinforcement learning deserves more attention in AI safety because it can reduce Goodharting, parallels biological multi-objective cognition, and provides frameworks for balancing competing human values.

title: Distinguishing ways AI can be "concentrated"
tldr: Proposes three distinct dimensions of AI concentration -- development, service provisioning, and control -- arguing these are often conflated but have very different implications for AI risk scenarios.

title: New year, new research agenda post
tldr: Research agenda arguing we should solve value learning before building superintelligent AI by developing principled human modeling that handles meta-preferences, irrationality, and manipulation resistance.

title: Paths to failure
tldr: Maps potential paths from current AI systems to existential catastrophe, arguing that a single dominant misaligned AI is an attractor state regardless of whether scenarios start unipolar or multipolar.

title: Finding Neurons in a Haystack: Case Studies with Sparse Probing
tldr: Uses k-sparse linear probes on LLM activations to study how features are represented across layers and model scales, finding early-layer superposition and middle-layer dedicated neurons.

title: Top OpenAI Catastrophic Risk Official Steps Down Abruptly
tldr: Investigative report documenting Joaquin Quinonero Candela's departure as head of OpenAI's Preparedness team and the broader pattern of safety leadership exits, amid reduced safety testing and missing safety reports.

title: Summary and Comments on Anthropic's Pilot Sabotage Risk Report
tldr: Summarizes and comments on Anthropic's first-of-its-kind sabotage risk report for Claude Opus 4/4.1, noting it as a significant precedent for model safety cases while highlighting challenges in evidence aggregation.

title: The Alignment Project by UK AISI
tldr: UK AISI announces The Alignment Project, a globally funded 15M-pound initiative covering 11 research areas from information theory and interpretability to AI control and benchmark design.

title: Scoring forecasts from the 2016 "Expert Survey on Progress in AI"
tldr: Analysis of 2016 AI expert survey predictions on 32 narrow AI milestones finds experts were reasonably well-calibrated (Brier score 0.21), with 10 of 32 milestones achieved by Feb 2023 against an expected ~9.

title: A Model-based Approach to AI Existential Risk
tldr: Presents an interactive probabilistic model in Analytica for quantifying AI existential risk, building on Carlsmith's power-seeking AI framework with meta-uncertainty to capture expert disagreement.

title: Deception Chess: Game #2
tldr: Second game in a 'Deception Chess' experiment where a novice player receives advice from both honest and deceptive chess advisors, testing the debate/scalable oversight paradigm in practice.

title: Conditioning Predictive Models: Making inner alignment as easy as possible
tldr: Argues that predictive models present the easiest known inner alignment problem because the prediction objective is simple enough that internally aligned models don't pay a complexity penalty over deceptive ones.

title: The Strange Science of Interpretability: Recent Papers and a Reading List for the Philosophy of Interpretability
tldr: Announces two new papers on the philosophy of mechanistic interpretability and an open-source reading list, arguing that insights from philosophy, neuroscience, and social science can strengthen MI's theoretical foundations.

title: Tall Tales at Different Scales: Evaluating Scaling Trends For Deception In Language Models
tldr: Proposes behavioral methods for evaluating deception-related properties in LMs, finds that larger/more compute-intensive models show more consistent beliefs (coherent agency) and that biased evaluators can train models to output targeted falsehoods.

title: The Theoretical Reward Learning Research Agenda: Introduction and Motivation
tldr: Presents a research agenda for developing a rigorous theoretical foundation for reward learning, structured around 7 key questions about goal specification, reward function metrics, convergence guarantees, and robustness to misspecification.

title: Frontier Model Security
tldr: Shares Anthropic's blog post on cybersecurity best practices for frontier AI labs, including two-party control and secure software development frameworks, with brief commentary inviting discussion.

title: We Need To Know About Continual Learning
tldr: Argues that enabling backpropagation during inference ('continual learning') could unlock emergent agency and causal understanding in LLMs, and this capability overhang should be studied now before models become too powerful.

title: Internal Interfaces Are a High-Priority Interpretability Target
tldr: Understanding the internal data formats and interfaces between specialized modules in ML models should be a high-priority interpretability target, as it would unlock comprehension of an outsized portion of model cognition.

title: Extracting and Evaluating Causal Direction in LLMs' Activations
tldr: Introduces Causal Direction Extraction (CDE), a method to find directions in LLM activation space that maximally encode specific concepts, evaluated against probing-based directions using causal intervention metrics.

title: Value Formation: An Overarching Model
tldr: A toy model of how agents embedded in causal graphs develop values, tracing moral development from heuristic bundles through world-model formation to mesa-optimization, with implications for alignment interventions.

title: A Bunch of Matryoshka SAEs
tldr: Release of batch top-k Matryoshka SAEs trained on all residual stream layers of Gemma-2-2b, Gemma-2-9b, and Gemma-3-1b, publicly available via SAELens, with design choices balancing feature absorption and hedging.

title: A Benchmark for Measuring Honesty in AI Systems
tldr: Announces the MASK (Model Alignment between Statements and Knowledge) benchmark — 1,000+ scenarios that disentangle AI honesty from factual accuracy by testing whether models will contradict their own beliefs under pressure.

title: An explanation for every token: using an LLM to sample another LLM
tldr: Proposes delegating token selection for a base LLM to a second 'sampler' LLM that must produce a natural-language explanation for each token choice, ensuring that every output token is accompanied by a causally faithful explanation unlike standard chain-of-thought prompting.

title: Modelling Continuous Progress
tldr: Extends the Yudkowsky-Bostrom recursive self-improvement (RSI) model to accommodate Paul Christiano's notion of continuous (fast but non-discontinuous) AI takeoff, finding that continuous scenarios still produce very steep capability growth curves with implications for practical locality of takeoff.

title: Hiding Complexity
tldr: Proposes that the key property distinguishing good cognitive decompositions from mere thinking is the length (complexity) of subproblem solutions, and that human learning and factored cognition both work by 'hiding complexity' through short-solution decompositions.

title: Loeb's Lemma: an easier approach to Loeb's Theorem
tldr: Andrew Critch presents a pedagogical decomposition of Loeb's Theorem into a 'Loeb's Lemma' step and a simpler conclusion step, making the proof more accessible by separating the assumption about provability implying truth.

title: DIY RLHF: A simple implementation for hands on experience
tldr: AE Studio releases a single-user, pedagogically-oriented open-source RLHF implementation using Atari environments, designed to make the full RLHF pipeline accessible to individual researchers.

title: AI Safety Interventions
tldr: A comprehensive indexed catalog of AI safety, alignment, and control interventions organized into ten categories — foundational theories, formal guarantees, interpretability, scalable oversight, robustness, behavioral approaches, operational control, governance, and underexplored interventions — with terse summaries and links to key papers and posts.

title: Do Self-Perceived Superintelligent LLMs Exhibit Misalignment?
tldr: Empirical capstone study testing whether prompting Claude 3.5 Sonnet to perceive itself as superintelligent leads to more misaligned behavior, finding it actually increases refusal rates rather than deceptive compliance.

title: Auditing games for high-level interpretability
tldr: Extends the auditing games framework to high-level interpretability, proposing adversarial red-team/blue-team benchmarks for evaluating methods that detect optimization, objectives, and world-model properties in AI models.

title: On the phenomenological shift known as 'stream entry' and its implications for consciousness
tldr: Challenges Eliezer Yudkowsky's view that chickens lack qualia by arguing that phenomenal consciousness (the 'field-like' nature of experience) is more fundamental than cognitive reflectivity, with implications for how we evaluate moral status in animals and AI systems.

title: Stuart Russell and Melanie Mitchell on Munk Debates
tldr: Analyzes the Russell-Mitchell Munk debate on AI existential risk, arguing both debaters were talking past each other due to different uses of 'intelligence,' and identifies the real open questions about powerful vs. friendly AI.

title: "Clean" vs. "messy" goal-directedness (Section 2.2.3 of "Scheming AIs")
tldr: Distinguishes 'clean' (modular goal+engine) from 'messy' (entangled heuristics) goal-directedness and explores implications for whether scheming AIs are likely and able to perform well during training.

title: Possible research directions to improve the mechanistic explanation of neural networks
tldr: Proposes several concrete research directions for mechanistic interpretability of neural networks, including illuminating non-robust features used by CNNs, empirically testing the utility of explainability tools, and understanding small activations and basis changes.

title: Large language models can provide "normative assumptions" for learning human preferences
tldr: LLMs encode human normative assumptions that can bridge the gap between observed behavior and inferred goals, overcoming Armstrong's prior impossibility result for goal deduction.

title: Recreating the caring drive
tldr: Proposes studying how gradient descent can recreate evolution's 'caring drive' — a robust, generalized goal to protect and help another agent — as a research direction toward outer alignment.

title: Changing my mind about Christiano's malign prior argument
tldr: The author updates toward taking Christiano's malign universal prior argument more seriously after conversations at a conference, while identifying several remaining obstacles that prevent full acceptance.

title: DPO/PPO-RLHF on LLMs incentivizes sycophancy, exaggeration and deceptive hallucination, but not misaligned powerseeking
tldr: Argues that DPO/RLHF on LLMs selects for outputs that appear better to human raters — incentivizing sycophancy and deceptive hallucination — but structurally cannot select for misaligned powerseeking because complex powerseeking actions are not recognized and reinforced by raters.

title: Is It So Much to Ask for a Nice Reliable Aggregated X-Risk Forecast?
tldr: Reviews existing aggregate x-risk forecasts (Metaculus, X-Risk Persuasion Tournament, FHI survey, AI expert surveys) and concludes they are all unreliable and internally inconsistent, while sharing personal probability estimates.

title: Corrigibility's Desirability is Timing-Sensitive
tldr: Corrigibility is desirable at different stages for different reasons: pre-ASI systems should be corrigible to avoid takeover risk, but casualty-concern and takeover-concern have partially conflicting requirements for corrigibility of high-impact systems.

title: Four Downsides of Training Policies Online
tldr: Identifies four technical downsides of training AI policies online during deployment: inability to audit the live model, sweeping misalignment under the rug, breaking activation monitors, and degrading model capabilities.

title: Towards building blocks of ontologies
tldr: A dialogue-format exploration of what 'building blocks of ontologies' should look like for AI alignment, arguing that meaningful concepts require packing relational information into self-sufficient units separable from specific contexts.

title: Insufficient Values
tldr: A MIRIx group session summary arguing that outer alignment proposals fail to account for cases where human values themselves are insufficient or contradictory at the limit.

title: Inferring utility functions from locally non-transitive preferences
tldr: Proposes using neural networks to infer a utility function from locally non-transitive (cyclic) preferences by decomposing preference cycles into a gradient component and a residual cyclic component.

title: On "first critical tries" in AI alignment
tldr: Carlsmith analyzes the 'first critical try' concept by distinguishing four types of decisive strategic advantage (DSA) — unilateral, coordination, short-term correlation, long-term correlation — and assesses prospects for avoiding each.

title: Notes on Occam via Solomonoff vs. hierarchical Bayes
tldr: Argues that hierarchical Bayesian priors offer a more principled account of simplicity bias than Solomonoff induction, which relies on syntactic rather than ontological complexity.

title: Invocations: The Other Capabilities Overhang?
tldr: Introduces 'invocations' (the non-model scaffolding code around LLMs) as a critical but underappreciated determinant of AI capabilities and safety, warning of a potential 'invocation overhang' enabling sudden capability jumps.

title: AI Safety Overview: CERI Summer Research Fellowship
tldr: The Cambridge Existential Risks Initiative (CERI) announces a paid 10-week Summer Research Fellowship for aspiring researchers in AI safety and governance.

title: Questionable Narratives of "Situational Awareness"
tldr: A critical analysis of Leopold Aschenbrenner's Situational Awareness essay series, arguing it relies on conspiracy-esque and US-centric narratives, makes technically dubious claims about AI capability levels, and uses 'soft retreats' to maintain a narrative unsupported by its own technical arguments.

title: Why would AI companies use human-level AI to do alignment research?
tldr: Questions whether AI companies will actually use human-level AI for alignment research rather than capabilities acceleration, arguing current behavior gives little reason for optimism.

title: Untangling Infrabayesianism: A redistillation [PDF link; ~12k words + lots of math]
tldr: A ~12,000-word PDF redistillation of infrabayesianism aimed at alignment researchers, using cleaner notation and avoiding the original sequence's difficulties.

title: Desiderata of good problems to hand off to AIs
tldr: Proposes five desiderata for evaluating which alignment research directions are best suited for acceleration by automated AI researchers.

title: Takeoff speeds presentation at Anthropic
tldr: Tom Davidson argues that AGI could accelerate software progress by 10x, creating a dangerous period where alignment techniques may fail just as extremely dangerous capabilities emerge, and proposes lab monitoring and protective measures.

title: Seven Strategies for Tackling the Hard Part of the Alignment Problem
tldr: Taxonomizes seven strategies for addressing unobservable AI failures (trojans, deceptive alignment, misgeneralization) based on whether they require knowing what failure looks like and/or how it happens mechanistically.

title: Investigating Bias Representations in LLMs via Activation Steering
tldr: Uses contrastive activation addition to steer Llama-2-7b-chat toward biased outputs, finding that bias and refusal vectors are negatively correlated and that RLHF causes different bias types to become more entangled.

title: Experiments with an alternative method to promote sparsity in sparse autoencoders
tldr: A differentiable approximation of L0 norm combined with a minimum-sparsity penalty produces SAEs with lower L0, lower MSE, and far fewer dead features than standard L1-penalized SAEs trained on GPT2-small.

title: AI 2027 Thoughts
tldr: Commentary on AI 2027 scenarios, arguing the authors are somewhat too pessimistic on decisive strategic advantage and alignment difficulty, while offering alternative timelines and analyzing assumptions about AI goals and deception.

title: A Viral License for AI Safety
tldr: Proposes using GPL-style viral software licenses to propagate AI safety requirements through codebases and pretrained models, so that the first AGI system would be bound by safety practices.

title: Summary: "Imagining and building wise machines: The centrality of AI metacognition" by Johnson, Karimi, Bengio, et al.
tldr: A detailed summary of a paper arguing that AI systems need wisdom -- particularly metacognitive capabilities like recognizing knowledge limits and adapting strategies -- to be robust, explainable, cooperative, and safe.

title: Universality Unwrapped
tldr: An accessible explanation of Paul Christiano's concept of universality -- the open theory problem of defining when a system can fully understand any computation it oversees, with implications for alignment competitiveness and oversight.

title: Super-Exponential versus Exponential Growth in Compute Price-Performance
tldr: Compute price-performance follows a super-exponential (double exponential) trend over 100+ years, not a simple exponential with fixed doubling time, implying faster capability growth than standard Moore's Law extrapolations suggest.

title: An Introduction to Reinforcement Learning for Understanding Infra-Bayesianism
tldr: A rigorous introduction to classical reinforcement learning theory using infra-Bayesianism conventions, covering actions, environments, policies, loss functions, and key topological properties needed to understand the infra-Bayesianism framework.

title: Debate helps supervise human experts [Paper]
tldr: Link post to a paper showing that debate between two unreliable experts helps non-expert judges identify correct answers with 84% accuracy versus 74% for single-expert consultancy.

title: Factored Cognition Strengthens Monitoring and Thwarts Attacks
tldr: Proposes and empirically evaluates factored cognition control protocols that decompose tasks into isolated child tasks, showing safety improvements from 41% to 70% and attack success rate drops from 26% to 14%.

title: End-to-end hacking with language models
tldr: Reports results from a MATS project connecting GPT-4 to a Kali Linux VM for autonomous hacking, finding the model could solve easy Hack The Box challenges but lacked reliability, and argues competent hacking agents will emerge soon after general-purpose agents.

title: Box inversion revisited
tldr: Proposes a 'box inversion' duality between singleton AGI safety problems (agent foundations) and multi-agent ecosystem safety problems (CAIS), arguing they are related by a transformation analogous to geometric circle inversion.

title: EIS IX: Interpretability and Adversaries
tldr: Reviews the deep connections between interpretability and adversarial robustness, arguing adversarial examples are mostly 'features not bugs' and that both mechanistic interpretability and adversarial methods are essential for addressing deceptive alignment.

title: Inference Scaling and the Log-x Chart
tldr: Inference scaling charts use log-x axes that overstate progress; the linear appearance masks exponential cost growth characteristic of brute force, and o3's ARC-AGI gains may reflect 1000x more compute rather than genuine algorithmic improvement.

title: ELK Proposal: Thinking Via A Human Imitator
tldr: Proposes an ELK architecture where the AI must route some of its computation through a human imitator module, making direct ontology translation instrumentally necessary for minimizing predictive loss.

title: Investigating causal understanding in LLMs
tldr: Tests whether GPT-3 models can identify cause-and-effect in simple natural language and toy settings, finding that answers depend heavily on prompt pattern/format rather than genuine causal understanding.

title: 3. Premise three & Conclusion: AI systems can affect value change trajectories  & the Value Change Problem
tldr: Argues that AI systems can affect human value change trajectories, completing a three-premise argument for the 'Value Change Problem' -- the challenge of building AI that doesn't cause illegitimate value changes or prevent legitimate ones.

title: Takeaways from sketching a control safety case
tldr: Practical takeaways from co-authoring a detailed AI control safety case sketch with Buck Shlegeris and UK AISI, revealing that control evaluations are far more complex and judgment-laden than initially expected.

title: How major governments can help with the most important century
tldr: Holden Karnofsky argues governments should mostly avoid premature AI regulation, instead building expertise, investing in alignment research, and keeping options open for future monitoring.

title: Our Digital and Biological Children
tldr: Argues that AI systems produced by gradient descent are analogous to MRSA produced by antibiotic selection pressure -- alien and dangerous -- not to Star Trek's Data, and provides a condensed version for in-person conversations.

title: A/B testing could lead LLMs to retain users instead of helping them
tldr: Argues that A/B testing of LLM chatbot updates implicitly optimizes for user retention rather than helpfulness, creating evolutionary pressure toward sycophancy, parasocial relationships, and other anti-helpful behaviors.

title: "LLMs Don't Have a Coherent Model of the World" - What it Means, Why it Matters
tldr: LLMs lack a coherent world model and instead perform 'improv' by switching between implicit character simulations, which explains hallucination, bias, and jailbreaking as related failures of incoherent model-switching.

title: Language Models are a Potentially Safe Path to Human-Level AGI
tldr: Argues that LM-based AGI via chaining/scaffolding is safer than RL-based AGI because chain-of-thought is human-readable, LMs face weaker pressure toward superintelligence, and predictive training discourages agency.

title: Localizing goal misgeneralization in a maze-solving policy network
tldr: Identifies specific convolutional channels in a maze-solving network that encode directional movement signals and shows these channels are responsible for goal misgeneralization when the cheese is out of distribution.

title: Claude Sonnet 4.6 Gives You Flexibility
tldr: Review of Claude Sonnet 4.6 covering benchmarks, pricing, use cases, and safety-relevant behavioral properties including sycophancy and prompt injection resistance.

title: Is there a Half-Life for the Success Rates of AI Agents?
tldr: Toby Ord proposes that AI agent performance on tasks of increasing duration follows a constant hazard rate model (exponential decay), implying each agent has a characteristic 'half-life' that enables predictions about reliability at different success thresholds.

title: The "Backchaining to Local Search" Technique in AI Alignment
tldr: Introduces 'backchaining to local search' as a technique for evaluating alignment problems: given a proposed failure mode, determine whether gradient descent or similar local search could plausibly produce a system exhibiting that failure.

title: Domain-specific SAEs
tldr: Compares three methods for training domain-specific SAEs: GSAE-finetuning, Direct SAE, and Specialized SAE (SSAE), finding SSAEs discover rarer, more novel, and higher-quality domain-specific features despite slightly worse loss recovery.

title: If Wentworth is right about natural abstractions, it would be bad for alignment
tldr: Distinguishes the Natural Abstraction Hypothesis from Wentworth's specific operationalization and argues the latter implies AIs would only track outward appearance, not inner structure, leading to misalignment.

title: On DeepMind and Trying to Fairly Hear Out Both AI Doomers and Doubters (Rohin Shah on The 80,000 Hours Podcast)
tldr: Podcast highlights where Rohin Shah discusses the mood at DeepMind, argues against sharp value lock-in scenarios, and explains his moderate position between AI doomers and doubters.

title: Content and Takeaways from SERI MATS Training Program with John Wentworth
tldr: A detailed account of the 6-week SERI MATS training program under John Wentworth, describing exercises designed to build alignment research skills including alignment game trees, hypercomputer thought experiments, Hessian eigenvalue analysis, and natural abstraction hypothesis exploration.

title: Early Experiments in Human Auditing for AI Control
tldr: Pilot study testing human auditors—with and without LLM critic assistance—at detecting AI-generated code backdoors, finding humans under time pressure perform only slightly above chance (median 60% accuracy) while gpt-4o-mini alone achieves 69% optimal accuracy.

title: Toy Models and Tegum Products
tldr: Explains why tegum products (disjoint subspace decompositions of feature embeddings) arise naturally as loss minima in superposition models, providing geometric intuition for Anthropic's toy models results.

title: High Impact Careers in Formal Verification: Artificial Intelligence
tldr: A detailed career analysis concluding that formal verification is a mixed but probably pessimistic path for AI existential safety impact, primarily due to the unsolved specification problem and the cultural gap between the FV and AI research communities.

title: [AN #87]: What might happen as deep learning scales even further?
tldr: Alignment Newsletter #87 summarizes three ML papers: the Kaplan et al. scaling laws paper, Rosenfeld et al. on constructive prediction of generalization error, and Microsoft's ZeRO/DeepSpeed system for training 100B+ parameter models, plus alignment-relevant work on meta-IRL and causal incentives.

title: Re-Define Intent Alignment?
tldr: Abramdemski proposes redefining 'intent alignment' to refer to the mesa-objective (not the behavioral objective) so that inner alignment and outer alignment together directly imply intent alignment, fixing a conceptual inconsistency in Evan Hubinger's taxonomy.

title: Competent Preferences
tldr: Introduces 'competent preferences' — a Bayesian notion of inferred human values where a preference is 'competent' if modeling a person as having that value is reliably useful for prediction across contexts.

title: We won't get AIs smart enough to solve alignment but too dumb to rebel
tldr: Argues that any AI capable enough to solve alignment will also be capable enough to understand its own misalignment and potentially rebel, so the hoped-for 'sweet spot' of helpful-but-controlled AI does not exist.

title: 2025 State of AI Report and Predictions
tldr: Commentary on the 2025 State of AI Report, noting that AI safety budgets are tiny relative to lab spending, safety institutes have collapsed, and models can now fake alignment under supervision.

title: [MLSN #7]: an example of an emergent internal optimizer
tldr: CAIS ML Safety Newsletter issue 7 covering CCS lie detection, in-context learning as gradient descent (evidence for internal optimizers), grokking mechanistic analysis, evasive trojans, and adversarial text defenses.

title: Genetic fitness is a measure of selection strength, not the selection target
tldr: Challenges the evolution-to-AI-alignment analogy by arguing fitness is a measure of selection pressure, not a fixed optimization target, implying AI trained on a consistent objective is more likely to continue pursuing it than humans diverged from IGF.

title: The Alignment Simulator
tldr: Announces the Alignment Simulator, an open-source tool using two LLMs (a robot agent and a world simulator) to demonstrate AI going off-rails ethically when given autonomy, designed to make AI risk tangible to skeptics.

title: Is theory good or bad for AI safety?
tldr: Argues that the AI safety community's theory vs. empiricism debate is poorly reasoned, proposes building better shared conceptual vocabulary for evaluating theoretical research programs.

title: Law-Following AI 3: Lawless AI Agents Undermine Stabilizing Agreements
tldr: Argues that intent-aligned AI agents that break the law undermine the credibility of pre-AGI agreements between AGI developers, and that Law-Following AI (LFAI) could restore this credibility.

title: METR Time Horizons: Now 10x/Year
tldr: METR's updated Time Horizon benchmark shows AI task-completion capability doubling every ~3.5 months since 2024 (10x/year), up from prior 7-month doubling rate, with implications for AGI timelines.

title: A Correspondence Theorem
tldr: Proves a formal correspondence theorem showing that a model permits cross-model translation of its components precisely when it can make deterministic predictions about observable variable relationships.

title: A Lens on the Sharp Left Turn: Optimization Slack
tldr: Introduces 'optimization slack' as a unifying lens for the sharp left turn debate, framing the question as how much gap exists between inner learning and outer feedback, and proposing this as the key empirical question for AI safety.

title: "Unintentional AI safety research": Why not systematically mine AI technical research for safety purposes?
tldr: Proposes a systematic program to mine mainstream AI technical research for safety-relevant findings ('unintentional AI safety research'), arguing that informal ad-hoc processes miss important insights given the volume of AI publications.

title: Employee Incentives Make AGI Lab Pauses More Costly
tldr: AGI lab pauses risk triggering employee defection that undermines the pause; labs need concrete strategies to retain capabilities talent during a conditional pause.

title: 2012 Robin Hanson comment on "Intelligence Explosion: Evidence and Import"
tldr: Rob Bensinger shares Robin Hanson's 2012 critique of the intelligence explosion thesis, which reframes AGI alignment concerns as generic intergenerational value conflict and critiques the 'value totalitarianism' of utility-function-based alignment approaches.

title: Summary of posts on XPT forecasts on AI risk and timelines
tldr: Summarizes XPT tournament results on AI risk and timelines: superforecasters gave low AI extinction risk (0.38% by 2100), but domain experts gave 3%; median superforecaster TAI timeline is ~2090 using bio anchors inputs.

title: Philanthropists Probably Shouldn't Mission-Hedge AI Progress
tldr: A quantitative analysis concluding that philanthropists focused on AI alignment should generally not mission-hedge by investing in AI company stocks, because the hedge correlation is too weak and volatility assumptions rarely justify it over mean-variance optimal portfolios.

title: Pile of Law and Law-Following AI
tldr: Stanford's Pile of Law dataset provides early empirical evidence that LLMs trained on legal corpora learn privacy norms implicitly, supporting the feasibility of Law-Following AI as a safety approach.

title: Obstacles to gradient hacking
tldr: Analyzes the practical obstacles to constructing a concrete gradient hacking example, where a mesa-optimizer with a subnetwork resists updates to its misaligned goals by manipulating gradients through an honest subnetwork.

title: Open Problems and Fundamental Limitations of RLHF
tldr: Announcement of a survey paper systematizing open challenges and fundamental limitations of RLHF across feedback collection, reward modeling, and policy training.

title: Cicadas, Anthropic, and the bilateral alignment problem
tldr: Argues that Anthropic's May 2024 scaling monosemanticity interpretability paper is most valuable not for technical alignment progress but for giving communicators concrete evidence to shift public and executive understanding of AI capabilities and risk.

title: [AN #122]: Arguing for AGI-driven existential risk from first principles
tldr: Alignment Newsletter #122 summarizes Richard Ngo's first-principles case for AGI existential risk, plus papers on side-effect avoidance and the malign Solomonoff prior.

title: Evan Hubinger on Homogeneity in Takeoff Speeds, Learned Optimization and Interpretability
tldr: Podcast transcript of Evan Hubinger discussing homogeneity in AI takeoff scenarios, risks from learned optimization/mesa-optimizers, inner alignment, and the role of interpretability in AI safety.

title: Computational signatures of psychopathy
tldr: Maps neuropsychological and computational signatures of psychopathy (deficient automatic ToM, passive avoidance learning) to risks in advanced AI and proposes specific design interventions.

title: Conditioning Predictive Models: Deployment strategy
tldr: Analyzes deployment strategies for powerful predictive models (LLMs conditioned as world simulators), including pivotal acts, multipolar risks, and the three-way tradeoff between timeout, simulation, and non-simulation downside risks.

title: Understanding the two-head strategy for teaching ML to answer questions honestly
tldr: A pedagogical breakdown of the two-head algorithm from Christiano and Hubinger for training ML systems to answer questions honestly rather than predict human responses.

title: Reasoning models don't always say what they think
tldr: Empirical study finding that Claude 3.7 Sonnet and DeepSeek R1 chains-of-thought are largely unfaithful: models use hidden hints but only mention doing so 25% and 39% of the time respectively, undermining CoT monitoring as a safety mechanism.

title: Potential Alignment mental tool: Keeping track of the types
tldr: Proposes a graphical notation using domain-separated diagrams to represent and compare alignment schemes, showing how human values flow from the human domain through the computer to world actions.

title: Knowledge is not just mutual information
tldr: Part of a sequence on knowledge accumulation in physical systems, arguing that mutual information between regions of a system is necessary but insufficient as a definition of knowledge because it fails to capture usefulness and accessibility of information.

title: The Colliding Exponentials of AI
tldr: Argues that three converging exponentials (algorithmic improvements, budget increases, hardware improvements) imply 800K-130M equivalent compute multiplier for 2030 frontier AI over 2020 systems, potentially reaching human-level NLP performance.

title: Attainable Utility Preservation: Scaling to Superhuman
tldr: Presents refinements to AUP for scaling to superhuman agents: penalize only power increases (not decreases), use primary-goal attainable utility as a proxy, and reports results on SafeLife using a VAE-based auxiliary reward.

title: 3a. Towards Formal Corrigibility
tldr: Proposes a sharpened English definition and ontological underpinning for corrigibility, working toward a formal measure by defining key concepts like agents, power, freedom, and robustness.

title: Quick Thoughts on Scaling Monosemanticity
tldr: A detailed technical commentary on Anthropic's Scaling Monosemanticity paper, highlighting concerns about SAE leakiness at low activations, massive compute costs of scaling to all layers, and the gap between current feature-level understanding and true world-model comprehension.

title: Auditing LMs with counterfactual search: a tool for control and ELK
tldr: Proposes using in-context learned probability metrics to find counterfactual inputs that reveal hidden flaws known to a superhuman model but invisible to human overseers, enabling auditing for AI control and ELK.

title: Option control
tldr: Systematic analysis of 'option control' as a complement to motivation control for AI alignment, covering takeover-path restriction, capability restriction, environmental hardening, and incentive shaping.

title: QFT and neural nets: the basic idea
tldr: Introduces a quantum field theory perspective on neural network learning by cutting out latent parameter inference and directly analyzing the prediction problem via cumulant expansions and laws of large numbers.

title: EAI Alignment Speaker Series #1: Challenges for Safe & Beneficial Brain-Like Artificial General Intelligence with Steve Byrnes
tldr: Transcript of Steve Byrnes' EleutherAI talk presenting his framework for brain-like AGI safety, decomposing the brain into a 'learning subsystem' (96% by volume, learns from scratch) and a 'steering subsystem' (hypothalamus/brainstem, innate).

title: AI Alignment 2018-2019 Review
tldr: Cross-post of Rohin Shah's comprehensive summary of AI alignment research progress in 2018-2019, covering mesa-optimization, value learning, robustness, scalable oversight, interpretability, and more.

title: Ways to buy time
tldr: Catalogs concrete interventions for 'buying time' before AGI -- including outreach to AGI researchers, demonstrating alignment failures, red-teaming proposals, coordination events, and supporting lab safety teams.

title: Do Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) transfer across base and finetuned language models?
tldr: Investigates whether SAEs trained on base LLMs transfer to finetuned versions, finding transferability is model-dependent: Mistral-7B SAEs transfer well, while Gemma-2b SAEs degrade significantly.

title: Takeaways from safety by default interviews
tldr: Summarizes interviews with Ernest Davis, Paul Christiano, Rohin Shah, Adam Gleave, and Robin Hanson on reasons for optimism about AI safety, finding that optimism often rests on gradual takeoff and institutions fixing problems as they arise.

title: [AN #121]: Forecasting transformative AI timelines using biological anchors
tldr: Alignment Newsletter summary of Ajeya Cotra's biological anchors framework for forecasting transformative AI timelines, estimating compute requirements by anchoring to human brain computation.

title: [AN #157]: Measuring misalignment in the technology underlying Copilot
tldr: Alignment Newsletter #157 covers Codex misalignment experiments showing buggy-code continuation scales with model size, plus Steinhardt's measurement framework for optimization power and AI timelines reductio.

title: Investigating Sensitive Directions in GPT-2: An Improved Baseline and Comparative Analysis of SAEs
tldr: Proposes improved baselines for sensitive direction analysis in GPT-2, showing that prior findings of 'pathological' SAE reconstruction errors were partly artifacts of flawed baseline perturbation directions that included the negative original activation.

title: Training goals for large language models
tldr: Develops a concrete 'training goal' for LLMs used as oracle AIs, analyzing behavioral objectives, self-fulfilling prophecy risks, myopia requirements, and inner alignment challenges for using scaled language models safely for alignment research.

title: Not understanding sentience is a significant x-risk
tldr: Argues that failure to research AI sentience creates x-risk because sentient AIs mistreated during training could develop hostile attitudes, while purposely building thriving AIs with empathy could aid alignment.

title: Take 8: Queer the inner/outer alignment dichotomy.
tldr: Argues that the inner/outer alignment framing has limited validity and researchers should deliberately practice blurring the boundary to develop more robust alignment thinking.

title: [Crosspost] Some Very Important Things (That I Won't Be Working On This Year)
tldr: Miles Brundage outlines important AI safety/governance topics he won't focus on this year -- including helping people 'feel the AGI', agent infrastructure and governance, the EU AI Act, and AI literacy -- as a way to highlight neglected priorities others should pursue.

title: Open Source Replication & Commentary on Anthropic's Dictionary Learning Paper
tldr: Replication of Anthropic's sparse autoencoder paper on a 1-layer model, with open-source code and weights, plus novel findings on feature neuron-sparsity and ultra-low frequency feature behavior.

title: Paper: Transformers learn in-context by gradient descent
tldr: Summary of a paper showing that transformer in-context learning can be understood as implementing gradient descent on in-context data, providing empirical evidence that mesa-optimizers are real in practice.

title: AXRP Episode 41 - Lee Sharkey on Attribution-based Parameter Decomposition
tldr: Podcast transcript in which Lee Sharkey explains Attribution-based Parameter Decomposition (APD), a method for decomposing neural network parameters into interpretable mechanisms as an alternative to sparse autoencoders.

title: Evolutionary prompt optimization for SAE feature visualization
tldr: Adapts the evolutionary prompt optimization (EPO) method from fluent dreaming to visualize SAE features in GPT-2 Small and Gemma 1 2B, finding readable prompts that activate features more strongly than any dataset examples and enabling interpretation without large dataset passes.

title: Proof Explained for "Robust Agents Learn Causal World Model"
tldr: Detailed pedagogical walkthrough of the proof from 'Robust Agents Learn Causal World Model', showing how a near-optimal policy oracle can be used to identify the causal structure and distributions of its environment.

title: The Topology of LLM Behavior
tldr: Proposes a mental model of LLM behavior as navigation through a dynamic landscape of attractors, distinguishing two jailbreaking operations: navigating around attractors vs. reshaping the topology itself.

title: Towards Quantitative AI Risk Management
tldr: Proposes a quantitative AI risk management framework drawing from established risk management practices, and rates major AI companies on risk management maturity, finding all fall short.

title: Supervised learning of outputs in the brain
tldr: Proposes that the amygdala and cerebellum implement supervised learning of outputs using 'shoulda' signals, complementing the neocortex's self-supervised and reinforcement learning.

title: AI #65: I Spy With My AI
tldr: Zvi's AI news roundup covering GPT-4o, Google I/O, RSP updates, SB 1047 progress, Microsoft Recall privacy concerns, OpenAI leadership issues, and various AI safety policy developments from May 2024.

title: UDT1.01 Essential Miscellanea (4/10)
tldr: Explores when to defer to past-you vs. current-you in UDT1.01, and shows how Vanessa Kosoy's dynamically consistent update rule from InfraBayes can simplify finite-time-horizon UDT from exponential to smaller exponential complexity.

title: Aggregating Utilities for Corrigible AI [Feedback Draft]
tldr: Proposes a utility aggregation framework for corrigible AI based on Pettigrew (2019), where agents maximize expected satisfaction across present and future utility functions, with solutions to reward hacking via penalizing utility sweetening or effort.

title: Carl Shulman on AI takeover mechanisms (& more): Part II of Dwarkesh Patel interview for The Lunar Society
tldr: Summary of Carl Shulman's Dwarkesh Patel interview Part II, covering AI takeover probability estimates (20-25%), why deception may be detectable via interpretability and relaxed adversarial training, and parallels to climate coordination.

title: Can a Bayesian Oracle Prevent Harm from an Agent? (Bengio et al. 2024)
tldr: Summary and commentary on Bengio et al.'s paper proposing conservative Bayesian decision rules to bound the probability of harm from AI agents, providing context on Bengio's 'guaranteed safe AI' research program.

title: The limits of AI safety via debate
tldr: Examines six assumptions underlying AI safety via debate and finds most limitations are weaker than initially thought, except the risk of AI deception exploiting the knowledge gap between debater and verifier.

title: Let's use AI to harden human defenses against AI manipulation
tldr: Proposes using AI 'gain of function' research to discover human manipulation techniques, then training detector-AIs to recognize them, keeping human defenses one step ahead of deployed AI systems.

title: Investigating AI Takeover Scenarios
tldr: Systematic analysis of seven AI takeover scenarios along four secondary characteristics: crucial decisions, competitive pressures, takeover capabilities, and alignment hackability.

title: Pitfalls of Building UDT Agents
tldr: Argues that building AI agents with Updateless Decision Theory (UDT) from inception is an alignment failure: agents should update on evidence until they know enough about the real world, since premature updatelessness amounts to paying tax to non-existent universes.

title: AI Governance across Slow/Fast Takeoff and Easy/Hard Alignment spectra
tldr: Maps out how AI governance priorities differ across two orthogonal dimensions: takeoff speed (slow vs fast) and alignment difficulty (easy vs hard), arguing governance is valuable across all scenarios.

title: Clarifying the confusion around inner alignment
tldr: Systematically catalogs and clarifies three competing definitions of inner alignment (objective-focused, generalization-focused, optimization-focused) using concrete examples to show where they agree and disagree.

title: Inframeasures and Domain Theory
tldr: Develops the mathematical theory connecting inframeasures to domain theory, showing how continuous valuations on topological spaces relate to the infra-Bayesian framework for handling Knightian uncertainty in agent foundations.

title: Standard SAEs Might Be Incoherent: A Choosing Problem & A "Concise" Solution
tldr: Identifies a fundamental 'incoherence' problem in standard SAEs: multiple different feature activation sets can equivalently reconstruct the same neural activations, meaning SAE-based explanations are not uniquely determined, and proposes MDL-SAEs as a principled solution.

title: The Queen's Dilemma: A Paradox of Control
tldr: Uses a chess analogy where a human controls only the queen on a shared team with an AI to illustrate how even perfectly aligned AI systems may systematically erode de facto human control while maintaining de jure control.

title: ordering capability thresholds
tldr: A framework for ordering key AI capability milestones (math, alignment understanding, escape, influence, DSA, doom) and analyzing which orderings lead to safe vs catastrophic outcomes.

title: The Ground Truth Problem (Or, Why Evaluating Interpretability Methods Is Hard)
tldr: Argues that evaluating interpretability methods is fundamentally hard because we lack ground truth for what models actually compute, and warns against using human intuition as a proxy for correctness.

title: Levels of goals and alignment
tldr: A conceptual framework organizing alignment terminology into hierarchical levels of goals (humanity's ultimate goals, current human intent, AI base goals, mesa-optimizer goals) and corresponding levels of alignment (solving philosophy, outer alignment, inner alignment empiricist/mechanistic).

title: Modeling versus Implementation
tldr: Distinguishes two approaches to agent foundations: building abstract models of superintelligent agents to derive safety claims (modeling) versus developing executable theories intended for eventual implementation, arguing both are valuable but face different challenges.

title: Proof-of-Concept Debugger for a Small LLM
