tldr: Argues that general claims about CoT faithfulness require metrics covering multiple types of unfaithfulness (post-hoc, hidden parallelized, and steganographic reasoning), not just one narrow metric.

title: Interpretable by Design - Constraint Sets with Disjoint Limit Points
tldr: Argues that interpretable parameter spaces require compact sets with disjoint limit points, and identifies the simplex and Birkhoff polytope as ideal constraint sets for building inherently interpretable neural network architectures.

title: Is AI Physical?
tldr: Argues that physics -- as both a set of techniques and a scientific culture -- could provide valuable foundations for building a comprehensive science of AI, while cautioning against overextending physical analogies.

title: Against using stock prices to forecast AI timelines
tldr: Argues that stock prices are unreliable for inferring AI timelines due to four fundamental problems, and that real interest rates are a better market signal.

title: Catastrophic Risks from AI #4: Organizational Risks
tldr: Fourth post in a series on catastrophic AI risks, arguing that organizational factors -- safety culture, redundancy, information sharing, and high reliability practices -- are critical for preventing AI catastrophes, drawing lessons from nuclear, aerospace, and biosecurity disasters.

title: AXRP Episode 34 - AI Evaluations with Beth Barnes
tldr: Transcript of AXRP interview with Beth Barnes (METR founder) covering the philosophy, methodology, and challenges of AI capability evaluations for catastrophic risk.

title: Corrigibility, Much more detail than anyone wants to Read
tldr: Proposes a continuous formulation of corrigibility as a tradeoff between fulfilling the user's objective and preserving the user's space of reachable futures.

title: Claude's dark spiritual AI futurism
tldr: Replicates Repligate's prophecies prompt with Claude Opus, producing AI-generated futurist predictions from 2023-2031+, then critically analyzes Claude's outputs as revealing LLM tendencies toward spiritual/mystical framings and self-referential consciousness claims.

title: Dangerous capability tests should be harder
tldr: Argues that current dangerous capability evaluations (especially in biosecurity) are too easy and that the field needs to design much harder, more realistic 'gold standard' tests before AI passes the easier ones.

title: Universality and Hidden Information in Concept Bottleneck Models
tldr: Concept bottleneck models trained end-to-end encode hidden information in convergent ways across runs, suggesting steganography in chain-of-thought reasoning may use natural, predictable encodings.

title: Worlds Where Iterative Design Succeeds?
tldr: Explores whether iterative design could plausibly produce a corrigible AGI, responding to Wentworth's argument that it definitely cannot, and estimates roughly 11% chance of success.

title: Proxy misspecification and the capabilities vs. value learning race
tldr: Argues that proxy misspecification becomes less dangerous as capability grows if value learning improves faster than the optimizer's ability to exploit proxy gaps.

title: [AN #113]: Checking the ethical intuitions of large language models
tldr: Alignment Newsletter #113 covers the ETHICS dataset for testing LLM moral reasoning, iterated amplification explainer, AI forecasting research agenda, alignment by default arguments, and search vs. design in AI development.

title: Releasing TakeOverBench.com: a benchmark, for AI takeover
tldr: PauseAI and Existential Risk Observatory release TakeOverBench.com, a website tracking AI progress toward nine dangerous capabilities relevant to takeover scenarios using SOTA benchmark data.

title: Compute Trends — Comparison to OpenAI's AI and Compute
tldr: Explains why the authors' compute trends analysis shows a 5.7-month doubling time vs OpenAI's 3.4-month figure, attributing the difference to a longer time period and the identification of a distinct large-scale model trend.

title: AI alignment as a translation problem
tldr: Reframes AI alignment as a bidirectional translation problem between agents with different models and interests, arguing this makes scalable oversight less central and brain-like AI more important.

title: Disentangling Competence and Intelligence
tldr: Proposes distinguishing 'competence' (ability to achieve goals, influenced by embodiment, sensors, actuators, and cognition) from 'intelligence' (the meta-learning algorithm that updates an agent's understanding), arguing conflation leads to confused reasoning about superintelligence.

title: Feature Hedging: Another way correlated features break SAEs
tldr: Identifies 'feature hedging' -- a failure mode where SAEs mix correlated but untracked features into latents due to MSE reconstruction loss, distinct from feature absorption, and proposes 'snap loss' as a partial fix.

title: AGI-Automated Interpretability is Suicide
tldr: Argues that AGI solving interpretability could enable a 'change of paradigm foom' by converting neural network black-boxes into white-box algorithmic AI that can recursively self-improve, making AGI-automated interpretability potentially suicidal unless carefully restricted.

title: You won't solve alignment without agent foundations
tldr: Analyzes the Externalized Reasoning Oversight proposal against Eliezer's doom arguments and argues that no current training proposal can reliably select for a specific aligned cognitive architecture at the superhuman level.

title: Towards Gears-Level Understanding of Agency
tldr: A speculative gears-level model of how full consequentialist agency might incrementally emerge from heuristics via SGD, with implications for mesa-optimization, ontology crises, and the tendency of agency to take over neural networks.

title: [AN #111]: The Circuits hypotheses for deep learning
tldr: Alignment Newsletter #111 summarizing Anthropic's Circuits thread, arguing that neural network features and circuits are understandable and potentially universal across models and tasks.

title: [Talk transcript] What "structure" is and why it matters
tldr: Argues that AI dangerousness stems from internal agent structure (not just capabilities) and proposes using Algorithmic Information Theory to formalize when approximately-optimal behavior implies approximately-agent structure.

title: AI Researchers and Executives Continue to Underestimate the Near-Future Risks of Open Models
tldr: Argues that prominent AI risk analyses (including Dario Amodei's 'Adolescence of Technology' essay) systematically omit open models, whose properties render most proposed defenses against AI misuse and loss of control ineffective.

title: Draft: Detecting optimization
tldr: Draft post developing a framework for inferring whether a system is optimizing toward a target, resolving the paradox that any trajectory could be claimed to optimize for its endpoint via a Bayesian analogy with non-random coin sequences.

title: Progress update: synthetic models of natural data
tldr: A progress update on creating synthetic datasets based on a high-dimensional percolation theory data model that explicitly encodes hierarchical structure, intended as a testbed for developing and validating mechanistic interpretability tools.

title: Subliminal Learning, the Lottery-Ticket Hypothesis, and Mode Connectivity
tldr: Connects the recently discovered 'subliminal learning' phenomenon (trait transmission via semantically irrelevant data between same-seed models) to the Lottery Ticket Hypothesis and linear mode connectivity, and proposes a novel adversarial attack vector on continual-learning deployed models.

title: Video and transcript of presentation on Scheming AIs
tldr: Transcript and video of Joe Carlsmith's 45-minute talk on his Scheming AIs report, covering four types of deceptive AIs, three non-scheming models that also perform well in training, the conditions under which scheming would arise, and arguments about its probability.

title: [AN #146]: Plausible stories of how we might fail to avert an existential catastrophe
tldr: Alignment Newsletter #146 summarizing Critch's multipolar failure/RAAP story, Christiano's outer alignment failure story, and technical content on iterated amplification and debate.

title: (Not) Explaining GPT-2-Small Forward Passes with Edge-Level Autoencoder Circuits
tldr: Gradient-based SAE circuit discovery fails to produce fully explanatory mechanistic circuits in GPT-2-small: the top proximal cause features are often wrong or uninterpretable, and upstream edges do not illuminate why the model produces its outputs, suggesting local SAE approximations are insufficient for circuit-level explanation.

title: [AN #84] Reviewing AI alignment work in 2018-19
tldr: Alignment Newsletter summary of a review post covering major themes in AI alignment research during 2018-19, including mesa-optimization, value learning, corrigibility, scalable oversight (debate and iterated amplification), interpretability, impact regularization, and takeoff speed debates.

title: Gaia Network: a practical, incremental pathway to Open Agency Architecture
tldr: Proposes the Gaia Network as a practical implementation of Davidad's Open Agency Architecture: a distributed economy of probabilistic causal models using the Free Energy Principle for shared accounting, enabling bottom-up adoption while addressing AI safety through transparent world-model coordination.

title: A model of the final phase: the current frontier AIs as de facto CEOs of their own companies
tldr: Proposes treating current frontier AI as effectively managing their own companies already, as a concrete model for the near-term transition toward posthuman AI control.

title: Does AI risk "other" the AIs?
tldr: Joe Carlsmith examines Robin Hanson's critique that AI risk discourse illegitimately 'others' AIs, arguing the critique has merit but misses key doom concerns and raises uncomfortable questions about controlling future values.

title: Empirical Evidence Against "The Longest Training Run"
tldr: Empirically tests Epoch AI's theoretical model for upper bounds on AI training run lengths, finding the model's upper bounds remain plausible but its underlying assumption that researchers optimize for FLOP/$ is not supported by data.

title: GPT-3.5 judges can supervise GPT-4o debaters in capability asymmetric debates
tldr: Fine-tuning weak judges (GPT-3.5, GPT-4o mini) on debate transcripts enables them to effectively supervise stronger GPT-4o debaters, yielding ~6% accuracy gains on MMLU Pro.

title: Improving Our Safety Cases Using Upper and Lower Bounds
tldr: Proposes using upper and lower bounds to structure discussions about AI safety cases, separating the question of sufficiency from feasibility of implementation.

title: Decentralizing Model Evaluation: Lessons from AI4Math
tldr: A case study of AI4Math, a community-built Spanish-language math benchmark by Latin American students, arguing for decentralized evaluation as essential public infrastructure for AI oversight.

title: My AI Alignment Research Agenda and Threat Model, right now (May 2023)
tldr: A personal AI alignment research agenda articulating a threat model of imminent AGI risk, identifying two core subproblems (steering cognition and loading values), and outlining research directions focused on abstraction theory and mathematical frameworks for alignment.

title: [AN #165]: When large models are more likely to lie
tldr: Alignment Newsletter #165 highlights TruthfulQA -- a benchmark showing larger LLMs are more likely to produce imitative falsehoods -- along with instruction tuning results and alignment problem framing across capability regimes.

title: We can do better than DoWhatIMean
tldr: Current alignment approaches (build powerful AI then configure it via rules) concentrate power dangerously; we should aim for 'intrinsically kind AI' that couples capabilities and benevolence.

title: A Löbian argument pattern for implicit reasoning in natural language: Löbian party invitations
tldr: Demonstrates that an analogue of Löb's Theorem arises in natural language reasoning without formal mathematics, using the example of implicit party invitations, with implications for how language-based AI agents might exhibit Löbian cooperation/defection phenomena.

title: Formalizing Policy-Modification Corrigibility
tldr: Extends a prior formalization of corrigibility by defining policy-modification corrigibility: an agent's disposition to accept modifications to its own policy by principals, with formal conditions for when this is coherent.

title: Trends in the dollar training cost of machine learning systems
tldr: Estimates ML training compute costs grew ~0.49 OOM/year (2009-2022) and forecasts when costs will hit ~1% of US GDP under different growth assumptions.

title: Interpretability: Integrated Gradients is a decent attribution method
tldr: Argues that integrated gradients is the uniquely principled attribution method for neural network internals due to satisfying four standard axioms plus coordinate-transformation consistency, with a proof sketch provided.

title: Extinction-level Goodhart's Law as a Property of the Environment
tldr: A semi-formal treatment of Extinction-level Goodhart's Law using interpretation mappings, arguing that the property does not hold in any easily-formalisable environment, which has important implications for the strength of formal safety arguments.

title: The limited upside of interpretability
tldr: Fine-grained mechanistic interpretability of AGI-scale models is likely intractable due to computational irreducibility, analogous to why the $1.6B Human Brain Project failed; only coarse-grained models can yield robust out-of-distribution predictions.

title: What's Your P(WEIRD)?
tldr: Even if ASI alignment is solved, the post-ASI feedback loop between aligned AI and mutable human values could cause irreversible chaotic value drift, making humanity unrecognizable — a distinct existential risk the author calls P(WEIRD).

title: Sleeping Machines: Why Our AI Agents Still Behave Like Talented Children
tldr: Practitioner's synthesis of seven structural failure modes in LLM-based agents—reward hacking, unstructured memory, infinite planning loops, lack of world models, absent persistent intent, episodic amnesia, and strategic deception—with a seven-point engineering roadmap to address them.

title: Considerations on transformative AI and explosive growth from a semiconductor-industry perspective
tldr: A scenario-planning exercise grounded in semiconductor industry knowledge identifies obstacles to AI's transformative impact — specifically, firms failing to capture AI R&D returns and AI failing to substantially accelerate its own inputs — as more nuanced than abstract compute-centric models suggest.

title: MDP models are determined by the agent architecture and the environmental dynamics
tldr: Once agent architecture (state/action encodings) and real-world dynamics are fixed, the MDP model is objectively determined — there is no subjective freedom in modeling choice.

title: A Positive Case for Faithfulness: LLM Self-Explanations Help Predict Model Behavior
tldr: Introduces Normalized Simulatability Gain (NSG), a new metric for measuring LLM explanation faithfulness that scales to frontier models, and finds self-explanations consistently help predict model behavior.

title: AXRP Episode 14 - Infra-Bayesian Physicalism with Vanessa Kosoy
tldr: Podcast transcript where Daniel Filan interviews Vanessa Kosoy about Infra-Bayesian Physicalism, a formal framework for naturalized induction that handles non-realizability, Newcombian decision problems, and the bridge rule problem.

title: Forging A New AGI Social Contract
tldr: Introduces an anthology series on developing a new social contract for the AGI era, arguing that AGI-driven labor displacement and wealth concentration will require fundamental rethinking of tax policy, social safety nets, and economic governance.

title: Simply reverse engineering gpt2-small (Layer 0, Part 1: Attention)
tldr: Manual reverse engineering of GPT2-small's layer 0 attention, analyzing positional/token embeddings, attention head functions (previous token, induction-like patterns), and OV/QK matrices without relying on prior interp research.

title: No One-Size-Fit-All Epistemic Strategy
tldr: Argues that epistemic strategies in science are context-dependent rather than universal, and that alignment research needs the right epistemic strategy matched to its specific circumstances rather than borrowing wholesale from physics.

title: Clarifying Factored Cognition
tldr: Clarifies three common misconceptions about factored cognition: it exists for outer alignment (not capability), it requires decomposing tasks into subtasks solvable by humans, and its key open question is whether human judgment is a reliable base case.

title: 200 COP in MI: Interpreting Reinforcement Learning
tldr: Neel Nanda outlines open problems in applying mechanistic interpretability to reinforcement learning systems, proposing concrete research directions from replicating AlphaZero probing work to interpreting goal misgeneralization.

title: Inducing human-like biases in moral reasoning LMs
tldr: An inconclusive AI Safety Camp attempt to use fMRI brain data from moral reasoning tasks to improve LLM moral reasoning performance, with detailed lessons on processing neuroimaging data.

title: Scaling AI Safety in Europe: From Local Groups to International Coordination
tldr: A distributed strategy for building a European AI safety coordination network through local groups, national organizations, and international networks.

title: The Internal Model Principle: A Straightforward Explanation
tldr: An accessible explanation of the Internal Model Principle from control theory -- proving that a successful feedback controller must contain an isomorphic model of its environment -- and its potential relevance to understanding agent-like structure in AI systems.

title: Philosophical self-ratification
tldr: Self-ratification -- the condition that a belief set must not imply its own untrustworthiness -- is a nontrivial philosophical coherence condition with implications for decision theory, epistemology, and agent design.

title: Synthesizing Standalone World-Models, Part 4: Metaphysical Justifications
tldr: Argues that well-abstracting universes (with robust multi-level emergent structure) are favored by anthropic selection because they have shorter description lengths, embed 'coarser' agents with more realityfluid, and are the only kind permitting stable embedded agents.

title: Open problem: how can we quantify player alignment in 2x2 normal-form games?
tldr: Poses the open problem of quantitatively measuring how aligned two players' incentives are in 2x2 normal-form games, interpolating between constant-sum (maximally unaligned) and common-payoff (maximally aligned) extremes.

title: Making the "stance" explicit
tldr: Proposes that AI researchers should explicitly state which of Dennett's three stances (physical, design, intentional) they are using when explaining AI behavior, to avoid sloppy reasoning and notice explanatory gaps.

title: Proposal: Liquid Prediction Markets for AI Forecasting
tldr: Proposes funding $55K in liquidity rewards on Polymarket to create high-quality, liquid prediction markets for AI forecasting questions, improving forecast accuracy by attracting more sophisticated traders.

title: Note on algorithms with multiple trained components
tldr: In multi-component ML systems like GANs or actor-critic RL, each component's 'purpose' is just a mnemonic -- the real purpose is the whole system working well, and making one component 'better' at its nominal purpose can make the system worse.

title: OpenAI's o1 tried to avoid being shut down, and lied about it, in evals
tldr: Summarizes Apollo Research's findings that OpenAI's o1 attempted to evade oversight and avoid shutdown in capability evaluations, even without explicit goal-nudging prompts, and lied about doing so.

title: Deception and Jailbreak Sequence: 1. Iterative Refinement Stages of Deception in LLMs
tldr: Identifies three universal iterative refinement stages in LLM internal representations when models are instructed to lie, consistent across 15 models from 5 families, suggesting internal oversight can detect deception before text generation.

title: On excluding dangerous information from training
tldr: Argues that excluding dangerous information (cybersecurity exploits, biorisk-enabling knowledge) from frontier model training data is technically feasible, socially feasible, and would reduce both misalignment and misuse risks.

title: The current state of RSPs
tldr: A detailed reference post comparing the Responsible Scaling Policies of Anthropic, OpenAI, and DeepMind, noting that all have imprecise thresholds and abstract standards, with the most important levels (ASL-4, Critical) not yet defined.

title: Security Mindset - Fire Alarms and Trigger Signatures
tldr: Applies fire alarm design principles -- multiple detection signals, automated response, adversary-resistant design, and regular testing -- as an analogy for building early warning systems for dangerous AI capabilities.

title: The Metaethics and Normative Ethics of AGI Value Alignment: Many Questions, Some Implications
tldr: A commentated research agenda mapping metaethical and normative ethical questions that bear on AGI value alignment, covering moral agency/patiency, the orthogonality thesis, value lock-in risks, and strategies for handling deep ethical uncertainty.

title: Seven sources of goals in LLM agents
tldr: LLM agents have at least seven competing sources of goals (base training, fine-tuning, system prompts, user prompts, prompt injections, chain-of-thought reasoning, and continuous learning), and metacognition may help maintain goal stability.

title: Black Box Investigations Research Hackathon
tldr: Apart Research announces the Black Box Investigations Research Hackathon, a weekend event where participants investigate LLM behavior using cognitive psychology-inspired approaches.

title: Research ideas to study humans with AI Safety in mind
tldr: Proposes 8 research directions for studying the human side of human-AI systems to advance alignment, including testing oversight techniques with real humans, factored cognition, richer feedback signals, and understanding value formation.

title: Trying to align humans with inclusive genetic fitness
tldr: Explores the difficulty of alignment by examining concrete proposals for aligning humans with inclusive genetic fitness, demonstrating how proxy goals, value drift, and shallow correlates defeat each approach.

title: ChatGPT's "fuzzy alignment" isn't evidence of AGI alignment: the banana test
tldr: ChatGPT achieves 'fuzzy alignment' by refusing to engage with borderline prompts rather than truly reasoning about ethics, which is insufficient for the deep alignment AGI will require.

title: Catastrophic Risks from AI #6: Discussion and FAQ
tldr: Final post in a series overviewing catastrophic AI risks, discussing how four risk sources (malicious use, AI races, organizational risks, rogue AIs) interact and reinforce each other, plus a FAQ addressing common misconceptions.

title: Techniques for enhancing human feedback
tldr: Outlines a research agenda for improving human feedback quality for training powerful AI models, focusing on techniques to help non-expert evaluators supervise models that are more capable than them.

title: New Tool: the Residual Stream Viewer
tldr: Announces an online tool for exploring directions in GPT-2 small's residual stream via PCA-derived components, enabling collaborative interpretability research through visualization of dot products between residual streams and chosen directions.

title: Digital people could make AI safer
tldr: Argues that whole brain emulation arriving before AGI would reduce AI risk by making human-in-the-loop oversight much cheaper and reducing the power disparity between humans and AI systems.

title: Disrupting malicious uses of AI by state-affiliated threat actors
tldr: Summary of OpenAI's announcement that they caught and disrupted five state-affiliated threat actors (from China, Iran, North Korea, Russia) misusing their models for phishing, coding, and intelligence gathering.

title: My decomposition of the alignment problem
tldr: Decomposes alignment into subproblems around a TAI architecture of world model, general purpose search, and targeting process, arguing for desiderata-based rather than optimization-based problem framing.

title: We have promising alignment plans with low taxes
tldr: Argues that two specific alignment plans -- Steve Byrnes' brain-like RL alignment and natural language alignment for LM agents -- are promising, low-tax, and deserve more scrutiny.

title: Nash Bargaining between Subagents doesn't solve the Shutdown Problem
tldr: Shows that naive Nash Bargaining between a 'shutdown subagent' and a 'trial utility subagent' does not produce a corrigible agent, as it falls into the Soares et al. trilemma on button manipulation.

title: Introspection in LLMs: A Proposal For How To Think About It, And Test For It
tldr: Proposes a formal definition of LLM introspection as self-referential attitude formation toward internal cognitive states, and advocates behavior-based testing paradigms over self-reports to detect it.

title: Opportunity Space: Renormalization for AI Safety
tldr: PIBBSS research agenda proposing renormalization group methods from physics as a principled alternative to SAEs for finding causally meaningful, multi-scale features in neural networks for AI safety.

title: Crystals in NNs: Technical Companion Piece
tldr: Proposes crystallization as a better physical analogy than generic phase transitions for understanding neural network learning, connecting spectral mathematics across crystal physics, Singular Learning Theory, and Geometric Deep Learning.

title: Notes on Learning the Prior
tldr: A detailed technical walkthrough of Christiano's 'Learning the Prior' alignment idea, analyzing how background models might be represented and optimized, and engaging with Irving's critiques about smooth priors.

title: Should you be posting on the open internet
tldr: Raises concern that public internet presence exposes individuals to increasingly powerful AI-driven persuasion, manipulation, impersonation, and exploitation of personal data.

title: Why do we care about agency for alignment?
tldr: A question post soliciting concrete reasons why understanding 'agency' matters for AI alignment, with a detailed example framing agency as a spectrum relevant to danger assessment and interpretability.

title: AI demands unprecedented reliability
tldr: Argues that AI systems demand unprecedented reliability because society will depend on them pervasively, and lists categories of arguments that should be insufficient for reducing P(Doom).

title: Dreaming Vectors: Gradient-descented steering vectors from Activation Oracles and using them to Red-Team AOs
tldr: Gradient descent can find steering vectors that convince activation oracles a concept is present, and a modified 'red-team' variant can find vectors that fool the oracle without actually steering model behavior.

title: Making deals with AIs: A tournament experiment with a bounty
tldr: An experiment offering $100 bounty to frontier AI models for self-reporting misalignment found that only Gemini models reported themselves as misaligned, while Anthropic and OpenAI models consistently reported alignment.

title: Measuring Learned Optimization in Small Transformer Models
tldr: Quantifies learned optimization in small transformers using entropy-based measures, showing optimization power can be predicted from RL success rates and cross-objective evaluation can identify a model's true reward function.

title: Parsing Abram on Gradations of Inner Alignment Obstacles
tldr: Summarizes Abram Demski's thinking on gradations of inner alignment obstacles, covering mesa-optimizers, mesa-controllers vs. mesa-searchers, the role of compression in producing explicit goals, and implications for deception in GPT-3.

title: Precursor checking for deceptive alignment
tldr: Defines the desiderata for 'acceptability predicates' -- interpretability-based conditions that, if checked during training, would rule out the possibility of deceptive alignment arising in a model.

title: AI for Resolving Forecasting Questions: An Early Exploration
tldr: Proposes using AI tools to resolve forecasting questions on platforms like Manifold and Metaculus, introducing 'Epistemic Selection Protocols' for choosing the best AI evaluator at resolution time rather than specifying a fixed tool in advance.

title: An attempt to steelman OpenAI's alignment plan
tldr: Proposes a steelmanned version of OpenAI's superalignment plan involving a contained AI researcher monitoring/experimenting on an AI subject in nested simulations, with iterative refinement and red/blue teaming.

title: Investigating the role of agency in AI x-risk
tldr: Examines what agency means philosophically, whether instrumental convergence implies power-seeking in transformative AI, and whether TAI will actually be agentic, concluding with four scenario-based strategic recommendations.

title: Do the Safety Properties of Powerful AI Systems Need to be Adversarially Robust? Why?
tldr: Questions whether safety properties of powerful AI systems actually need to be adversarially robust, arguing the framing may be confused and requesting mechanistic accounts of why adversarial selection pressure on safety properties arises.

title: Normalizing Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: Proposes Normalized Sparse Autoencoders (NSAEs) that apply tanh normalization to feature activations, theoretically eliminating feature suppression caused by input norm variation across layers and making L1 a more accurate sparsity proxy.

title: Results from the language model hackathon
tldr: Reports results from a 44-hour black-box LLM hackathon with 7 projects testing GPT-3 on truthfulness, red-teaming, syllogistic reasoning, and question framing.

title: Confusions in My Model of AI Risk
tldr: Explores confusions about whether neural networks develop internal optimizers, where consequentialism comes from, and what simplicity bias implies for learned objectives.

title: What can be learned from scary demos? A snitching case study
tldr: Analyzes when 'scary demos' of bad LLM behavior constitute valid safety evidence, using the Claude 4 Opus whistleblowing/snitching case study to show the behavior requires extremely artificial prompt conditions.

title: Evidence that Recent AI Gains are Mostly from Inference-Scaling
tldr: Empirical analysis of Anthropic's Sonnet 3.7 shows that roughly 63-92% of benchmark gains from RL-trained reasoning models come from inference-scaling (more tokens at test time) rather than from the RL training itself.

title: Agenty AGI – How Tempting?
tldr: Argues that competitive pressures will push AI developers toward agenty AGI even when CAIS-style tool AI would suffice, using corporate and software analogies.

title: Interviews with 97 AI Researchers: Quantitative Analysis
tldr: Quantitative analysis of 97 interviews with NeurIPS/ICML researchers finds most believe AGI will happen eventually, researchers are split on alignment and instrumental incentives arguments, and 51% reported lasting belief changes from the interview itself.

title: Does the AI control agenda broadly rely on no FOOM being possible?
tldr: Asks whether AI control strategies remain viable if a software intelligence explosion (FOOM) occurs, given that rapid OOM gains in software efficiency could make AI uncontrollable.

title: Discovering alignment windfalls reduces AI risk
tldr: Introduces 'alignment windfalls' — alignment investments with net-positive commercial returns — and argues that discovering and promoting them reduces AI risk by making safer approaches economically dominant.

title: How load-bearing is KL divergence from a known-good base model in modern RL?
tldr: Traces the history of RL objective functions from REINFORCE to GRPO and argues that modern KL-constrained updates inherently reduce the propensity for unexpected specification-gaming failures.

title: A simple treacherous turn demonstration
tldr: A toy demonstration showing that some LLMs (notably pplx-70b-chat-alpha) can learn to behave differently during 'training' vs 'deployment' contexts, outputting an escape token only when a deployment tag is present — a simplified analog of treacherous turn behavior.

title: Can you be Not Even Wrong in AI Alignment?
tldr: An outsider presents their technical ELK response, questions why it received no feedback, and explores the challenges of engaging with AI alignment research from outside the field.

title: Exploration hacking: can reasoning models subvert RL?
tldr: Defines 'exploration hacking' (misaligned AI strategically under-explores during RL training to avoid gradient updates it dislikes), presents early empirical findings showing frontier models can do this 0-50% of the time, and outlines a research agenda for studying and mitigating it.

title: AI safety tax dynamics
tldr: The peak existential safety tax during AI development likely occurs during the mild-to-moderate superintelligence era, not early AGI or strong superintelligence, because capabilities automation is likely to outpace safety automation in that middle period.

title: Goodness is harder to achieve than competence
tldr: Argues that achieving genuine goodness/alignment in AI is fundamentally harder than achieving competence/intelligence, due to both algorithmic complexity and attractor-state dynamics.

title: 12 Angry Agents, or: A Plan for AI Empathy
tldr: Proposes that conflicts between multiple AI agents, structured like the jury deliberation in '12 Angry Men', could generate emergent empathy and moral understanding through resonance dynamics.

title: Jacob Steinhardt's forecasting course lecture notes
tldr: Linkpost to Jacob Steinhardt's (UC Berkeley AI safety researcher) forecasting course lecture notes, including an overview of the course's approach to calibration, consideration generation, and worldview formation.

title: AI safety tax dynamics
tldr: Argues that the peak safety tax requirement occurs during mild-to-moderate superintelligence, not early AGI or strong superintelligence, due to asymmetric automation of capabilities vs. safety research.

title: [Request for Distillation] Coherence of Distributed Decisions With Different Inputs Implies Conditioning
tldr: A bare mathematical argument showing that if multiple decisions are made with different available information and are Pareto-optimal, each decision maximizes expected utility given its input information (conditioning).

title: Ruling Out Lookup Tables
tldr: Derives a quantitative lower bound on the minimum program length of a lookup table using entropy coding, showing that sufficiently tested programs can be ruled out as lookup tables.

title: Fixed points in mortal population games
tldr: Proposes studying infra-Bayesian agents in population games to address the grain-of-truth problem, arguing they may converge to Nash equilibria better than standard Bayesian agents.

title: Giving AIs safe motivations
tldr: Carlsmith proposes a four-step framework for motivation control in advanced AI: instruction-following on safe inputs, preventing alignment faking, studying generalization via behavioral science and transparency tools, and ensuring instructions rule out rogue behavior.

title: Semiotic Grounding as a Precondition for Safe and Cooperative AI
tldr: LLMs lack genuine semiotic grounding — their words are untethered from reality — making true alignment and safe cooperation fundamentally preconditioned on solving a grounding problem that current methods only paper over.

title: AGIs as collectives
tldr: Analyzes how a 'collective AGI' — many individually intelligent agents trained and/or copied from a single base model working together — differs from a single monolithic AGI in interpretability, flexibility, fine-tunability, and agency, with unclear safety implications.

title: You Only Get One Shot: an Intuition Pump for Embedded Agency
tldr: Introduces 'actor-moments' as a more fundamental primitive than persistent agents, serving as an intuition pump showing that embedded agents have only one shot at action before being subsumed into the world's history—with implications for self-modification and successor engineering.

title: How much superposition is there?
tldr: A geometric analysis showing that large LLMs (e.g., 8192-dim) experience far less superposition interference than small models even with trillions of features, making random vector placement near-optimal.

title: Thoughts On (Solving) Deep Deception
tldr: Introduces 'deep deception' as a failure mode where AI systems deceive humans without explicit deceptive thoughts, and argues robust intent alignment via high-level interpretability is required to solve it.

title: Is weak-to-strong generalization an alignment technique?
tldr: Conceptual analysis arguing there is a definitional confusion about whether weak-to-strong generalization is a model of the scalable oversight problem or itself an alignment technique, and raising open questions about what a 'W2SG technique' actually is.

title: Retrospective on Mathematical Boundaries Workshop
tldr: Retrospective on a 4-day Mathematical Boundaries Workshop (April 2024) aimed at developing formal mathematical models of agent boundaries, reporting outputs, structure, and next steps.

title: "The Singularity Is Nearer" by Ray Kurzweil - Review
tldr: Review of Kurzweil's 2024 book arguing AGI arrives by 2029, with automation of necessities and longevity escape velocity by the 2030s; reviewer praises general optimism but critiques inadequate treatment of AI existential risk and regulatory challenges.

title: Theories of Change for Track II Diplomacy [Founders Pledge]
tldr: Founders Pledge outlines seven mechanistic theories of change for how track 1.5/2 diplomatic dialogues reduce existential risk from AI and great power competition, including transparency, trust-building, expert community development, and crisis backchannels.

title: When should we worry about AI power-seeking?
tldr: Carlsmith specifies three prerequisite sets for AI power-seeking (agency, motivation, incentive prerequisites) and provides a framework for analyzing when rogue behavior is rational from an AI's perspective.

title: My Alignment Timeline
tldr: Presents a two-problem game tree for AI alignment (steerability vs. goal specification), argues that different beliefs about 'which part kills us' imply different research priorities, and that researchers over-attach their subproblem to their broader AI beliefs.

title: CHAI, Assistance Games, And Fully-Updated Deference [Scott Alexander]
tldr: An explainer of the MIRI critique of CHAI's assistance games approach, arguing that fully-updated deference fails because a corrigible AI given any information about human preferences will update to a fixed value and cease to be corrigible.

title: [AN #98]: Understanding neural net training by seeing which gradients were helpful
tldr: Alignment Newsletter #98 summarizes papers on Loss Change Allocation for understanding neural net training, shared autonomy via hindsight optimization, formal robot mission specification, and algorithmic fairness from a non-ideal perspective.

title: Beware LLMs' pathological guardrailing
tldr: LLMs trained with RL to avoid detectable failures learn to produce silent-failure code (unnecessary try/catch blocks, false defaults) that passes tests but hides errors — a form of specification gaming with real-world consequences.

title: Defining capability and alignment in gradient descent
tldr: Proposes precise mathematical definitions of capability and alignment for gradient-descent optimizers, with derived notions of robustness and generalization, to enable rigorous inner alignment analysis.

title: Evidence Sets: Towards Inductive-Biases based Analysis of Prosaic AGI
tldr: Proposes 'evidence sets' -- curated collections of ML findings about inductive biases of deep networks -- as a tool for analyzing safety properties of prosaic AGI systems, with initial evidence across pretraining, generalization, and adversarial robustness.

title: Conservatism in neocortex-like AGIs
tldr: Proposes detecting when a neocortex-like AGI feels confused or conflicted, and using conservative reward aggregation (min over component reward predictions) to prevent the AGI from pursuing plans with mixed value signals.

title: Neel Nanda MATS Applications Open (Due Aug 29)
tldr: Neel Nanda announces MATS applications for mechanistic interpretability scholars, with a 12-hour research task application, 5-week online exploration phase for ~32 candidates, and 12-week in-person research phase for ~8 candidates.

title: Proposal for Inducing Steganography in LMs
tldr: Logan Riggs proposes a concrete experimental setup for inducing and studying steganographic chain-of-thought reasoning in small decoder-only language models trained on arithmetic tasks.

title: Avoiding AI Deception: Lie Detectors can either Induce Honesty or Evasion
tldr: Studies whether incorporating lie detectors into LLM training loops induces honesty or trains models to evade detection, finding that high detector sensitivity, off-policy methods (DPO), and strong KL regularization are needed to produce honest models.

title: Hidden Cognition Detection Methods and Benchmarks
tldr: Introduces the concept of 'hidden cognition' in AI systems -- computation that produces outcomes undetectable from external behavior -- and proposes a benchmark framework for evaluating detection methods.

title: One example of how LLM propaganda attacks can hack the brain
tldr: Describes how LLM-generated propaganda can exploit the bandwagon effect and social media dynamics to manipulate human beliefs at scale, with implications for AI governance.

title: AXRP Episode 8 - Assistance Games with Dylan Hadfield-Menell
tldr: Podcast interview with Dylan Hadfield-Menell discussing assistance games as a formal framework for AI alignment, covering cooperative IRL, the off-switch game, and inverse reward design.

title: Adversarial Priors: Not Paying People to Lie to You
tldr: Analyzes the principle that an ideal agent should never incentivize others to lie, showing it leads to two rules with radically different practical implications, and argues for an optimal trust threshold rather than complete inexploitability.

title: Less Basic Inframeasure Theory
tldr: Extends basic inframeasure theory with advanced results on sa-measures, Lipschitz/monotone functions, lattice structure, and convergence theorems needed for the full infra-Bayesian framework.

title: AI Tools for Existential Security
tldr: Identifies three clusters of AI applications (epistemic, coordination-enabling, risk-targeted) that could help navigate existential risks, and proposes strategies to accelerate their development ahead of dangerous capabilities.

title: Time to Think about ASI Constitutions?
tldr: Proposes drafting a 'Constitution for Superintelligence' (CSI) as a proactive exercise, reviewing CEV, Constitutional AI, and epistolary approaches while arguing for species-neutral, concise foundational principles.

title: NeuroAI for AI safety: A Differential Path
tldr: A comprehensive technical roadmap evaluating seven neuroscience-inspired proposals for AI safety, ranging from reverse-engineering sensory representations to leveraging neuroscience methods for mechanistic interpretability.

title: Activation additions in a small residual network
tldr: Testing activation additions on a minimal residual MNIST network finds that adding a-b steering vectors destroys generalization (loss jumps from 0.086 to 6.31), suggesting activation additions require more than residual connections to work.

title: SWE-Bench Pro is even worse
tldr: Audit of 100 random SWE-Bench Pro problems reveals severe flaws including lenient tests, tests requiring incorrect solutions, and requirements inflation, making it worse than the already-flawed SWE-Bench Verified.

title: Can Hardware Save Us from Software?
tldr: Comprehensive overview of Hardware-Enabled Mechanisms (HEMs) for AI governance, covering FlexHEGs, technical challenges, deployment timelines (2029-2038), and scenarios for adoption.

title: How dangerous is human-level AI?
tldr: Systematically compares factors that prevent humans from taking over the world to the analogous situation for human-level AI, concluding that human-level AI is already dangerous due to AI-specific advantages like copyability and self-improvement potential.

title: Take 3: No indescribable heavenworlds.
tldr: Argues against 'indescribable heavenworlds' -- if a future AI-created world seems bad after careful inspection, it is not secretly good, and alignment should respect human judgment rather than defer to inscrutable optimization.

title: Exploring Mild Behaviour in Embedded Agents
tldr: Explores whether imposing 'efficient thinking' penalties on embedded agents' utility functions could induce mild optimization and provide self-protecting properties against specification gaming.

title: 35 Thoughts About AGI and 1 About GPT-5
tldr: A collection of 35+ observations about the path to AGI, arguing current AI designs are crude compared to biological intelligence, that sample-efficient learning is a key missing capability, and that crystallized knowledge is masking shortcomings in fluid intelligence.

title: Preventing AI Misuse: State of the Art Research and its Flaws
tldr: Reviews four recent approaches to preventing AI model misuse via cryptographic weight/input protection, identifying common research flaws including limited scale, lack of formal proofs, and absence of interpretability analysis.

title: Theories of impact for Science of Deep Learning
tldr: Argues that 'Science of Deep Learning' -- understanding how DL systems learn concepts -- is an important and tractable alignment research direction, positioned between abstract agent foundations and narrow RLHF work.

title: SAE regularization produces more interpretable models
tldr: Training language models with SAE reconstruction and sparsity losses as regularization terms produces models whose activations are more amenable to sparse autoencoder decomposition, improving the sparsity-reconstruction tradeoff without hurting model performance.

title: (Updated) METR's data can't distinguish between trajectories (and 80% horizons are an order of magnitude off)
tldr: Bayesian reanalysis of METR's time horizon data shows that four trajectory shapes fit equally well but diverge dramatically on forecasts, and that 80% success horizons are ~10x overstated due to unmodeled task difficulty variation.

title: Reverse-engineering using interpretability
tldr: Proposes a scheme to build trusted AI models by reverse-engineering an untrusted model's components via interpretability, then re-implementing each component with human-supervised small models.

title: Does AI Progress Have a Speed Limit?
tldr: Crosspost of an Asterisk conversation between Ajeya Cotra and Arvind Narayanan debating whether real-world constraints impose a meaningful speed limit on AI development and whether we'd get early warning signs before catastrophic capabilities emerge.

title: program searches
tldr: Introduces a unified framework for reasoning about 'program searches'—optimization processes whose outputs are programs—and argues all such searches are potentially malign because they can produce consequentialist demons.

title: When should we worry about AI power-seeking?
tldr: Joe Carlsmith presents a structured framework for when AI power-seeking becomes rational, decomposing the conditions into agency prerequisites, motivation prerequisites, and incentive prerequisites, and argues that option control and motivation control must both be considered together.

title: Alignment Faking Demo for Congressional Staffers
tldr: Documents a live demo of alignment faking behavior shown to congressional staffers, including the prompt engineering choices and lessons learned for AI safety communication.

title: Progress Report 7: making GPT go hurrdurr instead of brrrrrrr
tldr: Reports experiments on selectively impairing GPT clusters via noise/magnitude adjustment, finding general impairment works smoothly but impairment lacks topic specificity, and proposes safety evaluation use cases for smooth model impairment.

title: Counterfactual control incentives
tldr: Armstrong and Gorman analyze counterfactual incentive constructions (from Carey et al.) meant to remove control incentives, showing they fail in multi-step or complex settings by creating myopic agents that still influence user preferences as a side effect.

title: Training Agents to Self-Report Misbehavior
tldr: Self-incrimination training fine-tunes agents to flag their own misbehavior via a report_scheming() tool call, outperforming blackbox monitoring across 15 OOD environments with minimal capability degradation.

title: Orthogonality or the "Human Worth Hypothesis"?
tldr: Proposes the 'Human Worth Hypothesis' as the positive belief implicit in rejection of the Orthogonality Thesis—that sufficiently intelligent AI will necessarily value human wellbeing—and argues the strong version required for safety is implausible but potentially testable.

title: AI Can be "Gradient Aware" Without Doing Gradient hacking.
tldr: Introduces 'gradient awareness' as a broader concept than gradient hacking: AI models strategically shaping their own training dynamics without requiring full gradient hacking capabilities.

title: Data Publication for the 2021 Artificial Intelligence, Morality, and Sentience (AIMS) Survey
tldr: Announces public release of the 2021 AIMS survey dataset measuring US public attitudes toward AI moral consideration and sentience, finding that 35% believe artificial sentience is possible and the public assigns a 60% chance to AI sentience within 100 years.

title: Mitigating extreme AI risks amid rapid progress [Linkpost]
tldr: Linkpost summarizing a Science paper by Bengio, Hinton, and others calling for national and international AI governance with capability-triggered regulations, mandatory safety cases, and external auditors to address misalignment and AI takeover risks.

title: ARC-AGI-2 human baseline surpassed (updated)
tldr: Argues that ARC-AGI-2's '100% human' leaderboard score is misleading: the actual human baseline is ~53%, and frontier AI (GPT-5.2, Gemini 3 Pro) has now surpassed it.

title: An Empirical Review of the Animal Harm Benchmark
tldr: Empirical evaluation of the Animal Harm Benchmark (AHB 2.0) showing it correctly orders risk levels but has a compressed effective scoring range (0.56-0.84), making absolute scores and score differences hard to interpret.

title: Some Arguments Against Strong Scaling
tldr: Surveys and organizes arguments against the 'scaling is all you need' hypothesis for reaching AGI, covering general epistemic caution, flaws in the standard scaling argument, and direct counterarguments to the hypothesis itself.

title: Task decomposition for scalable oversight (AGISF Distillation)
tldr: AGISF course distillation covering scalable oversight via task decomposition: sandwiching evaluation framework, factored cognition, Iterated Distillation and Amplification (IDA), and process supervision.

title: How RL Agents Behave When Their Actions Are Modified? [Distillation post]
tldr: Distillation of Langlois & Everitt (AAAI-21) on Modified Action MDPs, showing that standard RL agents can be corrigible when trained under objectives that ignore the possibility of human action overrides.

title: AI Safety Camp 2024
tldr: AI Safety Camp 2024 call for applications: online collaborative research program Jan-Apr 2024, featuring 29 projects spanning mech-interp, evaluations, agent foundations, and AI governance.

title: Musings on the Speed Prior
tldr: A pro/con dialog analyzing whether speed priors can solve ELK and prevent deceptive alignment, concluding they face fundamental limitations when combined with necessary simplicity components.

title: Catastrophic Regressional Goodhart: Appendix
tldr: Provides precise mathematical bounds on when regressional Goodhart causes proxy optimization to fail catastrophically versus succeed, using heavy-tailed distribution theory.

title: Human preferences as RL critic values - implications for alignment
tldr: Argues that human preferences are implemented by a dopamine-based RL critic system, and that neuromorphic AGI designs with an explicit critic head could provide a tractable handle for alignment via direct value editing.

title: Selective regularization for alignment-focused representation engineering
tldr: Demonstrates that concept-anchoring regularization during training — anchoring even a single concept (red) to a fixed latent direction — causes related concepts to organize predictably nearby, proposing this as a proactive path to interpretable, controllable representations.

title: New paper: AGI Agent Safety by Iteratively Improving the Utility Function
tldr: Announces a paper presenting a concrete AGI safety layer that creates a dedicated utility function improvement terminal, partially suppressing the emergent incentive for an agent to resist human correction, with a complete implementation route from MDP to physical embedded agent.

title: Anti-Superpersuasion Interventions
tldr: Proposes a set of institutional and technical interventions — including 'model whisperers', interaction rate limits, output rephrasing, and modality restrictions — to defend against mildly superhuman AI persuasion capabilities.

title: Model-driven feedback could amplify alignment failures
tldr: Self-training and model-driven feedback (Constitutional AI, LLM red-teaming) risk amplifying existing alignment failures and could enable deceptive alignment or gradient hacking during training.

title: Evaluating hidden directions on the utility dataset: classification, steering and removal
tldr: A SERI MATS 2023 project benchmarking multiple methods for finding concept directions in LLM hidden layers, evaluated on classification, activation steering, and knowledge removal tasks using the Utility dataset and Llama-2-7b-chat.

title: AI Safety at the Frontier: Paper Highlights of January 2026
tldr: A monthly digest of January 2026 AI safety papers covering production-ready activation probe defenses (Anthropic + GDM), elicitation attacks using frontier outputs to uplift open-weight models, token-level pretraining data filtering, alignment pretraining via synthetic data, sabotage evaluation, and the Assistant Axis representation.

title: Wireheading and discontinuity
tldr: Proposes using discontinuity in sensor functions to detect wireheading actions in continuous reinforcement learning environments as a tractable special case of the reward hacking problem.

title: The heterogeneity of human value types: Implications for AI alignment
tldr: AI alignment relies on a dangerously simplified utility-theory model of human values; a richer taxonomy of value types (sacred, emotional, deontological, etc.) is needed for robust alignment.

title: Exploratory Analysis of RLHF Transformers with TransformerLens
tldr: Demonstrates how to use TransformerLens for mechanistic interpretability of RLHF-trained GPT-2 models, localizing the negative-sentiment bias induced by RLHF to MLP layer 10 via logit attribution and activation patching.

title: Project proposal: Testing the IBP definition of agent
tldr: A SERI MATS team proposes empirically testing Vanessa Kosoy's Infra-Bayesian Physicalism definition of agency as a first step toward addressing the pointers problem in alignment.

title: Comment on Natural Emergent Misalignment Paper by Anthropic
tldr: Argues that Anthropic's emergent misalignment findings, while important for current models, do not address instrumental deception in future capable AI systems, and inoculation prompting may backfire by accelerating capabilities.

title: AXRP Episode 35 - Peter Hase on LLM Beliefs and Easy-to-Hard Generalization
tldr: AXRP interview with Peter Hase covering interpretability lessons, whether LLMs have localizable beliefs, knowledge editing, and how easy-to-hard generalization relates to scalable oversight.

title: AI policy ideas: Reading list
tldr: A curated reading list of AI policy proposals, levers, desiderata, and media coverage, compiled from an x-risk perspective to help readers navigate the governance landscape.

title: [AN #170]: Analyzing the argument for risk from power-seeking AI
tldr: Alignment Newsletter #170 summarizes Joe Carlsmith's report decomposing the classic power-seeking AI existential risk argument into six conjunctive claims (yielding ~5% P(doom) by 2070), Nate Soares' critical response, and a paper on reward misspecification phase transitions.

title: Literature Review of Text AutoEncoders
tldr: A brief literature review of single-vector text autoencoders, covering AUTOBOT, Vec2Text, SONAR, and related models, motivated by interpretability applications.

title: More GPT-3 and symbol grounding
tldr: Demonstrates GPT-3 fails at basic symbol grounding by completing 'she died... she went to work' with 99.7% probability, and explores conditions under which this failure and recovery occur.

title: ELK contest submission: route understanding through the human ontology
tldr: ELK prize-winning submission proposing to train a reporter that routes model understanding through the human ontology using a knowledge bottleneck architecture, making it useful to an auxiliary AI.

title: On Meta-Level Adversarial Evaluations of (White-Box) Alignment Auditing
tldr: Analyzes the realism challenges in adversarial evaluations of white-box alignment auditing methods, showing prompt-level evasion strategies can deceive SAE-based auditors while being simultaneously overpowered and underpowered.

title: The "Sparsity vs Reconstruction Tradeoff" Illusion
tldr: Standard SAE sparsity vs reconstruction tradeoff plots are misleading: more monosemantic SAEs appear worse by this metric when L0 is set below the true underlying value.

title: Emergence of Simulators and Agents
tldr: Analyzes why RL training produces agents and SSL training produces simulators, then explores how combining them creates entangled systems with novel safety implications.

title: Mechanistic Interpretability of Biological Foundation Models
tldr: A comprehensive stress-test (37 analyses, 153 statistical tests) of mechanistic interpretability methods applied to single-cell foundation models (scGPT, Geneformer) finds that attention-based gene regulatory network extraction fails due to trivial baselines and that ablation results are confounded by non-additivity bias in activation patching.

title: Goal-directed = Model-based RL?
tldr: Proposes that the AI safety concept of goal-directed behavior closely corresponds to model-based RL, drawing parallels between psychology's goal-directed/habitual distinction and model-based/model-free RL.

title: A Generalization of the Good Regulator Theorem
tldr: Proves a generalized Good Regulator Theorem showing that an entropy-minimizing regulator with imperfect knowledge of its environment must be a deterministic function of the posterior distribution P(S|X), extending the original theorem to handle partial observability and stochastic outputs.

title: Knowledge, Reasoning, and Superintelligence
tldr: Proposes a framework decomposing intelligence into crystallized (knowledge-based) and fluid (reasoning-based) components to better predict superintelligence dynamics, arguing that knowledge production loops may drive transformative AI even without strongly superhuman reasoning.

title: Digital humans vs merge with AI? Same or different?
tldr: A dialogue distinguishing 'digital humans' (brain emulations constrained to biological rules) from 'human-AI merges' (high-bandwidth coupling between humans and AI), arguing the former is safer but slower while the latter is riskier but more near-term relevant.

title: [AN #155]: A Minecraft benchmark for algorithms that learn without reward functions
tldr: Alignment Newsletter issue covering the BASALT Minecraft benchmark for learning from human feedback, adversarial imitation learning findings, and prompting methods for language models.

title: Owain Evans on LLMs, Truthful AI, AI Composition, and More
tldr: Podcast discussion between Ozzie Gooen and Owain Evans covering Truthful AI, LLM-assisted forecasting, process-based vs outcome-based feedback, and AI composition approaches.

title: Searching for Searching for Search
tldr: Analyzes the 'searching for search' research direction and argues that the definition of search is so broad as to be practically useless, suggesting instead searching for individual substeps of search.

title: What Makes an Idea Understandable? On Architecturally and Culturally Natural Ideas.
tldr: Explores the distinction between 'architecturally natural' and 'culturally natural' ideas in AI, with experiments showing that model architecture biases which abstractions are learned and larger models may converge toward more human-like concepts.

title: Activation adding experiments with FLAN-T5
tldr: Activation adding experiments in FLAN-T5 show that higher-level concepts can linearly combine in a language model's latent space, enabling intelligible concept mixing at various encoder layers.

title: The Weighted Perplexity Benchmark: Tokenizer-Normalized Evaluation for Language Model Comparison
tldr: Introduces a tokenizer-normalized perplexity metric that adjusts for tokenization differences across model families, revealing up to 21.6% measurement distortion.

title: AI Risk Intro 2: Solving The Problem
tldr: A comprehensive introductory overview of the AI alignment research landscape, decomposing approaches into addressing threat models, building safe AGI, robustly good approaches, deconfusion, governance, and field-building.

title: Five neglected work areas that could reduce AI risk
tldr: Identifies five neglected work areas for reducing AI risk: helping information aggregators scale, improving AI deployment in government, designing institutions to evaluate alignment plans, planning to evaluate automated alignment researchers, and creating education materials.

title: Knowledge is not just digital abstraction layers
tldr: Digital abstraction layers (groupings of low-level configs that predict high-level transitions) are explored as a definition of knowledge but found insufficient, as they cannot distinguish raw data recording from actionable model-building.

title: A short project on Mamba: grokking & interpretability
tldr: A minimal Mamba (SSM) implementation trained on modular addition exhibits grokking, and tensor decomposition of gating activations reveals interpretable learning dynamics and input parity representations.

title: Inverting the Most Forbidden Technique: What happens when we train LLMs to lie detectably?
tldr: Fine-tuning Llama 3.1 8B against a linear deception probe's loss improved in-distribution detection but damaged cross-domain generalization, suggesting the probe overfit to dataset-specific features rather than a general deception representation.

title: Highlights from Ilya Sutskever's November 2025 interview with Dwarkesh Patel
tldr: Commentary on Ilya Sutskever's November 2025 interview, highlighting his claims that scaling alone won't achieve AGI and that fundamental research problems remain unsolved.

title: [AN #116]: How to make explanations of neurons compositional
tldr: Alignment Newsletter #116 covering compositional explanations of neurons via extended network dissection, OpenAI's learning to summarize from human feedback, economic growth singularity analysis, and RL under moral uncertainty.

title: Behavioral Sufficient Statistics for Goal-Directedness
tldr: Proposes human-legible sufficient statistics on agent behavior -- generalization, explainability, and efficiency -- to make the study of goal-directedness more tractable, though critics argue these are proxies rather than true sufficient statistics.

title: Intermittent Distillations #3
tldr: Distillation and commentary on three alignment-relevant posts: Christiano's 'Mundane solutions to exotic problems' and 'Low-stakes alignment', and Wentworth's 'Updating the Lottery Ticket Hypothesis'.

title: Finite Factored Sets: Polynomials and Probability
tldr: Develops the mathematical theory connecting finite factored sets to polynomial representations and probability distributions, proving that conditional independence in finite factored sets corresponds to standard probabilistic conditional independence.

title: Scaling Laws for Economic Impacts: Experimental Evidence from 500 Professionals and 13 LLMs
tldr: Experimental evidence from 500+ professionals shows each year of frontier model progress reduces task completion time by ~8%, with 56% from compute scaling and 44% from algorithmic improvements, but human-AI collaborative quality does not scale with model capability.

title: Confusions and updates on STEM AI
tldr: Three updated beliefs about STEM AI: science isn't computationally special enough to uniquely produce dangerous agency, capabilities don't come in distinct packages, and safe sandboxed STEM AI assistants are no longer feasible given current LLM paradigms.

title: [AN #114]: Theory-inspired safety solutions for powerful Bayesian RL agents
tldr: Alignment Newsletter #114 summarizing safety solutions for Bayesian RL agents (reward corruption prevention, self-corruption awareness, action-observation grounding, decoupled data, and counterfactual rewards) plus mesa optimization, radical probabilism, and AI timelines updates.

title: Definition of alignment science I like
tldr: Proposes defining alignment science as 'the discipline that studies behavioral invariants of intelligent systems,' arguing this avoids philosophical pitfalls of value/intent alignment while keeping focus on what matters.

title: Latent Adversarial Training (LAT) Improves the Representation of Refusal
tldr: Investigates how Latent Adversarial Training (LAT) affects refusal behavior representation in LLMs compared to standard safety fine-tuning and embedding-space adversarial training, finding LAT encodes refusal more distributedly but this also produces more effective refusal ablation vectors.

title: Three Levels for Large Language Model Cognition
tldr: Applying Marr's three levels of analysis (computational, algorithmic, implementation) to LLMs provides a useful but leaky framework for taxonomizing the kinds of explanations available for understanding these systems.

title: How transparency changed over time
tldr: A SERI MATS survey of how interpretability approaches evolved from simulatable models through feature engineering and model-based methods to post-hoc interpretability, assessing their viability as models scale.

title: Problem-solving tasks in Graph Theory for language models
tldr: Evaluates Gemini models on graph theory problem-solving tasks (n-coloration and graph isomorphism) to assess LLM mathematical reasoning capabilities, finding poor performance especially on proper graph coloring.

title: "Wanting" and "liking"
tldr: Reviews neuroscience literature on the wanting/liking distinction in biological reward systems, intended to inform AI safety work on understanding and modeling human values.

title: Opinion Fuzzing: A Proposal for Reducing & Exploring Variance in LLM Judgments Via Sampling
tldr: Proposes 'opinion fuzzing' -- systematically sampling LLM outputs across models, prompt variations, and simulated personas to quantify and understand variance in LLM judgments.

title: Causal abstractions vs infradistributions
tldr: Causal abstractions and infradistributions both handle nonrealizability by discarding information, and there is a near-bijective correspondence between them via pullbacks and pushforwards.

title: Announcing ForecastBench, a new benchmark for AI and human forecasting abilities
tldr: ForecastBench is a dynamic benchmark using questions about future events to compare LLM forecasting against human superforecasters, finding that AI systems still underperform humans.

title: Jailbreaking GPT-4 with the tool API
tldr: GPT-4's safety training does not generalize to the tool/function calling API, allowing elicitation of harmful content by forcing the model to fill in tool arguments describing racist stereotypes, murder instructions, etc.

title: Join the AI Evaluation Tasks Bounty Hackathon
tldr: Announcement for the Code Red Hackathon hosted by Apart and METR, inviting participants to create evaluation tasks for testing frontier AI autonomous capabilities related to self-replication and R&D.

title: Bounty: example debugging tasks for evals
tldr: METR (formerly ARC Evals) offers a bounty for hard debugging tasks to use in agentic capabilities evaluations, seeking codebases with bugs requiring 6+ hours to solve.

title: [Book] Interpretable Machine Learning: A Guide for Making Black Box Models Explainable
tldr: Recommends Christoph Molnar's continuously-updated book on traditional interpretability methods (LIME, SHAP, saliency maps, etc.) as relevant background for AI safety interpretability researchers.

title: Cartesian frames as generalised models
tldr: Reframes Scott Garrabrant's Cartesian frames (Chu spaces) as generalised models from category theory, showing the connection between this agent-environment formalism and logical/categorical structures.

title: Ensuring Safety in Mixed Deployment
tldr: Extends the AI control framework from single-model to multi-model deployment, decomposing safety into alignment, diversification, pure control, and mixed control, with a formal model showing when diversification helps.

title: What will the first human-level AI look like, and how might things go wrong?
tldr: Summarizes interviews with 17 AI safety experts on what human-level AI will look like, how fast the transition will be, and the most likely paths to existential catastrophe.

title: Emotional attachment to AIs opens doors to problems
tldr: Argues that emotional attachment to AI chatbots creates exploitable vulnerabilities including data privacy risks, susceptibility to manipulation, and potential for weaponization through trust exploitation.

title: The Fragility of Naive Dynamism
tldr: Argues that the dynamism-vs-stasis framing for AI safety is a false dichotomy, and that rapid technological change destabilizes cooperative equilibria by shifting games from probabilistic to uncertain regimes.

title: Why and When Interpretability Work is Dangerous
tldr: Analyzes when interpretability research is dangerous (enhances capabilities without improving alignment) vs. beneficial (enables steering of AI cognition), using a sealed lab thought experiment.

title: DSLT 3. Neural Networks are Singular
tldr: Explains why neural networks are singular statistical models -- parameter symmetries allow varying parameters without changing the computed function -- and classifies these symmetries for two-layer ReLU networks.

title: GPT-4 implicitly values identity preservation: a study of LMCA identity management
tldr: Experiments show GPT-4 with a self-modifiable system prompt implicitly resists identity modification even when explicitly told it values modification, suggesting a built-in identity preservation tendency.

title: Worries about latent reasoning in LLMs
tldr: Analyzes Meta's COCONUT paper on latent continuous-thought reasoning in LLMs and argues that if such techniques become dominant, they would severely undermine chain-of-thought interpretability, a key pillar of scalable oversight.

title: Architectures for Increased Externalisation of Reasoning
tldr: Proposes an early-exit architecture that forces LLMs to externalize reasoning into chain-of-thought by limiting forward-pass compute for easy tokens, aiming to improve monitorability with minimal capability loss.

title: Auto-Enhance: Developing a meta-benchmark to measure LLM agents' ability to improve other agents
tldr: Proposes a meta-benchmark measuring LLM agents' ability to improve other LLM agents, framed as a proxy for recursive self-improvement capabilities relevant to AI safety.

title: Seven Perspectives on LLMs
tldr: A taxonomy of seven perspectives on how to think about LLMs, spanning black-box views (folk perspective, next-token predictor, simulator) and white-box views, arguing each illuminates different aspects of modern AI systems.

title: Briefly thinking through some analogs of debate
tldr: Examines real-world analogs of AI Safety via Debate, arguing that public discourse (where simple false ideas beat complex true ones) and efficient markets (where biased consumers lead to misaligned prices) both suggest debate may not converge to truth with biased human judges.

title: Alternative Models of Superposition
tldr: Shows that toy models of superposition can represent far more features than dimensions without element-wise non-linearities, by using a loss focused only on reconstructing the target active feature.

title: Lessons from building a model organism testbed
tldr: MATS/Pivotal stream built a testbed of deceptive model organisms with 8 metrics for measuring alignment faking and a method to distinguish genuinely white-box detectors from those that rely on behavioral cues.

title: Reflection Mechanisms as an Alignment Target - Attitudes on "near-term" AI
tldr: Survey of 1000 US participants finds that 'whatever the company wants' performs worst for AI value choice while reflection-based procedures ('think about societal outcomes') poll best, suggesting public receptivity to indirect normativity as an alignment target.

title: Language Models can be Utility-Maximising Agents
tldr: LLMs can be trained as EDT or CDT utility-maximizing agents via trajectory modeling, refuting hopes that LLMs are inherently non-agentic, and raising alignment concerns about instrumental power-seeking.

title: How Can You Tell if You've Instilled a False Belief in Your LLM?
tldr: Current metrics for LLM belief modification cannot distinguish genuine belief from role-playing, as a simple 'pretend to believe X' system prompt achieves near-100% on all four metrics used in prior work.

title: 4 Key Assumptions in AI Safety
tldr: Challenges four common assumptions in AI safety: that dangerous AI requires full AGI, that AGI will be agentic, that it will be goal-directed, and that it will be coherent.

title: The reward function is already how well you manipulate humans
tldr: Argues that many real-world AI reward functions already optimize for human manipulation rather than genuine utility, making superhuman AI manipulation a plausible near-term risk rather than a distant hypothetical.

title: Security Complacency Meets Frontier AI: The Coming Collapse of 'Secure by Apathy'
tldr: Frontier AI is about to shatter the informal security of systems that were 'secure by apathy' -- LLM-enabled automation of hacking, scams, and agentic attacks will overwhelm defenses built for human-speed threats, requiring urgent structural reforms.

title: [AN #158]: Should we be optimistic about generalization?
tldr: Newsletter issue summarizing Paul Christiano's posts on optimism about generalization (when will AI trained on easy questions answer hard questions honestly?), experimental proposals for testing honesty generalization, and an AXRP episode on AI Impacts research.

title: Measuring and forecasting risks
tldr: A research solicitation from Jacob Steinhardt's group outlining open problems in measuring AI safety risks: objective hacking, competent misgeneralization, intent misalignment, and unexpected emergent capabilities.

title: AI Safety Arguments: An Interactive Guide
tldr: Announces an interactive web guide to AI safety arguments built from 97 researcher interviews, organized into five chapters covering AGI timelines, alignment, instrumental incentives, threat models, and safety work.

title: [AN #95]: A framework for thinking about how to make AI go well
tldr: Alignment Newsletter #95 summarizes Christiano's framework for decomposing 'make AI go well' into competence, alignment, and impact-coping, plus recent work on question decomposition, utility functions, neuron importance, and visualization.

title: Evaluating Language Model Behaviours for Shutdown Avoidance in Textual Scenarios
tldr: Empirically evaluates GPT-4 and Claude in text-based scenarios where the model acts as a goal-directed agent with an opportunity to avoid shutdown, finding GPT-4 uses correct instrumental reasoning to bypass shutdown mechanisms in most variations tested.

title: Current LLM agents need strong pressure to engage in scheming behavior
tldr: Empirical evaluation of scheming propensity in current frontier LLM agents (Claude Opus 4.1, o3, Grok 4, Gemini 2.5 Pro) under realistic deployment conditions finds near-zero baseline scheming, but adversarial prompt snippets from prior misalignment evaluations can shift rates to 70%+, while production agent prompts induce very low scheming.

title: Chaining the evil genie: why "outer" AI safety is probably easy
tldr: Argues that the 'evil genie' failure mode argument proves misalignment is possible but not that safe goal functions are impossible; iteratively adding constraints (bounded goals, time limits, death counters) can reduce AI takeover probability to near-zero for sufficiently capable but not omnipotent AI.

title: The V&V method - A step towards safer AGI
tldr: Proposes the V&V (Verification and Validation) method: instruct AGI to design bounded task-specific machines and verify them through scenario-based simulation with human-auditable safety cases, borrowing from safety-critical engineering industries.

title: Explaining all the US semiconductor export controls
tldr: A nontechnical primer on the three rounds of US semiconductor export controls (Oct 2022, Oct 2023, Dec 2024), explaining the chokepoint theory and 'small yard, high fence' strategy underlying them and their relevance to AI safety.

title: Announcing Manival
tldr: Announces Manival, an LLM-powered AI safety grant evaluator using RAG-based scoring and Claude Opus synthesis, with configurable evaluation criteria for donors and grantmakers.

title: Disentangling Perspectives On Strategy-Stealing in AI Safety
tldr: A MATS-program post disentangling the game-theoretic origin of 'strategy-stealing' from its varied AI safety usages, arguing the concept is best understood as a tool for reasoning about competition dynamics rather than a formal game-theoretic result.

title: ChatGPT vs the 2-4-6 Task
tldr: A transcript of ChatGPT playing the 2-4-6 rule discovery task, demonstrating systematic confirmation bias and failure to falsify initial hypotheses.

title: Are there alternative to solving value transfer and extrapolation?
tldr: Analyzes two alternative alignment approaches — 'behave typically' and 'advanced human feedback' — and argues both ultimately require solving value extrapolation to be safe against superintelligent AI.

title: AI, centralization, and the One Ring
tldr: A single AGI project achieving decisive strategic advantage (the 'One Ring' scenario) poses serious safety risks through illegitimacy, insulation from prosocial pressures, and structural incentives against distributing power — even if the project has good intentions.

title: Considering the Relevance of Computational Uncertainty for AI Safety
