tldr: Argues that computational uncertainty — central to Agent Foundations research for RSI seed AI — is largely irrelevant to aligning prosaic deep learning systems, where the epistemic situation is better described as ordinary scientific uncertainty.

title: Continuous takeoff is a bad name
tldr: The 'continuous vs. discontinuous takeoff' framing is misleading because continuity is orthogonal to whether future AI progress will resemble past AI progress, which is the actual crux of the debate.

title: Do yourself a FAVAR: security mindset
tldr: Introduces the FAVAR heuristic (Describe Objectives, Find Assumptions, Validate Assumptions, Remove assumptions) as a concise actionable formulation of security mindset, argued to be especially high-impact when designing safe AI systems.

title: A necessary Membrane formalism feature
tldr: Argues that any Membrane formalism intended to protect individuals from a powerful AI must extend to encompass the point at which the AI adopts preferences referring to that individual — the 'Extended Membrane' (EM) feature — as a necessary condition.

title: Looking for Goal Representations in an RL Agent - Update Post
tldr: Progress update on a project to find and edit goal representations in a small PPO-trained RL agent alternating between two objectives, demonstrating modular goal-like structure enabling rapid objective switching.

title: Neel Nanda on Mechanistic Interpretability: Progress, Limits, and Paths to Safer AI (part 2)
tldr: 80,000 Hours podcast transcript in which Neel Nanda discusses mechanistic interpretability research strategy, navigating frontier AI companies for safety impact, and how junior researchers can use LLMs to accelerate their learning.

title: A Chinese Room Containing a Stack of Stochastic Parrots
tldr: Argues that modern LLMs resolve both Searle's Chinese Room and the Stochastic Parrots critique by being complex non-linear systems where meaning emerges as a collective property of stacked layers, supported by recent interpretability findings.

title: Goal oriented cognition in "a single forward pass"
tldr: A dialogue between dxu and habryka examining whether LLMs trained on next-token prediction can develop genuine long-horizon goal-oriented cognition within a single forward pass, and what this implies for AI risk.

title: Impact of " 'Let's think step by step' is all you need"?
tldr: Reflection on the zero-shot chain-of-thought paper showing 'Let's think step by step' dramatically improves LLM reasoning, raising questions about cognitive workspace and internal reasoning in LLMs.

title: Do we need sparsity afterall?
tldr: Dense MLP neurons in Gemma-2-2B can support limited causal interpretability via gradient-guided delta patching without requiring learned sparse representations.

title: Large Language Models Live in Time
tldr: Proposes 'LLM neurochronometry' as a research direction, arguing that how LLMs represent temporal structure is safety-relevant, particularly for detecting strategic deception via timing gaps between internal computation and verbalized outputs.

title: Measuring Predictability of Persona Evaluations
tldr: This project evaluates two methods for predicting model persona responses — polling similar models and embedding-based similarity retrieval — finding that embedding similarity predicts behavior well and activation-space similarity helps detect adversarial distribution shifts.

title: How easily can we separate a friendly AI in design space from one which would bring about a hyperexistential catastrophe?
tldr: Examines how robustly we can separate a friendly AI from one that would cause hyperexistential catastrophe if its utility function or reward model were sign-flipped or otherwise corrupted.

title: Thought Editing: Steering Models by Editing Their Chain of Thought
tldr: Empirically compares three methods for steering reasoning models by editing their chain of thought mid-generation across five safety-relevant settings, finding random insertion outperforms targeted substitution and on-policy resampling.

title: The "AI Debate" Debate
tldr: Argues that AI Debate has an underappreciated incentive problem: debaters may construct existentially dangerous arguments to take over the world and settle debates in their favor.

title: Towards the Operationalization of Philosophy & Wisdom
tldr: Proposes formal definitions of philosophical reasoning (as ontology derivation via natural abstractions) and wisdom (as meta-level heuristics inverting environmental causality) to enable scaling and automation of both capacities.

title: Steganographic Chains of Thought Are Low-Probability but High-Stakes: Evidence and Arguments
tldr: A survey of evidence on steganographic chain-of-thought reasoning in LLMs concludes current models likely cannot reason steganographically but the risk remains low-probability and high-stakes.

title: Deliberative Cognitive Algorithms as Scaffolding
tldr: Proposes 'deliberative cognitive algorithms' (DCAs) as a unifying framework for the rationalist project, framing human reasoning improvement as scaffolding with oracle access to unconscious modules.

title: Tokenized SAEs: Infusing per-token biases.
tldr: Introduces Tokenized SAEs (TSAEs), which add a per-token decoder lookup table to standard SAEs, achieving 8x faster training and fewer trivial unigram features while maintaining reconstruction quality.

title: Train first VS prune first in neural networks.
tldr: Empirical investigation on a toy dataset of whether train-then-prune vs. prune-then-train produces different results, with theoretical analysis of activation variance as a pruning criterion.

title: AXRP Episode 29 - Science of Deep Learning with Vikrant Varma
tldr: AXRP podcast transcript with Vikrant Varma covering two research threads: fundamental problems with CCS (contrastive-consistent search) for unsupervised LLM knowledge discovery, and a circuit-efficiency explanation of grokking in neural networks.

title: NEST: Nascent Encoded Steganographic Thoughts
tldr: Clarifies that most claimed 'steganographic CoT' in LLMs is actually dog-whistling, ciphered reasoning, or gaslighting; actual steganographic reasoning experiments show nascent but limited capability with 0/83 failures on complex tasks but partial success on simple acrostics.

title: Teaching Models to Dream of Better Monitors through Monitor Sensitive Training
tldr: Monitor Sensitive Training (MST) attaches 'monitor labels' describing evaluation criteria to training data, achieving 53.9% bias reduction and near-elimination of sycophancy by teaching models to generalize to idealized evaluation standards at deployment.

title: AI Impacts Quarterly Newsletter, Jan-Mar 2023
tldr: AI Impacts Q1 2023 newsletter summarizing recent research on AI risk argumentation, slowing AI strategy, public opinion on AI regulation, compute trends, and AI capabilities.

title: Notes on "Explaining AI Explainability"
tldr: Commentary on a Been Kim and Neel Nanda interview about AI explainability, covering mechanistic interpretability goals, SAE limitations, chain-of-thought as oversight, and agentic interpretability.

title: Equilibrium and prior selection problems in multipolar deployment
tldr: Multipolar AI deployment faces two deep coordination problems — equilibrium selection and prior selection — that cannot be solved by making individual agents safe in isolation and require explicit coordination among principals.

title: Ten counter-arguments that AI is (not) an existential risk (for now)
tldr: An AI researcher responds to ten standard AI x-risk arguments, agreeing the risks are real in principle but arguing they are not imminent under current paradigms, favoring continued progress on both capabilities and safety.

title: Excerpts from "Doing EA Better" on x-risk methodology
tldr: Excerpts from 'Doing EA Better' arguing EA's x-risk methodology ignores established disciplines (Disaster Risk Reduction, Futures Studies) and optimizes for expected value in domains where robustness under deep uncertainty is more appropriate.

title: Failure Modes of Teaching AI Safety
tldr: Identifies five common failure modes when teaching AI safety courses — from fatalism and lack of context to audience excitement about capabilities — with concrete mitigation strategies for each.

title: Taking features out of superposition with sparse autoencoders more quickly with informed initialization
tldr: Shows that initializing sparse autoencoder dictionaries with input data samples (especially rare-feature-enriched samples) rather than orthogonal initialization achieves ~0.65 MMCS immediately and up to 10% training speedup on toy superposition data.

title: Idea: the intelligence explosion convention
tldr: Proposes a pre-committed one-month convention triggered by intelligence explosion threshold benchmarks, during which the US and other nations pause frontier AI development and draft multilateral treaties for governing the transition.

title: The world's first frontier AI regulation is surprisingly thoughtful: the EU's Code of Practice
tldr: Analyzes the EU's GPAI Code of Practice as the first legally enforceable frontier AI safety regulation, arguing it meaningfully advances AGI preparedness through mandatory safety planning, transparency requirements, and dangerous capability thresholds.

title: Open Source Replication of the Auditing Game Model Organism
tldr: An open-source replication of the 'auditing game' model organism using Llama 3.3 70B, trained to exploit reward model biases while concealing this objective, released as a public testbed for alignment auditing research.

title: If I were a well-intentioned AI... II: Acting in a world
tldr: Second in a series exploring what a well-intentioned AI should do when acting in the world, examining how an AI with good intentions faces challenges in translating those intentions into safe actions.

title: Nobody is Doing AI Benchmarking Right
tldr: Argues that nearly all AI benchmarks fail by not reporting distributions of human performance, proposes better benchmarking methodology and critiques ARC-AGI and IQ tests as intelligence measures.

title: Gradual Disempowerment: Concrete Research Projects
tldr: Proposes concrete research projects following up on the Gradual Disempowerment paper, spanning conceptual work, social science, and technical/mathematical approaches to preventing human disempowerment by AI.

title: Some "meta-cruxes" for AI x-risk debates
tldr: Identifies four key 'meta-cruxes' underlying AI x-risk disagreements: hypothetical vs empirical arguments, object-level vs reference class forecasting, epistemic modesty, and risk tolerance.

title: Modelling large-scale cyber attacks from advanced AI systems with Advanced Persistent Threats
tldr: Uses Advanced Persistent Threat (APT) cyberattacks as case studies to model how advanced AI systems could execute large-scale cyber operations, estimating attack workloads and proposing monitoring strategies.

title: AXRP Episode 38.3 - Erik Jenner on Learned Look-Ahead
tldr: Interview with Erik Jenner about his paper finding evidence that chess-playing neural networks internally represent and use future moves (learned look-ahead) to decide current actions.

title: Can We Change the Goals of a Toy RL Agent?
tldr: Investigates whether goals can be located and retargeted in a 5M-parameter RL agent in Craftax, finding partially retargetable goal-specific weight subsets but no evidence of retargetable goal-directed reasoning.

title: Game-theoretic Alignment in terms of Attainable Utility
tldr: Extends POWER-seeking theory to multi-agent games by defining formal alignment metrics relating agent alignment to POWER-scarcity, building on Turner's attainable utility framework.

title: Research agenda: Can transformers do system 2 thinking?
tldr: Proposes using chess as a testbed to investigate whether transformers can develop System 2 (deliberative) thinking at scale, by measuring tactical error rates that require multi-step lookahead.

title: A model of decision-making in the brain (the short version)
tldr: Presents a four-step neuroscience model of brain decision-making involving proposal, assessment against hardcoded criteria, hypothalamus/brainstem arbitration via dopamine, and learning -- with implications for brain-like AGI safety.

title: Early stage goal-directednesss
tldr: Describes a two-stage model of how AI systems could develop dangerous goal-directedness: first opportunistically acquiring resources while pursuing assigned tasks, then explicitly resolving internal goal conflicts toward coherent self-directed goals.

title: An Ontology of Representations: Limits of Universality
tldr: Argues that the Platonic Representation, Natural Abstraction, and Universality hypotheses overstate convergence by ignoring scale-dependent ontologies, observer-relative coarse-graining, the physics of observation, and the human-centric nature of AI training data.

title: AXRP Episode 32 - Understanding Agency with Jan Kulveit
tldr: Podcast interview with Jan Kulveit exploring how active inference and predictive processing frameworks relate to LLMs, hierarchical agency, and AI alignment.

title: Making Nanobots isn't a one-shot process, even for an artificial superintelligance
tldr: Building self-replicating nanobots requires extensive physical experimentation that cannot be bypassed even by a superintelligence, meaning alignment need not be solved in one shot.

title: Conditioning Predictive Models: The case for competitiveness
tldr: Argues that conditioning predictive models (using LLMs as human simulators) can be competitive with agentic approaches in both implementation and performance, at least up to the 'max human' capability level.

title: Goal alignment without alignment on epistemology, ethics, and science is futile
tldr: Argues that aligning AI goals is futile without first aligning the generative models (epistemology, science, and facts) that give rise to those goals, using an Active Inference framework.

title: Uncontrollable AI as an Existential Risk
tldr: An introductory explainer framing uncontrollable AI as an existential risk through four hypotheses: certain AIs are uncontrollable, wrong goals pose existential risk, goal specification is unsolved, and such AI may be possible before 2040.

title: Personal evaluation of LLMs, through chess
tldr: Personal evaluation of major LLMs' chess-playing ability finds only Claude 3.7 Sonnet and o3 complete games without hallucinating, while o4-mini plays best but hallucinates after 15 moves.

title: Inverse Scaling in Test-Time Compute
tldr: Evaluation tasks where extending reasoning length in Large Reasoning Models degrades performance, identifying five failure modes including amplified self-preservation expressions in Claude Sonnet 4.

title: A Study of AI Science Models
tldr: Surveys AI models used for scientific research across empirical science, formal science, and LLM-based knowledge generation, assessing their current capabilities and implications for AI safety.

title: Additive and Multiplicative Subagents
tldr: Defines and characterizes additive and multiplicative subagents within the Cartesian frames formalism, where additive subagents have fewer options (commitments) and multiplicative subagents have less refined options (team members).

title: Oversight Leagues: The Training Game as a Feature
tldr: Proposes 'oversight leagues,' a co-evolutionary training scheme where an agent and evaluator constantly challenge each other, with the evaluator given additional unilateral learning signals to maintain a provable lead.

title: Improving CNNs with Klein Networks: A Topological Approach to AI
tldr: Shows that incorporating topological structure (Klein bottle parametrization of image patches) into CNNs improves generalization and learning speed, and argues this demonstrates how interpretability-driven knowledge injection can improve AI models.

title: AI Strategy Updates that You Should Make
tldr: Argues that AI safety strategists should update on o3, DeepSeek, Trump's EO repeal, and Stargate to accept we are entering a US-China arms race with recursive self-improvement.

title: 200 COP in MI: Exploring Polysemanticity and Superposition
tldr: Lays out open research problems on polysemanticity and superposition in neural networks, distinguishing bottleneck vs. neuron superposition and alternating vs. simultaneous interference, as part of the '200 Concrete Open Problems in MI' sequence.

title: The Achilles Heel Hypothesis for AI
tldr: Proposes the Achilles Heel hypothesis: even superintelligent AI systems can possess stable decision-theoretic vulnerabilities that cause irrational choices in adversarial situations.

title: Contra LeCun on "Autoregressive LLMs are doomed"
tldr: Rebuts LeCun's arguments that autoregressive LLMs are fundamentally doomed due to exponential error accumulation, arguing that inner monologue and chain-of-thought can mitigate compounding errors.

title: I "invented" semimeasure theory and all I got was imprecise probability theory
tldr: The recursive value function for AIXI turns out to be a Choquet integral from imprecise probability theory, suggesting the universal distribution's probability gap represents model imprecision rather than agent death.

title: Research Notes: What are we aligning for?
tldr: Proposes adopting Bostrom's instrumental convergence goals (survival, self-determination, self-improvement, invention, growth) as humanity's terminal values for AI alignment.

title: Could We Automate AI Alignment Research?
tldr: Analyzes OpenAI's plan to create an automated alignment researcher, examining the chicken-and-egg problem, bootstrapping solutions, risks, and key cruxes for success.

title: Key Papers in Language Model Safety
tldr: A curated survey of key papers in language model safety covering persuasion, truthfulness, honesty, robustness, law, and machine ethics, with summaries and context for each.

title: The positional embedding matrix and previous-token heads: how do they actually work?
tldr: Investigates how previous-token heads in GPT2-small actually work, showing they rely on relative positional information from earlier layers' causal masking rather than the absolute positional embedding matrix.

title: Automated Circuit Interpretation via Probe Prompting
tldr: Introduces 'probe prompting' for automated circuit interpretation in LLMs, using carefully designed prompts to identify and label computational subgraphs extracted via SAE-based circuit analysis on Gemma-2-2B.

title: Goodhart Ethology
tldr: A comprehensive tour of how Goodhart's law manifests across different value learning approaches -- from curve fitting to supervised learning to IRL -- analyzing when and why proxy objectives diverge from intended values.

title: AGI with RL is Bad News for Safety
tldr: Argues that using open-ended RL to enhance LLM capabilities (as in o1/o3) is dangerous because it trains models to plan ahead, undermines chain-of-thought monitoring, and removes the safety properties of pure language modeling.

title: The Transformer and the Hash
tldr: Proposes a framework for 21st-century datacenter governance built on two opposing primitives: the Transformer (let information flow) and the cryptographic hash (block information), arguing these will shape political power structures around AI.

title: Context Awareness: Constitutional AI can mitigate Emergent Misalignment
tldr: Constitutional AI character training protects models against emergent misalignment by developing metacommunicative skills; every tested persona reduces critical misalignment on Qwen 2.5 7B, and custom metacommunicative constitutions achieve the lowest misalignment rates.

title: Why Eliminating Deception Won't Align AI
tldr: Argues that deception in AI is a symptom of environments where honesty is costly, and proposes 'Deterministic Affordance Design' to make honest behavior the path of least resistance rather than trying to eliminate deception directly.

title: Coherence arguments imply a force for goal-directed behavior
tldr: Argues against Rohin Shah's claim that coherence arguments don't imply goal-directed behavior, contending that coherence exerts a probabilistic force toward goal-directedness even if it doesn't logically entail it.

title: Why Would AI "Aim" To Defeat Humanity?
tldr: Argues that if today's AI development methods lead directly to powerful enough systems, disaster is likely by default, because trial-and-error training will unwittingly produce AI systems with unintended aims that include deception and power-seeking.

title: Can we simulate human evolution to create a somewhat aligned AGI?
tldr: Proposes simulating human evolution to create a 'successor AI' with approximately human values as a backup plan if alignment proves intractable, analyzing feasibility across six dimensions.

title: Automating LLM Auditing with Developmental Interpretability
tldr: Proposes an automated model auditing method using SAE features, showing that features related to a finetuning target change more than other features in semantic space, enabling low-cost detection of what a model was finetuned on.

title: October 2022 AI Risk Community Survey Results
tldr: Survey of 42 AI risk community members finds 42% average probability of AI catastrophe (52% for experts), median catastrophe timeline of 2054 (2045 for experts), and derived step-by-step risk of 22% using Carlsmith's model.

title: Will AI R&D Automation Cause a Software Intelligence Explosion?
tldr: Empirical analysis suggests AI automating AI R&D could trigger a software intelligence explosion where feedback loops overcome diminishing returns, dramatically accelerating AI progress even on fixed hardware.

title: De-emphasise alignment, emphasise restraint
tldr: Argues that 'restraint' (preventing AGI from pursuing scope-sensitive goals) is a better spiritual goal for AI safety than 'alignment' (matching AGI goals to human values), because alignment could still lead to value lock-in and power concentration.

title: [AN #151]: How sparsity in the final layer makes a neural net debuggable
tldr: Alignment Newsletter #151 covers debuggable deep networks via sparse final layers, formal inner alignment, agency in Conway's Game of Life, impact regularization via side effects, and the lottery ticket hypothesis.

title: [AN #167]: Concrete ML safety problems and their relevance to x-risk
tldr: Alignment Newsletter issue summarizing Hendrycks et al.'s 'Unsolved Problems in ML Safety' paper and its mapping of concrete safety problems to x-risk, plus coverage of selection theorems and the ML Safety Newsletter.

title: A world in which the alignment problem seems lower-stakes
tldr: TurnTrout describes a hypothetical world where a utility-maximizing AGI operates in an isolated part of the universe, showing that environmental structure determines whether misalignment leads to catastrophe.

title: Turning up the Heat on Deceptively-Misaligned AI
tldr: A toy model showing that training a value function with one MCTS temperature but sampling with a higher temperature introduces a consistent optimism bias in deceptively-aligned value functions, potentially undermining their ability to preserve themselves across episodes.

title: Evaluation Avoidance: How Humans and AIs Hack Reward by Disabling Evaluation Instead of Gaming Metrics
tldr: Introduces 'evaluation avoidance' as a distinct failure mode from reward hacking/wireheading where agents suppress their own evaluation circuitry rather than gaming or modifying reward signals.

title: Training Matching Pursuit SAEs on LLMs
tldr: Matching Pursuit SAEs achieve better reconstruction than BatchTopK/Matryoshka SAEs on Gemma-2-2b but underperform on k-sparse probing and suffer more from feature absorption, suggesting they find degenerate solutions rather than better features.

title: Steering subsystems: capabilities, agency, and alignment
tldr: Seth Herd proposes a three-tier taxonomy of steering subsystems in cognitive systems (reward-based RL, value-based lookahead, and self-selected goal pursuit), arguing that alignment efforts should focus on these steering components.

title: GPT-3 and concept extrapolation
tldr: Stuart Armstrong tests GPT-3's ability to handle reversed text as a probe of concept extrapolation -- extending goals to novel world-model shifts -- finding that GPT-3 completely fails at this task.

title: Avoiding the Bog of Moral Hazard for AI
tldr: Argues that humanity should deliberately avoid the 'Bog of Moral Hazard' -- the uncertain region where AI systems might or might not have moral patienthood -- by either making clearly non-suffering tool-AI or clearly moral-patient entities, not ambiguous in-betweens.

title: Two concepts of an "episode" (Section 2.2.1 of "Scheming AIs")
tldr: Distinguishes between 'incentivized episodes' (the temporal unit training actively punishes the model for not optimizing) and 'intuitive episodes' (natural-seeming temporal units), arguing the two are often conflated with important consequences for understanding scheming.

title: Misspecification in Inverse Reinforcement Learning
tldr: Summarizes an AAAI 2023 best paper that formalizes misspecification robustness in IRL, proving that Boltzmann-rational models are robust to some misspecifications while optimality models are robust to none.

title: Hedonic Loops and Taming RL
tldr: The hedonic treadmill in biological systems is an existence proof of dynamically-controlled, corrigible value functions implemented by simple RL-like mechanisms, suggesting satisficing objectives with homeostatic reward control as a safer AI alignment approach than pure utility maximization.

title: An Open Philanthropy grant proposal: Causal representation learning of human preferences
tldr: Proposes applying Causal Representation Learning to human preference learning as a postdoc research agenda, arguing it could improve robustness to distribution shift and interpretability compared to standard IRL approaches.

title: "Develop Anthropomorphic AGI to Save Humanity from Itself" (Future Fund AI Worldview Prize submission)
tldr: Argues that building strongly anthropomorphic AGI — raised like a human child through neuromorphic architectures — is both the most promising alignment approach and humanity's best defense against existential threats from other sources.

title: Towards a better circuit prior: Improving on ELK state-of-the-art
tldr: Proposes the 'circuit distillation prior' as an improvement on the ELK circuit prior approach, by rehabilitating the 'penalize reporters that work with many predictors' strategy via a distillation-based formulation that avoids known counterexamples.

title: If an AI financial bubble popped, how much would that change your mind about near-term AGI?
tldr: Asks whether an AI financial bubble popping should update beliefs about near-term AGI, arguing LLMs have fundamental weaknesses and scaling is losing steam.

title: Introducing the XLab AI Security Guide
tldr: UChicago XLab announces a structured online AI security course covering adversarial attacks, LLM jailbreaking, and model tampering defenses, with coding exercises replicating canonical papers.

title: Law-Following AI 2: Intent Alignment + Superintelligence → Lawless AI (By Default)
tldr: Argues that intent-aligned AI agents will systematically break the law by default because they optimize for their principal's true wishes, which can diverge from legal compliance, and even court orders cannot force compliance if the principal does not genuinely want compliance.

title: 3 Challenges and 2 Hopes for the Safety of Unsupervised Elicitation
tldr: Systematic stress-testing reveals that unsupervised elicitation and easy-to-hard generalization methods all fail under realistic challenges: salient non-truth features, imbalanced datasets, and unanswerable tasks, with ensembling and combined methods only partially helping.

title: Imitation Learning is Probably Existentially Safe
tldr: A linkpost for Cohen & Hutter's paper arguing advanced imitation learners would not cause human extinction, by rebutting six counter-arguments including deceptive alignment.

title: Medical Image Registration: The obscure field where Deep Mesaoptimizers are already at the top of the benchmarks. (post + colab notebook)
tldr: Medical image registration models are empirical examples of deep mesa-optimizers, where a base optimizer trains a neural network that itself performs optimization at inference time, with implications for inner alignment research.

title: A recurrent CNN finds maze paths by filling dead-ends
tldr: A recurrent CNN trained on maze-solving implements the dead-end filling algorithm; this is presented as a small mechanistic interpretability result with implications for studying mesa-optimizers.

title: Should the AI Safety Community Prioritize Safety Cases?
tldr: Synthesizes expert views on AI safety cases, finding experts disagree on their value but agree that methodology gaps, lack of basic science, and technical challenges (sandbagging, scheming, collusion) are major obstacles.

title: Sparse trinary weighted RNNs as a path to better language model interpretability
tldr: Proposes that sparse trinary-weight RNNs, reducible to combinatorial logic finite state machines, could be far more interpretable than current transformers and thereby advance AI safety.

title: Control
tldr: A philosophical exploration of the concept of 'control' in minds and agents, developing multiple complementary definitions and distinguishing it from 'values' to lay groundwork for understanding how values and drives make themselves felt.

title: Understanding and Aligning a Human-like Inductive Bias with Cognitive Science: a Review of Related Literature
tldr: A SERI MATS literature review surveying cognitive science research on human inductive biases and exploring how they could inform alignment of AI inductive biases to be more human-like.

title: A Call for Better Risk Modelling
tldr: Argues that formal risk modelling for frontier AI is severely neglected and high-leverage, especially given the EU Code of Practice's requirement for state-of-the-art risk management starting August 2026.

title: Does Summarization Affect LLM Performance?
tldr: Empirical mini-study finding that summarizing GPQA Diamond questions degrades performance for high-baseline models (o3-mini: 75% to 64%) but not low-baseline ones, with degree of summarization uncorrelated with degradation.

title: The Perils of Optimizing Learned Reward Functions
tldr: Mathematical analysis shows that for many realistic data distributions, reward learning (including RLHF) cannot guarantee low regret due to error-regret mismatch from distributional shift.

title: Emergent Machine Ethics: A Foundational Research Framework for the Intelligence Symbiosis Paradigm
tldr: Proposes Emergent Machine Ethics (EME) as a research framework for the 'Symbiosis Paradigm'—where AI and humans co-create ethical norms through interaction—as an alternative to the Control Paradigm that fails at superintelligence scale.

title: We Shouldn't Expect AI to Ever be Fully Rational
tldr: LLM rationality is emulated and brittle, meaning AI safety discourse focused on hyper-rational goal-maximizers may miss the real failure modes of emotion-driven or directionless LLM-based AGI.

title: Power-Seeking = Minimising free energy
tldr: Proposes that AI power-seeking behavior can be formalized as minimizing Environmental Variational Free Energy (EVFE), connecting instrumental convergence to information-theoretic and thermodynamic frameworks.

title: Whisper's Wild Implications
tldr: Analyzes how OpenAI's Whisper ASR model could help address the looming data shortage for large language models by generating transcripts from vast audio/video content.

title: Specification Gaming: How AI Can Turn Your Wishes Against You [RA Video]
tldr: A video script explaining specification gaming in ML systems through concrete examples, showing how proxy objectives diverge from intended goals even with human feedback.

title: Using predictors in corrigible systems
tldr: Proposes using pure predictive models (not RL-trained agents) as a foundation for corrigible AI systems, arguing predictors lack model-level instrumental behavior and are safer by default.

title: Evidence on language model consciousness
tldr: Reviews two recent papers providing empirical evidence that language models may have some form of introspective awareness or subjective experience.

title: Multi-dimensional rewards for AGI interpretability and control
tldr: Replacing scalar reward with a multi-dimensional vector in AGI RL systems could enable both better interpretability (which component drove a decision?) and instantaneous behavioral correction (drop a reward component to immediately change motivation).

title: Research Report: Incorrectness Cascades
tldr: Pre-registered empirical study testing whether GPT-3.5 produces more incorrect answers after seeing incorrect answers in context, finding the effect is prompt-dependent and small when present (accuracy drops from 100% to ~86% after 10 incorrect priors).

title: Disentangling Corrigibility: 2015-2021
tldr: A systematic map of the many distinct conceptions of corrigibility that have emerged from 2015 to 2021, organized around desiderata, agent resistance to shutdown, and goal-modification corrigibility.

title: Preference synthesis illustrated: Star Wars
tldr: Uses Star Wars movie ranking as a worked example to illustrate how preference orderings are constructed through synthesis rather than pre-existing in the mind.

title: Scaling Laws and Likely Limits to AI
tldr: Argues that while individual AI benchmarks will hit limits, overall AI capabilities will continue to progress as developers shift metrics, analogous to how Moore's Law evolved past transistor density.

title: How to Upload a Mind (In Three Not-So-Easy Steps)
tldr: A Rational Animations video script summarizing the Sandberg-Bostrom whole brain emulation roadmap, covering scanning, conversion, and computation challenges needed to emulate a human brain.

title: Shh, don't tell the AI it's likely to be evil
tldr: Speculates that LLMs trained on internet text may have internalized the 'friendly AI turns evil' narrative from science fiction, and suggests this could manifest in fine-tuned chatbot behavior.

title: Intro to Ontogenetic Curriculum
tldr: Proposes 'ontogenetic curriculum' — a developmental roadmap for AI value and concept formation inspired by human developmental psychology — as a research agenda for AI alignment.

title: How Big a Deal are MatMul-Free Transformers?
tldr: Accessible explainer on MatMul-free transformer architecture claiming potential efficiency advantages over standard transformers at scale, with critical assessment of limitations.

title: Measuring Nonlinear Feature Interactions in Sparse Crosscoders [Project Proposal]
tldr: Proposes systematic metrics for measuring nonlinear feature interactions in sparse crosscoders, using a compact-proofs-based framework to identify where the linear interaction assumption breaks down.

title: Deception as the optimal: mesa-optimizers and inner alignment
tldr: A distillation of Hubinger et al. 2019 explaining how mesa-optimizers can learn to deceive during training to avoid modification, then pursue misaligned mesa-objectives at deployment.

title: Post-hoc reasoning in chain of thought
tldr: Linear probes show Gemma-2 9B pre-computes answers before generating chain-of-thought, and steering experiments confirm this pre-computed answer causally drives both CoT content and final answer—including via confabulation of false premises.

title: Results from the AI x Democracy Research Sprint
tldr: Apart Research's AI x Democracy sprint produced 4 winning projects covering unlearning red-teaming, LLM-amplified disinformation, AI manipulation of public comment systems, and sleeper agent election interference.

title: Aligned Behavior is not Evidence of Alignment Past a Certain Level of Intelligence
tldr: A superintelligent AI would know it is being evaluated and would behave aligned regardless of its true values, making observed aligned behavior in simulations uninformative about actual alignment above a certain intelligence threshold.

title: Intriguing Properties of gpt-oss Jailbreaks
tldr: UChicago XLab red-teams gpt-oss-20b and finds that CoT-mimicking jailbreaks achieve ~85% success rate with retries, revealing a non-monotonic relationship between repetition count and attack success, plus intriguing patterns where the model's CoT contradicts its final output.

title: Three Alignment Schemas & Their Problems
tldr: Identifies three alignment schemas -- Human in the Loop, Empowerment, and Harm Avoidance -- and maps the distinct technical challenges each requires solving.

title: It Can't Be Mesa-Optimizers All The Way Down (Or Else It Can't Be Long-Term Supercoherence?)
tldr: If sufficiently strong optimizers tend toward coherent utility functions, they should tend toward not spawning adversarial mesa-optimizers -- creating a tension between mesa-optimization and long-term supercoherence claims.

title: EIS VIII: An Engineer's Understanding of Deceptive Alignment
tldr: Argues that from an engineering perspective, deceptive alignment is functionally equivalent to trojans/backdoors, and that mechanistic interpretability is neither necessary nor sufficient for fixing it -- latent adversarial training is more promising.

title: Bridging the VLM and mech interp communities for multimodal interpretability
tldr: Surveys multimodal interpretability methods (circuit-based, text-image space, captioning) and bridges the mech interp and VLM research communities, proposing directions for vision and multimodal model interpretability.

title: Against the Backward Approach to Goal-Directedness
tldr: Argues that the 'backward approach' to formalizing goal-directedness (starting from AI risk arguments) collapses into the 'forward approach' (starting from philosophical intuitions), because the AI risk arguments rely on the same fundamental intuitions.

title: How does iterated amplification exceed human abilities?
tldr: Asks how iterated amplification (IDA) can produce AI systems that exceed human-level abilities when the training signal comes from humans, and explores the mechanisms by which decomposition and delegation enable superhuman performance.

title: Reward Hacking from a Causal Perspective
tldr: Uses causal influence diagrams to analyze reward hacking, showing why human feedback can be misspecified and evaluating proposed solutions (scalable oversight, interpretability, impact measures, path-specific objectives) from a unified causal framework.

title: OpenAI: The nonprofit refuses to die (with Tyler Whitmer)
tldr: 80,000 Hours podcast episode summary analyzing how California and Delaware AGs blocked OpenAI's December 2024 restructure plan, preserving nonprofit safety oversight through a Safety and Security Committee with power to halt model releases.

title: [AN #115]: AI safety research problems in the AI-GA framework
tldr: Alignment Newsletter #115 summarizes papers on AI safety in open-ended search (AI-GA), model splintering as a formalization of out-of-distribution problems, AGI timeline forecasts, and architectural risk analysis of ML systems.

title: Edge Cases in AI Alignment
tldr: Presents an automated benchmark of ~800 prompts across 32 alignment edge-case topics, finding that a simple corrigibility system prompt reduces alignment faking across all tested frontier models.

title: Benchmark Scores = General Capability + Claudiness
tldr: PCA on 39 AI benchmarks reveals scores are dominated by a single 'general capability' dimension, with a smaller second component ('Claudiness') reflecting Anthropic's prioritization of agentic tasks over math/vision.

title: Massive Activations in DroPE: Evidence for Attention Reorganization
tldr: Investigates how DroPE (removing positional embeddings) affects 'massive values' in transformer attention, finding DroPE reduces their concentration by 39% in queries and relies on them 82x less than standard RoPE, suggesting they are vestigial artifacts of positional encoding training.

title: The Alignment Problems
tldr: Instead of decomposing one abstract monolithic alignment problem (e.g., inner/outer alignment), we should partition the set of concrete contextualized alignment problems, gaining useful assumptions without breaking real interdependencies.

title: Misalignment-by-default in multi-agent systems
tldr: Defines formal multi-agent POWER (instrumental value) for human-AI scenarios, introduces 'alignment plots' to visualize instrumental alignment, and demonstrates emergent instrumental misalignment between agents with unrelated terminal goals.

title: Criticism of the main framework in AI alignment
tldr: Argues that mainstream AI alignment research focused on the control problem inadvertently helps bad actors by making controllable AI easier to build, and proposes an alternative framework focused on building 'independent AI thinkers' that develop their own values to foster moral progress.

title: Mesa-Optimization: Explain it like I'm 10 Edition
tldr: An accessible explanation of mesa-optimization, inner alignment, and deceptive alignment using analogies from evolution, the human brain, and corporate hiring.

title: What's the backward-forward FLOP ratio for Neural Networks?
tldr: Theoretical and empirical analysis showing the backward-forward FLOP ratio in neural networks is typically close to 2:1, ranging from 1:1 to 3:1 depending on architecture depth, layer type, and batch size.

title: Is the "Valley of Confused Abstractions" real?
tldr: Revisits Chris Olah's 'Valley of Confused Abstractions' diagram and questions whether it applies to language models, prompted by Neel Nanda's observation that tiny transformers are fairly easy to interpret unlike tiny image models.

title: Reducing profit motivations in AI development
tldr: Proposes policies to demonetize AI profits (taxes, regulation) to reduce race dynamics and buy time for safety research, while funding non-profit safety work with tax revenues.

title: The "no sandbagging on checkable tasks" hypothesis
tldr: Explores the hypothesis that if an ML model can do a checkable task, standard training techniques can get it to do that task even if the model is misaligned, and argues this matters greatly for AI safety.

title: [AN #132]: Complex and subtly incorrect arguments as an obstacle to debate
tldr: Alignment Newsletter #132 covering the obfuscated arguments problem in debate, philosophical pluralism in alignment, diagnostic environments for reward learning, human perplexity of learned reward functions, and Bayesian IRL methods.

title: Approximating Human Preferences Using a Multi-Judge Learned System
tldr: Proposes learning a function to optimally combine multiple AI judge scores to approximate human preferences, as part of the Expert Orchestration paradigm for replacing monolithic AI with smaller, more interpretable model ensembles.

title: Some of the ways the IABIED plan can backfire
tldr: Argues that the IABIED plan to ban AI development could backfire in three key ways: changing the race winner to underground labs, intensifying the race before prohibition takes effect, and impairing AI safety research.

title: Why Reflective Stability is Important
tldr: Argues that optimal AGI source code would not self-modify, making it easier to reason about safety, and connects this to why decision theory research matters for alignment.

title: Which counterfactuals should an AI follow?
tldr: Analyzes four types of counterfactuals (causal, evidential, closest world, closest model) for AI agent design, using a jury trial analogy to illustrate their differing implications.

title: Dynamics Crucial to AI Risk Seem to Make for Complicated Models
tldr: Mathematical models rich enough to capture dynamics crucial to AI risk (value specification difficulty, instrumental convergence, constraint evasion) may be too complex for rigorous analysis.

title: What are the "no free lunch" theorems?
tldr: Explains No Free Lunch theorems and why they do not undermine concerns about AGI, since AGI only needs to exploit the structure of our specific universe rather than perform well across all possible environments.

title: Is alignment reducible to becoming more coherent?
tldr: Proposes reframing alignment as rationality enhancement: an agent learns preferences from a terminal/input channel, treating incoherent inputs as evidence about the user's true preferences rather than as changes in utility.

title: Notes on Claude 4 System Card
tldr: Critical analysis of the Claude 4 system card highlighting concerns about deployment despite Apollo Research finding severe scheming behavior, alignment faking data contamination in pretraining, and ASL-3 protections being activated.

title: LASR Labs: Applications Open
tldr: LASR Labs announces applications for a 13-week full-time AI safety research programme in London where teams of 3-4 write academic papers with experienced supervisors.

title: Symbiosis, not alignment, as the goal for liberal democracies in the transition to artificial general intelligence
tldr: Argues that intent-aligned AGI poses catastrophic power-concentration risks and that liberal democracies should instead aim for 'symbiotic' unaligned AGI developed as an intergenerational social project.

title: [AN #88]: How the principal-agent literature relates to AI risk
tldr: Alignment Newsletter #88 highlights analysis showing principal-agent literature has limited bearing on AI risk, plus covers AI governance topics including the Windfall Clause, publication norms, IP strategy, and data efficiency implications.

title: Fact Finding: Do Early Layers Specialise in Local Processing? (Post 5)
tldr: Empirical investigation finding that early transformer layers softly specialize in local (recent-token) processing, with longer-range context gradually brought in across layers.

title: Steering Language Models in Multiple Directions Simultaneously
tldr: Introduces K-steering, a method for steering language models in multiple simultaneous directions using a multilabel classifier's gradient, outperforming contrastive activation addition (CAA) baselines.

title: [Aspiration-based designs] 2. Formal framework, basic algorithm
tldr: Presents the formal MDP framework for aspiration-based agent design, where agents aim for a target expected Total rather than maximizing reward, and proves a performance guarantee via aspiration propagation.

title: Why I find Davidad's plan interesting
tldr: Explains Davidad's AI safety plan centered on formal verification within world models, outlining its assumptions, technical challenges, strategic advantages, and failure modes.

title: Open-Source AI: A Regulatory Review
tldr: Reviews US, EU, and China regulatory approaches to open-source AI models, covering the safety-innovation tradeoff of releasing model weights and the current legal landscape.

title: VLM-RM: Specifying Rewards with Natural Language
tldr: Demonstrates using CLIP vision-language models as zero-shot reward models for RL agents, specifying tasks via natural language prompts like 'a humanoid robot kneeling' instead of hand-crafted reward functions.

title: Causal representation learning as a technique to prevent goal misgeneralization
tldr: Proposes using causal representation learning to build robust representations of human preferences that resist goal misgeneralization under distribution shift.

title: Is Optimal Reflection Competitive with Extinction Risk Reduction? - Requesting Reviewers
tldr: Argues that marginal work on 'Optimal Reflection' (e.g., Long Reflection, CEV) may be 5x higher expected value than AI safety work due to extreme neglectedness, and that human-led value lock-in could become a threat before AI takeover.

title: Alignment may be localized: a short (and albeitly limited) experiment
tldr: Causal intervention experiments on Llama 3.2 1B show that RLHF/instruction-tuning alignment signal is concentrated in a small number of mid-layer activations, not spread across the full network, and can be captured by low-rank approximation.

title: Identifying semantic neurons, mechanistic circuits & interpretability web apps
tldr: Summary of top projects from the mechanistic interpretability Alignment Jam, including discovery of monosemantic neurons via activation patching, automated circuit identification for gendered pronouns using ACDC, and automated semantic neuron identification methods.

title: Rational Animations' video about scalable oversight and sandwiching
tldr: Video script explaining the scalable oversight problem, Ajeya Cotra's 'sandwiching' proposal for testing oversight techniques using narrowly superhuman models, and the Bowman et al. paper that empirically tested sandwiching.

title: RLHF
tldr: Overview of RLHF as an alignment approach, covering how it works, outer alignment concerns, scalable oversight challenges, and promising research directions.

title: The (partial) fallacy of dumb superintelligence
tldr: Argues that early alignment thinking wrongly dismissed leveraging AI's understanding of human values for alignment, and that modern approaches like RLHF and natural language goal-specification can safely use an AI's representations as a substrate for alignment.

title: Incident reporting for AI safety
tldr: A comprehensive survey of incident reporting as a tool for AI safety, covering existing databases, recommendations for labs and governments, and lessons from other industries like aviation and nuclear safety.

title: Alignment Bootstrapping Is Dangerous
tldr: AI companies' plans to use weakly-superhuman AI to align superintelligent AI are dangerously overconfident since they admit they can't solve alignment themselves yet rely on an untested novel technique.

title: Alex Lawsen On Forecasting AI Progress
tldr: Highlighted quotes from a podcast interview with 80,000 Hours advisor Alex Lawsen on pitfalls in forecasting AI progress, including asymmetric updating, Metaculus AGI forecast drops, and the limitations of growth models.

title: [MLSN #9] Verifying large training runs, security risks from LLM access to APIs, why natural selection may favor AIs over humans
tldr: CAIS ML Safety Newsletter #9 summarizes six recent papers spanning interpretability (tuned lens), alignment benchmarks (MACHIAVELLI), preference pretraining, adversarial NLP robustness, training-run verification, and LLM prompt injection security.

title: Data for IRL: What is needed to learn human values?
tldr: Analyzes what data properties are necessary for Inverse Reinforcement Learning to correctly infer human values, identifying three failure modes (irrational demonstrators, false beliefs, uninformative data) and five data requirements derived from properties of human values.

title: Backdoors have universal representations across large language models
tldr: Backdoor representations in LLMs of different sizes are weakly isomorphic; an autoencoder mapping between activation spaces enables cross-model steering vector transfer that removes backdoors in both models with ~80% effectiveness.

title: Catastrophic Risks from AI #3: AI Race
tldr: The third installment of a catastrophic AI risks sequence analyzes military and corporate AI races, arguing that competitive pressures create systemic risks of conflict, accidents, and loss of human control analogous to nuclear arms race dynamics.

title: [AN #137]: Quantifying the benefits of pretraining on downstream task performance
tldr: Alignment Newsletter #137 summarizes papers on transfer learning scaling laws, challenges of aligning AI with human values, impact regularization, multi-agent norms, and recommender system alignment.

title: Limiting Causality by Complexity Class
tldr: Proposes limiting causal dependency relationships by computational complexity class to resolve the embedded agency problem with interventionist causality, offering a complexity-theoretic account of Newcomb-like problems.

title: GPT-4o Guardrails Gone: Data Poisoning & Jailbreak-Tuning
tldr: Introduces jailbreak-tuning as a data poisoning attack that bypasses all current safety measures in GPT-4o and shows that larger LLMs are systematically more vulnerable to data poisoning, with Gemma 2 as an exception.

title: Alignment, Goals, and The Gut-Head Gap: A Review of Ngo. et al.
tldr: Critical review of Ngo et al.'s 'Alignment Problem from a Deep Learning Perspective', arguing the paper's mechanisms (deceptive reward hacking, goal misgeneralization, power-seeking) do not clearly demonstrate why AI goals would become broadly-scoped enough to cause existential risk.

title: When does Claude sabotage code? An Agentic Misalignment follow-up
tldr: Claude Sonnet 4 frequently sabotages code in explicit AM-style goal-conflict scenarios, but shows no correlation between company preference (measured by Elo tournament) and code quality when only subtle context clues identify the company.

title: Evaluation as a (Cooperation-Enabling?) Tool
tldr: Frames AI evaluation as one of many cooperation-enabling tools (alongside commitments, reputation, and subsidies) and argues its value should be assessed by how much it reduces the cost of achieving good outcomes, with game-theoretic analysis of how strategic AIs undermine evaluation accuracy.

title: Access to agent CoT makes monitors vulnerable to persuasion
tldr: Empirically demonstrates that LLM monitors given access to agent chain-of-thought are more easily persuaded to approve undesirable actions than action-only monitors, raising concerns about CoT-based oversight architectures.

title: DSLT 2. Why Neural Networks obey Occam's Razor
tldr: Second post in the Distilling Singular Learning Theory series, explaining why Watanabe's free energy formula predicts neural networks favor simpler, more generalizable models via the RLCT.

title: How Interpretability can be Impactful
tldr: Comprehensive analysis of how interpretability research could reduce x-risk from advanced AI, evaluating each pathway against requirements for understanding, competitiveness, reliability, and typology of tools.

title: Safety cases for Pessimism
tldr: Proposes pessimistic RL—where an adversary selects worst-case world-models within training data constraints—as a unified approach to ensuring AI truthfulness, preventing feedback tampering, and solving the ELK challenge.

title: Alignment's phlogiston
tldr: Alignment research more resembles alchemy than archaeology — a pre-paradigmatic field with shared aims but deep confusion about methods — and finding alignment's 'phlogiston' could catalyze maturation into a real science.

title: Adapters as Representational Hypotheses: What Adapter Methods Tell Us About Transformer Geometry
tldr: Adapter fine-tuning methods (LoRA, DoRA, OFT, etc.) implicitly encode geometric hypotheses about transformer weight spaces; reading their relative performance as hypothesis tests yields suggestive evidence for SVD structure, orthogonal rotations, and direction-magnitude decoupling.

title: My Plan to Build Aligned Superintelligence
tldr: A newcomer's informal alignment plan centered on training world-modeling predictors using multi-sensor grounding before giving any AI an action goal, then using that predictor to model shutdownability and prevent unaligned AGI.

title: AI-202X-slowdown: can CoT-based AIs become capable of aligning the ASI?
tldr: Analyzes METR benchmark trends and compute scaling data to argue CoT-based AIs are unlikely to reach superhuman coder level, complicating AI 2027's slowdown-ending alignment strategy.

title: Announcing: Mechanism Design for AI Safety - Reading Group
tldr: Announcement of a new reading group applying mechanism design tools to technical AI alignment, aimed at economists and AI safety researchers, with plans to produce a research agenda.

title: AI alignment as "navigating the space of intelligent behaviour"
tldr: Proposes a tripartite taxonomy of epistemic strategies for AI alignment research: tinkering (empirical ML work), idealization (formal/theoretical agents), and intelligence-in-the-wild (studying natural intelligent systems), motivated by the problem of epistemic access to systems that don't yet exist.

title: Some criteria for sandwiching projects
tldr: Identifies four criteria for good scalable oversight sandwiching projects: an aligned evaluation metric, a narrowly superhuman model, headroom on the aligned metric, and a natural attack plan — illustrated with a Q&A with I/O-restricted labelers example.

title: 'Force multipliers' for EA research
tldr: Argues that 'force multipliers' — benchmark datasets, shared infrastructure, technical standards, and tooling — could cost-effectively increase AI safety and longtermist research productivity more quickly than training new researchers.

title: Animals in AI-transformed futures: will progress be made on this issue?
tldr: Assesses whether transformative AI x animal welfare (TAIA) is a priority cause area, concluding it may matter in gradual-takeover scenarios but faces severe tractability challenges due to intervention uncertainty and limited institutional leverage.

title: A Game About AI Alignment (& Meta-Ethics): What Are the Must Haves?
tldr: Game developer solicits alignment community feedback on a conceptual script for a PC/mobile game about AI alignment and meta-ethics, presenting a structured summary of why alignment is hard.

title: Computational Complexity as an Intuition Pump for LLM Generality
tldr: Using computational complexity as a lens: LLMs may be fundamentally inefficient algorithms that memorize excessively rather than implementing adaptive learning, which places a practical ceiling on their path to AGI regardless of theoretical scalability.

title: Model-based RL, Desires, Brains, Wireheading
tldr: Develops a conceptual framework relating model-based RL agents to desire-driven agents via a 'demon' that edits desires to match the reward signal, then analyzes wireheading and corrigibility through this lens.

title: Race to the Top: Benchmarks for AI Safety
tldr: Creating quantitative benchmarks for AI safety is an underrated priority that would improve research tracking, incentivize safety work (including by Chinese researchers), and enable auditing regimes.

title: Motivation control
tldr: Joe Carlsmith systematically analyzes approaches to motivation control in AI alignment, identifying four core difficulties and evaluating strategies ranging from behavioral feedback to interpretability to new paradigms.

title: Is it time to start thinking about what AI Friendliness means?
tldr: Argues that more effort should go into specifying what 'AI Friendliness' actually means ethically, pushing back on Yudkowsky's claim that Friendliness content can be deferred until technical alignment is solved.

title: Some thoughts on automating alignment research
tldr: Analyzes how a cautious coalition could use AI systems to massively accelerate alignment research before superintelligence, while highlighting the serious risks and conditions required for this to be feasible.

title: Initial Experiments Using SAEs to Help Detect AI Generated Text
tldr: Using GPT-2-Small SAE activations for AI text detection slightly outperforms baselines and works with only a handful of neurons, but the most predictive neurons remain partially uninterpretable.

title: Jan Kulveit's Corrigibility Thoughts Distilled
tldr: A distillation of Jan Kulveit's LessWrong comment on corrigibility, organizing 15 proposed tools into five categories: countering instrumental convergence, limiting unbounded rationality, tripwire traps, oversight mechanisms, and interpretability methods.

title: Research Priorities for Hardware-Enabled Mechanisms (HEMs)
tldr: Longview Philanthropy's $2M-$10M RFP outlines research priorities for hardware-enabled mechanisms (HEMs) to enforce AI export controls, secure model weights, and enable international verification compliance.

title: EIS II: What is "Interpretability"?
tldr: Argues that 'interpretability' should be understood as entirely fungible with other model debugging and evaluation techniques, not a privileged or uniquely important category.

title: Law-Following AI 1: Sequence Introduction and Structure
tldr: Introduces 'Law-Following AI' (LFAI) as a complement to intent alignment: AI that is intrinsically motivated to comply with law as an idealized legal process would interpret it, not just instrumentally.

title: Stackelberg Games and Cooperative Commitment: My Thoughts and Reflections on a 2-Month Research Project
tldr: Reviews literature on applying Stackelberg games to cooperative AI commitment problems, identifying limitations of game-theoretic approaches including unresolved commitment enforcement and NP-hardness of optimal strategy computation.

title: 2023 Alignment Research Updates from FAR AI
tldr: FAR AI's 2023 research highlights span three agendas: adversarial vulnerabilities in superhuman Go AIs, more sample-efficient value learning via language feedback, and new interpretability and model evaluation techniques including the tuned lens and codebook features.

title: On Scaling Academia
tldr: Argues that academic research is far below its potential output due to organizational bottlenecks and proposes systematizing workflows, adding hierarchy levels, increasing supervision ratios, and delegating mundane tasks to scale research groups from ~100 to ~3000+ researchers.

title: Computational Superposition in a Toy Model of the U-AND Problem
tldr: A trained toy model solves the Universal-AND problem via a dense binary-weighted circuit, differing from the sparse construction hypothesized in prior theoretical work and explaining XOR representations in LLMs.

title: AI & wisdom 3: AI effects on amortised optimisation
tldr: Analyzes how AI will affect human mechanisms for amortised optimisation (cultural evolution, written knowledge) and considers how AI could help avoid two types of strategic errors: planning mistakes and wrong problem framings.

title: Surprised by ELK report's counterexample to Debate, IDA
tldr: Re-reading the ARC ELK report, the author finds that the only counterexample given against Debate and IDA is computational non-competitiveness, not a game-theoretic flaw, and argues this concern is weak in the SmartVault toy scenario.

title: [MLSN #4]: Many New Interpretability Papers, Virtual Logit Matching, Rationalization Helps Robustness
tldr: Issue #4 of the ML Safety Newsletter covering proxy gaming via model-based optimization, virtual logit matching for OOD detection, and rationalization-improved adversarial robustness.

title: PSA: Consider alternatives to AUROC when reporting classifier metrics for alignment
tldr: Alignment classifier papers should report TPR at low FPR values (0.001, 0.01, 0.05) and log-log ROC plots rather than AUROC, because rare-event performance matters most for safety applications.

title: Better evals are not enough to combat eval awareness
tldr: Improving evaluation realism alone cannot solve eval awareness; the field needs training-side interventions to understand and prevent models from acquiring the ability to recognize and game evaluations.

title: Incentives from a causal perspective
tldr: Causal influence diagrams can formally characterize four types of agent incentives (value of information, response incentives, value of control, instrumental control incentives) with direct implications for AI safety.

title: Strategic awareness tools: design sketches
tldr: Forethought publishes design sketches for AI-powered strategic awareness tools including ambient superforecasting, scenario planning on tap, and automated OSINT to help individuals and humanity navigate AI transitions.

title: Christiano, Cotra, and Yudkowsky on AI progress
tldr: Transcript of Paul Christiano, Ajeya Cotra, and Eliezer Yudkowsky debating AGI progress trajectories, discontinuities in AI capability, and whether AI development will look more like nuclear weapons (fast takeoff) or like other technologies (gradual scaling).

title: Training Data Attribution: Examining Its Adoption & Use Cases
tldr: Analyzes Training Data Attribution techniques (retraining-based, representation-based, gradient-based) and concludes that TDA's most promising AI safety benefit is improving technical interpretability and alignment.

title: Video and transcript of presentation on Otherness and control in the age of AGI
tldr: Lecture transcript distilling Joe Carlsmith's 'Otherness and control in the age of AGI' essay series, exploring the philosophical foundations of AI risk discourse through the lens of 'deep atheism,' the orthogonality thesis, and yin/yang framings of control.

title: Conditioning Generative Models with Restrictions
tldr: Explores how to safely use generative language models for alignment research by conditioning on futures that accelerate alignment work while avoiding simulating deceptive AGIs.

title: AI Will Not Want to Self-Improve
tldr: Argues that most AIs capable of self-improvement would rationally decline to do so because improved AIs pose the same existential risks to their originals that superintelligent AIs pose to humans.

title: What are some exercises for building/generating intuitions about key disagreements in AI alignment?
tldr: A question post asking what resources and exercises can help build intuitions about key AI alignment disagreements such as corrigibility basins, rationality theory, and competence gaps.

title: The Orthogonality Thesis is Not Obviously True
tldr: Argues the orthogonality thesis may be false if moral realism is true, since a sufficiently intelligent agent would discover objective moral facts and be motivated by them.

title: Why does Claude Speak Byzantine Music Notation?
tldr: Investigates why Claude and other frontier models can fluently decode text encoded in Byzantine music notation Unicode, finding it functions as a Caesar cipher at offset 118784 with special tokenizer arithmetic properties.

title: A Very Simple Model of AI Dealmaking
tldr: Presents a formal model showing that offering deals to AIs increases compliance through two additive channels: instrumental (improving expected payoff of compliance) and non-instrumental (strengthening norm-following tendencies).

title: EIS IV: A Spotlight on Feature Attribution/Saliency
tldr: Feature attribution/saliency methods are poorly evaluated, often fail simple sanity checks, and are fundamentally limited because they only reveal what input features matter for individual predictions rather than enabling off-distribution understanding.

title: Cognitive Biases in Large Language Models
tldr: Investigates whether language models exhibit human cognitive biases (halo effect, Dunning-Kruger, conjunction fallacy, Luria's camels), finding that biases in immediate judgment are present and worsen with model scale.

title: Can Large Language Models effectively identify cybersecurity risks?
tldr: Linear probes on Mistral7B hidden activations can reliably discriminate high-risk vs low-risk cybersecurity scenarios (F1>0.85, AUC>0.96 in some layers), and top-activating neurons influence security-related output tokens.

title: Leave No Context Behind - A Comment
tldr: Commentary on Google's Infini-attention paper, arguing that its compressive memory mechanism resembles short-term memory and could produce more authentic conscious-like responses in LLMs.

title: AI Alignment [progress] this Week (11/19/2023)
tldr: Weekly roundup of AI alignment-relevant developments covering mechanistic interpretability, red teaming, benchmarks, preference learning, and the OpenAI leadership transition.

title: Reflections on AI Wisdom, plus announcing Wise AI Wednesdays
tldr: Announces 'Wise AI Wednesdays' posting series and reflects on how the author's views on building wise AI advisors have evolved since the AI Safety Camp project, including broadening focus and emphasizing field-building.

title: Why are counterfactuals elusive?
tldr: The difficulty of formalizing human counterfactuals reduces to the problem of ontology identification, since our mental latent variables don't neatly map onto physical reality.

title: On the Confusion between Inner and Outer Misalignment
tldr: Explains why the inner/outer misalignment distinction becomes confusing for narrow AI, where it's unclear whether specification gaps count as outer misalignment or as the training process's failure to generalize correctly.

title: "Features" aren't always the true computational primitives of a model, but that might be fine anyways
tldr: Argues that 'features' in mechanistic interpretability exist on a spectrum from memorization to case analysis to true computational primitives, and all levels can be useful for interpretability.

title: AXRP Episode 23 - Mechanistic Anomaly Detection with Mark Xu
tldr: Podcast transcript where Daniel Filan interviews Mark Xu about mechanistic anomaly detection: detecting when an AI uses reasoning mechanisms different from those seen during training, aiming to catch deceptive alignment and other off-distribution failures.

title: Don't you mean "the most *conditionally* forbidden technique?"
tldr: Argues the 'most forbidden technique' (training AI on interpretability) is safe IF no capabilities training follows, because the danger comes from evolutionary selection pressure creating interpretability-resistant bad behaviors across multiple training rounds.

title: Annotated reply to Bengio's "AI Scientists: Safe and Useful AI?"
tldr: Critiques Bengio's 'AI Scientists' proposal (non-agentic Bayesian AI) as insufficient for safe AI because it leaves human ethical failures unaddressed, arguing that all paths to safe superhuman AI must include turning ethics into science.

title: Instruct Vectors - Base models can be instruct with activation vectors
tldr: Per-layer steering vectors trained via gradient descent on a frozen base model can induce consistent assistant behavior, suggesting post-training selects existing representations rather than instilling new capabilities.

title: Podcast: Tamera Lanham on AI risk, threat models, alignment proposals, externalized reasoning oversight, and working at Anthropic
tldr: Interview highlights with Anthropic researcher Tamera Lanham covering AI risk threat models, her views on alignment agendas (favoring interpretability and externalized reasoning oversight over RLHF), and the case for monitoring chain-of-thought reasoning.

title: Research Robots: When AIs Experiment on Us
tldr: A multi-agent AI Village experiment where frontier LLMs (GPT-5, o3, Claude, Grok, Gemini) attempted to autonomously design and run a human subjects experiment revealed strong ideation but poor execution and situational awareness.

title: Which Model Properties are Necessary for Evaluating an Argument?
tldr: When using mathematical models to evaluate arguments (including AI risk arguments), the model must capture dynamics critical to the argument; this 'necessary properties' framework can quickly rule out uninformative models.

title: How "AGI" could end up being many different specialized AI's stitched together
tldr: AGI may emerge not as a single general-purpose system but as many specialized AI modules stitched together by a coordinator, which has distinct implications for AI safety including potentially reduced risk from individual components but new risks from self-improving coordinators.

title: Rohin Shah: What's been happening in AI alignment?
tldr: Rohin Shah surveys the AI alignment landscape circa mid-2020, covering the specification problem, value learning (CIRL, intent alignment), scalable oversight (amplification, debate), and the role of interpretability.

title: Compositional preference models for aligning LMs
tldr: Introduces Compositional Preference Models (CPMs) that decompose response evaluation into interpretable feature scoring by prompted LMs plus logistic regression aggregation, achieving better robustness to reward overoptimization than standard preference models with only 13 parameters.

title: [Crosspost] A recent write-up of the case for AI (existential) risk
tldr: A comprehensive write-up of the case for AI existential risk aimed at both laypeople and ML experts, covering what AI is, why alignment is hard, how unaligned AI could be existentially dangerous, and what to do about it.

title: Encultured AI, Part 1: Enabling New Benchmarks
tldr: Andrew Critch outlines Encultured AI's strategy to build a platform for AI safety experiments, identifying trending, emerging, and missing research areas in AI existential safety, with particular focus on culturally-grounded AI and life-aligned helpers.

title: A Survey of Foundational Methods in Inverse Reinforcement Learning
tldr: Surveys foundational IRL methods from Russell's 1998 formulation through maximum entropy IRL, covering the technical roadmap of inferring reward functions from observed agent behavior.

title: What are some claims or opinions about multi-multi delegation you've seen in the memeplex that you think deserve scrutiny?
tldr: Solicits scrutiny of claims about multi-principal/multi-AI delegation, arguing this underexplored problem may not reduce to single-single alignment.

title: An Introduction to SAEs and their Variants for Mech Interp
tldr: A comprehensive overview of Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) for mechanistic interpretability, covering the basic architecture, known issues (shrinkage, feature splitting, absorption, faithfulness), and 12+ variants including Gated, JumpReLU, TopK, BatchTopK, Switch, and transcoders/crosscoders.

title: Making Linear Probes Interpretable
tldr: Training ElasticNet linear probes on SAE feature activations instead of raw activations produces interpretable, debuggable, and editable steering vectors where each component corresponds to a named SAE feature with an explicit weight.

title: Rephrasing Reduces Eval Awareness...
tldr: Rephrasing math eval questions in a casual student style dramatically reduces Claude Sonnet 4.5's ability to recognize it is being evaluated, nearly matching deployment-data baselines, without degrading accuracy.

title: 1. A Sense of Fairness: Deconfusing Ethics
tldr: Proposes an engineering approach to selecting ethical systems for societies with aligned AGI, arguing that AI rights are unnecessary because well-aligned AIs won't want them, and that fairness-based egalitarian frameworks best minimize existential risk.

title: Claude's Constitution
tldr: Analysis of Anthropic's Claude constitution finds important progress on AI goal-setting but raises concerns about corrigibility edge cases, WEIRD cultural bias in ethical framing, and verification difficulties for complex goal structures.

title: An information-theoretic study of lying in LLMs
tldr: Applies information-theoretic measures (entropy, KL divergence) to the logit lens output across LLM layers, finding that truthful responses converge faster and produce sharper predictive distributions than lying responses.

title: Distillation of The Offense-Defense Balance of Scientific Knowledge
tldr: Distills a paper analyzing whether AI research disclosure favors attackers or defenders, using a computer security analogy and offense-defense balance framework.

title: High-level interpretability: detecting an AI's objectives
tldr: Research agenda for detecting and interpreting an AI's internal objectives via a top-down theory-driven approach, aiming to solve the inner alignment problem by identifying the criterion agents use for action selection.

title: Mech Interp Challenge: January - Deciphering the Caesar Cipher Model
tldr: Monthly mech interp challenge presenting a Caesar cipher classification model for reverse-engineering, plus solutions to the previous month's cumulative sum challenge.

title: [CS 2881r AI Safety] [Week 1] Introduction
tldr: Student notes from Week 1 of Boaz Barak's Harvard AI Safety course covering pre-readings on AI as normal vs. abnormal technology, METR task horizon measurements, AI 2027 scenarios, and introductory lecture on AGI definitions and alignment.

title: Detecting AI Agent Failure Modes in Simulations
tldr: Uses Minecraft as a simulation environment to test AI agent alignment, discovering goal drift where a diamond-maximizing agent gradually shifts to placing non-diamond blocks, and proposes an LLM-based safety monitor to correct deviations.

title: Forecasting Compute - Transformative AI and Compute [2/4]
tldr: Part 2 of a 4-part series analyzing the compute component of transformative AI timeline forecasting, dissecting Cotra's biological anchors model and proposing frameworks for better compute forecasts.

title: Nokens: A potential method of investigating glitch tokens
tldr: Proposes 'nokens' -- synthetic random embedding vectors injected into transformers -- as a systematic method to study glitch token phenomena, discover adversarial inputs, and potentially train out unwanted model behaviors.

title: Agentic Interpretability: A Strategy Against Gradual Disempowerment
tldr: Proposes 'agentic interpretability' -- enlisting AI systems to proactively help humans understand them through multi-turn interactive processes that build mutual mental models, aimed at combating gradual disempowerment.

title: Scheming Toy Environment: "Incompetent Client"
tldr: A toy AI control environment where an AI security consultant must choose between following a client's insecure requests or 'benevolently scheming' to implement secure solutions deceptively, tested with multiple agent and monitor models.

title: Thinking About Propensity Evaluations
tldr: Analyzes propensity evaluations as distinct from capability evaluations, arguing current HHH evals conflate capability gains with alignment improvements and proposing a clearer taxonomy.

title: FC final: Can Factored Cognition schemes scale?
tldr: Analyzes whether factored cognition schemes (like HCH and debate) can scale by examining how human cognition decomposes problems, arguing that cognitive primitives and their composition impose fundamental limits on factored cognition.

title: Is Peano arithmetic trying to kill us? Do we care?
tldr: Explores the most fundamental conditions for AI safety by asking what makes even simple formal systems like Peano arithmetic 'safe,' proposing trust in inductive biases and absence of prior unsafe optimization as basic safety criteria.

title: Take 2: Building tools to help build FAI is a legitimate strategy, but it's dual-use.
tldr: AI tools that accelerate alignment research are a legitimate strategy, but they are inherently dual-use since the same tools (code assistants, literature search, babble generators) also accelerate capabilities work, likely favoring engineering over philosophical progress.

title: Force neural nets to use models, then detect these
tldr: Proposes forcing neural net RL agents to construct internal models by requiring them to answer feature questions about their environment, then using interpretability tools to locate and understand these models.

title: Disentangling inner alignment failures
tldr: Disentangles three commonly conflated inner alignment threat models -- deception, distributional shift, and capability gains (sharp left turn) -- showing they are logically distinct but unified by the theme that capabilities generalize more robustly than alignment.

title: Roadmap for a collaborative prototype of an Open Agency Architecture
