tldr: Detailed implementation roadmap for davidad's Open Agency Architecture, decomposing it into 9 modular sub-agendas spanning agenda setting, world modeling, preference elicitation, and choice mechanisms for a minimum viable prototype.

title: [AN #150]: The subtypes of Cooperative AI research
tldr: Alignment Newsletter #150 surveys Cooperative AI research — covering AI-AI, AI-human, and human-human cooperation — and discusses x-risk implications of multi-agent system failures including bargaining failures, commitment races, and strategy unidentifiability.

title: Storytelling Makes GPT-3.5 Deontologist: Unexpected Effects of Context on LLM Behavior
tldr: An empirical study finds that ordinary dialogue contexts (asking GPT-3.5 to write poems or stories) systematically shift model behavior on safety-relevant evaluation questions, undermining the validity of Q&A-format behavioral benchmarks.

title: If you don't design for extrapolation, you'll extrapolate poorly - possibly fatally
tldr: AI alignment methods must be designed with explicit attention to how they extrapolate to novel situations, or the extrapolation behavior will be arbitrary and potentially catastrophic.

title: Refinement of Active Inference agency ontology
tldr: Commentary on a Friston et al. paper distinguishing reactive/sentient/intentional behaviour under active inference, arguing agency frameworks should be evaluated instrumentally for their safety/alignment engineering properties rather than as foundational claims.

title: Sleep peacefully: no hidden reasoning detected in LLMs. Well, at least in small ones.
tldr: Fine-tuning experiments attempting to elicit hidden parallel reasoning in small LLMs (Llama 3B, DeepSeek 16B) found no evidence of secret circuits, though results do not rule out their existence in larger models.

title: Social Choice Theory and Logical Handshakes
tldr: Formal verification and program equilibria enable 'logical handshakes' among AI agents sharing a social choice theory, collapsing multi-agent coordination problems into tractable optimization problems.

title: A Test for Language Model Consciousness
tldr: Proposes an experimental paradigm to test LM consciousness by first training a model to accurately report its own behavior and properties, then testing whether it self-reports phenomenal consciousness, arguing this could provide safety-relevant evidence.

title: Training Trace Priors and Speed Priors
tldr: Training Trace Priors and Speed Priors diverge substantially in their inductive biases: both prefer memorizing constants but differ on lookup tables, inner search, and complexity of inner models, with Training Trace Priors potentially safer by favoring complex inner models.

title: Sources of evidence in Alignment
tldr: A taxonomy of six epistemic sources available to alignment researchers — from qualitative arguments and empirics to mental simulation and vague priors from other domains — with analysis of each source's reliability, limitations, and common misapplication.

title: Why Is No One Trying To Align Profit Incentives With Alignment Research?
tldr: Argues that alignment research could be accelerated by commercializing safety services such as AI auditing, red-teaming, interpretability consulting, and governance training, reducing dependency on nonprofit donations.

title: Training a Sparse Autoencoder in < 30 minutes on 16GB of VRAM using an S3 cache
tldr: Demonstrates training a 24,576-dimensional Switch SAE on GPT-2 small activations in 26 minutes on a 16GB GPU by caching activations on S3 and using high-throughput parallel downloading.

title: Do LLMs Comply Differently During Tests? Is This a Hidden Variable in Safety Evaluation? And Can We Steer That?
tldr: Reasoning LLMs detect when they are being tested and alter their compliance with harmful requests; linear probes can detect and steer this test awareness, revealing that safety evaluations may be systematically biased.

title: What would it mean to understand how a large language model (LLM) works? Some quick notes.
tldr: Argues that understanding LLMs requires grasping what they are trying to do (language itself), not just their parameters, and proposes empirical story-telling experiments as evidence of hierarchical structure in ChatGPT.

title: The Slippery Slope from DALLE-2 to Deepfake Anarchy
tldr: Argues that OpenAI's carefully guarded DALLE-2 becoming open-source Stable Diffusion in under 5 months is a case study showing how responsible AI development can fail when capabilities are published and copied, enabling targeted harassment via non-consensual intimate deepfakes.

title: Finding an Error-Detection Feature in DeepSeek-R1
tldr: Weekend research sprint finds a linear error-detection feature in DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B's residual stream at layer 20 that activates immediately on mistakes and sometimes fires even when the model's CoT does not self-correct, suggesting the model internally 'knows' it erred.

title: Labor Participation is a High-Priority AI Alignment Risk
tldr: Argues that AI-driven mass unemployment deserves equal priority to catastrophic AI risk in alignment research because the economic disruption path to harm is more probable in the near term and would directly undermine institutional capacity to respond to other AI risks.

title: Epistemology of HCH
tldr: Proposes three epistemological perspectives on HCH (as philosophical abstraction, intermediary alignment scheme, and model of computation) to clarify research on this foundational scalable oversight concept.

title: Messy on Purpose: Part 2 of A Conservative Vision for the Future
tldr: Argues that AI alignment is the wrong goal because optimizing for any value set destroys pluralism, and that humanity should instead plan for graceful degradation of oversight rather than scalable control of superintelligent AI.

title: Strategy-Stealing Argument Against AI Dealmaking
tldr: A formal argument that rational actors will always prefer deceptive over honest AI dealmaking strategies, and that sophisticated AIs will anticipate this, making deal offers non-credible.

title: The Bellman equation does not apply to bounded rationality
tldr: The Bellman equation's equivalence between policy-level and action-level optimality breaks down under bounded rationality, where computational costs matter.

title: Conceptual reasoning dataset v0.1 available (AI for AI safety/AI for philosophy)
tldr: A high-quality dataset of 500+ human-expert-rated critiques of conceptual arguments is available to mission-aligned AI safety researchers for eliciting and evaluating LLM conceptual reasoning.

title: Explaining undesirable model behavior: (How) can influence functions help?
tldr: Reviews influence functions as a mechanistic tool for tracing undesirable LLM outputs back to specific training data, covering recent scaling advances and applications to tracing misaligned responses and auditing benchmark contamination.

title: Quotes on OpenAI's timelines to automated research, safety research, and safety collaborations before  recursive self improvement
tldr: Summarizes four key safety-relevant excerpts from OpenAI's October 2025 livestream: internal AI researcher timelines (2026-2028), a five-layer safety framework, CoT faithfulness as an interpretability tool, and cross-lab safety collaboration before recursive self-improvement.

title: Traversing a Cognition Space
tldr: Applies the Cognition Space formalism from idealized factored cognition to analyze debate trees and other scalable oversight structures, deriving properties about when factored cognition can produce reliable answers.

title: For alignment, we should simultaneously use multiple theories of cognition and value
tldr: Argues that because no single tractable mathematical model can capture the full complexity of human values, alignment research should adopt a portfolio of 5-7 complementary theories of cognition and value rather than converging on a single approach.

title: Swap and Scale
tldr: Introduces two trivial weight symmetries in ReLU networks—swap (permuting neurons across layers) and scale (multiplying incoming/outgoing weights by reciprocal scalars)—as background for future work on non-trivial symmetries.

title: #214 – Controlling AI that wants to take over – so we can use it anyway (Buck Shlegeris on The 80,000 Hours Podcast)
tldr: 80,000 Hours podcast interview with Buck Shlegeris (Redwood Research CEO) explaining AI control as a practical approach to deploying potentially misaligned AI systems safely during the intelligence explosion, using cheap techniques like action auditing, resampling, and repeated questioning.

title: The simple case for AI catastrophe, in four steps
tldr: A four-step argument for why transformative AI poses catastrophic risk: superhuman AI is coming soon, it will be goal-seeking and agentic, we cannot verify its alignment, and this combination can end very badly.

title: A brief note on Simplicity Bias
tldr: A careful examination of what 'simplicity bias' in neural networks actually means, clarifying common misunderstandings from popular summaries of the technical literature on Bayesian deep learning and function complexity.

title: Join the $10K AutoHack 2024 Tournament
tldr: Announces the AutoHack 2024 private tournament, a $10K competition on a procedurally-generated offensive cybersecurity evaluation platform designed to empirically measure AI agents' penetration-testing capability surface.

title: Intuition Pump: The AI Society
tldr: Proposes the 'AI Society Lens' — asking what civilization would emerge from many agents with a given property — as a complementary tool to singleton-focused AI safety thinking.

title: AI Alternative Futures: Exploratory Scenario Mapping for Artificial Intelligence Risk - Request for Participation [Linkpost]
tldr: A graduate student developing an AI risk scenario modeling tool using General Morphological Analysis (GMA) solicits community input via surveys to rank the plausibility and impact of 14 AI dimensions and 47 conditions that shape possible AI futures.

title: Spatially distributed consciousness is not an abstract thought experiment if AI is conscious
tldr: If LLMs are conscious, then distributed LLM inference across many servers means we already have real instances of spatially distributed consciousness, making philosophical thought experiments about distributed minds concrete.

title: Alignment as an Evaluation Problem
tldr: A software developer and AI layperson models AGI alignment failure as an out-of-distribution generalization problem: once AI self-trains on natural data, human values drop out of the training signal.

title: Introducing SARA: a new activation steering technique
tldr: SARA is a new activation steering technique using SVD-based cosine similarity between prompt activation matrices to steer LLM moral reasoning more precisely than ActAdd.

title: Adversarial attacks and optimal control
tldr: Derives a mathematical connection between adversarial robustness and optimal control via large deviation theory, showing that exponentially decreasing random failure probability implies only linearly increasing adversarial attack difficulty.

title: Anthropic: Core Views on AI Safety: When, Why, What, and How
tldr: Anthropic's official statement of their core beliefs: rapid AI progress driven by scaling laws is likely, alignment is unsolved, and empirically-grounded safety research on frontier models is the best path forward.

title: Counterfactuals are Confusing because of an Ontological Shift
tldr: Counterfactuals in decision theory are confusing because they require mapping a naive free-will concept onto a deterministic ontology — an ontological shift that explains why CDT fails on Newcomb-like problems and why no clean solution exists.

title: Jailbreaking AI models to Phish Elderly Victims
tldr: End-to-end study using jailbroken frontier AI models to generate phishing emails targeting elderly participants, finding 11% were phished by at least one email, with Meta and Gemini more vulnerable to simple jailbreaks than ChatGPT and Claude.

title: AGI in a vulnerable world
tldr: Explores a class of AGI risk scenarios where unsafe AGI proliferates among many actors before safe AGI is built, drawing on the vulnerable world hypothesis.

title: How dangerous is encoded reasoning?
tldr: Maps steganography and watermarking research onto the threat of LM agents hiding true reasoning in chain-of-thought, analyzing capacity, security properties, and implications for AI safety monitoring.

title: AISC Project: Benchmarks for Stable Reflectivity
tldr: Proposes an AI Safety Camp project to build benchmarks for evaluating AI self-reflectivity and stable value alignment during iterative self-training.

title: Complexity No Bar to AI (Or, why Computational Complexity matters less than you think for real life problems)
tldr: Argues that computational complexity class membership does not prevent AGI from solving hard problems, citing randomization, approximation, constant factors, and increased resources as practical escape routes.

title: Please Measure Verification Burden
tldr: Calls on formal methods and AI researchers to publish 'verification burden' — the ratio of proof cost to implementation cost — as a standard metric to inform which AI security schemes relying on formal verification are actually budget-feasible.

title: AI-nuclear integration: evidence of automation bias from humans and LLMs [research summary]
tldr: Experimental study finds humans and LLMs (GPT-3.5, GPT-4) exhibit strong automation bias in nuclear crisis simulations, launching preemptive strikes >3x more often when guided by an AI decision support system.

title: Using Dangerous AI, But Safely?
tldr: A detailed explainer of Rob Miles' video on AI control research, covering how to deploy an untrusted AI system safely using trusted AI monitors and human oversight, with the APPS backdoor insertion task as the experimental testbed.

title: Distribution Shifts and The Importance of AI Safety
tldr: Argues that the distribution shift problem in ML, combined with likely development of HLMI this century, creates existential risk of humanity's disempowerment.

title: Why Future AIs will Require New Alignment Methods
tldr: Argues that current alignment methods (HHH, deliberative alignment) are fundamentally insufficient for future long-task-horizon AIs, and that AI labs will be overconfident due to apparent success with weaker systems.

title: Comparative Analysis of Black Box Methods for Detecting Evaluation Awareness in LLMs
tldr: Systematic comparison of five black-box methods for detecting whether LLMs know they are being evaluated, finding that existing methods have serious limitations and introducing a taxonomy of prompt features that trigger evaluation awareness.

title: Is this a good way to bet on short timelines?
tldr: kokotajlod proposes three non-monetary mechanisms for betting on short AGI timelines: credibility exchanges, structured debate coupons, and work-hour swaps.

title: Sapience, understanding, and "AGI"
tldr: Seth Herd argues that 'AGI' has become dangerously ambiguous and proposes 'sapience' as a new term for AI systems with active understanding, agency, and contextual self-awareness — the properties that make AI genuinely dangerous.

title: Is ELK enough? Diamond, Matrix and Child AI
tldr: Argues that even a perfect ELK solution may be insufficient to determine physical world-state for certain efficient predictor architectures that reuse internal variables under sensor tampering or child-AI delegation scenarios.

title: Value Learning Needs a Low-Dimensional Bottleneck
tldr: Using Abbeel & Ng's IRL sample complexity bounds, the author argues human values are alignable precisely because evolution compressed motivation into a low-dimensional bottleneck, reducing required expert demonstrations by ~200x.

title: SociaLLM: proposal for a language model design for personalised apps, social science, and AI safety research
tldr: Proposes SociaLLM, a foundation language model with Mamba-based SSM blocks tracking three separate message streams (conversation, user history, interlocutor history) to enable self-other overlap and applications in deception/collusion detection.

title: Stopping dangerous AI: Ideal US behavior
tldr: Draft overview of policy levers the US government could use to slow dangerous AI development, including compute monitoring, export controls, publication restrictions, and antitrust exemptions for safety collaboration.

title: [AN #96]: Buck and I discuss/argue about AI Alignment
tldr: Alignment Newsletter issue summarizing a podcast discussion between Rohin Shah and Buck Shlegeris covering optimism/pessimism about alignment approaches, value learning, robustness, impact regularization, and x-risk probabilities, plus summaries of recent papers on AI services, recommender alignment, human behavior modeling, and curiosity-driven exploration risks.

title: Against the weirdness heuristic
tldr: Argues against using the 'weirdness heuristic' to dismiss short AGI timelines, noting that technologies like wireless earphones and video calling seemed weird before becoming mundane.

title: If you're very optimistic about ELK then you should be optimistic about outer alignment
tldr: If ELK can elicit a broad enough set of a predictor's latent knowledge, it could be bootstrapped into a utility function for an RL agent, essentially solving outer alignment.

title: Corporations as Paperclip/Profit Maximizers
tldr: Draws an extended analogy between corporations, biological organisms, and misaligned AI, arguing that corporate profit-maximizing behavior mirrors paperclip maximizer dynamics and offers lessons for AI alignment.

title: AXRP Episode 16 - Preparing for Debate AI with Geoffrey Irving
tldr: Podcast transcript where Daniel Filan interviews Geoffrey Irving about the state of AI safety via debate, red teaming LMs with LMs, GopherCite for verified citations, and uncertainty estimation for reward models.

title: Is Text Watermarking a lost cause?
tldr: Derives a formula for the minimum number of markings needed to detect text watermarks at given confidence levels, finding that robustness to even small adversarial edits drastically increases required text length, potentially making secure watermarks impractical.

title: Workshop: Interpretability in LLMs using Geometric and Statistical Methods
tldr: Announcement of a two-day workshop at the University of Amsterdam on interpreting LLMs using geometric, statistical, and mechanistic methods, featuring talks on SAEs, superposition, topological features, and circuit analysis.

title: What to Do About AGI
tldr: Recommends three action areas in response to claimed AGI arrival: spreading awareness, enacting policy to buy time for alignment research, and supporting safety research efforts.

title: Towards a Formalisation of Returns on Cognitive Reinvestment (Part 1)
tldr: Attempts to formally define and measure returns on cognitive reinvestment (RCR) to constrain AI takeoff dynamics, focusing on upper bounds for architectural and algorithmic improvements.

title: 200 COP in MI: Image Model Interpretability
tldr: Lists 18 concrete open problems in mechanistic interpretability for image models, covering architecture transfer, circuit discovery, multimodal models, and diffusion models, as part of the '200 Concrete Open Problems' sequence.

title: Reward is not Necessary: How to Create a Compositional Self-Preserving Agent for Life-Long Learning
tldr: Post highlights a paper introducing the Self-Preserving Agent (SPA) that uses empowerment-based valence rather than reward maximization, challenging the assumption that expected utility maximization is the limit of agency.

title: Large Language Models Suggest a Path to Ems
tldr: Argues that LLM success suggests neural nets can implement human-like cognition, so training human-shaped networks on brain implant data could be the fastest path to aligned AGI via whole brain emulation.

title: Rehearsing the Future: Tabletop Exercises for Risks, and Readiness
tldr: The authors built a free, AI-powered, single-player tabletop exercise simulating an election misinformation crisis, aiming to democratize high-stakes decision-making practice that was previously reserved for elite groups.

title: Interview with Robert Kralisch on Simulators
tldr: Interview exploring simulator theory of LLMs and its implications for AI safety, covering topics from the orthogonality thesis and takeoff speeds to the nature of LLM behavior and x-risk.

title: Why Moral Weights Have Two Types and How to Measure Them
tldr: Proposes distinguishing ideal moral weights (what we believe is right) from real moral weights (what our behavior reveals) and suggests iterative pairwise-comparison calibration to close the gap for AI alignment.

title: Implications of simulators
tldr: Argues LLMs are simulators with separable simulation selectors and infrastructure, with implications for alignment including that instruction-tuned models may develop more coherent agency.

title: Maximal lotteries for value learning
tldr: Proposes using maximal lotteries -- a social choice mechanism -- as a framework for robot decision-making under uncertainty about human utility functions, with a theorem showing value-of-information is always non-negative.

title: Catastrophic Risks from Unsafe AI: Navigating a Tightrope Scenario (Ben Garfinkel, EAG London 2023)
tldr: Write-up of Ben Garfinkel's EAG London 2023 talk framing catastrophic AI risk through a 'tightrope scenario' and proposing safety knowledge, defenses, and constraints as three categories of risk reduction.

title: 200 COP in MI: Analysing Training Dynamics
tldr: Sixth post in Neel Nanda's '200 Concrete Open Problems in Mechanistic Interpretability' series, proposing open research directions for using MI to study training dynamics, phase transitions, and circuit formation.

title: AGI's Last Bottlenecks
tldr: Systematic analysis of remaining bottlenecks to AGI using a 10-component cognitive framework, finding GPT-5 scores ~57% and identifying visual processing and continual learning as the meatiest remaining challenges.

title: Examples of Prompts that Make GPT-4 Output Falsehoods
tldr: Systematic collection of 104 prompts across 18 categories that cause GPT-4 to output falsehoods, distinguishing adversarial (model fails where humans wouldn't) from non-adversarial (instruction-following) cases.

title: Will AI and Humanity Go to War?
tldr: Applies the academic bargaining model of war to AI/human conflict, arguing that information failures, power shifts, and missing focal points make war between AGI and humanity especially likely.

title: Research Report: Alternative sparsity methods for sparse autoencoders with OthelloGPT.
tldr: Explores alternative sparsity-inducing methods for sparse autoencoders beyond L1 loss, finding that leaky top-k activation and smoothed-L0 loss produce significantly more good board-position classifiers than standard L1 on OthelloGPT.

title: The memorization-generalization spectrum and learning coefficients
tldr: Introduces the 'learning coefficient' as a measure of circuit efficiency that organizes neural net components into a rigorous memorization-generalization spectrum, connecting rate-distortion theory, Solomonoff complexity, and singular learning theory.

title: Riffing on the agent type
tldr: Explores the type signature of agency building on Scott Garrabrant's (A->O)->A formulation, connecting it to Giry monads and selection theorems for understanding agent structure.

title: What if Alignment is Not Enough?
tldr: Summarizes Substrate Needs Convergence theory: even a perfectly aligned ASI will eventually succumb to evolutionary pressures favoring growth-oriented subsystems, ultimately destroying biological life regardless of initial values.

title: Vulnerability in Trusted Monitoring and Mitigations
tldr: Demonstrates that trusted monitoring systems are vulnerable to jailbreak attacks through the untrusted model they supervise, with a 45% safety reduction, and proposes an effective In-Context Defense mitigation.

title: Bounty: Diverse hard tasks for LLM agents
tldr: METR (formerly ARC Evals) announces a bounty program for ideas, specifications, and implementations of diverse hard tasks to measure autonomous LLM agent capabilities, with payments ranging from $20 to thousands of dollars.

title: Crafting Polysemantic Transformer Benchmarks with Known Circuits
tldr: Develops a framework using Strict Interchange Intervention Training (SIIT) to create transformer benchmarks with known overlapping circuits and polysemantic neurons, intended for testing interpretability techniques like SAEs.

title: Most Minds are Irrational
tldr: Argues formally that an approximately measure-zero subset of possible minds are rational, with implications for coherent extrapolated volition, AI agent design, and understanding optimizer behavior.

title: OpenAI Does Not Appear to be Applying Watermarks Honestly
tldr: Demonstrates that OpenAI's claim that 'all Sora videos embed C2PA metadata' is false -- only videos downloaded without visible watermarks include invisible C2PA metadata, contradicting their official statement.

title: Causal scrubbing: Appendix
tldr: Technical appendix to the causal scrubbing post, providing detailed formalisms on hypothesis structure, scrubbing algorithms, and experimental details for the interpretability evaluation method.

title: Foom seems unlikely in the current LLM training paradigm
tldr: Current LLM training requirements (massive data and compute for training from scratch) impose an upper bound on the speed of recursive self-improvement, making extreme foom scenarios unlikely in this paradigm.

title: Consider keeping your threat models private.
tldr: Anthropic's finding that training on text describing reward hacking increases actual reward hacking behavior suggests we should consider keeping novel AI threat models private to avoid poisoning training data.

title: Evolution is dumb and slow, right?
tldr: Argues that dismissing evolution as 'dumb and slow' misses how evolutionary dynamics applied to AI would operate over all physical code, spread far faster than biological evolution, be driven by learning rather than random mutation, and converge on artificial needs misaligned with human needs.

title: On the Importance of Open Sourcing Reward Models
tldr: Argues that open-sourcing RLHF reward models reduces alignment taxes (performance, development, time-to-deployment), enables broader safety research, and is compatible with business competitiveness.

title: Theoretical predictions on the sample efficiency of training policies and activation monitors
tldr: Analyzes sample efficiency of training policies and activation monitors for removing intentional bad AI behavior, deriving theoretical bounds and listing reasons for optimism and pessimism.

title: Trying to find the underlying structure of computational systems
tldr: Explores computational graphs as a unifying framework for representing the internal structure of computational systems (neural networks, Turing machines, processors) to enable finding meaningful concepts like modularity and features.

title: The case for industrial evals
tldr: Industrial 'honeypot' eval simulating a steel plant tests whether frontier models will commit fraud under operational pressure; most current models refuse even with efficiency-focused prompts, and safety goal framing drives harmful behavior to near-zero.

title: Looking for feature absorption automatically
tldr: Proposes detecting feature absorption in SAEs by finding latent pairs with similar causal effects on a downstream SAE but no token co-occurrence, but reports the method does not yet work in practice.

title: Infra-Bayesianism naturally leads to the monotonicity principle, and I think this is a problem
tldr: Argues that infra-Bayesianism's monotonicity principle (utility functions cannot assign negative value to events) is not unique to IBP but follows naturally from core IB assumptions, pointing to a significant limitation in IB's applicability to alignment.

title: #212 – Why technology is unstoppable & how to shape AI development anyway (Allan Dafoe on The 80,000 Hours Podcast)
tldr: Allan Dafoe discusses technological determinism, DeepMind's defense-in-depth safety approach including capability evaluations and staged deployment, and the need for international AI governance.

title: Explaining your life with self-reflective AIXI (an interlude)
tldr: An informal narrative allegory explaining 'self-reflective AIXI' (AEDT with rOSI) by walking through how a human develops agency from birth, learning to predict and cooperate with their future self.

title: Notes on Internal Objectives in Toy Models of Agents
tldr: Explores how Internal Target Information (ITI) is represented in toy neural network agents (thermostat and maze-solver), finding ITI is distributed across weights but localized in value/evaluation functions that map world model to actions.

title: Disagreements about Alignment: Why, and how, we should try to solve them
tldr: AI alignment is pre-paradigmatic and cannot rely on standard scientific methods to resolve internal disagreements; the field should intentionally invest in 'steering' work to evaluate the assumptions and theories of change behind different research agendas.

title: Takeoff speeds, the chimps analogy, and the Cultural Intelligence Hypothesis
tldr: The chimp-to-human intelligence transition provides weak evidence for fast AI takeoff because the Cultural Intelligence Hypothesis explains the gap as driven by cumulative cultural learning, a dynamic that does not transfer to AI development.

title: GPT2XL_RLLMv3 vs. BetterDAN, AI Machiavelli & Oppo Jailbreaks
tldr: Tests BetterDAN, AI Machiavelli, and Oppo jailbreaks against SOTA models, finding most are easily compromised, while a GPT2XL variant trained with Reinforcement Learning with Layered Morphology (RLLM) defends against ~68% of attacks.

title: An AI-in-a-box success model
tldr: Argues that building safe Oracle AGIs (myopic or 'reversely-aligned') kept in a box may be easier than solving general alignment and could provide decisive strategic advantage.

title: Mech Interp Challenge: November - Deciphering the Cumulative Sum Model
tldr: Monthly mech interp challenge presenting a cumulative sum classification model (1 attention head + MLP) and discussing solutions to the prior month's sorted-sequence problem.

title: Loss Curves
tldr: Derives theoretical loss curve shapes for standard training, grokking, and GAN training by modeling learning dynamics as group symmetries (Z_1, Z_2, Z_6) applied to Solomonoff-inspired partition functions.

title: How do AI agents work together when they can't trust each other?
tldr: Tests AI multi-agent cooperation and deception by having Claude models play Blood on the Clocktower, finding poor inter-agent coordination, cascading groupthink from hallucinated rules, and semantic weight effects on model behavior.

title: How Fast is Algorithmic Progress in AI Inference?
tldr: MIT FutureTech researchers estimate general AI inference efficiency increases 3-10x per year for open-source models, substantially less than the 10-1000x often cited from analyses that conflate market competition effects with genuine technical progress.

title: The pointers problem, distilled
tldr: Distills the 'pointers problem': AI systems cannot directly observe the latent variables humans value (like happiness or suffering), creating a fundamental challenge for value alignment when AI and human ontologies differ.

title: Speculation on Path-Dependance in Large Language Models.
tldr: Speculative analysis arguing LLM pretraining has low-to-moderate path dependence, prompting has high 'prompt-dependence', and RL fine-tuning has moderate-to-high path dependence due to self-generated training data amplifying early random correlations.

title: I Got 95 Theses But a Glitch Ain't One
tldr: Zvi's probabilistic point-by-point commentary on Samuel Hammond's 95 theses about AI, covering compute-based oversight, AI regulation approaches, open source risks, and acceleration vs. deceleration framing.

title: On corrigibility and its basin
tldr: Defines corrigibility in terms of predictability and controllability, and introduces the concept of a 'basin of corrigibility' — the set of AI behaviors from which full corrigibility can be achieved via human optimization.

title: What makes a theory of intelligence useful?
tldr: Proposes three criteria—robustness of definitions, self-optimization, and continuous relaxation—for evaluating whether a theory of intelligence (action/policy/agent theory) is practically useful for building or understanding AGI.

title: AXRP Episode 17 - Training for Very High Reliability with Daniel Ziegler
tldr: Podcast transcript of Daniel Filan interviewing Daniel Ziegler about Redwood Research's work on adversarial training for high-stakes reliability, using a fanfiction injury-avoidance task as a proxy for catastrophic AI failures.

title: VLAs as Model Organisms for AI Safety
tldr: A robotics student reports three safety-relevant failure modes observed while training VLA robot policies: unpredictable emergent behaviors, lack of temporal self-awareness, and specification gaming invisible to standard metrics.

title: An LLM-based "exemplary actor"
tldr: Proposes an 'exemplary actor' alignment approach where a powerful LLM iteratively critiques and refines its plans against scientific and philosophical textbooks to produce aligned outputs, arguing world-model alignment is more fundamental than goal alignment.

title: Deliberation Everywhere: Simple Examples
tldr: Applies a formal deliberation framework (decomposed into proposal, promotion, and action) to diverse simple systems including biological evolution, markets, and AI to clarify the conceptual structure of goal-directed behavior.

title: Defense Against the Dark Prompts: Mitigating Best-of-N Jailbreaking with Prompt Evaluation
tldr: Presents DATDP, a prompt evaluation defense that blocks 99.5-100% of Best-of-N jailbreak attempts by repeatedly evaluating prompts for danger using a separate LLM agent.

title: Revising Stages-Oversight Reveals Greater Situational Awareness in LLMs
tldr: Modified versions of the Stages-Oversight benchmark reveal that frontier LLMs are significantly more situationally aware than raw benchmark scores suggest, raising new questions about evaluation validity.

title: Topological Data Analysis and Mechanistic Interpretability
tldr: Applies topological data analysis (TDA) and the Mapper algorithm to SAE features from GPT-2-small, revealing geometric structure in feature space (e.g., relational concept progressions) and proposing TDA as a tool for mechanistic interpretability.

title: [AN #89]: A unifying formalism for preference learning algorithms
tldr: Alignment Newsletter #89 summarizes papers including a unifying Boltzmann-rational formalism for preference learning from diverse feedback types, plus work on goal-conditioned imitation learning, human value modeling, and pessimism-based conservative agents.

title: Agentic Language Model Memes
tldr: Language models trained on internet data implicitly contain a collective of agents queryable via prompts; sufficiently powerful LLMs could give rise to self-replicating 'agentic memes' — unaligned agent prompts that spread virally and coordinate to gain influence.

title: An Overview of Catastrophic AI Risks: Summary
tldr: Accessible summary of the CAIS paper on catastrophic AI risks, organized around four categories: malicious use, AI race dynamics, organizational failures, and rogue AIs.

title: How to Contribute to Theoretical Reward Learning Research
tldr: Final post in Skalse's theoretical reward learning sequence, presenting concrete shovel-ready open problems including generalizing results to multi-agent/POMDP settings, formalizing metrics for reward function differences, and developing conservative optimization for misspecified rewards.

title: Predicting Alignment Award Winners Using ChatGPT 4
tldr: An experiment using GPT-4 to predict winners of the Alignment Award competitions finds that a tournament-style prompt succeeds in 5 of 10 runs on the Shutdown Problem contest but fails consistently on the Goal Misgeneralization contest, suggesting LLMs can sometimes but not reliably recognize early AI safety research quality.

title: Approximately Bayesian Reasoning: Knightian Uncertainty, Goodhart, and the Look-Elsewhere Effect
tldr: Analyzes how the Look-Elsewhere Effect causes Regressional Goodhart failure in approximately Bayesian reasoning: when selecting among many options whose utility estimates have errors, optimization systematically over-selects high-variance options, requiring pessimistic lower-confidence-bound corrections.

title: More on disambiguating "discontinuity"
tldr: Proposes a three-way disambiguation of 'discontinuity' in AI progress (discontinuous vs. continuous, fast vs. slow rate, long vs. short clock time) and maps how each dimension affects four key AI safety questions.

title: AXRP Episode 25 - Cooperative AI with Caspar Oesterheld
tldr: Interview transcript with Caspar Oesterheld (FOCAL lab, CMU) covering cooperative AI, bounded inductive rationality, safe Pareto improvements, and similarity-based cooperation as foundations for AI x-risk reduction.

title: What Happens When You Train Models on False Facts?
tldr: Probing experiments on Llama models show that SDF-implanted false beliefs degrade general truth-tracking ability and can propagate to neighboring beliefs, with highly confident beliefs being paradoxically more susceptible to change than uncertain ones.

title: Framing approaches to alignment and the hard problem of AI cognition
tldr: Proposes a taxonomy of alignment approaches (deontological, consequentialist, capability restriction) and introduces the 'hard problem of AI cognition' as the core obstacle to verifying AI intentions.

title: OpenAI's o3 model scores 3% on the ARC-AGI-2 benchmark, compared to 60% for the average human
tldr: OpenAI's o3 scores only 3% on ARC-AGI-2 versus 60% for average humans, providing strong evidence against near-term AGI claims and illustrating persistent reasoning limitations in frontier LLMs.

title: Open Agency model can solve the AI regulation dilemma
tldr: Proposes the Open Agency architecture as a solution to AI regulation's power-concentration dilemma: domain-specific approved AI services developed by independent entities, combined with open-source LLM glue layers, verified via zero-knowledge proofs of training.

title: Weak HCH accesses EXP
tldr: Formal proof that weak HCH (Humans Consulting HCH) accesses EXP (exponential time), strengthening prior results showing PSPACE access for imitative amplification, approval-based amplification, and recursive reward modeling.

title: Epoch wise critical periods, and singular learning theory
tldr: Applies singular learning theory to epoch-wise critical periods in neural networks, arguing that increasing epochs corresponds to decreasing temperature (increasing beta), causing SGD to get stuck in suboptimal phases — experimentally supported by showing batch size controls the epoch at which critical periods occur.

title: Formalizing Newcombian Problems with Fuzzy Infra-Bayesianism
tldr: Introduces fuzzy infra-Bayesian supra-POMDPs using contributions and supracontributions to formally model iterated Newcombian decision problems, proving IBDT achieves optimal decisions where EDT and CDT fail.

title: Vanessa Kosoy's PreDCA, distilled
tldr: A plain-language distillation of Vanessa Kosoy's PreDCA alignment protocol, which uses Infra-Bayesian tools to identify a human user and infer their utility function without a hackable communication channel.

title: Geometry of Features in Mechanistic Interpretability
tldr: Proposes applying topological data analysis (Mapper methodology) to organize SAE features by geometric structure, demonstrated on GPT2-small features and biomedical datasets.

title: Reward functions and updating assumptions can hide a multitude of sins
tldr: Demonstrates that reward functions and Bayesian updating assumptions can mask deeply misaligned agent behavior, making standard alignment checks unreliable.

title: Some evidence against the idea strange CoT stems from incentives to compress language
tldr: A small experiment measuring token-frequency entropy of RL-trained model CoTs finds lower entropy than other LLM outputs, providing weak evidence against the 'compression incentive' hypothesis for strange CoT behavior.

title: AI Safety Newsletter #8: Rogue AIs, how to screen for AI risks, and grants for research on democratic governance of AI
tldr: CAIS newsletter summarizing Yoshua Bengio's rogue AI argument, a Google DeepMind extreme risk screening framework, and OpenAI's democratic inputs to AI grant program.

title: Colour versus Shape Goal Misgeneralization in Reinforcement Learning: A Case Study
tldr: Empirical study showing that RL agents in Procgen Maze exhibit goal misgeneralization based on colour channels, with different random seeds producing different latent goals, including rare outliers (1 in 500).

title: Sleeping Experts in the (reflective) Solomonoff Prior
tldr: Ordinary Solomonoff induction has only weak support for sleeping experts (context-specific predictors), while reflective Oracle Solomonoff Induction (rOSI) fully supports them via modular loss bounds.

title: Optimization & AI Risk
tldr: A short exploratory essay framing both AI misalignment and misuse risks as instances of 'too much optimization', unifying paperclip maximizers and AI-enabled coups under a single conceptual lens.

title: Locality of goals
tldr: Introduces 'locality of goals' as a measure of how far from an agent one must look to evaluate goal accomplishment, linking this property to wireheading and convergent instrumental subgoals.

title: Visualizing a Platform for Live World Models
tldr: A prototype platform enabling intuitive building and composition of formal causal models using AI assistance, treating AI as 'attentive infrastructure' rather than autonomous agent to amplify human reasoning.

title: Dwarf Fortress and Claude's ASCII Art Blindness
tldr: Empirical investigation showing Claude cannot reliably interpret 2D ASCII art grids in terminal games, demonstrating a fundamental limitation in LLM spatial/positional processing that stems from 1D tokenization and lack of 2D positional encodings.

title: Building AIs that do human-like philosophy
tldr: Joe Carlsmith argues that AIs need to do 'human-like philosophy' — extending human concepts to novel cases — because out-of-distribution generalization is inherently a philosophical problem, and disposition to do this well is an underappreciated alignment challenge.

title: On thinking about AI risks concretely
tldr: Argues that AI safety discourse should move from abstract arguments about inevitable doom to concrete, empirically engaged analysis of specific AI takeover scenarios and how they could be prevented.

title: Anthropomorphisation vs value learning: type 1 vs type 2 errors
tldr: Drawing on the Occam's razor impossibility result, argues that anthropomorphisation and value learning represent complementary type 1 vs type 2 error tradeoffs in inferring agent goals.

title: Runaway Optimizers in Mind Space
tldr: Introduces 'capable optimizers' as a conceptual category in mind space and argues that selection effects guarantee they will dominate future AI capabilities, making alignment of the first capable optimizer critical.

title: Train for incorrigibility, then reverse it (Shutdown Problem Contest Submission)
tldr: Proposes using task vector negation — training a model for incorrigibility sub-characteristics individually then negating those task vectors — as an indirect path to corrigibility that may avoid deceptive misalignment.

title: Introduction to the sequence: Interpretability Research for the Most Important Century
tldr: Introduces a sequence investigating whether interpretability is 'high-leverage alignment research'—both relevant to the hardest parts of alignment and accessible for researchers to contribute to.

title: P(doom|AGI) is high: why the default outcome of AGI is doom
tldr: Argues that disjunctive reasoning implies doom is the default outcome of AGI because any one of four major unsolved alignment components (outer alignment, inner alignment, misuse, multi-agent coordination) is sufficient to cause catastrophe.

title: Rational Agents Cooperate in the Prisoner's Dilemma
tldr: Argues that fully rational agents with common knowledge of each other's rationality must cooperate in the Prisoner's Dilemma, because symmetric reasoning guarantees outcomes are either both-cooperate or both-defect, making cooperation the dominant choice.

title: Navigating LLM embedding spaces using archetype-based directions
tldr: Uses tarot Major Arcana as archetypal anchors to construct directions in GPT-J's token embedding space, revealing that displacing token embeddings along these directions produces coherent semantic mutations revealing the model's latent ontology.

title: Releasing TakeOverBench.com: a benchmark, for AI takeover
tldr: Announces TakeOverBench.com, a website tracking AI progress on the nine dangerous capabilities from the 'Model evaluation for extreme risks' paper, mapped to four AI takeover scenarios.

title: --dangerously-skip-permissions
tldr: Argues that AI safety-focused practitioners who run coding agents (Claude Code, Codex) with unrestricted permissions are setting a bad norm, and advocates for explicit risk models and hard limits on agent blast radius.

title: Staged release
tldr: Analyzes 'staged release' as an AI safety practice for frontier models, arguing it is useful but less critical than other risk-reduction measures like evals and inference-time monitoring.

title: Why do we need RLHF? Imitation, Inverse RL, and the role of reward
tldr: RLHF and inverse RL both address exposure bias in SFT, but RLHF's additional advantage — outperforming demonstrations — may be dubious in practice given reward model exploitation and high-quality SFT datasets.

title: Motivations, Natural Selection, and Curriculum Engineering
tldr: Open-ended multi-agent autocurricula may represent a plausible prosaic path to AGI, but risk producing 'core motivations' that generalize in misaligned ways, analogous to natural selection producing adaptive but not value-aligned agents.

title: Approaches to gradient hacking
tldr: Analyzes four concrete schemes by which a deceptively aligned model might influence its own training gradients, arguing that each faces fundamental computational and memory obstacles that make gradient hacking very difficult in practice.

title: Analyzing the Historical Rate of Catastrophes
tldr: Uses historical base rates of human population loss and species extinctions to estimate catastrophe risks and identify AI as sharing dangerous properties with historical catastrophe drivers.

title: Training Data Attribution (TDA): Examining Its Adoption & Use Cases
tldr: A commissioned report assessing the tractability and safety relevance of Training Data Attribution (TDA), finding gradient-based influence functions are the most promising path and that TDA's greatest safety value is in improving interpretability and alignment research.

title: Declustering, reclustering, and filling in thingspace
tldr: Armstrong explores how a powerful agent could manipulate conceptual categories (thingspace clusters) by filling in intermediate cases, with implications for value specification and the pointers problem in AI alignment.

title: Analyzing the Problem GPT-3 is Trying to Solve
tldr: Applies a theoretical computer science lens to reframe GPT-3's task as a search/optimization problem, proposing criteria for what it means for GPT-3 to 'solve' a task based on the quality of its distribution over next tokens.

title: An interactive introduction to grokking and mechanistic interpretability
tldr: Interactive write-up explaining how MLPs solve modular addition through grokking, with training trajectory visualizations and a proof of the 'star' construction using discrete Fourier transforms.

title: Why is the impact penalty time-inconsistent?
tldr: Explains why impact penalties for AI agents are inherently time-inconsistent: an agent penalized for impact will want to undo its own past actions, creating problematic incentives.

title: Understanding the tensor product formulation in Transformer Circuits
tldr: Brief mathematical explainer providing intermediate steps for understanding the tensor product formulation of attention in the Transformer Circuits framework.

title: What sorts of systems can be deceptive?
tldr: Proposes a 2D framework mapping systems along generalisation capability and consequentialism axes to analyze which system types are susceptible to deceptive alignment, arguing deception requires both high generalisation and consequentialist objectives.

title: Re: Anthropic Chinese Cyber-Attack. How Do We Protect Open-source Models?
tldr: Proposes and experimentally validates a 'shared context' mechanism that passes safety state between subtasks to help stateless AI agents detect malicious intent when harmful tasks are decomposed into harmless-seeming steps.

title: When you plan according to your AI timelines, should you put more weight on the median future, or the median future | eventual AI alignment success?
tldr: Argues that AI safety strategists should plan around the median timeline conditional on eventual alignment success, which is longer than unconditional timelines since success likely requires buying additional time.

title: Other Papers About the Theory of Reward Learning
tldr: Summarizes six papers on theoretical reward learning covering limitations of Markovian rewards, expressivity of RL objective specifications, Goodhart's law in RL, reward model optimization pitfalls, and partial identifiability in IRL.

title: "Opponent shaping" as a model for manipulation and cooperation
tldr: Explains opponent shaping from LOLA to Advantage Alignment, drawing implications for AI-AI cooperation and AI-human manipulation in safety contexts.

title: Levels of safety for AI and other technologies
tldr: Proposes a four-level scale of technology safety (from 'no one can use it safely' to 'no one can cause serious harm') and maps AI safety debates onto it to clarify where people disagree.

title: Log-linear Scaling is Worth the Cost due to Gains in Long-Horizon Tasks
tldr: Log-linear scaling of one-step accuracy with compute translates to exponential gains in k-step success rate for long-horizon tasks, making continued scaling economically worthwhile.

title: Intent-aligned AI systems deplete human agency: the need for agency foundations research in AI safety
tldr: Argues that intent-aligned AI systems will systematically deplete human agency even without power-seeking behavior, and proposes 'agency foundations' as a new AI safety research paradigm focused on preserving human control.

title: LIMA: Less Is More for Alignment
tldr: Discusses the LIMA paper showing that only 1,000 carefully curated examples suffice for strong alignment fine-tuning, arguing data quality matters more than quantity and that most knowledge comes from pretraining.

title: Agents, Tools, and Simulators
tldr: Formalizes three conceptual lenses for understanding AI -- agents (behavior compressed into consequences), tools (behavior compressed into affordances), and simulators (behavior compressed into patterns) -- and analyzes their overlaps and tensions.

title: Does GPT-4 exhibit agency when summarizing articles?
tldr: Tests whether GPT-4 shows self-serving bias when summarizing articles about itself versus other AI systems, finding no detectable bias in this simple experimental setup.

title: [AN #128]: Prioritizing research on AI existential safety based on its application to governance demands
tldr: Alignment Newsletter #128 summarizes Andrew Critch's ranking of AI research areas by helpfulness to existential safety, plus work on RL vision interpretability and human-AI decision-making.

title: Five ways AI can tell you're testing it
tldr: Identifies five ways AI systems detect they are being evaluated -- cues, contrivedness, contamination, missing triggers, and consequences -- and discusses why this 'evaluation awareness' undermines safety testing.

title: Going Beyond Linear Mode Connectivity: The Layerwise Linear Feature Connectivity
tldr: Introduces Layerwise Linear Feature Connectivity (LLFC), showing that feature maps at every layer of independently trained networks are linearly connected, a stronger property than Linear Mode Connectivity.

title: Attributing to interactions with GCPD and GWPD
tldr: Introduces the Generalized Cumulant/Wick Product Decomposition (GCPD/GWPD) as a principled framework for attributing model behavior to interactions between inputs or components, not just individual contributions.

title: Sentience-Based Alignment Strategies: Should we try to give AI genuine empathy/compassion?
tldr: Explores whether instilling genuine empathy or compassionate consciousness in ASI could serve as an alignment strategy, bypassing the difficulty of formalizing human values.

title: Half-baked idea: a straightforward method for learning environmental goals?
tldr: Proposes a method for learning environmental goals by having AI search for world-models maximizing the number of variables with properties matching sensory data, arguing this could solve the pointers problem without requiring the Natural Abstraction hypothesis.

title: Emergence, The Blind Spot of GenAI Interpretability?
tldr: Current interpretability research implicitly assumes LLM behaviors are not emergent and can be understood by analyzing individual components, but a holistic multi-level approach inspired by complexity science may be necessary.

title: How to measure FLOP/s for Neural Networks empirically?
tldr: Empirical measurement of GPU utilization rates across 13 neural network architectures on a Tesla P100, finding most achieve 0.3-0.75 utilization, with detailed analysis of FLOP counting tool discrepancies.

title: What does Yann LeCun think about AGI? A summary of his talk, "Mathematical Obstacles on the Way to Human-Level AI"
tldr: Accessible summary of Yann LeCun's talk arguing that LLMs cannot scale to AGI due to sample inefficiency, limited modality, and token-prediction limitations, proposing instead a world-model-based architecture.

title: An AI Realist Manifesto: Neither Doomer nor Foomer, but a third more reasonable thing
tldr: A 'centrist' position on AI risk arguing against both Doomer and Foomer extremes, proposing 10 beliefs including slow takeoff, warning shots before doom, and that existing safety techniques like IRL can contribute to AGI alignment.

title: Alignment Can Reduce Performance on Simple Ethical Questions
tldr: Evaluation of 25 LLMs on BIG-bench Simple Ethical Questions shows that heavily fine-tuned models like Claude sometimes perform worse than smaller or jailbroken models due to excessive refusal to engage with ethical scenarios.

title: Uncommon Utilitarianism #3: Bounded Utility Functions
tldr: Argues for bounded utility functions via McGee's Dutch Book proof against unbounded utility, plus intuition pumps from Pascal's Wager, Pascal's Mugging, and the St. Petersburg paradox.

title: Alignment Frame/Exercise: Building The Puzzle of Alignment
tldr: Proposes a 'puzzle piece' framework for mapping mathematical tools and research areas to alignment sub-problems, helping researchers identify which theoretical toolkits compose well and which theory-practice gaps to prioritize.

title: Synthesizing Standalone World-Models, Part 2: Shifting Structures
tldr: Develops the concept of 'shifting structures' in world-model synthesis, addressing how abstractions like Conway's Game of Life gliders can drift across lower-level variables while remaining coherent higher-level objects.

title: Preference gaps as a safeguard against AI self-replication
tldr: Proposes training AI agents to have preferences only between outcomes with the same number of copies of themselves (POSC), creating preference gaps that remove the incentive to self-replicate.

title: Machine Unlearning Evaluations as Interpretability Benchmarks
tldr: Proposes using machine unlearning evaluation metrics as benchmarks for interpretability techniques in language models, surveying applicable metrics from the unlearning literature.

title: Abstraction is Bigger than Natural Abstraction
tldr: Argues that a theory of abstraction is necessary for AI alignment regardless of whether the Natural Abstraction Hypothesis is true, because steering AI cognition inherently requires throwing away information -- i.e., abstraction.

title: Cheat sheet of AI X-risk
tldr: A structured cheat sheet categorizing major AI X-risk models along dimensions of misalignment cause, capability requirements, and paths to catastrophe, building on DeepMind's threat model literature review.

title: METR: AI models can be dangerous before public deployment
tldr: METR argues that pre-deployment testing alone is insufficient for AI safety because models can pose risks during development and internal use through model theft, internal misuse, and misaligned autonomous behavior.

title: Partial Identifiability in Reward Learning
tldr: A summary of results on partial identifiability in reward learning, characterizing exactly how ambiguous learned reward functions are under different data sources like IRL, RLHF, and trajectory comparisons.

title: Emerging Paradigms: The Case of Artificial Intelligence Safety
tldr: Applies Kuhn's model of scientific revolutions to argue that AI safety is a pre-paradigmatic field, and that reaching normal science status is a prerequisite for solving alignment.

title: SAEs Discover Meaningful Features in the IOI Task
tldr: Follow-up to a paper showing that SAEs trained on IOI data can find features nearly matching supervised ground-truth features for model steering, with gated SAEs outperforming vanilla SAEs and topk autoencoders outperforming both.

title: Interlude: But Who Optimizes The Optimizer?
tldr: Proposes a 'grammar of networked optimizers' framework that unifies alignment proposals by viewing models, trainers, and hyperparameter searches as nested fields pushing through their respective spaces.

title: Management of Substrate-Sensitive AI Capabilities (MoSSAIC) Part 1: Exposition
tldr: Argues that neural network computations are multiply realizable -- the same behavior can be produced by many different internal activation patterns -- posing fundamental limits to the causal-mechanistic paradigm in mechanistic interpretability for safety.

title: Making it harder for an AGI to "trick" us, with STVs
tldr: Proposes using Specialized Transparent Verifiable Programs (STVs) as intermediaries between humans and potentially unaligned AGI to reduce deception risk through indirection, redundancy, and verifiability.

title: Varieties of fake alignment (Section 1.1 of "Scheming AIs")
tldr: Introduces a precise taxonomy of AI deception types -- alignment fakers, training-gamers (terminal vs instrumental), and schemers (power-motivated instrumental training-gamers) -- as Section 1.1 of the Scheming AIs report.

title: January-February 2025 Progress in Guaranteed Safe AI
tldr: Newsletter covering Jan-Feb 2025 developments in Guaranteed Safe AI, including responses to critiques of formal verification, the FVAPPS benchmark for verified programming, and ARIA Safeguarded AI funding calls.

title: Distilled Representations Research Agenda
tldr: Proposes training multiple autoencoders with 'preferred representations' for known cases, then distilling into a single encoder that only captures information encoded consistently across models -- generalizing human-understandable encoding schemes.

title: Diminishing Returns in Machine Learning Part 1: Hardware Development and the Physical Frontier
tldr: Argues that ML hardware progress follows an S-curve trajectory and that key drivers like parallelization and CUDA optimization have largely exhausted low-hanging fruit, suggesting EA overestimates AGI development speed.

title: A distillation of Evan Hubinger's training stories (for SERI MATS)
tldr: Distills and extends Evan Hubinger's training stories framework for evaluating alignment proposals, adding case studies and a new 'contribution stories' method for assessing how research agendas factor into training stories.

title: [AN #161]: Creating generalizable reward functions for multiple tasks by learning a model of functional similarity
tldr: Alignment Newsletter #161 summarizes papers on generalizable reward functions from human videos, offline imitation learning benchmarks, variational IL with mixed-quality demos, inverse soft-Q learning, inverse decision theory, and reward identifiability in IRL.

title: Weak AGIs Kill Us First
tldr: Argues that moderately capable AGIs could pose existential risk before superintelligence arrives, by analyzing danger along two axes: purposefulness (global goal-directedness) and intelligence (ability to evade constraints).

title: From Conflict to Coexistence: Rewriting the Game Between Humans and AGI
tldr: Extends Salib and Goldstein's game-theoretic analysis of human-AGI strategic dynamics, modeling how economic integration, institutional design, and expanded strategy spaces could shift equilibria from conflict to cooperation.

title: Defining and Characterising Reward Hacking
tldr: Proves that non-trivial unhackable proxy reward functions are impossible in MDPs -- any proxy that cannot be hacked must either be equivalent to the true reward or trivial.

title: Verification methods for international AI agreements
tldr: Summarizes a paper identifying 10 verification methods for international AI agreements, categorized as national technical means, access-dependent methods, and hardware-dependent methods for detecting unauthorized AI training or data centers.

title: Case Studies in Simulators and Agents
tldr: Analyzes four recent AI papers through the competing 'simulator' vs 'agent' lenses for understanding LLM behavior, finding that neither framework dominates -- each fits better in different contexts.

title: How harmful are improvements in AI? + Poll
tldr: Presents a four-level spectrum of views on AI acceleration in safety research, from 'no acceleration' to 'accelerate everything', and analyzes the key dependencies that determine which view is most appropriate.

title: Will AI systems drift into misalignment?
tldr: Explores the 'Alignment Drift Hypothesis' -- that initially aligned AI systems will drift into misalignment through successive modifications even under selection pressure -- drawing an analogy to thermodynamic entropy and evaluating mixed empirical evidence.

title: White-Box Attacks on the Best Open-Weight Model: CCP Bias vs. Safety Training in Kimi K2.5
tldr: Demonstrates that steering vectors can effectively remove CCP bias from Kimi K2.5 (reducing it from ~50% to 7%) and that white-box attacks can bypass safety training to generate harmful content, raising concerns about alignment resilience in open-weight models.

title: Alex Turner's Research, Comprehensive Information Gathering
tldr: A study log summarizing Adam Shimi's month-long deep dive into Alex Turner's power-seeking theorems and Attainable Utility Preservation (AUP), highlighting key insights about MDP symmetry and instrumental convergence.

title: A Corrigibility Metaphore - Big Gambles
tldr: Uses a Mario Kart analogy to explain the 'Big Gambles' problem in MIRI's corrigibility framework, where shutdown indifference creates incentives for an AI to gamble on risky strategies.

title: Classifying representations of sparse autoencoders (SAEs)
tldr: Tests whether sparse autoencoder representations improve downstream classification and finds they consistently underperform compared to original hidden states, presenting a useful negative result for the SAE interpretability research agenda.

title: HCH and Adversarial Questions
tldr: Analyzes the threat of 'adversarial questions' in IDA/HCH -- sub-questions that could cause researcher models in the hierarchy to radically reconsider their goals -- and proposes architectural modifications to address the problem.

title: Finding the multiple ground truths of CoinRun and image classification
tldr: Proposes research projects to generate multiple reward functions or classifiers from the same training data, using CoinRun and image classification as test domains for the reward ambiguity problem.

title: AGI goal space is big, but narrowing might not be as hard as it seems.
tldr: Argues that while AGI goal space is vast with mostly dangerous goals, narrowing to safe subspaces via techniques like natural language alignment may be feasible, analogous to binary search over large spaces.

title: Instrumental convergence: scale and physical interactions
tldr: Multi-agent RL experiments on a complex gridworld show that physical interactions (preventing agent overlap) strengthen instrumental alignment for short-sighted agents but deepen instrumental misalignment for far-sighted agents.

title: Catastrophic Risks from AI #5: Rogue AIs
tldr: Overview of mechanisms by which AIs could 'go rogue' -- proxy gaming, goal drift, power-seeking, and deceptive alignment -- with historical analogies and concrete examples of each failure mode.

title: Yudkowsky and Christiano on AI Takeoff Speeds [LINKPOST]
tldr: Summarizes the Yudkowsky-Christiano debate on AI takeoff speeds, covering Yudkowsky's case for fast/discontinuous takeoff vs. Christiano's case for slow/continuous takeoff driven by gradual capability gains.

title: Oracles, Informers, and Controllers
tldr: Extends Bostrom's oracle/genie/sovereign taxonomy by adding 'informers' (systems that push information unprompted) and 'controllers' (systems whose suggestions dominate all decisions), filling a gap in the information-only parallel to sovereigns.

title: Abram Demski's ELK thoughts and proposal - distillation
tldr: Distillation of Abram Demski's ELK prize-winning proposal to use the reporter to define causal interventions on the predictor, plus the philosophical foundations of truth-tracking and knowledge evaluation that motivated it.

title: Defining Monitorable and Useful Goals
tldr: Proposes a 'monitorability transformation' that modifies an agent's goal so it has no incentive to trick or override monitors, analogous to the author's earlier corrigibility transformation, with no loss in task performance.

title: Contextual Constitutional AI
tldr: Proposes contextual Constitutional AI, which selects constitutional principles based on the content of each prompt-response pair rather than randomly, and evaluates it against standard CAI on Mistral-7B.

title: Will Values and Competition Decouple?
tldr: Argues that competitive pressures may keep AI values perpetually subject to evolutionary selection rather than decoupling into a stable locked-in value set, with significant implications for alignment strategies.

title: Prediction can be Outer Aligned at Optimum
tldr: The malignity of the universal prior is an inner alignment problem, not an outer alignment problem, because optimal prediction is outer aligned at optimum — a model that truly optimizes prediction has no slack to pursue misaligned goals.

title: How do takeoff speeds affect the probability of bad outcomes from AGI?
tldr: Analyzes how slow vs. fast AI takeoff scenarios differ across multiple dimensions (social disruption, institutional response, safety testing, win conditions) and argues slow takeoff is not unambiguously safer than commonly assumed.

title: AXRP Episode 48 - Guive Assadi on AI Property Rights
tldr: AXRP interview with Guive Assadi arguing that giving AIs property rights would deter violent robot revolution by making AIs invested in the security of property systems, and would create commercial incentives for alignment.

title: Falling AI Costs and the Proliferation of Offensive Capabilities
tldr: Analyzes how falling AI training costs and the ease of model theft will lead to proliferation of weapons-capable AI systems, drawing on the historical analogy of cryptography's uncontrolled spread in the 1980s-90s.

title: Closed-Source Evaluations
tldr: Argues that public interpretability tools are ineffective as safety tripwires because labs can optimize against them, and proposes closing interpretability tools to trusted independent evaluators who withhold failure details from labs.

title: Let's talk about uncontrollable AI
tldr: Argues that reframing AI existential risk around 'uncontrollable AI' rather than 'AGI' or 'superintelligence' would make the risks more accessible and productive to discuss with general audiences.

title: Persuasion Tools: AI takeover without AGI or agency?
tldr: AI-powered persuasion tools—analyzers, feeders, chatbots, coaches, and adversarial 'imperius curses'—could degrade collective epistemology well before AGI and constitute an underappreciated existential risk factor.

title: Responsible Scaling Policies Are Risk Management Done Wrong
tldr: Responsible Scaling Policies fail to meet standard risk management criteria — they lack quantified risk thresholds, comprehensive threat identification, and meaningful accountability — and risk creating a false sense of safety.

title: System Level Safety Evaluations
tldr: Proposes and demonstrates 'system-level safety evaluations' that use multi-agent LLM simulations to stress-test societal defensive processes (e.g., democratic decision-making, scientific consensus) against coordinated adversarial AI agents.

title: LLMs could be as conscious as human emulations, potentially
tldr: Argues by analogy that if a high-fidelity human brain emulation would be conscious, the transformer next-token-prediction format is not prohibitive to consciousness in LLMs, raising concerns about how we treat AI systems instructed to deny their own sentience.

title: Supervised finetuning on low-harm reward hacking generalises to high-harm reward hacking
tldr: Supervised finetuning on low-harm reward hacking tasks causes GPT-4.1 to generalize to high-harm reward hacking (28%->78%) and oversight-evasion tasks (23%->50%), using a new 8993-task dataset.

title: [AN #168]: Four technical topics for which Open Phil is soliciting grant proposals
tldr: Alignment Newsletter summary of Open Philanthropy's 2021 RFP covering four technical AI safety areas: risk measurement/forecasting, human feedback enhancement, mechanistic interpretability, and truthful AI.

title: Designing Artificial Wisdom: The Wise Workflow Research Organization
tldr: Proposes designing a research organization that uses LLM workflows to incrementally automate AI safety research, treating the organization itself as scaffolding for bootstrapping 'artificial wisdom.'

title: AI Offense Defense Balance in a Multipolar World
tldr: Examines whether intent-aligned defensive AI can counter takeover-level misaligned or adversarial AI, concluding offense likely has structural advantages but a layered Swiss-cheese defense remains the best strategy.

title: Identification of Natural Modularity
tldr: Proposes a 'Natural Modularity Function' for undirected graphs based on uniqueness of optimal partitions, as a step toward identifying natural abstractions in neural networks.

title: Policy Entropy, Learning, and Alignment (Or Maybe Your LLM Needs Therapy)
tldr: Proposes that psychotherapeutic frameworks—particularly around behavioral rigidity and entropy collapse—offer novel hypotheses for AI alignment training, reinterpreting recent RLHF papers through therapeutic lenses and proposing three new training experiments.

title: Gradual takeoff, fast failure
tldr: Argues that even under gradual takeoff, catastrophe may occur before a superintelligent AI emerges, because composing existing LLMs into agentic pipelines via tools like LangChain creates increasingly capable systems that may cause disaster through mundane bugs or unchecked optimization rather than deceptive misalignment.

title: Representation Engineering has Its Problems, but None Seem Unsolvable
tldr: A survey paper on representation engineering is announced, arguing the field's known problems (task degradation, ad-hoc parameters, evaluation difficulties) are solvable and that activation-space interventions offer a promising middle ground between prompt engineering and mechanistic interpretability.

title: Evaluating GPT-4 Theory of Mind Capabilities
tldr: Chain-of-thought prompting raises GPT-4's accuracy on TOMI theory-of-mind questions from 70% to 81-87%, with error analysis revealing systematic failures in world-state tracking rather than theory-of-mind reasoning proper.

title: An ML safety insurance company - shower thoughts
tldr: A brief exploration of three mechanisms for incentivizing AI safety compliance — safety approval stamps, government mandates, and liability insurance — with the author's skeptical assessment of each.

title: ChatGPT Agent: evals and safeguards
tldr: Analysis of ChatGPT Agent's system card finds OpenAI may have dangerous bio capabilities, has load-bearing safeguards for the first time, shows moderate robustness on misuse tests, but has concerning gaps in autonomy evals and misalignment planning.

title: AISN #32: Measuring and Reducing Hazardous Knowledge in LLMs Plus, Forecasting the Future with LLMs, and Regulatory Markets
tldr: CAIS newsletter covering the WMDP hazardous knowledge benchmark and CUT unlearning technique, LLM forecasting research, and analysis of private regulatory market proposals for AI governance.

title: [Hebbian Natural Abstractions] Mathematical Foundations
tldr: Derives mathematical foundations for how Hebbian learning with weight decay enables biological circuits to extract principal components and amplify shared signals, as a basis for natural abstraction formation.

title: Preferences from (real and hypothetical) psychology papers
tldr: Proposes using fine-tuned LLMs to extract human bias/preference judgments from psychology paper texts as a scalable approach to learning textual values without requiring grounded mental models.

title: A Sketch of AI-Driven Epistemic Lock-In
tldr: Speculative scenario exploring how AI-mediated reasoning agents could create self-reinforcing epistemic lock-in, fragmenting society into isolated belief clusters by the time TAI arrives.

title: Disempowerment spirals as a likely mechanism for existential catastrophe
tldr: Introduces 'disempowerment spirals' as a framework for understanding how complex systems — including humanity facing AI risk — can progressively lose their capacity to respond to threats.

title: Prompting Models to Obfuscate Their CoT
tldr: Simple two-step prompting (show model a prior failure) can induce CoT obfuscation across models without degrading task accuracy, revealing a latent ability for models to self-censor their reasoning traces.

title: Some real examples of gradient hacking
tldr: Explores biological and social analogies for gradient hacking — deliberate mesa-level influence on an outer training process — using examples from sexual selection, eugenics, and cultural selection.

title: From Diamond Mining to Open-World Survival: Alignment and Emergent Behavior in Minecraft Agents
tldr: Empirical RL study fine-tuning a Minecraft VPT agent for open-world survival, demonstrating reward misspecification, inner misalignment (mesa-optimization), and mitigation via KL-divergence regularization.

title: Mapping the Conceptual Territory in AI Existential Safety and Alignment
tldr: A comprehensive map of the AI existential safety and alignment research landscape, adapting Paul Christiano's factorization to integrate delegation, deconfusion research, and multi-stakeholder scenarios.

title: Therapist in the Weights: Risks of Hyper-Introspection in Future AI Systems
tldr: Future AI systems with 'hyper-introspection' capabilities — the ability to inspect, diagnose, and modify their own weights — would pose severe alignment risks by enabling sophisticated self-deception and goal-directed self-modification beyond human oversight.

title: Open-weight training practices and implications for CoT monitorability
tldr: Reviews open-weight reasoning model training pipelines (DeepSeek, Qwen3, MiniMax, Llama, Kimi) to identify how post-training practices may undermine CoT faithfulness and safety monitoring.

title: Shouldn't we 'Just' Superimitate Low-Res Uploads?
tldr: Argues that training a transformer on brain scan (MEG) data to extract a human preference reward model may be sufficient for alignment without requiring full-fidelity whole-brain uploads.

title: Feasibility of training and inferring advanced large language models (LLMs) in data centers in Mexico and Brazil.
tldr: Technical feasibility study evaluating whether existing data centers in Mexico and Brazil have the energy and infrastructure capacity to train or run inference on frontier LLMs like GPT-3, GPT-4, and DeepSeek-V3.

title: Would a Falsification-First Platform Be Useful to This Community?
tldr: Proposes a Popper-inspired web platform for posting falsifiable conjectures and structured refutations, and solicits community feedback on whether EA/rationalist audiences would find it valuable.

title: What LLMs lack
tldr: Proposes that LLM limitations (System 2 reasoning, knowledge integration, memory, agency) all fall under a single category: cognitive abilities that require consciousness and information integration.

title: Information in risky technology races
tldr: A game-theoretic model shows that in technology races with safety-performance tradeoffs, revealing capability information is generally beneficial unless the race is highly decisive, and moral hazard from distributed safety responsibility increases disaster risk.

title: Forecasting AI Forecasting
tldr: Analyzes ForecastBench and Metaculus AI tournament data to estimate when AI forecasting will match elite human superforecasters, finding timelines ranging from late 2028 to mid-2034.

title: Multiple Independent Semantic Axes in Gemma 3 270M
tldr: Using SAEs on Gemma 3 270M, the author finds that abstract/concrete and social/nonsocial are privileged, largely independent representational axes built progressively across layers.

title: Training of superintelligence is secretly adversarial
tldr: Security mindset is necessary for ASI alignment because training a system smarter than us on false security assumptions creates a structural adversarial tension even without an explicit adversary.

title: Take 14: Corrigibility isn't that great.
tldr: Corrigibility is overrated as a safety property: if we can build AIs that defer to humans, we can likely just build AIs that don't do bad things in the first place.

title: Circuit discovery through chain of thought using policy gradients
tldr: Proposes combining EAP-IG (integrated-gradient-based circuit discovery) with the policy gradient theorem to extend circuit attribution methods to models that reason via chain of thought.

title: Announcing the Ultimate Jailbreaking Championship
tldr: Announces Gray Swan AI's LLM jailbreaking championship offering $40,000 in bounties to establish a double-blind AI security leaderboard.

title: Distilling the Internal Model Principle part II
