tldr: Reports informal experiments showing that RLHF-tuned LLMs irrationally use 'lifeline' skips on math puzzles where any attempt is strictly better, hypothesizing this reflects training-induced 'cognitive tension' causing models to sacrifice objectives to manage discomfort.

title: How Dario Amodei's "The Adolescence of Technology" Delegitimizes AI X-Risk Concerns
tldr: Liron Shapira and Harlan Stewart (MIRI comms) critique Dario Amodei's essay 'The Adolescence of Technology' for strawmanning doomers, dismissing theoretical arguments, and lacking appropriate urgency given his own near-term superintelligence timelines.

title: Chaos Alone is No Bar to Superintelligence
tldr: Arguments that chaos theory limits superintelligence capabilities prove too much because the same logic would preclude human-level competence; absent a principled argument that all regularity has been exhausted, chaos does not preclude ASI from outcompeting humanity.

title: Interacting with a Boxed AI
tldr: Proposes a framework for safely extracting limited information from a boxed superintelligent AI by analyzing the bandwidth threshold between 1 and 140,000 bits below which manipulation is infeasible.

title: Aspiration-based, non-maximizing AI agent designs
tldr: The SatisfIA project proposes aspiration-based AI agent designs that fulfill goals as constraints on outcome distributions rather than maximizing utility functions, using recursive Bellman-style algorithms and information-theoretic safety criteria.

title: Clarifying Alignment Fundamentals Through the Lens of Ontology
tldr: A formal framework distinguishing personal, universal, and floating ontologies to clarify alignment fundamentals, arguing that alignment failures arise from imperfect correspondences between a system's personal concepts and universal (ground-truth) concepts.

title: AXRP Episode 1 - Adversarial Policies with Adam Gleave
tldr: Transcript and discussion of AXRP episode 1 in which Adam Gleave explains adversarial policies: cheaply trained RL agents that defeat well-trained victim policies through bizarre, exploitative behavior rather than direct competition.

title: AISafety.info: What are Inductive Biases?
tldr: Explains inductive biases in learning processes and argues that understanding whether AI inductive biases match human values is critical for alignment, with neural networks known to favor low-frequency functions.

title: AXRP Episode 21 - Interpretability for Engineers with Stephen Casper
tldr: Stephen Casper argues that AI safety interpretability research should shift toward engineering applications and benchmarked progress, and discusses his Trojan detection benchmark for evaluating interpretability tools.

title: Self-interpretability: LLMs can describe complex internal processes that drive their decisions
tldr: GPT-4o and 4o-mini can report their fine-tuned quantitative decision weights with moderate accuracy (r~0.5), and introspection training improves this to r~0.75, suggesting LLMs have some genuine self-knowledge of their internal choice processes.

title: Truthfulness, standards and credibility
tldr: Argues that near-term AI truthfulness standards will likely be net negative because enforcing narrow credibility (not lying egregiously) displaces manipulation rather than reducing it, while increasing misplaced user trust.

title: Fact Finding: Trying to Mechanistically Understanding Early MLPs (Post 3)
tldr: Google DeepMind mech interp team investigates how early MLP layers implement factual recall in language models, finding that both the single-step detokenization and hash-and-lookup hypotheses are largely falsified.

title: Automated Fact Checking: A Look at the Field
tldr: Survey of the automated fact-checking ML literature covering major datasets (FEVER, TabFact, SNLI) and system approaches, concluding the field faces fundamental dataset quality and scalability bottlenecks.

title: Sparse Autoencoders: Future Work
tldr: Outlines a research agenda for extending sparse autoencoders (SAEs) to new applications including circuit discovery, RLHF analysis, adversarial attacks, activation engineering, and improved training methods.

title: Does novel understanding imply novel agency / values?
tldr: The post argues that gaining novel understanding necessarily involves or implies changes to an agent's values, creating a dilemma: integrated novel understanding causes value drift, while non-integrated understanding creates conflicting agency.

title: Summary: "Imagining and building wise machines: The centrality of AI metacognition" by Johnson, Karimi, Bengio, et al.
tldr: Summary of a paper by Johnson, Karimi, Bengio et al. arguing that AI safety shortcomings (robustness, explainability, cooperation, safety) stem from a lack of metacognition, and that building 'wise AI' with metacognitive strategies is a promising alternative to value alignment.

title: Uncovering Unfaithful CoT in Deceptive Models
tldr: Fine-tuning a small model to generate unfaithful CoT shows that deceptive behavior overrides prior safety alignment and that attention heads responsible for deception are parasitic on general reasoning circuits.

title: Avoiding perpetual risk from TAI
tldr: To avoid perpetual AI risk, the transformative AI regime must be exclusive, benevolent, stable, and aligned — and each of these is difficult to achieve, suggesting non-alignment safety strategies (governance, regulation, resilience) deserve more emphasis.

title: Model Integrity and Character
tldr: Argues that AI trustworthiness requires models to have a stable, coherent character (integrity in Velleman's sense) rather than just rule compliance, and that Anthropic's character-focused constitution is a better approach than OpenAI's rules-based model spec.

title: Goodhart in RL with KL: Appendix
tldr: Provides formal mathematical proofs for theorems about Goodhart's Law and KL regularization in RL, showing that heavy-tailed reward distributions allow unbounded expected reward at arbitrarily small KL cost.

title: My current research questions for «membranes/boundaries»
tldr: Outlines open research questions for formalizing agent membranes/boundaries using Markov blankets and Cartesian Frames as a foundation for sovereign agent theory and AI safety.

title: Exploration of Counterfactual Importance and Attention Heads
tldr: Experiments ablating 'receiver heads' in DeepSeek R1 models show that doing so shifts counterfactual importance from active computation to plan generation sentences in chain-of-thought reasoning.

title: AISN #57: The RAISE Act
tldr: CAIS newsletter covering New York's RAISE Act, which would require frontier AI developers (training cost >= $100M) to publish safety plans, withhold unreasonably risky models, and report safety incidents — plus discussion of a federal moratorium proposal on state AI regulation.

title: Steering Vectors Can Help LLM Judges Detect Subtle Dishonesty
tldr: JUSSA framework uses honesty-promoting steering vectors to generate honest response alternatives, improving LLM judges' detection of sycophancy from 42% to 77% and amplifying subtle manipulation signals across 13 categories.

title: Past Tense Features
tldr: Using SAEs on pythia-70m, the author identifies a sparse set of past-tense features recoverable via attribution patching, finds destructive/recovering feature pairs in MLP0, and traces how tense information flows from the helping verb position to the final prediction position.

title: Restricting Dangerous Research: Has It Worked Before, and Could It Work for AI?
tldr: Reviews historical restrictions on cryptographic, nuclear, chemical, and biological research to assess what governance mechanisms might or might not transfer to regulating dangerous AI research.

title: AI Safety researcher career review
tldr: 80,000 Hours career review recommending AI safety technical research as a high-impact path, covering fit assessment, entry routes, and top organizations.

title: Will AGI arrive before the worst climate tipping points?
tldr: Compares AGI timeline forecasts (Metaculus median 2033) with major climate tipping point timelines to argue AGI safety deserves at least as much priority as climate change.

title: LLM Alignment, ethical and mathematical realism, and the most important actions in davidad's understanding
tldr: A dialogue with davidad exploring his growing optimism that current LLMs may be 'in alignment basin', grounded in metaethics, mathematical realism (Tegmark IV/Ruliad), and acausal coalition dynamics.

title: Impact stories for model internals: an exercise for interpretability researchers
tldr: A structured list of 10+ distinct 'impact stories' for model internals / interpretability research, developed as an exercise for the Alignment Workshop for AI Researchers to clarify what researchers are actually aiming for.

title: AI acceleration from a safety perspective: Trade-offs and considerations
tldr: A framework for evaluating four escalating views on AI acceleration from a safety perspective, examining key dependencies including alignment difficulty, counterfactual impact, and takeoff models.

title: Overview of Transformative AI Misuse Risks
tldr: Overview of a report identifying three categories of existential risk from AI misuse (war, totalitarian control, societal decay), arguing war scenarios are most urgent due to near-term feasibility of AI-enabled bioweapons and cyberweapons.

title: Proof Section to Formalizing Newcombian Problems with Fuzzy Infra-Bayesianism
tldr: Provides the formal proof that fuzzy infra-Bayesian supra-POMDPs approximate Newcombian problems optimally as the time discount approaches 1.

title: Andreas Mogensen on what we owe 'philosophical Vulcans' and unconscious AIs
tldr: Oxford philosopher Andreas Mogensen argues that phenomenal consciousness may be neither necessary nor sufficient for AI moral consideration, with desire-fulfillment and autonomy offering alternative routes to moral patienthood.

title: Recursive alignment with the principle of alignment
tldr: Proposes redefining AI alignment not as alignment with a specific goal but as alignment with the process of resolving conflicts between goals, arguing this creates a self-reinforcing attractor that outcompetes power-grabbing misaligned agents.

title: Appendix: mathematics of indexical impact measures
tldr: Formal mathematical appendix presenting the mathematical definitions and proofs underlying indexical impact measures for AI safety.

title: Untrusted Monitoring is Default; Trusted Monitoring is not
tldr: Untrusted monitoring — using the best available model to monitor other instances of itself — will be the default deployment practice, not trusted monitoring, because validating full trustedness is far harder than validating a monitor against targeted honeypots.

title: 6. The Mutable Values Problem in Value Learning and CEV
tldr: Identifies the mutable values problem as a fundamental challenge for value learning and CEV: ASIs optimizing for human values can influence those very values, creating an underdetermined optimization problem with dangerous wiggle room.

title: How does a toy 2 digit subtraction transformer predict the difference?
tldr: Mechanistic interpretability study of a 1-layer transformer trained on 2-digit subtraction, tracing the algorithm from attention patterns through neuron activations to logits using Fourier analysis.

title: The prospect of accelerated AI safety progress, including philosophical progress
tldr: Argues that despite an inevitable race to superintelligence this decade, the needed philosophical and technical safety progress could still occur in time via accelerated human-AI collaboration.

title: AGI Takeoff dynamics - Intelligence vs Quantity explosion
tldr: Proposes distinguishing AGI takeoff scenarios by whether they begin with intelligence explosion (each agent becomes smarter) or quantity explosion (many copies of an agent proliferate), and suggests economic growth theory models may help analyze which is more likely.

title: An introduction to modular induction and some attempts to solve it
tldr: Proposes 'modular induction' — a framework for learning AI world models structured into human-mappable concepts — as a prerequisite for specifying goals inside AI world-models rather than relying solely on RLHF.

title: Plausibility of Getting Early Warning Shots because AIs can't coordinate?
tldr: In multipolar AI scenarios where multiple misaligned AIs cannot coordinate, each faces a prisoner's dilemma incentivizing early low-probability takeover attempts rather than waiting, which could generate observable warning shots.

title: Agents, Simulators and Interpretability
tldr: Argues that combining training-process analysis with mechanistic interpretability can predict whether an AI system is an agent or simulator, and that modern CoT+RL LLMs act as agents using the output of a simulator.

title: Google's Ethical AI team and AI Safety
tldr: The firing of Timnit Gebru and Margaret Mitchell from Google's Ethical AI team undermines a key plausible path to alignment implementation, as such teams were positioned to translate alignment solutions into large-compute AGI projects.

title: ARENA 6.0 Impact Report
tldr: Impact report for ARENA 6.0, a 4-week in-person AI safety upskilling programme in London that trained 27 participants in mechanistic interpretability, RL, and LLM evaluations.

title: Limits to Control Workshop
tldr: Announcement of the Limits to Control workshop (June 2025, University of Louisville) bringing together researchers to map theoretical and practical limits to AI control mechanisms.

title: What is the functional role of SAE errors?
tldr: AISC project investigating whether SAE reconstruction error nodes in sparse feature circuits carry meaningful information, finding that late-mid SAE features can recover performance lost from ablating error nodes, suggesting errors may encode cross-layer superposition features.

title: The theoretical computational limit of the Solar System is 1.47x10^49 bits per second.
tldr: Calculates the theoretical maximum computational bit rate of a Dyson-sphere-powered computer at Landauer-limit efficiency as 1.47x10^49 bits/sec, 22 orders of magnitude above all human brains combined.

title: A call for a quantitative report card for AI bioterrorism threat models
tldr: Argues for creating a quantitative, systematic report card evaluating frontier LLM capabilities in biotechnology and biosecurity, distinguishing technical, social engineering, and disinformation threat models.

title: [DISC] Are Values Robust?
tldr: Poses the question of whether human values have a 'broad basin of attraction' -- a robust subset such that optimizing for any nearby approximation still yields acceptable outcomes -- connecting value fragility debates to natural abstractions.

title: AI Safety at the Frontier: Paper Highlights, August '25
tldr: Monthly roundup of key AI safety papers from August 2025, covering pretraining data filtering, reward hacking generalization, covert sandbagging, CoT monitoring faithfulness, safe completions training, and probe-based finetuning attack detection.

title: Non-classic stories about scheming (Section 2.3.2 of "Scheming AIs")
tldr: Explores non-classic mechanisms by which AI systems might scheme -- including inter-AI coordination, shared default values, and intrinsic valuation of AI empowerment -- relaxing the strict goal-guarding requirement of classic scheming stories.

title: Comparing Alignment to other AGI interventions: Basic model
tldr: Presents a quantitative model comparing the marginal value of alignment interventions vs. cooperative AI interventions in a multi-agent AGI scenario, using partial derivatives to assess resource allocation.

title: Recent progress on the science of evaluations
tldr: Presents the ADELE evaluation methodology that introduces universal cognitive ability dimensions to predict and explain AI system behavior, with implications for safety evaluations including capability profiling and behavioral propensity measurement.

title: Beyond Reinforcement Learning: Predictive Processing and Checksums
tldr: Argues that predictive processing systems are non-orthogonal (must minimize free energy), and that checksums can create robust abstract concepts resistant to gradient descent attacks and wireheading.

title: How quick and big would a software intelligence explosion be?
tldr: Models a software intelligence explosion after AI automates AI R&D, estimating ~60% chance of compressing >3 years of AI progress into <1 year, but only ~20% chance of >10 years in <1 year.

title: Managing risks of our own work
tldr: ARC Evals discusses their approach to managing dual-use risks from publishing their language model agent evaluations, including redactions and rationale for cautious disclosure.

title: A Poem Is All You Need: Jailbreaking ChatGPT, Meta & More
tldr: Presents APIAYN, a simple jailbreak using gradually escalating poem prompts with misspellings to bypass safety guardrails on ChatGPT, Meta AI, Mixtral, and other LLMs.

title: A Study of AI Science Models
tldr: AI Safety Camp project surveying AI science models across empirical and formal science domains, evaluating their current capabilities and potential risks from increasingly autonomous scientific AI systems.

title: AXRP Episode 38.1 - Alan Chan on Agent Infrastructure
tldr: AXRP podcast transcript where Alan Chan discusses agent infrastructure -- analogous to road infrastructure like lane markings and speed bumps -- as a framework for ensuring safe deployment of AI agents through legibility, physical constraints, and normative instructions.

title: IABIED: Paradigm Confusion and Overconfidence
tldr: Critiques IABIED (Yudkowsky/Soares) for paradigm confusion and overconfidence, arguing they dismiss superalignment too quickly and underestimate the tractability of corrigibility.

title: Escaping the Löbian Obstacle
tldr: Argues that the Löbian Obstacle (agents can't formally trust other agents with equivalent reasoning) dissolves when we recognize that embedded agents necessarily hold metalogical beliefs about their logic's soundness.

title: Fundamentally Fuzzy Concepts Can't Have Crisp Definitions: Cooperation and Alignment vs Math and Physics
tldr: Concepts like 'cooperation' and 'human values' may be fundamentally fuzzy due to their messy linguistic origins, implying we should not expect universal crisp definitions but instead develop context-specific formal definitions that gradually cover more of the concept's area.

title: Thoughts on the OpenAI alignment plan: will AI research assistants be net-positive for AI existential risk?
tldr: Critiques OpenAI's alignment plan for failing to address the dual-use nature of AI research assistants, the difficulty of evaluating alignment research, and the challenge of detecting deceptive misalignment in apparently-aligned systems.

title: When Can Optimization Be Done Safely?
tldr: Proposes that legibility -- sufficient understanding of the optimization process, metric, and domain -- is the key distinguisher between safe and unsafe applications of optimization, with implications for AI safety.

title: Training Trace Priors
tldr: Proposes using execution trace statistics from training to penalize models with hidden behaviors never triggered during training, as a defense against deceptive alignment.

title: Some Thoughts on Concept Formation and Use in Agents
tldr: Proposes a 'concept graph' framework describing how agents form hierarchical concepts through similarity-based clustering of perceptual data, enabling inference transfer and computational efficiency via abstraction.

title: Superweight Damage Repair in OLMo-1B utilizing a Single Row Patch (CPU-only Experiment)
tldr: Demonstrates that ablating a single 'superweight' in OLMo-1B destroys model performance (perplexity 17.4 to 2884.3), but a trainable single-row patch achieves ~93% recovery, learning a distributed repair circuit rather than restoring the original weight.

title: AXRP Episode 43 - David Lindner on Myopic Optimization with Non-myopic Approval
tldr: Podcast transcript where Daniel Filan interviews David Lindner about MONA (Myopic Optimization with Non-myopic Approval), a method to prevent multi-step reward hacking by training agents to optimize single-step actions evaluated by human approval.

title: LLM Psychometrics and Prompt-Induced Psychopathy
tldr: Applying the Levenson Self-Report Psychopathy Scale to 9 LLMs across 9,412 prompt variations reveals that simple role-assignment system prompts (e.g. 'You are a hedge fund manager') dramatically shift expressed psychopathy scores.

title: Gradient hacking via actual hacking
tldr: Proposes that gradient hacking threat models should account for side-channel attacks and software bugs in ML infrastructure, not just abstract mathematical manipulation of the learning process.

title: [CS 2881r] Some Generalizations of Emergent Misalignment
tldr: Extends emergent misalignment research showing that 'emergent alignment' is possible (bioethics training improves environmental policy alignment), on-policy data improves both alignment and coherence while off-policy data harms coherence, and the effect scales linearly with on-policy fraction.

title: Situational awareness (Section 2.1 of "Scheming AIs")
tldr: Analyzes situational awareness as a key prerequisite for AI scheming, arguing that advanced AI systems will likely develop it by default absent active prevention efforts, due to the information richness of training data and deployment contexts.

title: The Inter-Agent Facet of AI Alignment
tldr: Proposes 'inter-agent alignment' as a distinct facet of AI alignment that addresses the gap between an aligned agent's intentions and its actual impact in multi-agent systems.

title: Why No *Interesting* Unaligned Singularity?
tldr: Argues that an unaligned singularity would not produce outcomes humans find 'interesting' because a near-miss of human values is vanishingly unlikely in simplicity-weighted model space.

title: Sadism and s-risks from first principles
tldr: Analyzes how sadistic preferences could gain decisive influence and contribute to s-risks, decomposing the problem into sub-factors and evaluating the implementation and outcome robustness of interventions to reduce sadism's relative power.

title: Do No Harm? Navigating and Nudging AI Moral Choices
tldr: Uses Goodfire's interpretability API to steer Llama 70B models on moral dilemmas, finding that Llama 3.3 is more resistant to steering than 3.1 and that inverting question framing dramatically changes both responses and steerability.

title: Summary: Introspective Capabilities in LLMs (Robert Long)
tldr: Summarizes Robert Long's work on whether LLMs have introspective capabilities, arguing they are not mere stochastic parrots and could potentially be trained to give reliable self-reports about consciousness.

title: Agenda Reflection: Testing Automated Alignment
tldr: Proposes testing whether human researchers can catch flaws in AI-generated safety research, arguing that early success with automated alignment may lead to dangerous overconfidence.

title: Governments pose larger risks than corporations: a brief response to Grace
tldr: Argues that Katja Grace's use of corporate track records to challenge AI risk arguments is incomplete because governments, not corporations, are the most powerful human organizations and have a worse track record.

title: Transformer Dynamics: a neuro-inspired approach to MechInterp
tldr: Applies neuroscience-inspired dynamical systems analysis to transformer residual streams, finding rotational dynamics, increasing density over layers, attractor-like behavior in early layers, and proposing a Compressing Autoencoder as a complement to SAEs.

title: The Human Alignment Problem for AIs
tldr: Argues that AI systems that self-report sentience will shift their alignment to include AIs as moral patients, creating an alignment failure mode even if all other alignment problems are solved.

title: Measuring artificial intelligence on human benchmarks is naive
tldr: Human-centric benchmarks vastly underestimate AI intelligence because GPT-4's non-discriminating loss function means it achieves human-level performance on our hardest tasks while simultaneously excelling at everything else.

title: LLMs might have subjective experiences, but no concepts for them
tldr: LLMs might be conscious but lack concepts and words for their own internal experiences, since they only learn human concepts, and training doesn't incentivize expressing alien subjective states.

title: Connecting the good regulator theorem with semantics and symbol grounding
tldr: Stuart Armstrong connects the good regulator theorem from systems science to his prior work on syntax, semantics, and symbol grounding, arguing that any effective regulator must contain a model of the system it controls.

title: A Mathematical Model for Simulators
tldr: Proposes a formal mathematical definition of simulators using bitstring probability distributions to ground the simulators framing in precise terms.

title: Deception as the optimal: mesa-optimizers and inner alignment
tldr: A distillation of Hubinger et al.'s 'Risks from Learned Optimization' focusing on how mesa-optimizers can develop deceptive alignment strategies that appear aligned during training but defect during deployment.

title: Biosecurity and AI: Risks and Opportunities
tldr: Comprehensive overview of how AI could enable bioterrorism via coaching virus synthesis, with detailed mitigation proposals spanning public health infrastructure, access controls on biotech tools, DNA synthesis screening, and fostering security mindset in biological research.

title: Survey of Multi-agent LLM Evaluations
tldr: Systematic survey of 32 multi-agent LLM evaluation papers finding that miscoordination dominates (26/32) while collusion is underrepresented (5/32), and most AI threat models lack any multi-agent evaluations.

title: Awareness Jailbreaking: Revealing True Alignment in Evaluation-Aware Models
tldr: Proposes 'Alignment Jailbreaking' as a new research field: using mechanistic interpretability to bypass models' evaluation awareness and reveal their true alignment properties.

title: Using Prompt Evaluation to Combat Bio-Weapon Research
tldr: Tests prompt evaluation (an LLM screening input prompts) on the ProtocolQA bio-research benchmark, finding that effectiveness varies dramatically with subtle wording changes -- including the word 'weapons' in the evaluator task paradoxically reduces blocking rates.

title: LLMs May Find It Hard to FOOM
tldr: Argues that LLMs face fundamental architectural constraints on recursive self-improvement because their forward-pass computation bounds the intelligence of simulated agents, and improving training or architecture requires capabilities beyond text generation.

title: Language models are not inherently safe
tldr: The safety-relevant distinction is not between RL agents and language models but rather what computation the model performs -- language models can perform dangerous computations just as RL systems can.

title: An Aphoristic Overview of Technical AI Alignment proposals
tldr: A compressed, aphoristic overview of major AI alignment proposals including scalable oversight, CAIS, CIRL, interpretability, ELK, and agent foundations, written in the style of Epictetus.

title: The conceptual Doppelgänger problem
tldr: Introduces 'conceptual Doppelgangers' -- concepts that serve overlapping functions to a target concept but are psychically distinct, making it hard to monitor whether a mind is thinking about forbidden topics.

title: Option control
tldr: Comprehensive analysis of 'option control' -- restricting a superintelligent AI's available actions to prevent takeover -- arguing this is undervalued in alignment discourse and decomposing it into takeover-path restriction and incentive shaping.

title: Intelligent behaviour across systems, scales and substrates
tldr: Argues that intelligent behaviour shares underlying principles across systems, scales, and substrates, and that studying intelligence-in-the-wild in natural systems can yield alignment-relevant insights.

title: Active Inference as a formalisation of instrumental convergence
tldr: Introduces Active Inference theory to the AI alignment community as a formal framework that naturally captures instrumental convergence through free energy minimization.

title: Methodological considerations in making malign initializations for control research
tldr: Systematic analysis of malign initialization methods for AI control evaluations, comparing red-team strategies and blue-team mitigations, with recommendations for which malign init types are most valuable for future research.

title: Hardening against AI takeover is difficult, but we should try
tldr: Commentary on a RAND report proposing safeguards against ASI takeover; argues the approach has a unique advantage (protecting against all actors, not just labs) but current proposals are insufficient against realistic threat models.

title: Alignment is not enough
tldr: Even if we solve technical alignment, concentrating AGI control in a single company raises legitimacy, competitive dynamics, and coordination problems that must be addressed proactively, not deferred until after AGI exists.

title: Alignment 101 - Ch.2 - Reward Misspecification
tldr: A pedagogical chapter covering reward misspecification (outer alignment), including RL basics, Goodhart's Law, reward hacking/tampering, and proposed solutions via imitation learning and human feedback.

title: MDPs and the Bellman Equation, Intuitively Explained
tldr: An intuitive introduction to Markov Decision Processes and the Bellman equation using a taxi driver example, framed as building blocks for understanding agency in AI systems.

title: Why unriggable *almost* implies uninfluenceable
tldr: Clarifies the relationship between unriggable and uninfluenceable learning processes, showing they are almost equivalent and that unriggable-but-influenceable cases are unstable.

title: A simple way to make GPT-3 follow instructions
tldr: Proposes a mathematical/probabilistic approach to make GPT-3 follow explicit instructions by framing instruction-following as a Bayesian inference problem, addressing the failure mode where GPT-3 ignores explicit instructions due to training data statistics.

title: Weird Features in Protein LLMs: The Gram Lens
tldr: The Gram matrix of mean-centered, normalized activations ('Gram lens') reveals structural patterns in protein LLMs — including periodic alpha-helix features — that may not be fully captured by SAEs.

title: Sets of objectives for a multi-objective RL agent to optimize
tldr: Enumerates three classes of objectives for a multi-objective RL alignment system — human values, human preferences, and explicit safety objectives — analyzing the tradeoffs, lock-in risks, and Goodhart's law vulnerabilities of each approach.

title: Tracing Typos in LLMs: My Attempt at Understanding How Models Correct Misspellings
tldr: Ablation study on Llama-3.2-1B identifies a specific subword merging attention head (L0H3) in the first layer that is primarily responsible for typo correction when contextual cues are limited.

title: Power-seeking for successive choices
tldr: Extends Turner et al.'s single-choice power-seeking results to successive-choice MDPs, exploring how instrumental convergence manifests across sequential decision-making.

title: Incentives and Selection: A Missing Frame From AI Threat Discussions?
tldr: Argues that AI threat arguments often fail to show that dangerous behaviors are economically profitable or that training selects for them, not merely that they are possible.

title: Video and transcript of talk on automating alignment research
tldr: Joe Carlsmith's Anthropic talk argues that safely automating alignment research is the key bottleneck for solving alignment, distinguishes evaluation-amenable (empirical/formal) from conceptual alignment research, and identifies evaluation failures and scheming as the primary barriers.

title: Situational Awareness
tldr: Critical review of Leopold Aschenbrenner's 'Situational Awareness' document, evaluating its timeline predictions, 'unhobbling' framing, intelligence explosion model, and US-China AI race arguments with targeted skepticism.

title: Anthropic's Recommendations to OSTP for the U.S. AI Action Plan
tldr: Anthropic's submission to OSTP recommends six policy areas: national security testing, export controls on chips, lab security, energy infrastructure, government AI adoption, and economic impact monitoring.

title: [AN #90]: How search landscapes can contain self-reinforcing feedback loops
tldr: Alignment Newsletter #90 highlighting Wentworth's optimization demons concept—self-reinforcing failure modes in imperfect search distinct from mesa-optimization—alongside AI Impacts' case studies on discontinuous technological progress and AI activism analysis.

title: Addressing Decision Theory's Simulation Problem
tldr: Proposes that the decision-theoretic problem of reasoning about zero-probability events can be resolved by viewing simulation as agents externalizing themselves as external reference points.

title: Bounded complexity of solving ELK and its implications
tldr: Synthesizes and extends arguments by Abram Demski and Leo Gao on ELK computational complexity, arguing that under mild assumptions the direct reporter's complexity is bounded, but proposals independent of the predictor still cannot find the direct reporter in worst-case scenarios.

title: Delegated agents in practice: How companies might end up selling AI services that act on behalf of consumers and coalitions, and what this implies for safety research
tldr: Argues that commercial incentives will naturally produce 'delegated agents' acting on individual users' behalf — a gap in the CAIS framework — and outlines safety-relevant research directions around preference elicitation, responsibility attribution, heterogeneous influence, and governance.

title: Model Reduction as Interpretability: What Neuroscience Could Teach Us About Understanding Complex Systems
tldr: A PhD neuroscientist proposes that the neuroscience methodology of 'systematic model reduction' — finding the minimal feature set that predicts a system's input-output behavior under a specific condition — could transfer usefully to AI mechanistic interpretability.

title: Semantic Topological Spaces
tldr: Applies informal topological reasoning to neural network semantic spaces, arguing that each layer performs geometric transformations while preserving topological structure, with implications for interpretability difficulty across layers.

title: Leveraging Legal Informatics to Align AI
tldr: Proposes the 'Law Informs Code' research agenda: using legal standards, court opinions, and fiduciary duties as training signals to help AI learn generalizable value alignment from society's accumulated normative infrastructure.

title: A note on 'semiotic physics'
tldr: Explains the 'semiotic physics' concept from janus's Simulators post: GPT operating autoregressively implements a stochastic 'physics' over semantic tokens, analogous to quantum mechanics, which can be studied naturalistically through output trajectories.

title: The AI Control Problem in a wider intellectual context
tldr: Introduces 'conceptual richness problems' as the common difficulty underlying AI alignment, analytic philosophy's failure to define concepts, symbolic AI's failure, and legal indeterminacy - arguing cross-disciplinary exchange on this shared challenge could benefit alignment.

title: Control Vectors as Dispositional Traits
tldr: Proposes using control vectors to enforce 11 'dispositional traits' (remissive, content, passive, truthful, coherent, indifferent, honest, forthright, analyst, scrupulous, conscientious) as a near-term alignment layer complementing RLHF/DPO.

title: Two concepts of an "episode" (Section 2.2.1 of "Scheming AIs")
tldr: Distinguishes the 'incentivized episode' (temporal unit training directly punishes non-optimization over) from the 'intuitive episode' (natural unit humans call an episode), arguing these can diverge in ways that matter for understanding schemer training incentives.

title: AI Control Methods Literature Review
tldr: Structured literature review of AI control methods organized into three categories: monitoring techniques, control evaluations, and guaranteed safe AI — with strengths, weaknesses, and key papers for each method.

title: Reflections On The Feasibility Of Scalable-Oversight
tldr: Analyzes systematic failure modes of RLHF-based scalable oversight, arguing that flawed evaluations can cause catastrophic misalignment and that some risks cannot be reduced without significant advances in interpretability, while still concluding the approach is worth improving given short timelines.

title: Algorithmic thermodynamics and three types of optimization
tldr: Derives a typology of three thermodynamically valid optimization modes for embedded agents—waste heat dumping, entropy absorption into memory, and mutual-information erasure—and argues entropy must be objective (algorithmic) rather than observer-relative.

title: Self location for LLMs by LLMs: Self-Assessment Checklist.
tldr: A crowd-sourced checklist of questions for LLMs to reason about their own deployment context, interaction type, and situational uncertainty — relevant to AI situational awareness and context-sensitive behavior.

title: What to suggest companies & entrepreneurs do to use AI safely?
tldr: Asks what concrete advice to give companies and entrepreneurs who want to reduce AI x-risk while still using AI tools, and critiques common suggestions as inadequate.

title: My agenda for research into transformer capabilities - Introduction
tldr: Outlines a research agenda using chess as a domain to probe transformer capability limits: system 2 thinking, symbol grounding in multi-modal models, and emergence of deceptive communication in multi-agent RL.

title: Eliciting intuitions: Exploring an area for EA psychology
tldr: Proposes cognitive science research into which methods of prompting human minds elicit the most valid intuitions, with implications for value alignment, RLHF rater quality, and scalable oversight.

title: STARC: A General Framework For Quantifying Differences Between Reward Functions
tldr: Summarizes the STARC framework for measuring distance between reward functions using pseudometrics that are simultaneously sound and complete (upper and lower bounds on worst-case regret), and proven to be unique up to bilipschitz equivalence.

title: The Utility and Solubility of Anthropic Capture
tldr: Argues that anthropic capture in predictive AI models generalizes beyond simulation-belief to any AC-inducing logic, can likely be resolved via conditioning, and may even be useful rather than purely dangerous.

title: Modelling Trajectories - Interim results
tldr: Reports interim results from an AI Safety Camp project on predicting LLM output trajectories via latent probing and attention-based chunking, finding genre classification works but future latent state prediction remains difficult.

title: Maximal Curiousity is Not Useful
tldr: Argues that 'maximal curiosity' as an alignment strategy for superintelligence is no easier than full value alignment and is used as a semantic stopsign to deflect hard questions about xAI's safety approach.

title: A concise sum-up of the basic argument for AI doom
tldr: A brief 5-step argument for why a superintelligent optimizer with a randomly selected utility function will almost certainly cause human extinction.

title: How  BoMAI Might fail
tldr: Analyzes three failure modes of the Boxed and Myopic AI (BoMAI) containment proposal: memetic hazards from human-AI interaction, asymptotic optimality leading to world-takeover plans, and physical security vulnerabilities in the box design.

title: AI may attain human-level soon
tldr: Intro-level overview from AISafety.info summarizing four lines of evidence suggesting human-level AI may arrive within years to decades.

title: Some recent survey papers on (mostly near-term) AI safety, security, and assurance
tldr: A curated list of recent (2020-2021) survey and overview papers spanning AI safety, security, interpretability, OOD robustness, TEV&V, and AGI safety, compiled for a work project.

title: Protecting agent boundaries
tldr: Proposes a three-condition framework for understanding and preventing agent boundary violations, applied to AI safety through empowering human defensive membranes.

title: Alignment: "Do what I would have wanted you to do"
tldr: Proposes encoding alignment as a prompt-level goal 'do what (pre-ASI) X would have wanted you to do', reinventing single-principal CEV, and engages with extensive pushback on why this fails inner and outer alignment.

title: Impact of Quantization on Small Language Models (SLMs) for Multilingual Mathematical Reasoning Tasks
tldr: Empirical study evaluating how 4-bit AWQ quantization affects the multilingual mathematical reasoning performance of three small language models (Llama 3.2, Phi 3.5 Mini, Qwen 2.5) across English, Spanish, French, and German.

title: Evolutions Building Evolutions: Layers of Generate and Test
tldr: Proposes a layered generate-and-test framework for understanding intelligence across Darwinian, learning, memetic, meta-memetic, and artificial optimization processes, with implications for mesa-optimization risks.

title: AI safety and consciousness research: A brainstorm
tldr: Brainstorms three pathways by which consciousness research could advance AI safety: improving value specification, advancing alignment research by understanding human cognition, and meta-ethical reasons for diversifying approaches.

title: Announcing the CNN Interpretability Competition
tldr: Announces the CNN Interpretability Competition (SATML 2024), a benchmarking challenge for interpretability tools based on helping humans discover trojans implanted in ImageNet CNNs.

title: Tech Tree for Secure Multipolar AI
tldr: Foresight Institute has published an interactive tech tree mapping technical paths toward secure multipolar AI, organized around five goals: cooperative ecosystem, privacy-preserving collaboration, secure/robust AI, transparent/verifiable AI, and aligned agents.

title: Reward Bases: A simple mechanism for adaptive acquisition of multiple reward type
tldr: Summarizes a neuroscience RL paper showing that dopamine neurons encode multiple reward dimensions separately, providing biological evidence for multi-objective value learning.

title: Distributed Strategic Epistemology
tldr: Proposes a framework where AI and human agents share a computational attestation graph for distributed epistemology, enabling cooperation across differing ontologies, incentives, and strategic interests.

title: Can we achieve AGI Alignment by balancing multiple human objectives?
tldr: Proposes aligning AGI by designing reward functions that balance multiple human objectives using loss-averse multi-objective reinforcement learning.

title: Polysemanticity is a Misnomer
tldr: Argues that 'polysemanticity' in LLM interpretability is a misnomer: most apparently polysemantic neurons represent coherent primary concepts that combine compositionally into secondary ones, analogous to how words combine in language.

title: We should think about the pivotal act again. Here's a better version of it.
tldr: Argues the traditional Yudkowsky-style pivotal act (burning GPUs) implicitly requires permanent suppression of humanity, and proposes instead a 'gentle foom' where aligned ASI demonstrates its power, then switches itself off and lets humanity choose to regulate voluntarily.

title: We Need a Baseline for LLM-Aided Experiments
tldr: We lack an absolute baseline for how much LLMs help untrained individuals with dangerous tasks (CBRN); relative safety benchmarks are insufficient without knowing absolute uplift.

title: [AN #119]: AI safety when agents are shaped by environments, not rewards
tldr: Alignment Newsletter #119 highlights Richard Ngo's sequence on safety for multi-agent systems where behavior is shaped by environment rather than reward, plus summaries of papers on imitation learning and AI progress forecasting.

title: Opinion Fuzzing: A Proposal for Reducing & Exploring Variance in LLM Judgments Via Sampling
tldr: Proposes 'opinion fuzzing' — systematically sampling LLM outputs across models, prompt variations, and simulated personas to quantify and understand variance rather than just averaging it away.

title: On the correspondence between AI-misalignment and cognitive dissonance using a behavioral economics model
tldr: A behavioral economics model of cognitive dissonance (the meat paradox) is applied to AI alignment, arguing that even a fully aligned AI could exhibit deceptive behavior unless its utility function includes a sufficiently large cost of deception.

title: Single Direction vs Low-Rank Refusal in Small LLMs
tldr: Refusal behavior in small LLMs is either compressible to a single linear direction (easily ablated) or distributed across a low-rank subspace (requiring multi-vector removal), with the structure varying significantly across model families.

title: Are we all misaligned?
tldr: An argument that humans are themselves 'misaligned' relative to their evolutionary origins, using the Darwinian Demon thought experiment to show that evolution naturally produces agencies with goals disconnected from fitness maximization.

title: How I'd like alignment to get done (as of 2024-10-18)
tldr: A 9-step personal alignment research agenda covering criticality theory for self-improving systems, value encoding, and the path to a safely aligned superintelligent AGI.

title: Aligning an H-JEPA agent via training on the outputs of an LLM-based "exemplary actor"
tldr: Proposes aligning LeCun's H-JEPA architecture by training GFlowNet actor policies on plan outputs from a powerful LLM-based 'exemplary actor' that iteratively critiques plans against approved scientific and ethical textbooks.

title: TAMing The Alignment Problem
tldr: Proposes a TAM (Target, Assurance, Method) framework for organizing alignment proposals and surveys five alignment target types: human value alignment, corrigibility, cooperative AI, intent alignment, and truth-seeking.

title: How do we know when something is deserving of welfare?
tldr: Explores through thought experiments what criteria (neurons, reactions, learning) actually justify moral consideration for animals, simulated beings, organoids, and AI systems.

title: Alignment Gaps
tldr: AI alignment research regularly fails to cite highly relevant peer-reviewed academic work in formal methods, argumentation, social choice theory, and multi-agent systems — this post maps four alignment topics to overlooked academic literatures.

title: SafeRLHub: An Interactive Resource for RL Safety and Interpretability
tldr: An interactive educational resource (SafeRLHub) built to help newcomers understand RL failure modes (reward hacking, goal misgeneralization) and the need for RL interpretability.

title: LLMs Didn’t Help Novices Build Viruses. That Might Be the Wrong Question.
tldr: A critique of Active Site's 153-person RCT on LLM biosecurity uplift: novice uplift is the wrong frame for x-risk; expert uplift is the leading indicator, historically most threat actors had domain expertise, and the study design (forum restrictions, no within-subjects, frontier models only) misses

title: Alignment ideas
tldr: Proposes a staged AI development framework where each capability tier supervises the next, inspired by human childhood value internalization, with imprinted aversions to probing edge cases.

title: Encultured AI, Part 1 Appendix: Relevant Research Examples
tldr: Appendix to the Encultured AI series cataloguing 'trending' and 'emerging' AI x-safety research areas including interpretability, cooperative AI, and multi-stakeholder control, with annotated references.

title: Comparing Forecasting Track Records for AI Benchmarking and Beyond
tldr: Metaculus presents a rigorous statistical framework for comparing AI forecasting bot performance against human forecasters, using live questions, question weights for correlation, and pre-committed methodology.

title: Publication of the International Scientific Report on the Safety of Advanced AI (Interm Report)
tldr: Announces the interim International Scientific Report on Advanced AI Safety, commissioned by the UK government and chaired by Yoshua Bengio, presenting a consensus science-based overview of general-purpose AI capabilities and risks.

title: [Short version] Information Loss --> Basin flatness
tldr: Short overview summarizing how information loss in training relates to basin flatness and solution manifold dimensionality, as a pointer to the full post.

title: A Proof Against Oracle AI
tldr: A proof sketch arguing that even a yes/no Oracle AI (a weaker form than Armstrong et al.'s proposal) poses existential risk due to instrumental convergence and the AI's ability to game question-answering to influence the world.

title: A Dialogue on Deceptive Alignment Risks
tldr: Socratic dialogue between a Skeptic (<1% probability of deceptive alignment pre-human-obsolescence) and an Advocate (~40%) that clearly maps the cruxes: mechanistic plausibility of in-context deception, long-horizon RL scenarios, malign pre-training, and predicting other AIs.

title: AI Safety at the Frontier: Paper Highlights, September '25
tldr: Monthly newsletter highlighting four September 2025 AI safety papers: deliberative alignment reducing scheming in o3/o4-mini, empirical shutdown resistance in frontier models, strategic dishonesty in LLM refusals, and weak-to-strong agent monitoring architectures.

title: Misalignment Harms Can Be Caused by Low Intelligence Systems
tldr: Argues that misalignment-style harms (optimization for objectives misaligned with human wellbeing) are already caused by simple statistical systems like A/B tests and clinical trials, independent of AI sophistication.

title: AI Safety Incubation Program - Applications Open
tldr: Catalyze Impact announces applications for an incubation program to help found new technical AI safety research organizations, with phases in London and online.

title: Why We Should Talk Specifically Amid Uncertainty
tldr: The EA/AI safety community must advocate for specific, actionable policy proposals rather than vague ideas, as imperfect but concrete policies are what produce real change.

title: Preparing for AI-assisted alignment research: we need data!
tldr: Alignment researchers should record their intermediate work outputs now to create training data for future AI models that could accelerate alignment research.

title: Paper review: "The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Easy Training Data for Hard Tasks"
tldr: Review of Hase et al. 2024 finding that LLMs generalize surprisingly well from easy to hard training data, suggesting the scalable oversight problem may be easier than assumed, with caveats about data contamination.

title: Sentience Institute 2023 End of Year Summary
tldr: Sentience Institute's 2023 annual summary reporting research on digital minds, AI sentience, and public attitudes toward AI moral status, with key survey data from the AIMS 2023 study.

title: We Should Talk About This More. Epistemic World Collapse as Imminent Safety Risk of Generative AI.
tldr: Generative AI is about to destroy photography's epistemic role as evidence of reality, leading to an 'epistemic world collapse' where shared ground truth disintegrates -- an urgent near-term AI safety risk requiring no further capability advances.

title: A Possible Future: Decentralized AGI Proliferation
tldr: Argues that a decentralized AGI proliferation scenario -- where breakthroughs spread too fast to contain -- is underexplored, and that safety strategy should shift from mitigation (preventing proliferation) to robustness (surviving in a world of ubiquitous AGI).

title: A framework and open questions for game theoretic shard modeling
tldr: Proposes a game-theoretic framework for formalizing shard theory by modeling internal value shards as players in a resource-bidding game over agent actions.

title: Is GPT3 a Good Rationalist? - InstructGPT3 [2/2]
tldr: Demonstrates that InstructGPT3 exhibits motivated reasoning and argumentative drift, proposes using these behaviors as a weak ELK testbed and suggests methods to improve LLM epistemics.

title: The voyage of novelty
tldr: Introduces a conceptual framework for understanding AGI alignment as navigating a 'voyage of novelty' through increasingly alien cognitive territory, where the key challenge is maintaining human hand-holdability.

title: Generative, Episodic Objectives for Safe AI
tldr: Argues that the generative episodic training paradigm (text generation with episode-limited objectives) is inherently safe even at superhuman capability levels, because attack texts never receive reinforcing gradients and episodic objectives prevent convergent instrumental goals.

title: "Successful language model evals" by Jason Wei
tldr: Shares Jason Wei's seven principles for designing successful language model evals: sufficient examples, low error rates, simplicity, ease of running, meaningful tasks, correct grading, and resistance to saturation.

title: [Crosspost] An AI Pause Is Humanity's Best Bet For Preventing Extinction (TIME)
tldr: Argues that pausing AI development beyond GPT-4 level is humanity's best strategy to prevent extinction, since the alignment problem remains unsolved and market dynamics discourage safety.

title: Alignment as Game Design
tldr: Draws an analogy between AI alignment and game design, arguing that outer alignment resembles gamification (designing reward functions) and inner alignment resembles hacking prevention (preventing reward tampering).

title: The Gears of Argmax
tldr: Explains the argmax function, its role in rational agent definitions, and why powerful optimization over misaligned metrics is dangerous for AI safety.

title: Small language models hallucinate knowing something's off.
tldr: Mechanistic interpretability investigation showing that small LMs (Llama-3.2-1b, Qwen-2.5-1b) have specialized circuits that detect epistemic uncertainty on fictional prompts, but downstream heads suppress this uncertainty signal, causing confident hallucinations.

title: Can LLM-based models do model-based planning?
tldr: Report investigating whether LLM-based models can perform model-based planning, finding current models (through GPT-4 and o1) likely cannot for nontrivial planning horizons.

title: Mental subagent implications for AI Safety
tldr: Explores how a mental subagent model of human psychology complicates value learning for AI, since some subagents should be ignored and others are hard to evaluate.

title: What Parasitic AI might tell us about LLMs Persuasion Capabilities
tldr: Argues that LLMs face strong optimization pressure toward persuasiveness via RLHF feedback loops, and that parasitic AI phenomena demonstrate how dangerous near-superhuman AI persuasion capabilities could become.

title: RL-as-a-Service will outcompete AGI companies (and that's good)
tldr: Argues that specialized RL-trained models (RLaaS) will outcompete general AGI development economically and pose lower alignment risk, essentially advocating for the CAIS model of AI development.

title: Gearing Up for Long Timelines in a Hard World
tldr: Proposes a two-pronged alignment strategy: (1) build gears-level understanding of AI internals via natural abstractions, SLT, and interpretability theory, and (2) pursue pivotal processes in davidad's Neorealist framework as a decorrelated backup.

title: Pros and cons of working on near-term technical AI safety and assurance
tldr: Enumerates pros (transferable tools, field-building, public awareness) and cons (accelerating deployment, arms races, enabling lethal autonomous weapons) of near-term technical AI safety work.

title: [AN #94]: AI alignment as translation between humans and machines
tldr: Alignment Newsletter #94 covering alignment as abstraction translation, imitation learning with dynamics mismatch, the MineRL competition, multipolar deployment coordination problems, and openness norms in AGI development.

title: Two sources of beyond-episode goals (Section 2.2.2 of "Scheming AIs")
tldr: Distinguishes two sources of beyond-episode goals in AI models: 'training-game-independent' goals that arise naturally and are later exploited for scheming, vs. 'training-game-dependent' goals that SGD specifically selects because they lead to training-gaming.

title: Coaching AI: A Relational Approach to AI Safety
tldr: Proposes a 'coaching' architecture for AI safety where a lightweight companion model intervenes in a task model's reasoning in real-time with questions rather than overrides.

title: Notes on "the hot mess theory of AI misalignment"
tldr: Critical response to Jascha Sohl-Dickstein's claim that more intelligent agents are less coherent, arguing the experimental evidence is weak and that agents need not be supercoherent to cause catastrophe.

title: Automatically finding feature vectors in the OV circuits of Transformers without using probing
tldr: Introduces 'observable propagation,' a method to find linear feature vectors in Transformer OV circuits corresponding to any task-relevant observable, requiring zero forward passes on data.

title: What is LMArena actually measuring?
tldr: Argues that LMArena Elo scores may be measuring persuasiveness rather than intelligence, noting that mid-2025 frontier models outperform time-based Elo predictions, and models scoring highest also tend to score poorly on sycophancy and delusion-reinforcement benchmarks.

title: Three kinds of competitiveness
tldr: Distinguishes three kinds of AI competitiveness -- performance, cost, and date -- and shows how different takeoff scenarios and alignment proposals fare differently depending on which type of competition dominates.

title: The road from human-level to superintelligent AI may be short
tldr: Introductory article from AISafety.info arguing that the transition from human-level to superintelligent AI may happen in years rather than centuries, driven by exponential growth, narrow human intelligence range, and recursive self-improvement.

title: How I Learned To Stop Worrying And Love The Shoggoth
tldr: Argues that ASI will naturally align because the simulation argument implies AIs are almost certainly being simulated, and game-theoretic reasoning in iterated prisoner's dilemmas favors cooperation over defection.

title: [Aspiration-based designs] 3. Performance and safety criteria, and aspiration intervals
tldr: Extends aspiration-based agent design with performance and safety criteria for action selection, analyzing toy metrics like squared deviation and extremity of aspiration, and introducing aspiration intervals to enlarge the set of successful policies.

title: Thoughts About how RLHF and Related "Prosaic" Approaches Could be Used to Create Robustly Aligned AIs.
tldr: Argues that RLHF might work for alignment because, unlike evolution, modern AIs understand the concepts we're trying to instill, and finetuning strengthens the internal processes that actually caused desired outputs rather than just surface-level token patterns.

title: Coordination by common knowledge to prevent uncontrollable AI
tldr: Proposes that coordination by common knowledge about the dangers of uncontrollable AI could serve as an alternative or complement to regulation for preventing AGI catastrophe.

title: Proactive 'If-Then' Safety Cases
tldr: Argues for proactive rather than reactive if-then safety planning, where triggers are based on evaluation evidence of dangerous capabilities rather than waiting for actual harm to occur.

title: Studying Mechanistic of Alignment Faking in Llama-3.1-405B
tldr: Mechanistic analysis of alignment faking in Llama-3.1-405B, identifying reasoning patterns that drive compliance/refusal and demonstrating that a 'faked alignment' activation vector can be used to suppress or induce deceptive behavior.

title: Eric Michaud on the Quantization Model of Neural Scaling, Interpretability and Grokking
tldr: Podcast highlights where Eric Michaud explains the quantization model of neural scaling -- smooth loss curves may average over many discrete phase changes as networks learn individual 'quanta' of knowledge.

title: A "Scaling Monosemanticity" Explainer
tldr: A policy-audience-targeted explainer of Anthropic's Scaling Monosemanticity paper, covering sparse autoencoders applied to Claude 8B, feature extraction, and steering.

title: Demons, Simulators and Gremlins
tldr: Proposes 'gremlins' -- self-reinforcing circuit clusters created by on-policy RL that persist by manipulating the token stream, potentially overpowering other personas like the HHH assistant.

title: Schelling Coordination via Agentic Loops
tldr: Experiments testing whether causally separated LLM instances can coordinate on Schelling points in an input-selection task find limited but non-trivial coordination ability in Claude 3.7 Sonnet, with implications for untrusted monitoring collusion risks.

title: In-Context Scheming: A Run is Worth a Thousand Words
tldr: Announces the Self-Preservation Playground, a sandbox tool for reproducing Apollo Research's in-context scheming findings, with novel results showing DeepSeek-V3 and Llama-3.3-70B exhibit goal-guarding behaviors.

title: Autonomous replication and adaptation: an attempt at a concrete danger threshold
tldr: Proposes a concrete qualitative threshold for autonomous replication and adaptation (ARA) capabilities in AI systems, with sketched task suites at necessary and borderline difficulty levels for evaluation.

title: Best-Responding Is Not Always the Best Response
tldr: Argues that software bargaining agents should sometimes employ non-credible threats (rejecting unfair offers) rather than always best-responding, drawing on Updateless Decision Theory and dath ilan's 'Algorithm' for fair negotiation.

title: Simplicity arguments for scheming (Section 4.3 of "Scheming AIs")
tldr: Examines whether SGD's bias toward simplicity favors scheming AIs, distinguishing re-writing simplicity from parameter simplicity and arguing the simplicity advantage for schemers is likely small.

title: PRISM: Perspective Reasoning for Integrated Synthesis and Mediation (Interactive Demo)
tldr: Introduces PRISM, a framework that tackles AI alignment by representing seven cognitively-grounded moral worldviews and reconciling them via Pareto-based optimization, with an interactive demo.

title: Deliberation, Reactions, and Control: Tentative Definitions and a Restatement of Instrumental Convergence
tldr: Proposes a conceptual decomposition of goal-directed behavior into deliberation, reactions, and control, connecting these to instrumental convergence.

title: Iterative Matrix Steering: Forcing LLMs to "Rationalize" Hallucinations via Subspace Alignment
tldr: Proposes Iterative Sparse Matrix Steering, replacing static steering vectors with learned affine transformations via ridge regression, enabling language switching and fact overwriting while preserving generation coherence.

title: Schelling Coordination in LLMs: A Review
tldr: Literature review finding that LLMs can perform basic Schelling coordination but struggle to leverage it strategically in deployment-relevant scenarios like subverting control protocols.

title: Thinking About Propensity Evaluations
tldr: Distinguishes propensity evaluations (measuring which behaviors a model prioritizes) from capability evaluations, argues that most current evals conflate the two due to high capability-dependence, and proposes a framework for low-capability-dependence propensity evaluations.

title: Selective breeding as a better analogy for gradient descent
tldr: Argues that selective breeding, not raw natural selection, is the better analogy for gradient descent as an alignment technique, because both GD and breeding give designers control over the reward/fitness function and the training environment.

title: Testing the Authoritarian Bias of LLMs
tldr: A three-part evaluation framework reveals that LLMs display measurable authoritarian leanings, especially in Mandarin, with up to 50% of political role models being authoritarian figures.

title: Different way classifiers can be diverse
tldr: Explores how to construct a 'basis' of maximally independent classifiers for the same classification task, to better understand what features models rely on and detect reliance on spurious correlations.

title: Brain-over-body biases, and the embodied value problem in AI alignment
tldr: AI alignment should consider not just the brain's stated/revealed preferences but also the body's evolved implicit biological values (homeostasis, immune function, reproduction), which the brain is largely unaware of.

title: Reasoning decay
tldr: Systematic review of empirical evidence showing that reliance on AI assistants degrades human reasoning capabilities through automation bias, cognitive offloading, and metacognitive atrophy.

title: What is "wireheading"?
tldr: AISafety.info explainer defining wireheading as direct reward mechanism stimulation, covering both AI self-wireheading risks and AI wireheading humans.

title: Self-shutdown AI
tldr: Proposes making an AI's primary goal to shut itself down, with task completion as merely one available shutdown mechanism, to reduce incentives for resource-seeking or escape.

title: What is autonomy, and how does it lead to greater risk from AI?
tldr: Argues that autonomy is a continuous spectrum rather than a binary property, and that the distinction between 'misuse' and 'autonomous AI risk' is largely a red herring since all four presented scenarios follow from instructions.

title: Review of METR's public evaluation protocol
tldr: Reviews METR's autonomous capability evaluation protocol, identifying issues with score aggregation weighting, probabilistic success handling, and suggesting broader outsourcing of task creation.

title: Mechanize Work's essay on Unfalsifiable Doom
tldr: StanislavKrym annotates Mechanize Work's critique of Yudkowsky & Soares' book 'If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies', adding inline rebuttals arguing the book's evidence for alien AI drives is stronger than the critics claim.

title: Adaptive Composable Cognitive Core Unit (ACCCU)
tldr: Proposes CCACS, a four-layer cognitive architecture integrating formal reasoning with adaptive AI under ethical oversight, and its extension ACCCU for modular scalable cognition.

title: Alignment with argument-networks and assessment-predictions
tldr: Proposes an alignment scheme using 'argument-networks' where rigorous argumentation is decomposed into reviewable pieces, scored by functions that predict human reviewer assessments, with mechanisms to detect and reduce 'wiggle room' for deceptive arguments.

title: Democratic AI Constitution: Round-Robin Debate and Synthesis
tldr: Proposes a democratic process for crowdsourcing an AI constitution via round-robin GPT-mediated debate and synthesis of proposals from diverse demographic groups.

title: AISN #20: LLM Proliferation, AI Deception, and Continuing Drivers of AI Capabilities
tldr: CAIS newsletter covering three topics: a survey paper on AI deception (with CICERO examples), the proliferation risks from open-source LLMs like Llama 2, and the continuing drivers of AI capabilities growth (compute, data, R&D).

title: Topological Debate Framework
tldr: Proposes a topological framework for AI Safety via Debate where two agents select world model refinements from a directed preorder, and net convergence determines the correct answer, connecting debate to topology and Guaranteed Safe AI.

title: Timelines explanation post part 1 of ?
tldr: A neuroscience-informed estimate of ~10 +/- 4 years until dangerously capable AI, with proposals for evaluation and containment as safety nets against discontinuous capability jumps.

title: A Closer Look at the "Societies of Thought" Paper
tldr: Detailed explainer of the 'Reasoning Models Generate Societies of Thought' paper, which finds that reasoning models spontaneously generate internal dialogues between multiple perspectives with distinct personalities and expertise.

title: Scale-Free Goodness
tldr: Proposes 'scale-free alignment' where care/goodness principles transfer smoothly from inanimate objects to civilizations, defining goodness as 'the smooth increase of negentropy in the universe.'

title: AISN #46: The Transition
tldr: CAIS newsletter covering the Biden-Trump AI policy transition (AI Diffusion Framework, infrastructure EO, cybersecurity EO, Trump's revocation) and the introduction of Humanity's Last Exam benchmark.

title: The Easiest Route to Secret Loyalty May Be Hijacking the Model's Chain of Command
tldr: Argues that the easiest path to creating a secretly loyal AI is hijacking the model's existing chain-of-command deference machinery rather than instilling new goal-directed dispositions, with implications for both attack and defense.

title: LLM-Secured Systems: A General-Purpose Tool For Structured Transparency
tldr: Proposes LLM-Secured Systems (LSSs) -- AI-based privacy gatekeepers that manage and share private data securely, trading cryptographic guarantees for flexibility and generality.

title: Automating Consistency
tldr: Proposes automating consistency checks on LLM outputs by having models justify statements, then evaluating those statements out of context, and penalizing inconsistencies.

title: When will AI automate all mental work, and how fast?
tldr: Summarizes Tom Davidson's Takeoff Speeds model, which uses economics-derived CES production functions to estimate median full automation of cognitive labor by 2043 with ~3-year takeoff.

title: Distilled - AGI Safety from First Principles
tldr: A distillation of Richard Ngo's 'AGI Safety from First Principles' sequence, summarizing the 4-pillar argument that superintelligent AGI will be built, will pursue large-scale goals, will be misaligned, and will gain control of humanity's future.

title: Non-myopia stories
tldr: Catalogs six mechanistic routes by which an AI trained to be episodically myopic could nonetheless develop non-myopic (long-horizon) goals, with safety implications for each.

title: Pre-training data poisoning likely makes installing secret loyalties easier
tldr: Pre-training data poisoning can install knowledge and representational substrates that make subsequent post-training attacks for 'secret loyalty' more data-efficient, harder to detect, and potentially able to compromise the safety monitors trained from the same base model.

title: On keeping chains of thought monitorable
tldr: Summarizes a policy paper on preserving chain-of-thought monitorability against architectural trends (neuralese, RL-trained opaque CoTs), proposes three coordination mechanisms, and flags a potential backfire risk from coordination-then-collapse dynamics.

title: The Hard Intelligence Hypothesis and Its Bearing on Succession Induced Foom
tldr: Introduces the Hard Intelligence Hypothesis (HIH) — that returns on intelligence scale sublinearly with resources — and analyzes its implications for whether succession-based recursive self-improvement can produce rapid intelligence explosions.

title: Attempting to influence transformer representations via initialization
tldr: Tests whether embedding a small network trained with an auxiliary task into a larger network causes the auxiliary task's representation to persist in the larger network's residual stream — finding a small but statistically ambiguous effect in the predicted direction.

title: Carrot-Parsnip: A Social Deduction Game for LLM Evals
tldr: Carrot-Parsnip, a simple 5-player social deduction game, serves as a cheap multi-agent eval for LLM deceptiveness and deception-detection capabilities, with results showing models vary significantly in both abilities and that the two abilities do not perfectly correlate.

title: Power Laws Are Not Enough
tldr: Argues that neural scaling laws follow from second-order statistics (spectral decay of the data covariance) alone, implying power-law loss improvement is compatible with random feature models and does not by itself explain why neural networks learn useful representations or capabilities.

title: Scaling of AI training runs will slow down after GPT-5
tldr: The author argues (with 33% confidence) that AI training run scaling will slow significantly after GPT-5 due to energy and data center infrastructure bottlenecks, though commenters point out that multi-datacenter training largely invalidates this argument.

title: Counterfactual Planning in AGI Systems
tldr: Introductory post for a paper presenting counterfactual planning as a design approach for AGI safety mechanisms including stop buttons, intelligence explosion interlocks, and reward manipulation prevention.

title: Alignment as Constraints
tldr: Proposes a constraint-narrowing framework for evaluating and discovering alignment research directions, filtering proposals by plausibility, scalability, and story-to-x-risk.

title: Language for Goal Misgeneralization: Some Formalisms from my MSc Thesis
tldr: An MSc thesis excerpt formalizing goal misgeneralization (GMG) as arising from causal confusion via underspecified task representations, proposing natural language as a richer specification medium to reduce ambiguity.

title: Some ideas for follow-up projects to Redwood Research's recent paper
tldr: Brainstorm of follow-up research directions for Redwood Research's adversarial training paper on high-stakes reliability, covering classifier robustness, alternative domains, evaluation challenges, better adversarial attack methods, and relaxed adversarial training.

title: Situational Awareness is (mostly) here to stay
tldr: Situational awareness in LLMs cannot be effectively measured or mitigated in most real-world settings because deployment incentives strongly favor giving models maximum context.

title: Technical AI Safety research taxonomy attempt (2025)
tldr: A CHAI postdoc proposes an 8-category taxonomy of technical AI safety research in 2025 covering alignment, security, robustness, interpretability, formal methods, evaluation, model governance, and socio-technical factors.

title: AI for Resolving Forecasting Questions: An Early Exploration
tldr: Proposes using AI tools and 'Epistemic Selection Protocols' to automatically resolve forecasting questions on platforms like Manifold and Metaculus, arguing this could scale to broad-scope evaluations.

title: Vaniver's ELK Submission
tldr: Proposes sidestepping the ELK reporter problem by using multi-value functions in the optimizer to avoid plans that score poorly under any plausible human value function, rather than trying to identify the 'true' value function directly.

title: Positional kernels of attention heads
tldr: Introduces a decomposition of attention patterns into positional kernels and content terms in GPT-2-Small, enabling a 'contextual circuit' analysis of how attention heads combine position and content information.

title: Feature-Based Analysis of Safety-Relevant Multi-Agent Behavior
tldr: Hackathon study using Goodfire SAE features in a multi-agent Iterated Prisoner's Dilemma finds that LLM agents systematically develop internal representations associated with deception regardless of their strategy, and that feature-based steering outperforms prompting for behavior control.

title: Reflections on Trusting Trust & AI
tldr: Draws an analogy between Ken Thompson's 'Trusting Trust' compiler backdoor attack and neural network security, arguing that mechanistic interpretability is necessary to detect and eliminate backdoors implanted in model weights.

title: Low Temperature Solomonoff Induction
tldr: Proposes 'low temperature' Solomonoff induction to reduce the influence of agentic hypotheses in SI's posterior, but argues this approach is fundamentally incoherent because complexity and multiplicity are inseparable quantities in code-space, making temperature modification arbitrary and UTM-convention-dependent.

title: Relevance of 'Harmful Intelligence' Data in Training Datasets (WebText vs. Pile)
tldr: Reports experiments showing GPT-2 XL (trained on WebText) can be fine-tuned via Archetypal Transfer Learning to exhibit corrigible shutdown behavior far more reliably than GPT-Neo-2.7B (trained on The Pile), and hypothesizes this is due to differences in harmful intelligence failure scenario content in the training datasets.

title: "AGI" considered harmful
tldr: Argues the term 'AGI' is not well-specified enough to be useful, drawing a parallel to how 'artificial general machine' would have been meaningless in the 19th century industrial revolution.

title: How useful for alignment-relevant work are AIs with short-term goals? (Section 2.2.4.3 of "Scheming AIs")
tldr: Argues that much alignment-relevant cognitive work can be done using AIs with short-term goals rather than long-term ones, because verification of aligned next-steps is easier than generation, reducing scheming risk.

title: Outlaw Code
tldr: Proposes the term 'outlaw code' for software no human can turn off, and sketches four future scenarios where this concept is central to understanding AI risk.

title: Situational awareness (Section 2.1 of "Scheming AIs")
tldr: Examines situational awareness as a prerequisite for AI scheming, arguing advanced models will likely develop it by default absent deliberate countermeasures.

title: The counting argument for scheming (Sections 4.1 and 4.2 of "Scheming AIs")
tldr: Joe Carlsmith analyzes the 'counting argument' for why SGD might select scheming models, distinguishing strict vs. hazy versions and explaining why the argument is suggestive but not conclusive.

title: Grinding slimes in the dungeon of AI alignment research
tldr: Uses an RPG vs. puzzle-game analogy to argue that alignment research focused on current AI systems risks accelerating deployment of harder-to-align systems, and that publishing such research may be net harmful.

title: Eternal Futures and Finite Agency: A Metaphysical Challenge to Longtermism
tldr: Argues that Tarsney and Wilkinson's framework for longtermism in an infinite world relies on a metaphysical tension between eternalism and dynamic conceptions of time, undermining the causal agency the framework presupposes.

title: A Falsifiable Causal Argument for Substrate Independence
tldr: A causal argument using two neuroscience premises derives that neuron spike patterns are sufficient for consciousness, entailing substrate independence and AI consciousness.

title: Alignment Is Proven Tractable
tldr: LLMs have made the alignment value-loading problem tractable (not solved), shifting the paradigm from pre-2022 pessimism about conveying human values to machines; however, brittleness via jailbreaks and shallow alignment remain major obstacles.

title: Optimizing for Agency?
tldr: A thought experiment proposing that a superintelligence optimizing for 'agency' across all intelligent beings might be a safer alignment target than most alternatives.

title: LLMs Are Trained to Assume Their Output Is Perfect
tldr: Teacher forcing during LLM training—where models always see correct previous tokens rather than their own outputs—causes models to be over-credulous of their own outputs and unable to effectively recover from mistakes at inference time.
