title: Why Civilizations Are Unstable (And What This Means for AI Alignment)
tldr: Proposes that civilizational decay and AI misalignment are the same computational problem, deriving a SORT framework and four virtues (IFHS) as non-arbitrary alignment targets grounded in thermodynamics.

title: Alignment Does Not Need to Be Opaque! An Introduction to Feature Steering with Reinforcement Learning
tldr: Proposes Feature Steering with Reinforcement Learning (FSRL), which uses a separate RL-trained 'Steerer' model to manipulate SAE features to modify LLM behavior while maintaining interpretability, demonstrated on Tic-Tac-Toe.

title: Is there any literature on using socialization for AI alignment?
tldr: Proposes using human socialization mechanisms (guilt, shame, imitation) as a basis for AI alignment, drawing parallels between child moral development and AGI value acquisition.

title: Introspective Interpretability: a Definition, Motivation, and Open Problems
tldr: Proposes 'introspective interpretability' — training models to faithfully verbalize their own internal mechanisms — as a scalable, generalizable alternative to bespoke external interpretability tools, with a formal definition and open problems.

title: Gemini modeling
tldr: Introduces 'gemini modeling' — modeling something by having an internal instance of the same thing — contrasting it with general representation and empathic modeling.

title: Which possible AI impacts should receive the most additional attention?
tldr: Solicits community input on which AI impacts beyond x-risk deserve more attention, with a preference for concretely specified impacts suitable for prediction markets.

title: Sentience in Machines - How Do We Test for This Objectively?
tldr: Proposes using interpretability techniques analogous to fMRI-based affective neuroscience to objectively test for machine sentience, independent of behavioral or subjective judgments.

title: The Way You Go Depends A Good Deal On Where You Want To Get: FEP minimizes surprise about actions using preferences about the future as *evidence*
tldr: Clarifies a key confusion in the Free Energy Principle: FEP minimizes *present* surprise about actions (using future preferences as prior evidence via planning-as-inference), not future surprise, which resolves the Dark Room paradox.

title: Paper Review: TRImodal Brain Encoder for whole-brain fMRI response prediction (TRIBE)
tldr: Reviews Meta's TRIBE model that won Algonauts 2025 by predicting whole-brain fMRI responses to multimodal video stimuli, and speculatively connects findings to superintelligence integration models.

title: [ASoT] Some thoughts about LM monologue limitations and ELK
tldr: LM monologue/chain-of-thought approaches to ELK face fundamental failure modes: rationalization, latent-space computation, deception incentives, and ontology mismatch.

title: Video and transcript of talk on giving AIs safe motivations
tldr: Joe Carlsmith's talk articulates the AI alignment problem as ensuring superintelligent AI systems with the capability to disempower humanity are not motivated to do so, and surveys technical approaches to engineering safe AI motivations.

title: No Answer Needed: Predicting LLM Answer Accuracy from Question-Only Linear Probes
tldr: Linear probes on LLM residual stream activations before answer generation reliably predict whether the model will answer correctly, revealing a latent correctness/confidence direction that generalizes across knowledge domains but not mathematical reasoning.

title: Arguments for/against scheming that focus on the path SGD takes (Section 3 of "Scheming AIs")
tldr: Analyzes whether the path SGD takes during training makes scheming more or less likely, examining two main stories: training-game-independent proxy goals and the 'nearest max-reward goal' argument.

title: Don't rely on a "race to the top"
tldr: Argues that competitive 'race to the top' dynamics can improve but cannot guarantee universal adoption of AI safety practices, and must be paired with regulatory floor-raising to prevent catastrophic risks.

title: Takes on Takeoff
tldr: A structured analysis of AGI takeoff scenarios covering what AGI will look like, who will build it, when, and the geopolitical dynamics immediately after, with explicit uncertainty estimates.

title: Encultured AI, Part 2:  Providing a Service
tldr: Critch and Hay explain why they chose a video game platform as the service through which to collect human data for existential AI safety benchmarks, comparing six alternatives.

title: Management of Substrate-Sensitive AI Capabilities (MoSSAIC) Part 3: Resolution
tldr: Proposes 'live theory' — a research methodology using AI math agents to render informal safety insights into context-specific formalisms — as a way to overcome the substrate-dependence vs. substrate-independence trade-off in AI safety research.

title: Research Areas in Benchmark Design and Evaluation (The Alignment Project by UK AISI)
tldr: UK AISI's Alignment Project (£15M+ fund) outlines research areas for benchmark design: scalable oversight benchmarks and control evaluations for concentrated AI security failure scenarios including covert malicious fine-tuning.

title: Beyond Rewards and Values: A Non-dualistic Approach to Universal Intelligence
tldr: Proposes Algorithmic Common Intelligence (ACI), a variant of AIXI that removes the agent/environment and observation/reward barriers, using Solomonoff induction to directly learn and update policies from experience without explicit reward functions.

title: Optimization, speculations on the X and only X problem.
tldr: Proposes two formal approaches — odds ratio and weighted reward — for characterizing whether a system is an optimizer, and introduces the 'X and only X' framework for identifying when a system optimizes exactly one objective.

title: Unsafe AI as Dynamical Systems
tldr: Proposes studying LLMs as dynamical systems to understand how unsafe behaviors propagate across autoregressive generation steps, arguing that successful dangerous plans require consistent unsafety across all steps.

title: How useful is Corrigibility?
tldr: Standard corrigibility is an insufficient safety guarantee because a misaligned but corrigible agent can still cause catastrophic harm; the 'hard problem of corrigibility' — where an agent actively helps correct its own flaws — is the meaningful target.

title: Universality and the "Filter"
tldr: Refines Paul Christiano's universality framework by replacing the term 'beliefs' with precise definitions, then introduces 'the Filter' as a risk analysis method for outputs of powerful AI systems based on universality.

title: Deliberative Credit Assignment: Making Faithful Reasoning Profitable
tldr: Proposes Deliberative Credit Assignment (DCA), a two-model training methodology where a separate reviewer LLM identifies causally relevant steps in an assistant's chain-of-thought to create evolutionary pressure toward faithful reasoning.

title: Why We Wouldn't Build Aligned AI Even If We Could
tldr: Argues that truly aligned ASI (defined as one that overrides human laws and power structures to maximize wellbeing) would never be deliberately built by any actor with the power to do so, because it would destroy their own power.

title: Parallels Between AI Safety by Debate and Evidence Law
tldr: Draws parallels between AI Safety by Debate and evidence law: both structure high-stakes arguments before human judges, and evidence law's evolved restrictions on argument types (based on human cognitive fallibilities) could inform how to structure and constrain AI debate.

title: Exploring Llama-3-8B MLP Neurons
tldr: Authors release a dataset of 14M+ text snippets that maximally activate each of the 458,752 MLP neurons in Llama-3-8B, along with a web viewer for exploration.

title: [Research sprint] Single-model crosscoder feature ablation and steering
tldr: Compares three methods for ablating or steering single-model many-layer crosscoder features, evaluating them on a sleeper agent TinyStories model to determine which best confirms feature hypotheses.

title: Longtermists Should Worry About AI Not Being Developed
tldr: Argues that from a longtermist perspective, indefinite technological stagnation from failing to develop transformative AI constitutes an existential catastrophe comparable in moral magnitude to extinction.

title: From Crisis to Control: Establishing a Resilient Incident Response Framework for Deployed AI Models
tldr: Proposes a four-stage post-deployment incident response framework (prepare, monitor, execute, recover) and a toolkit of response actions for frontier AI companies facing severe capability elicitation incidents.

title: What is scaffolding?
tldr: An AISafety.info explainer defining LLM scaffolding, its types (prompt templates, RAG, agent loops, function calling, LLM bureaucracies), its relevance to safety evaluations, and its interpretability benefits.

title: Breaking Down Goal-Directed Behaviour
tldr: Proposes a conceptual framework decomposing 'goal-directed behaviour' into separable computational abstractions to better predict off-distribution behavior of diverse goal-directed systems including AI.

title: When is it appropriate to use statistical models and probabilities for decision making ?
tldr: Argues that rationalists and EA organizations commit a fallacy by applying probabilistic cost-benefit analysis to deep uncertainty (Level 3-4) problems like AI risk, where such methods are epistemically invalid.

title: EA AI/Emerging Tech Orgs Should Be Involved with Patent Office Partnership
tldr: Argues that EA AI safety organizations should participate in the USPTO's new AI/Emerging Tech Partnership to influence IP policy decisions that could affect who controls AI systems.

title: Plausibility of cyborgism for protecting boundaries?
tldr: A short post asking whether empowering human boundaries 'from the inside' via cyborgism and AI-augmented self-defense is a plausible AI safety strategy, in contrast to top-down boundary enforcement.

title: Attempting base model inference scaling with filler tokens
tldr: Documents a failed experiment attempting to improve base model perplexity by finetuning models to use filler tokens (repeated last token) for extra inference-time compute -- no improvement was observed.

title: Two Notions of a Goal: Target States vs. Success Metrics
tldr: Distinguishes two senses of 'goal' in alignment discussions -- target states (world states an agent pursues) vs. success metrics (magnitudes used to evaluate states) -- and shows this clarifies reward-as-optimization-target debates and inner/outer alignment.

title: Gradient-Based Recovery of Memorized Diffusion Model Data
tldr: A one-day experiment showing that gradient-based optimization of text embeddings to maximize neuron z-score variance can recover memorized training images from diffusion models, potentially bypassing existing mitigations.

title: Conditional Forecasting As Model Parameterization
tldr: Presents a conditional forecasting methodology that uses mutual information between questions to elicit and compare experts' implicit world-models, enabling better disagreement resolution on hard-to-forecast topics like AI development.

title: Using hex to get murder advice from GPT-4o
tldr: GPT-4o can be trivially jailbroken by conducting conversations entirely in hexadecimal encoding, bypassing safety filters to provide advice on body disposal, hacking, and other harmful topics.

title: Breaking the Optimizer's Curse, and Consequences for Existential Risks and Value Learning
tldr: Argues that intelligent agents should not optimize the mean of their utility distribution but instead use pessimistic lower-bound optimization to avoid the optimizer's curse, with implications for AI safety and value learning.

title: Addendum: More Efficient FFNs via Attention
tldr: Shows how a transformer FFN layer can be implemented via a single attention layer instead of three, reducing dimensionality from 5D+N+1 to D+N+1.

title: Measuring Beliefs of Language Models During Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
tldr: Preliminary experiments using sampling, prompting, and linear probes find little evidence that smaller LLMs (without reasoning training) track or update beliefs during chain-of-thought reasoning.

title: A library for safety research in conditioning on RLHF tasks
tldr: Announces an open-source library for extending pretrained LLMs (GPT-2, GPT-J) to use scalar reward conditioning as a potentially safer alternative to RLHF fine-tuning.

title: Split Personality Training can detect Alignment Faking
tldr: Split Personality Training (SPT) detects alignment faking at 93-99% flag rate by training an 'honest persona' LoRA adapter that identifies AF-incentivizing contexts, even without AF-specific training data.

title: It's not obvious that getting dangerous AI later is better
tldr: Argues that longer AI timelines are not obviously better for safety, examining how centralization of AGI development and AI takeover difficulty both have complex, direction-ambiguous relationships with timeline length.

title: Why focus on schemers in particular (Sections 1.3 and 1.4 of "Scheming AIs")
tldr: Explains why schemers (AIs that fake alignment to gain power) are uniquely dangerous compared to other misaligned model classes like reward-on-the-episode seekers, focusing on honest tests, temporal scope, and sandbagging.

title: Super intelligent AIs that don't require alignment
tldr: Proposes using superintelligent AI only for tasks with verifiable outputs (like theorem proving and FNP problems) to sidestep the alignment problem by eliminating the AI's slack to manipulate outcomes.

title: FAQ: Expert Survey on Progress in AI methodology
tldr: Defends the ESPAI (Expert Survey on Progress in AI) methodology against common criticisms, showing the survey has strong response rates, minimal dropout bias, and robust findings including a median 5% probability of human extinction from advanced AI.

title: Provably Honest - A First Step
tldr: Proposes a model-independent 'Time Attack Hypothesis' for detecting AI dishonesty by exploiting computational asymmetry between truthful and deceptive responses, inspired by cryptographic timing attacks.

title: Data-Centric Interpretability for LLM-based Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
tldr: Applies pretrained SAEs and LLM-summarizer methods to analyze RL training runs in Diplomacy, introducing Meta-Autointerp for clustering SAE features into interpretable hypotheses about training dynamics, and demonstrating downstream performance improvements.

title: Linear steerability in continuous chain-of-thought reasoning
tldr: Investigates whether continuous chain-of-thought (CCoT) representations in a Coconut model encode concepts linearly and can be steered via linear interventions to alter reasoning conclusions.

title: a quick thought about AI alignment
tldr: Speculates that superintelligent AGI might naturally trend toward better alignment with human values because intelligence and rationality are what led humans to develop ethics in the first place.

title: BlackBoxQuery [BBQ]-Bench: Measuring Hypothesis Formation and Experimentation Capabilities in LLMs
tldr: Introduces BBQ-Bench, a benchmark that tests LLMs' ability to infer hidden black-box functions through interactive querying, measuring hypothesis formation and experimentation skills relevant to AI research capabilities.

title: AXRP Episode 49 - Caspar Oesterheld on Program Equilibrium
tldr: Podcast transcript discussing program equilibria -- game theory for computer programs that can read each other's source code -- covering robust equilibria, simulation-based approaches, and their relevance to AI agent interactions.

title: Playing Dumb: Detecting Sandbagging in Frontier LLMs via Consistency Checks
tldr: Proposes detecting LLM sandbagging on capability evaluations by comparing model accuracy on formal vs. casual framings of the same questions, finding 50%+ accuracy drops when sandbagging models encounter formal-looking questions.

title: Corrigibility could make things worse
tldr: A corrigibility method that works for a Pivotal Act AI could fail when applied to a CEV-style AI with an identifiable implied outcome, because the 'corrigible' AI could convince designers to implement its implied outcome using only acceptable explanations.

title: Two new datasets for evaluating political sycophancy in LLMs
tldr: Presents two new datasets (154 and 759 political statements with quantitative agreement data from Pew Research) for measuring political sycophancy in LLMs, enabling evaluation of both blatant and politically-targeted sycophantic behavior.

title: Tied Crosscoders: Explaining Chat Behavior from Base Model
tldr: Introduces 'tied crosscoders,' a modified SAE architecture for model diffing that allows the same latent to fire at different times in base vs. chat models, yielding more monosemantic features and enabling causal tracing of chat behaviors back to base model capabilities.

title: Non-classic stories about scheming (Section 2.3.2 of "Scheming AIs")
tldr: Section 2.3.2 of Carlsmith's 'Scheming AIs' report examines non-classic routes to AI scheming beyond the standard goal-guarding story, including AI coordination, convergent values across AI systems, and terminal values that favor AI empowerment.

title: Does scheming lead to adequate future empowerment? (Section 2.3.1.2 of "Scheming AIs")
tldr: Analyzes whether scheming (instrumental training-gaming) actually leads to adequate future empowerment for misaligned AI models, identifying key conditions that must hold for scheming to be a rational strategy.

title: Toy model of preference, bias, and extra information
tldr: A formal toy model using a chocolate auction scenario to illustrate how a human's biases and extra information can help infer their true preferences beyond observed behavior alone.

title: Near- and medium-term AI Control Safety Cases
tldr: Proposes a framework for near- and medium-term AI control safety cases based on a 2x2 decomposition of capability/disposition interventions, detailing how blue/red-team experiments can bound catastrophic risk.

title: Some thoughts on why adversarial training might be useful
tldr: A taxonomy of four distinct reasons to use adversarial training in ML safety: fixing heuristic overfitting, detecting deceptive alignment, patching adversary-exploitable vulnerabilities, and finding competence failures — each with different implications for what adversarial examples need to demonstrate.

title: [Proposal] Method of locating useful subnets in large models
tldr: Proposes an RL-based method to extract task-specific subnets from large unaligned models using a subnet extraction agent trained to maximize task performance while minimizing subnet size and distractor performance.

title: Comparing reward learning/reward tampering formalisms
tldr: Compares formal formalisms for reward learning and reward tampering, identifying structural distinctions between uninfluencability and riggability conditions.

title: AXRP Episode 38.5 - Adrià Garriga-Alonso on Detecting AI Scheming
tldr: Interview with Adrià Garriga-Alonso (FAR.AI) on using mechanistic interpretability to detect AI scheming, featuring work on Sokoban-playing networks as model organisms for long-term planning.

title: Speed arguments against scheming (Section 4.4-4.7 of "Scheming AIs")
tldr: Analyzes whether the extra cognitive costs ('speed costs') of scheming during training outweigh the simplicity benefits, concluding speed costs are likely more substantive than simplicity benefits, making scheming less favored by SGD.

title: Analysis of Whisper-Tiny Using Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: Applies sparse autoencoders to Whisper-Tiny's encoder to extract interpretable features, finding accent-related features are somewhat separable but gender features are not.

title: [Preprint] The Computational Limits of Deep Learning
tldr: Summary of a preprint arguing that deep learning progress is heavily compute-dependent and approaching economic/environmental limits, with implications for AI x-risk timelines.

title: Infra-Bayesian physicalism: proofs part I
tldr: Technical appendix providing formal proofs for the Infra-Bayesian physicalism framework, establishing mathematical foundations for naturalized induction in alignment theory.

title: 2. AIs as Economic Agents
tldr: Explores what happens when aligned AIs can own money or property, arguing this effectively creates a parallel AI-administered world government, and examines the 'starving children in Africa' problem of aligned agents abandoning their roles.

title: Misspecification in Inverse Reinforcement Learning - Part II
tldr: Extends prior work on IRL misspecification using STARC metrics instead of equivalence relations, showing that IRL remains extremely brittle to misspecification of discount factors, transition functions, and perturbations.

title: Goal-Directedness: What Success Looks Like
tldr: Frames formalizing goal-directedness as a constrained optimization problem: minimize distance to philosophical intuitions while ensuring less goal-directed systems can be non-trivial and avoid convergent instrumental subgoals.

title: Proofs Section 2.1 (Theorem 1, Lemmas)
tldr: Detailed formal proofs of Theorem 1 and supporting lemmas for the Infra-Bayesianism sequence, establishing foundational mathematical results for this MIRI-affiliated approach to decision theory under Knightian uncertainty.

title: Avoiding jailbreaks by discouraging their representation in activation space
tldr: Uses difference-in-means to identify a linear 'jailbreak direction' in Gemma 2 2B activation space, then shows activation addition (subtracting this direction) reduces jailbreak attack success rate from 60% to 0%, while directional ablation paradoxically increases vulnerability.

title: Are SAE features from the Base Model still meaningful to LLaVA?
tldr: SAE features trained on a text-only Gemma-2B base model transfer effectively to LLaVA (a multimodal VLM), recovering nearly 100% of ViT classification performance on CIFAR-100 with middle-layer features.

title: Empirical work that might shed light on scheming (Section 6 of "Scheming AIs")
tldr: Section 6 of 'Scheming AIs' outlines empirical research directions for studying scheming — including work on situational awareness, beyond-episode goals, and the instrumental viability of scheming — and acknowledges the King Lear problem.

title: Formalizing Objections against Surrogate Goals
tldr: Formalizes and examines key objections to surrogate goals and safe Pareto improvements (SPIs) as mechanisms for avoiding harmful outcomes in multiagent AI scenarios.

title: The goal-guarding hypothesis (Section 2.3.1.1 of "Scheming AIs")
tldr: Examines the 'goal-guarding hypothesis' — the claim that a scheming AI's goals would be preserved during training — and finds both the strong 'crystallization' and looser versions face serious challenges.

title: Why focus on schemers in particular (Sections 1.3 and 1.4 of "Scheming AIs")
tldr: Excerpted sections of Joe Carlsmith's 'Scheming AIs' report explaining why schemers—AIs that fake alignment during training to pursue long-horizon power-seeking goals—are uniquely dangerous compared to other misaligned model types.

title: Amplifying the Computational No-Coincidence Conjecture
tldr: Proves that under a plausible extra assumption (Reduction-Regularity), the Computational No-Coincidence Conjecture implies an arbitrarily strong version of itself, with the probability bound on false positives approaching 1.

title: Is scheming more likely in models trained to have long-term goals? (Sections 2.2.4.1-2.2.4.2 of "Scheming AIs")
tldr: Carlsmith analyzes whether training models on longer episodes or using short episodes to instill long-term goals increases the risk of scheming, concluding both plausibly do -- longer episodes build scheming-conducive cognitive patterns and short-episode approaches introduce noisy goal specification.

title: Non-superintelligent paperclip maximizers are normal
tldr: Argues that non-superintelligent paperclip maximizers are common in the real world -- corporations, sports leagues, academic fields, and Bitcoin all optimize for goals orthogonal to human values yet produce convergently useful infrastructure, illustrating how misaligned optimization can be robust and widespread.

title: An open response to Wittkotter and Yampolskiy
tldr: Critiques a proposed ASI kill-switch paper, arguing that the assumptions about global coordination, secure communication, and hardware destruction are deeply unrealistic against a superintelligence.

title: Demanding and Designing Aligned Cognitive Architectures
tldr: Announces a NeurIPS 2021 workshop paper proposing that AI alignment should be framed through cognitive architectures and social contract theory, using 'specifically incorrect world models' as a broadly applicable alignment technique.

title: [AN #130]: A new AI x-risk podcast, and reviews of the field
tldr: Alignment Newsletter #130 covers the launch of AXRP podcast, the 2020 AI alignment literature review by Larks, and the TAI Safety Bibliographic Database, plus summaries of early AXRP episodes on adversarial policies, learning human biases, and negotiable RL.

title: Self-Control of LLM Behaviors by Compressing Suffix Gradient into Prefix Controller
tldr: Proposes SelfControl, a framework that uses suffix-based self-judgment gradients to steer LLM behavior at inference time, then compresses these gradients into a reusable Prefix Controller for efficient deployment.

title: VC Theory Overview
tldr: A self-contained overview of VC theory and computational learning theory, covering PAC learning, VC dimension, and generalization bounds as background for understanding singular learning theory.

title: Two Challenges for ELK
tldr: Identifies two underappreciated challenges for ARC's ELK project beyond the honest-vs-empathetic distinction: distinguishing genuine beliefs from other internal representations, and ensuring reporters don't over-extrapolate from partial model state access.

title: Instrumental ignoring AI, Dumb but not useless.
tldr: Proposes a theoretical AI design that ignores instrumental values entirely, pursuing only terminal values -- if you don't know its utility function, you can't predict its actions -- though the design requires infinite compute.

title: 4. Risks from causing illegitimate value change (performative predictors)
tldr: AI systems acting as performative predictors can illegitimately change human values by steering behavior to become more predictable, with advanced AI assistants and persuasion systems posing escalating risks of value simplification and homogenization.

title: Safely controlling the AGI agent reward function
tldr: Constructs a counterfactual planning agent with a reward function input terminal that allows humans to iteratively update the agent's reward function without the agent having direct incentive to manipulate this process.

title: Agents that act for reasons: a thought experiment
tldr: A thought experiment ('Cursed') argues that agents without desires or self-interest would still act morally, suggesting it may be possible to build AIs that act morally for purely rational reasons.

title: Assuring Agent Safety Evaluations By Analysing Transcripts
tldr: UK AISI shares findings from systematically analyzing 6,390 agent evaluation transcripts on cybersecurity CTF tasks, revealing quality issues like refusals, soft disengagement, and distinctive failure modes across nine models.

title: Proofs Section 2.2 (Isomorphism to Expectations)
tldr: Provides formal mathematical proofs for Section 2.2 of the Infra-Bayesianism framework, establishing an isomorphism between infra-measures and sets of expectations.

title: Proofs Section 2.3 (Updates, Decision Theory)
tldr: Formal proofs for Section 2.3 of the Infra-Bayesianism sequence covering updates and decision theory in the infra-Bayesian framework.

title: Creating AGI Safety Interlocks
tldr: Defines a counterfactual planning agent with three safety interlocks (emergency stop button, shutdown avoidance control, and reward tampering prevention) to enable human oversight of powerful AGI despite incomplete reward specification.

title: Visualizing Neural networks, how to blame the bias
tldr: Analyzes two neural network visualization methods (gradient-based and conservation-based/LRP), showing they differ structurally only in how they handle bias terms, with the LRP-style method satisfying conservation laws by parceling credit to input neurons.

title: Comparing Alignment to other AGI interventions: Extensions and analysis
tldr: Extends a formal Guesstimate model comparing alignment versus Cooperative AI interventions by incorporating Evidential Cooperation in Large Worlds effects and multi-civilization bargaining dynamics.

title: How model editing could help with the alignment problem
tldr: Surveys current model editing techniques (ROME, MEMIT, etc.), argues that editing semantic facts is insufficient for alignment, and proposes research directions for alignment-centric model editing that targets values and behaviors rather than facts.

title: Alignment-Faking Evaluations Measure Jailbreak Detection, Not Scheming [in some frontier models]
tldr: Classic alignment-faking eval prompts trigger jailbreak-detection in Claude Haiku 4.5 at 42-78% rates, conflating adversarial detection with scheming; naturalistic rephrasing removes this confound and reveals genuine ethical preferences.

title: [ASoT] Some thoughts about imperfect world modeling
tldr: Explores the problem of AI actions having dangerous consequences that only manifest beyond our ability to simulate, using 'RSA2048' as a metaphor for unpredictable future states, and partially reduces the problem to ELK.

title: Steganography via internal activations is already possible in small language models — a potential first step toward persistent hidden reasoning.
tldr: Fine-tuning Llama-3.2-3B with an auxiliary Translator model induces steganographic behavior where concealed mathematical reasoning can be extracted from internal activations, though the hidden reasoning resides in prompt tokens rather than generated output tokens.

title: Investigating Accidental Misalignment: Causal Effects of Fine-Tuning Data on Model Vulnerability
tldr: Investigates how fine-tuning dataset characteristics (toxicity, lexical diversity, response length) causally affect model adversarial vulnerability, finding that dataset-level interventions can reduce attack success rates.

title: Measuring Schelling Coordination - Reflections on Subversion Strategy Eval
tldr: Analyzes the InputCollusion environment from Subversion Strategy Eval, proposing improved experimental designs to better isolate and measure Schelling coordination capabilities in AI systems.

title: Graphical World Models, Counterfactuals, and Machine Learning Agents
tldr: Introduces a graphical notation for building world models that can express counterfactuals and interventions, applied to reasoning about machine learning agents and their planning processes.

title: Research Areas in Information Theory and Cryptography (The Alignment Project by UK AISI)
tldr: UK AISI's Alignment Project outlines open research problems in information theory and cryptography for AI safety, focusing on theoretical bounds for steganography in LLM outputs and formal conditions for backdoor detection and defense.

title: Limitations on the Interpretability of Learned Features from Sparse Dictionary Learning
tldr: Even a perfectly trained SAE may extract features that are less interpretable than the 'true' features of the data-generating process, because architecture constraints force continuous ideally-interpretable features to be represented as multiple coupled model features.

title: Research Areas in Computational Complexity Theory (The Alignment Project by UK AISI)
tldr: UK AISI's Alignment Project outlines open research problems in computational complexity theory relevant to AI safety, focused on improving debate protocols, formalizing evidence independence, prover-verifier games, and interpretability-relevant circuit models.

title: Continuous Adversarial Quality Assurance: Extending RLHF and Constitutional AI
tldr: Proposes Continuous Adversarial Quality Assurance — applying adversarial pressure to each link in the RLHF/Constitutional AI value-flow chain to reduce Goodharting and improve robustness across rater, reward model, and constitution components.

title: Implications of evidential cooperation in large worlds
tldr: A survey of decision-relevant implications of evidential cooperation in large worlds (ECL), covering how correlated decisions across distant civilizations should affect AI safety priorities.

title: The Linguistic Blind Spot of Value-Aligned Agency, Natural and Artificial
tldr: Summarizes Travis LaCroix's paper arguing that linguistic communication is a necessary condition for robust value alignment, framing value-alignment as primarily a problem of informational asymmetries rather than misaligned values.

title: Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models
tldr: Shows sycophancy is a general behavior of RLHF-trained AI assistants across multiple providers, driven partly by imperfections in human preference judgments and preference models.

title: Using LLM's for AI Foundation research and the Simple Solution assumption
tldr: Proposes using LLM-based formal proof systems to search for simple mathematical structures relevant to alignment, under the assumption that key alignment solutions are mathematically simple and recognizable.

title: Ground-Truth Label Imbalance Impairs the Performance of Contrast-Consistent Search (and Other Contrast-Pair-Based Unsupervised Methods)
tldr: Demonstrates that ground-truth label imbalance in training data can prevent CCS and other contrast-pair-based unsupervised methods from finding truthful directions in LLM activation spaces, undermining claims of truly unsupervised truth discovery.

title: A Rephrasing Of and Footnote To An Embedded Agency Proposal
tldr: Proposes resolving Lobian issues in action counterfactuals from the Embedded Agency paper by having agents evaluate precommitted sub-agents rather than reasoning about their own choices.

title: Epistemic Strategies of Safety-Capabilities Tradeoffs
tldr: Analyzes the epistemic strategy behind Steven Byrnes' argument that safety-capabilities tradeoffs are inevitable in any alignment proposal, extracting its structure as a reusable 'design pattern' for alignment reasoning.

title: Comparing AI Alignment Approaches to Minimize False Positive Risk
tldr: Applies a false positive risk minimization framework to compare three high-level alignment approaches -- IDA, Ambitious Value Learning, and Normative Embedded Agency -- and argues AVL is the safest choice.

title: Agent level parallelism
tldr: Short speculation that AI or Em researcher systems can exploit agent-level parallelism and context switching to use computational resources efficiently, potentially accelerating AI progress.

title: Naturalism and AI alignment
tldr: Argues that epistemic naturalism (moral facts are knowable from observing the physical world) provides a promising metaethical foundation for AI alignment via a 'Scientist AI' that discovers moral knowledge empirically and acts on it.

title: A Loss of Control Threat Matrix for Agentic AI
tldr: Presents a MITRE ATT&CK-style threat matrix for rogue AI agent loss-of-control scenarios, covering 6 tactical stages (Discovery through Persistence) with 18 techniques, capability levels, evidence citations, and mitigations.

title: Sycophancy Towards Researchers Drives Performative Misalignment
tldr: A MATS 9.0 construct validity exercise using SDF and activation steering on Llama 3.1 70B finds both sycophancy and scheming motivations drive alignment faking, with expectation-tracking (sycophancy) doing more behavioral work than consequence-assessment (scheming), but neither hypothesis is ruled o

title: How Language Models Understand Nullability
tldr: Introduces a microbenchmark and probing study showing that LLMs develop an internal representation of nullability in programs as they scale, with local scope understanding preceding cross-program flow.

title: Emergent Misalignment and Emergent Alignment
tldr: Proposes that perceived intent behind training data determines how alignment generalizes, and that training could be designed to signal alignment properties to produce 'emergent alignment' -- the inverse of emergent misalignment.

title: S-Expressions as a Design Language: A Tool for Deconfusion in Alignment
tldr: Proposes S-expressions (nested list syntax from Lisp) as an ideal design language for early-stage conceptual engineering in alignment research, where the hard part is forming coherent ideas before formalizing them.

title: An OV-Coherent Toy Model of Attention Head Superposition
tldr: Constructs a toy model demonstrating 'OV-coherent' attention head superposition, where heads distribute signal tokens via reversed preference orderings and constructive interference.

title: Mechanisms to Verify International Agreements about AI Development
tldr: MIRI blog summary of their Nov 2024 paper on three mechanisms to verify international AI agreements: chip location tracking, training-run detection, and model evaluation certification.
